reportTrainingRecords.name: Database Locks
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows active database locks and blocking. Identify database performance issues caused by locking and contention.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display active database locks showing what processes are holding locks and what is blocked. Identify 
database performance problems caused by locking. Essential for DBA troubleshooting and performance tuning.

What You'll See: Database locks showing: (1) Locked objects (tables, rows), (2) Lock types (shared, exclusive, update), 
(3) Processes holding locks (SPIDs), (4) Blocked processes waiting for locks, (5) Lock wait times, (6) User/application 
causing locks, (7) SQL statements involved. Highlights blocking chains where process A blocks B, B blocks C, etc. Organized 
by blocking relationships.

Criteria: Real-time snapshot (no date selection), option to show only blocking locks, filter by object or user, and set 
minimum wait time thresholds.

Key Information: Database locks prevent data corruption when multiple users access the same data simultaneously. Normal 
operation - locks acquired and released quickly. Problems occur when: (1) Long-running transactions hold locks too long, (2) 
Blocking chains form - multiple processes waiting on each other, (3) Deadlocks occur - circular waits. Symptoms: users 
report slowness or freezing. This report shows what is locked and who is blocking whom. Use to identify problem transactions, 
kill blocking processes if needed, and optimize queries causing excessive locking. Essential for resolving database 
performance issues.

When to Use This Report:
• Users report database slowness or freezing
• Troubleshoot performance problems
• Identify blocking processes and chains
• Decide whether to kill blocking processes
• Find queries causing excessive locking
• Monitor database concurrency health

Good to Know: Brief locks are normal. Locks held for minutes indicate problems. Kill blocking processes carefully - causes 
their transactions to rollback. Frequent blocking indicates queries need optimization. DBA-level tool for database performance 
troubleshooting.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Database Logins
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows active database connections and user sessions. Monitor who is connected to the database and their activity.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display active database connections showing who is logged in and what they are doing. Monitor database 
user activity and connection health. Essential for database monitoring and security.

What You'll See: Active database sessions showing: (1) User logins and applications, (2) Connection times (when connected), 
(3) Host machines (where connecting from), (4) Database activity (idle, active, sleeping), (5) Session IDs (SPIDs), (6) 
Current SQL statements if executing, (7) Connection counts by user/application. Shows who is using the database right now. 
Organized by user or application.

Criteria: Real-time snapshot (no date selection), filter by user or application, show only active or all sessions, and set 
detail level.

Key Information: Each user connection creates a database session. This shows: (1) Who is connected (users and applications), 
(2) How many connections (total user load), (3) Where connections from (security - expected machines?), (4) What they're 
doing (idle, active, running what?), (5) Long-lived connections (potential issues). Use for: Database user monitoring, 
security auditing (unauthorized access?), capacity planning (connection limits), troubleshooting connection leaks (connections 
not closing), killing problem sessions if needed. Essential for database monitoring and security.

When to Use This Report: Monitor database user activity, identify active connections and sessions, troubleshoot connection 
issues or leaks, verify who is connected (security), check connection capacity usage, and find sessions to kill if needed.

Good to Know: Too many connections can hit database limits. Idle connections waste resources - applications should close 
connections. Unexpected users or machines indicate security issues. DBA-level monitoring tool.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Database Statements
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows active SQL statements executing in database. Monitor query performance and identify long-running or problem queries.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display SQL statements currently executing in the database. Monitor query performance and identify 
long-running or problem queries. Essential for database performance monitoring and optimization.

What You'll See: Active SQL statements showing: (1) SQL query text being executed, (2) Execution time (how long running), 
(3) User/application running the query, (4) Session IDs (SPIDs), (5) CPU and I/O usage, (6) Wait states (blocked, waiting), 
(7) Query plans and statistics. Highlights long-running queries consuming resources. Shows what the database is currently 
working on. Organized by execution time or resource usage.

Criteria: Real-time snapshot, set minimum execution time thresholds (e.g., over 10 seconds), filter by user or database, 
show only active or include recent, and set detail level.

Key Information: Shows what SQL the database is currently executing - the actual queries running right now. Use to: (1) Find 
long-running queries causing slowness, (2) Identify inefficient queries needing optimization, (3) See what is consuming 
database resources (CPU, I/O), (4) Troubleshoot performance problems (which query is slow?), (5) Monitor database workload, 
(6) Kill runaway queries if needed. Queries running for minutes typically indicate problems. Essential for database 
performance monitoring and query optimization.

When to Use This Report: Monitor active database queries, identify long-running or slow queries, troubleshoot performance 
problems, find queries to optimize, track database workload, and identify runaway queries to kill.

Good to Know: Queries taking over 30 seconds likely need optimization. High CPU or I/O indicates resource-intensive queries. 
Save slow query text for later optimization. Use with Database Locks report for complete picture. DBA performance monitoring 
tool.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Update Statistics
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows database table statistics status and runs statistics updates. Maintain query optimizer performance through current statistics.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display database table statistics and update them. Maintain query optimizer performance by keeping 
statistics current. Essential for database performance maintenance.

Key Information: Database statistics tell the query optimizer about data distribution - how many rows, value ranges, data 
patterns. Optimizer uses statistics to choose efficient query plans. Outdated statistics = poor query plans = slow queries. 
Statistics become outdated as data changes. This report shows statistics age and updates them. Run regularly (weekly or after 
major data changes) to maintain performance. Essential database maintenance task.

When to Use: Run weekly statistics updates, after major data loads or changes, when queries suddenly slow down, and as part of 
regular database maintenance. Good practice: Update statistics regularly to maintain optimal query performance.

reportTrainingRecords.name: List Foreign Keys
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows database foreign key relationships. Document database referential integrity constraints and table relationships.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display database foreign key constraints showing table relationships. Document referential integrity. 
Essential for understanding database structure and data relationships.

What You'll See: Foreign key constraints showing: (1) Parent tables (referenced tables), (2) Child tables (referencing 
tables), (3) Columns involved in relationships, (4) Constraint names, (5) Cascade rules (what happens on delete/update). 
Shows complete database relationship structure. Organized by parent table or child table.

Key Information: Foreign keys enforce referential integrity - child records must reference valid parent records. Example: 
invoice_item must reference valid invoice. This report documents all these relationships. Use for: Understanding database 
structure, troubleshooting foreign key violations, planning data changes (what depends on what?), database documentation. 
Essential for database structure understanding.

When to Use: Document database relationships, understand table dependencies, troubleshoot foreign key errors, plan data 
migrations or changes, and support database development.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Foreign Key Violations
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows foreign key violations in database (orphaned records). Identify and fix referential integrity problems and data quality issues.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display foreign key violations showing orphaned child records without valid parents. Identify 
referential integrity problems. Essential for database data quality and integrity maintenance.

What You'll See: Foreign key violations showing: (1) Child records with invalid parent references, (2) Missing parent 
records, (3) Tables and columns involved, (4) Orphaned record counts, (5) Specific violating records with details. Highlights 
data integrity problems requiring correction. Organized by foreign key constraint.

Key Information: Foreign key violations = child records referencing non-existent parents. Example: invoice_item referencing 
deleted invoice (orphan). Causes: (1) Data imports without validation, (2) Delete operations bypassing constraints, (3) Data 
corruption, (4) Disabled constraints. Problems: Query results incorrect, joins fail, reports incomplete. This report finds all 
violations so they can be fixed. Essential for maintaining data integrity and quality.

When to Use: After data imports or migrations, troubleshoot data integrity issues, verify database integrity, identify orphaned 
records for cleanup, and support data quality initiatives. Fix violations by either deleting orphans or creating missing 
parents.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Columns
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows database column definitions and metadata. Document database structure including data types, sizes, and constraints.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display database column definitions showing complete database structure. Document table columns, data 
types, and properties. Essential for database documentation and development.

What You'll See: Database columns showing: (1) Table and column names, (2) Data types and sizes, (3) Null/not null 
constraints, (4) Default values, (5) Identity columns, (6) Column descriptions/comments. Complete database structure 
documentation. Organized by table or column name.

When to Use: Document database structure, support database development, understand table definitions, plan schema changes, 
create data dictionaries, and analyze database design. Essential database documentation tool.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Index Columns
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows database indexes and their columns. Document index structure for performance tuning and query optimization.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display database indexes showing which columns are indexed. Document index structure for performance 
optimization. Essential for database performance tuning and query optimization.

What You'll See: Database indexes showing: (1) Index names and types (clustered, non-clustered, unique), (2) Tables indexed, 
(3) Columns in indexes, (4) Index column order, (5) Include columns, (6) Index properties (unique, primary key). Shows 
complete index structure. Organized by table or index.

Key Information: Indexes speed up queries by providing fast lookup paths. This shows which columns are indexed - critical for 
query optimization. Use to: Understand existing indexes, identify missing indexes (why query slow?), find redundant indexes, 
plan index strategy. Essential for database performance analysis.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Weekly Usage By Hour
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows database usage patterns by hour over a week. Analyze database usage trends for capacity planning and maintenance scheduling.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display database usage patterns by hour across the week. Analyze usage trends and peaks. Essential for 
capacity planning and maintenance window scheduling. Shows activity patterns: busy times (avoid maintenance), quiet times 
(schedule maintenance), peak loads (capacity planning), usage trends over time. Use for: Schedule maintenance during quiet 
periods, plan capacity for peak times, understand user patterns, and optimize database resources based on usage.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Scheduled Jobs
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows SQL Server scheduled jobs and their status. Monitor automated database maintenance jobs and task execution.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display SQL Server Agent scheduled jobs showing automated tasks and their execution status. Monitor 
database automation. Essential for ensuring maintenance jobs run successfully.

What You'll See: Scheduled jobs showing: (1) Job names and descriptions, (2) Schedules (when they run), (3) Last run status 
(success, failure), (4) Last run time, (5) Next run time, (6) Job owners, (7) Failure notifications. Shows automated task 
health. Organized by schedule or status.

Key Information: SQL Server Agent runs automated jobs - backups, statistics updates, index maintenance, cleanups. This shows 
whether they are running successfully. Failed jobs mean missed maintenance. Use to: Monitor job execution, identify failed 
jobs, verify backup success, ensure maintenance runs, troubleshoot automation issues. Essential for database maintenance 
oversight.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Monthly Usage by Hour
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows database usage patterns by hour over a month. Analyze longer-term database usage trends for capacity planning and optimization.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display database usage patterns by hour across a month showing longer-term trends. Analyze usage 
patterns over time. Similar to Weekly Usage but monthly view for trend analysis. Use for: Identify long-term usage trends, 
plan capacity based on growth patterns, schedule maintenance during consistent quiet periods, and support database capacity 
planning and optimization.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Error Log Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows system error log entries. Monitor application errors, warnings, and system events for troubleshooting and quality.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display system error log showing application errors, warnings, and events. Monitor system health and 
troubleshoot problems. Essential for application monitoring and error management.

What You'll See: Error log entries showing: (1) Error/event date and time, (2) Severity levels (error, warning, info), (3) 
Error messages and descriptions, (4) Users affected, (5) Application modules/functions involved, (6) Error context and stack 
traces, (7) Frequency counts for recurring errors. Shows complete error history for troubleshooting. Can filter by severity, 
date range, user, or module. Organized by date or severity.

Criteria: Select date ranges, filter by severity levels (critical, error, warning, info), choose specific users or modules, 
show only unresolved errors, and set detail level.

Key Information: The error log captures application problems: (1) Critical Errors - system failures requiring immediate 
attention, (2) Errors - problems causing feature failures, (3) Warnings - potential issues or unusual conditions, (4) Info - 
informational events for auditing. Use the log to: Troubleshoot user-reported problems (what error did they get?), Identify 
recurring issues needing fixes, Monitor system health and stability, Track error trends over time, Support quality improvement 
efforts. Recurring errors indicate bugs needing attention. Essential for proactive system monitoring and quality management.

When to Use This Report:
• Troubleshoot user-reported problems
• Monitor system health and error rates
• Identify recurring errors needing fixes
• Track error trends and patterns
• Support quality improvement initiatives
• Prepare error reports for development team
• Verify fixes resolved recurring errors

Good to Know: Review the error log regularly (weekly) to catch problems early. High error rates indicate quality issues. Focus 
on recurring errors - one-time errors may be user mistakes. Critical errors always require investigation. Error logs grow 
over time - archive or clean up old entries periodically using the Error Log Clean Up function. Essential tool for maintaining 
application quality and user satisfaction.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Report Usage Statistics
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows report usage statistics and metrics. Analyze which reports are used most frequently for system optimization and training.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display report usage statistics showing which reports are used and how often. Analyze report usage 
patterns for system optimization and training needs. Essential for understanding user behavior and system usage.

What You'll See: Reports with usage statistics showing: (1) Report names and descriptions, (2) Usage counts (how many times 
run), (3) Last run dates, (4) Most frequent users, (5) Usage trends over time (increasing, decreasing), (6) Average run times, 
(7) Comparison between reports (which are most popular). Shows complete picture of report usage patterns. Can rank by usage 
frequency, last use, or module. Organized by usage frequency or report category.

Criteria: Select date ranges for analysis, choose specific report categories or modules, set minimum usage thresholds (e.g., 
used over 100 times), filter by users or companies, and set detail level.

Key Information: Report usage statistics reveal: (1) Most valuable reports - heavily used, clearly meeting needs, (2) Rarely 
used reports - may indicate poor design, lack of awareness, or outdated functionality, (3) Usage trends - are reports being 
adopted or abandoned over time?, (4) User preferences - which reports do specific user groups prefer?, (5) Training needs - 
unused reports may need more training/documentation. Use statistics to: Prioritize report improvements (focus on heavily used), 
Identify candidates for retirement (never used), Plan training (educate about underutilized reports), Optimize system 
resources (cache frequently used reports), Understand user workflows and needs. Essential for data-driven system management 
and optimization.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze report usage patterns and trends
• Prioritize report development and improvements
• Identify underutilized reports needing promotion
• Plan user training and documentation
• Support system optimization decisions
• Understand user behavior and preferences
• Measure report adoption after new releases

Good to Know: The 80/20 rule often applies - 20% of reports get 80% of usage. Focus improvement efforts on the heavily used 
20%. Compare usage across companies to identify best practices. Sudden usage drops may indicate problems. New reports need time 
to gain adoption - track trends. Use with "Reports Never Used" report to identify retirement candidates. Essential for 
evidence-based system management and continuous improvement.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Reports Never Used
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows reports that have never been used. Identify unused functionality for system cleanup and retirement decisions.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display reports that have never been run. Identify unused functionality for system cleanup or 
retirement. Essential for system maintenance and understanding user needs.

What You'll See: Reports with zero usage showing: (1) Report names and descriptions, (2) Report categories/modules, (3) When 
reports were added to system, (4) Age (how long available but never used), (5) Similar reports that ARE used (alternatives?), 
(6) Report complexity or requirements. Shows complete list of unused reports for evaluation. Can be filtered by age (e.g., 
available over 1 year), module, or company. Organized by module or age.

Criteria: Set minimum age thresholds (e.g., available over 6 months with no use), choose report categories or modules, filter 
by companies (not used by any? not used by specific company?), and set detail level.

Key Information: Reports never used indicate: (1) Poor fit with user needs - report doesn't solve real problems, (2) Lack of 
awareness - users don't know report exists, (3) Better alternatives available - other reports meet the need, (4) Outdated 
functionality - business processes changed, (5) Complex requirements - too hard to understand or use. Consider: Retire unused 
reports to reduce clutter and maintenance, Promote potentially useful reports through training, Investigate why similar reports 
were never adopted, Repurpose or redesign to meet actual needs. Be cautious - some specialized reports may be rarely needed 
but critical when used. Essential for system cleanup and focusing development on what users actually need.

When to Use This Report:
• Identify unused reports for retirement
• Clean up cluttered report menus
• Understand why reports aren't adopted
• Decide which reports to promote through training
• Focus development on needed functionality
• Reduce maintenance burden by retiring unused features
• Support system simplification initiatives

Good to Know: Don't rush to retire unused reports - verify they aren't meeting specialized needs. Some reports are used rarely 
but are critical (e.g., year-end reports). Check with power users before retiring. Age matters - reports unused after 1+ years 
are good retirement candidates. Compare across companies - unused everywhere vs. unused by one company. Use with Report Usage 
Statistics for complete picture. Essential for keeping the system lean, focused, and maintainable.

reportTrainingRecords.name: File Type Counts
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows database table row counts by file type. Monitor database size and growth for capacity planning and maintenance.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display database table row counts organized by file/table type. Monitor database size, growth trends, 
and capacity. Essential for database capacity planning and maintenance.

What You'll See: Database tables with row counts showing: (1) Table names and types (master files, transaction files, etc.), 
(2) Current row counts, (3) Growth trends (rows added over time), (4) Space consumption estimates, (5) Largest tables, (6) 
Table categories (job costing, payroll, A/P, A/R, etc.). Shows database size profile and growth patterns. Can compare across 
time periods to see growth rates. Organized by table size or category.

Criteria: Select as-of date for counts, choose table categories, set minimum row thresholds (e.g., over 100,000 rows), compare 
periods for growth analysis, and set detail level.

Key Information: Table row counts reveal database usage and growth: (1) Transaction Volume - invoice, timesheet, cheque tables 
show business activity, (2) Growth Rates - how fast is database growing?, (3) Capacity Planning - when will storage limits be 
reached?, (4) Data Retention - do old tables need archiving/purging?, (5) Performance Impact - huge tables may need 
partitioning or indexing. Use to: Plan storage capacity and upgrades, Identify tables needing archival (millions of rows), 
Support database maintenance (large table statistics, backups), Understand business growth (transaction volumes), Monitor 
database health and balance. Essential for proactive database capacity management and maintenance planning.

When to Use This Report:
• Monitor database size and growth trends
• Plan storage capacity and database expansions
• Identify tables needing archival or purging
• Support database performance optimization
• Track business activity through transaction volumes
• Prepare for database maintenance (backups, statistics)
• Understand data retention and lifecycle needs

Good to Know: Transaction tables (invoices, timesheets, cheques) grow continuously - plan for growth. Master tables (vendors, 
clients, employees) grow slowly. Tables with millions of rows need special attention - performance, backups, statistics. Growth 
rates predict future capacity needs. Review quarterly to track trends. Consider archiving historical data after 3-5 years. 
Essential for long-term database health and capacity management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cheques by Vendor
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Lists all cheques issued to vendors sorted by vendor code. Shows issue dates, cheque numbers,
amounts, and reconciliation status. Use for vendor payment history and cheque tracking.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows all payment cheques organized by vendor. Your primary report for tracking what
you've paid to each supplier and when.

What You'll See: For each vendor, you'll see every cheque issued including the issue date, cheque
number, form number (physical cheque number), cheque status (void, cleared, etc.), net payment amount,
holdback amount, reconciliation date (when it cleared the bank), and the G/L period.

Criteria: Select your company, vendor range, G/L period range, and date range. You can choose the date
type (issue date, reconcile date, or created date) and filter by cheque status (all, cleared, void,
etc.). Can also filter to show only credit card payments.

Key Information: Net payment is the amount actually paid to the vendor. Holdback payment is any
retainage being held. The reconcile date shows when the cheque cleared your bank account. Groups by
vendor with subtotals showing total paid to each supplier.

When to Use This Report: When you need to see payment history with a specific vendor. When reconciling
your bank statement and matching cleared cheques. When a vendor asks about payment status. When
preparing for year-end (seeing all payments to a vendor for 1099 purposes). When investigating voided
or missing cheques.

Good to Know: The report groups all cheques by vendor, making it easy to see your payment relationship
with each supplier. You can filter by file type to separate regular checks from credit card payments or
EFT transfers.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cheques by G/L Period
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Displays cheques organized by accounting period. Shows all payments made within selected G/L
periods with vendor, amount, and date details. Use for period-end reporting and cash flow analysis.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Organizes your payment cheques by accounting period (month/year). Essential for
understanding cash flow and preparing period-end reports.

What You'll See: Cheques grouped by G/L period showing vendor name, issue date, cheque number, form
number, payment amounts (net and holdback), reconciliation status, and when the cheque cleared the bank.
Each period shows subtotals.

Criteria: Select your company, G/L period range, vendor range, and optional date filters. Can choose
which date to use (issue, reconcile, or created) and filter by cheque status.

Key Information: Subtotals for each G/L period show exactly how much cash went out that month. This is
critical for cash flow reporting. The reconciliation dates help you understand timing differences between
when you issued cheques versus when they cleared your bank.

When to Use This Report: When closing a month and need to see all payments made that period. When
analyzing cash flow trends month-to-month. When reconciling your G/L to your bank statements. When your
accountant needs payment details for a specific period. When preparing budget vs actual reports.

Good to Know: The G/L period grouping helps you see spending patterns over time. Useful for spotting
unusual payment activity or verifying your month-end cash position.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Subcontractor Payments
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Summarizes payments to subcontractors for tax reporting purposes. Shows total amounts paid to
vendors flagged as subcontractors. Required for Canada Revenue Agency compliance.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Provides the summary of payments made to subcontractors that you need for government tax
reporting. Required by Canada Revenue Agency for construction businesses.

What You'll See: A list of vendors flagged as subcontractors showing the total sum of all payments made
to each one during the selected time period. Includes vendor code, name, and total payment amount.

Criteria: Select your company, date range (typically a full calendar year), and optionally a specific
vendor range. The report automatically includes only vendors marked as subcontractors in your vendor
file.

Key Information: This is a summary report - it shows totals only, not individual cheques. The amounts
shown are what you'll report to CRA. Make sure your vendors are properly flagged as subcontractors in
the vendor maintenance.

When to Use This Report: At year-end when preparing your subcontractor payment reports for Canada
Revenue. When you need to verify total payments to subcontractors for a specific time period. When your
accountant or auditor requests subcontractor payment totals.

Good to Know: This report is specifically designed for Canadian tax compliance. Make sure vendors are
properly classified in your system. Only vendors with the subcontractor flag will appear on this report.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cheques by Form Number
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Lists cheques sorted by physical cheque number (form number). Useful for finding specific
cheques, identifying gaps in cheque sequences, and reconciling physical cheque stock.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Organizes cheques by their physical cheque number (form number). Essential when you
need to locate a specific cheque or verify your cheque stock.

What You'll See: Cheques listed in form number order showing vendor name, issue date, cheque status,
payment amounts, and reconciliation dates. Makes it easy to scan through sequential cheque numbers.

Criteria: Select your company, form number range (or leave blank for all), G/L period range, vendor
range, and date filters. Can filter by status to find only cleared, voided, or outstanding cheques.

Key Information: The form number is the actual number printed on your physical cheque stock. This report
helps you track what happened to each numbered cheque. Gaps in the sequence might indicate missing or
stolen cheques.

When to Use This Report: When your bank asks about a specific cheque number. When reconciling and you
need to find gaps in your cheque sequence. When accounting for pre-numbered cheque stock. When
investigating possible fraud or missing cheques. When you need to void a specific form number.

Good to Know: The sequential order makes it easy to spot missing or duplicate cheque numbers. If you see
unexpected gaps, investigate immediately as this could indicate control issues.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cheque Invoice Payments
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows which invoices were paid by each cheque. Details each cheque with the specific invoice
items it paid. Use to trace payments back to original invoices.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows the detail of what each cheque paid for - breaking down each cheque to show
exactly which invoice items were covered by that payment.

What You'll See: Each cheque listed with complete details of the invoice items it paid. For each cheque
you'll see the vendor, cheque date, cheque number, and then a line-by-line breakdown of every invoice
item that cheque paid including invoice numbers, descriptions, and amounts.

Criteria: Select company, cheque number range (or specific cheques), vendor range, G/L period, and date
range. Can filter by cheque status.

Key Information: This report connects your payments back to the original invoices. If a cheque paid
multiple invoices or partial amounts, you'll see exactly how the payment was applied. Essential for
answering vendor questions about what a specific payment covered.

When to Use This Report: When a vendor calls asking what a specific cheque was for. When you need to
verify that invoices were paid correctly. When investigating payment discrepancies. When your accountant
needs to trace a payment back to source documents. When auditing payment application accuracy.

Good to Know: One cheque can pay multiple invoices, and one invoice can be paid by multiple cheques.
This report shows the complete relationship between your cheques and your invoices.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cheques by EFT Batch
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Lists electronic fund transfer (EFT) payments grouped by batch number. Shows vendors paid via
direct deposit or wire transfer. Use for tracking electronic payment batches.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows electronic payments (direct deposits, wire transfers) organized by the batch they
were sent to the bank in. Essential for tracking and reconciling electronic payments.

What You'll See: EFT payment batches with all the vendors paid in each batch. For each payment you'll
see vendor name, payment date, payment amount, and batch number. Grouped by EFT batch for easy
verification against your bank records.

Criteria: Select company, EFT batch number range, vendor range, G/L period, and date filters. Can choose
date type (issue, reconcile, or created).

Key Information: Each EFT batch represents a file sent to your bank for processing. The batch number
helps you match the payments in your system with what your bank processed. Subtotals for each batch show
the total amount sent to the bank.

When to Use This Report: When reconciling EFT payments with your bank statement. When the bank reports a
problem with an EFT batch and you need to identify which payments were in it. When verifying that all
payments in a batch were processed correctly. When vendors ask about direct deposit payments.

Good to Know: EFT batches are numbered sequentially when you create and send them to your bank. If a
batch fails at the bank, this report helps you identify which payments need to be reprocessed.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Payments by Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows payments organized by job number. Displays what was paid for each project including
vendor, invoice, and cost details. Use for job cost analysis and project payment tracking.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows all your vendor payments organized by which job they were for. Essential for
understanding job costs and tracking project spending.

What You'll See: Payments grouped by job showing vendor name, invoice details, payment date, cheque
number, payment amounts, and what the payment was for. Each job shows subtotals of all payments made for
that project.

Criteria: Select company, job range, vendor range, G/L period, and date range. Can filter by cheque
status and payment type.

Key Information: Shows the cash actually paid out for each job (as opposed to costs incurred). The job
totals help you track cash requirements for projects and compare actual payments to your job budgets.

When to Use This Report: When you need to know how much you've paid out for a specific job. When
analyzing job profitability and cash flow. When the client asks for backup documentation of job costs.
When comparing job payments to your budget. When preparing job cost reports for management.

Good to Know: This shows cash out for jobs, which is different from costs posted to jobs. A cost might
be posted in one period but paid in another. This report focuses on when cash actually left your bank
account.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Payments by G/L Account
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Displays payments grouped by general ledger account code. Shows spending by expense category.
Use for expense analysis and G/L account verification.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Organizes your payments by G/L account code (expense category). Shows where your money
went by accounting classification.

What You'll See: Payments grouped by G/L account showing vendor name, invoice details, cheque number,
date, and amount. Each G/L account shows subtotals so you can see total spending in each expense
category.

Criteria: Select company, G/L account range, vendor range, G/L period, and date filters. Can filter by
cheque status and payment type.

Key Information: The G/L account grouping helps you understand spending patterns. For example, you can
see all your office supply expenses, or all your equipment rental costs. The subtotals make it easy to
compare actual spending to budgets.

When to Use This Report: When analyzing spending by expense category. When your accountant needs to
verify G/L account postings. When preparing budget vs actual reports. When management wants to see
spending trends by account type. When investigating unusual expenses in a specific category.

Good to Know: This report helps you understand not just how much you spent, but what you spent it on.
Very useful for identifying areas where you might be overspending or for finding cost-cutting
opportunities.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cheques by Paid Amount
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Lists cheques sorted by payment amount from highest to lowest. Useful for finding large
payments, reconciliation issues, or when you know an amount but not the cheque number.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Sorts your cheques by dollar amount (largest to smallest). Helpful when you're looking
for a payment and you know the amount but not the cheque number.

What You'll See: All cheques listed in order by payment amount showing vendor name, cheque number, issue
date, form number, net payment, and holdback amounts. Makes it easy to scan for a specific dollar amount.

Criteria: Select company, vendor range, G/L period, and date filters. Can filter by cheque status and
payment type.

Key Information: The report is specifically designed to help with reconciliation problems. When your bank
statement shows a specific amount cleared but you're not sure which cheque it was, scan this report for
that dollar amount.

When to Use This Report: When reconciling your bank and you see a cleared amount but can't find the
matching cheque. When looking for large payments that might need special attention. When you remember the
amount of a payment but not who it was to. When identifying your biggest expenses. When investigating
duplicate payments (same amount appearing twice).

Good to Know: This is particularly useful during bank reconciliation. The amount-based sort makes it much
faster to match cleared items to your cheque records when you're working from a bank statement.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Uncashed Cheques
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows cheques that have been issued but haven't cleared the bank yet. Identifies stale-dated
cheques and outstanding payments. Use for bank reconciliation and identifying old uncashed items.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Identifies cheques you've written but that haven't cleared your bank yet. Essential for
bank reconciliation and finding stale-dated cheques.

What You'll See: All cheques issued on or before your selected date that don't have a reconciliation date
(meaning they haven't cleared the bank). Shows vendor, issue date, cheque number, and amount. Helps you
identify old cheques that vendors might have lost or forgotten.

Criteria: Select company and specify a cut-off date. The report shows all cheques issued on or before
that date that are still outstanding. Can filter by vendor range and cheque status.

Key Information: A cheque is considered uncashed if it doesn't have a reconciliation date. If a cheque
has been outstanding for a long time (say, more than 90 days), you should contact the vendor. They might
have lost it and need a replacement.

When to Use This Report: When doing bank reconciliation to identify outstanding cheques. When looking for
stale-dated cheques that should be voided and reissued. When a vendor claims they never received payment.
When preparing year-end financials and need to account for outstanding items. When cleaning up old
outstanding cheques.

Good to Know: Cheques that have been outstanding for more than 6 months are often stale-dated and can't
be cashed. You may need to void these and issue new payments. The total of uncashed cheques represents
money that has left your books but not yet left your bank account.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Payments by Client P/O
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Displays payments organized by client purchase order number. Shows costs paid against each
client P/O. Use for tracking billable costs and preparing client billing backup.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows payments organized by your client's purchase order numbers. Essential for tracking
costs against client authorizations and preparing billing documentation.

What You'll See: Payments grouped by client P/O showing vendor name, invoice details, payment date,
cheque number, and amounts. Each client P/O shows subtotals of all costs paid against that authorization.

Criteria: Select company, client P/O range, job range, vendor range, G/L period, and date filters. Can
filter by cheque status.

Key Information: When you bill clients, they often want to see exactly what you paid for their P/O. This
report gives you that breakdown. The subtotals help you track spending against client authorizations and
make sure you don't exceed approved amounts.

When to Use This Report: When preparing billing to clients and they want backup documentation. When a
client asks how much you've spent against their P/O. When verifying you haven't exceeded client
authorization amounts. When preparing change orders (showing costs already incurred). When auditing
reimbursable costs.

Good to Know: This is especially important for cost-plus or reimbursable contracts where clients need to
see actual costs you've paid. The client P/O grouping makes it easy to provide the backup they need for
their records.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Reprint Vendor Cheque Advice
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Reprints the cheque remittance advice (payment stub) for vendors. Shows what invoices were paid
by each cheque. Use when vendors lose their payment stub and need a replacement.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Reprints the payment stub (remittance advice) that shows vendors what their cheque paid
for. Use when vendors lose the original or need a copy for their records.

What You'll See: A formatted remittance advice showing the cheque number, payment amount, issue date, and
a detailed list of all invoice items that payment covered. Includes invoice numbers, descriptions,
original amounts, and payment amounts.

Criteria: Select company, specific cheque numbers, vendor range, G/L period, and date range. Usually
you'll select one or a few specific cheques to reprint.

Key Information: This produces the same stub that would have been attached to the original cheque. It
shows vendors exactly what invoices were paid and any partial payments or adjustments. Vendors need this
to apply payments correctly in their systems.

When to Use This Report: When a vendor calls saying they lost their payment stub and need to know what
the cheque paid for. When a vendor's accounting department is having trouble applying a payment. When
you need to mail proof of payment to a vendor. When resolving payment disputes (showing exactly what was
paid).

Good to Know: This doesn't reprint the actual cheque (you can't reissue the payment), only the stub that
explains what the payment covered. It's your backup documentation for payment details.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by Vendor
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Lists all vendor invoices organized by vendor. Shows invoice details, amounts, payment status,
and job information. Use for reviewing vendor activity and outstanding balances.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows all your vendor invoices grouped by supplier. Your main report for seeing what
you owe each vendor and reviewing vendor billing history.

What You'll See: For each vendor, all their invoices showing invoice number, date, description, amounts
(gross, tax, net), payment status (paid, partially paid, unpaid), job numbers, and any hold reasons. Each
vendor grouping shows subtotals.

Criteria: Select company, vendor range, job range, G/L period, and date filters. Can filter by payment
status (paid, unpaid, on hold, or all).

Key Information: The vendor grouping makes it easy to see all activity with each supplier. Subtotals show
what you owe each vendor. Payment status helps you identify which invoices need attention. Hold flags
explain why invoices aren't being paid.

When to Use This Report: When a vendor calls asking about their invoices. When you need to see all
activity with a specific supplier. When preparing to pay vendors and want to see what's outstanding.
When investigating vendor billing issues. When reconciling vendor statements to your records.

Good to Know: This is probably your most-used A/P report. It gives you a complete picture of your
relationship with each vendor. The subtotals show your total liability to each supplier.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Payment Approvals
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows invoices that have been approved for payment. Lists items ready to be included in the
next cheque run. Use to review and verify approved payments before processing.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows invoices that have been flagged as approved for payment. Your review list before
you run cheques to make sure everything is ready to pay.

What You'll See: All invoices marked for payment showing vendor name, invoice number, date, description,
amounts, approval information (who approved it and when), and job details. Shows exactly what will be
included in your next payment run.

Criteria: Select company, vendor range, job range, and approval date range. Usually you'll run this for
all currently approved items.

Key Information: The approval flag means someone has reviewed and authorized this invoice for payment.
This report helps you do a final review before actually cutting cheques. The total shows how much cash
will go out in the next payment run.

When to Use This Report: Right before running your cheque process to review what's being paid. When
verifying that invoices have been properly approved. When management wants to see what's about to be
paid. When you need to remove items from the payment run (you can see what's approved and unapprove if
needed).

Good to Know: The payment approval process adds a control step - invoices can't be paid until someone
approves them. This report is your final checkpoint before money goes out the door.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by G/L Account
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Displays invoices grouped by general ledger account. Shows spending by expense category. Use
for expense analysis and G/L account verification.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Organizes vendor invoices by G/L account (expense type). Shows what you're spending in
each expense category.

What You'll See: Invoices grouped by G/L account showing vendor name, invoice details, dates, amounts,
payment status, and job information. Each G/L account shows subtotals of all invoices charged to that
account.

Criteria: Select company, G/L account range, vendor range, job range, G/L period, and date filters. Can
filter by payment status.

Key Information: The G/L account grouping helps you understand spending patterns by expense type. For
example, you can see all your utilities, all your office supplies, or all your equipment rental costs.
Subtotals make it easy to compare to budgets.

When to Use This Report: When analyzing spending trends in specific expense categories. When your
accountant needs to verify G/L postings. When preparing budget vs actual reports. When investigating
unusual expenses in a specific account. When management asks about spending in a particular category.

Good to Know: This shows invoices, not payments. So you're seeing what was billed (costs incurred)
rather than when cash went out. Useful for accrual-basis accounting and understanding true expenses.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by Centre in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows invoices organized by job and cost center (area/centre). Displays costs within each phase
or section of work. Use for detailed job cost tracking and cost center analysis.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows vendor invoices broken down by job and then by cost center (area/centre) within
each job. Essential for detailed job cost tracking and phase-level analysis.

What You'll See: Invoices grouped first by job, then by cost center within that job, showing vendor name,
invoice details, amounts, and payment status. Each cost center shows subtotals. You can see exactly what
was spent in each phase or area of work.

Criteria: Select company, job range, area/centre range, vendor range, G/L period, and date filters. Can
filter by payment status. May have extraction options for further processing.

Key Information: Cost centers (areas and centres) break your job into smaller pieces like 'site prep,'
'foundation,' 'framing,' etc. This report shows actual vendor costs in each piece. Subtotals help you
compare costs to your cost center budgets.

When to Use This Report: When you need detailed job cost analysis by phase or section. When comparing
actual costs to cost center budgets. When identifying which parts of a job are over budget. When
preparing change orders (showing costs by work area). When the client wants to see detailed cost
breakdowns.

Good to Know: This is more detailed than just looking at job totals - it shows where within the job the
money went. Very useful for project managers tracking work phases.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by Vendor in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Displays invoices grouped by vendor within each job. Shows what each supplier billed on each
project. Use for job cost analysis and tracking vendor activity by project.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows invoices organized by job and then by vendor within that job. Helps you see what
each supplier charged on each project.

What You'll See: Invoices grouped first by job, then by vendor within that job, showing invoice numbers,
dates, descriptions, amounts, and payment status. Each vendor/job combination shows subtotals so you can
see total costs from each supplier on each project.

Criteria: Select company, job range, vendor range, G/L period, and date filters. Can filter by payment
status. May have extraction options for further processing.

Key Information: This helps you understand vendor spending patterns by project. You can see which
suppliers worked on which jobs and how much they charged. Useful for comparing vendor costs across
projects and identifying your major suppliers per job.

When to Use This Report: When analyzing job costs by supplier. When you need to see all invoices from a
specific vendor on a specific job. When comparing supplier costs across multiple projects. When preparing
job cost reports for clients. When investigating vendor billing issues on particular jobs.

Good to Know: The double grouping (job then vendor) gives you two perspectives - you can see all costs on
a job, and within that see which vendors contributed what amounts.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by Vendor P/O
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows invoices organized by your purchase orders to vendors. Displays what has been billed
against each P/O. Use for tracking P/O commitments and comparing invoices to orders.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows vendor invoices grouped by your purchase order numbers. Essential for tracking
what's been billed against each P/O and comparing invoices to your original orders.

What You'll See: Invoices grouped by P/O number showing vendor name, invoice details, dates, what was
billed, amounts, and payment status. Each P/O grouping shows subtotals so you can see total invoiced
against that order.

Criteria: Select company, P/O number range, vendor range, job range, G/L period, and date filters. Can
filter by payment status. May have extraction options for further processing.

Key Information: This helps you track P/O spending. You can see if vendors are billing more than you
ordered, if P/Os are fully invoiced, or if there are still outstanding deliveries. Subtotals show total
billed vs what you authorized.

When to Use This Report: When verifying that invoices match your P/Os. When a vendor bills more than you
authorized and you need to investigate. When tracking P/O completion (seeing what's been invoiced vs
ordered). When preparing accruals (identifying P/Os with goods received but not yet invoiced). When
closing out completed P/Os.

Good to Know: The P/O grouping helps you maintain purchase order control. You can quickly spot if
vendors are overbilling or if invoices don't match your authorizations.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by Client P/O
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Displays invoices grouped by client purchase order number. Shows costs incurred against client
authorizations. Use for tracking billable costs and client P/O analysis.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows vendor invoices organized by your client's purchase order numbers. Essential for
tracking costs against client authorizations and preparing billing.

What You'll See: Invoices grouped by client P/O showing vendor name, invoice details, dates, descriptions,
amounts, job information, and payment status. Each client P/O shows subtotals of all costs incurred
against that authorization.

Criteria: Select company, client P/O range, vendor range, job range, G/L period, and date filters. Can
filter by payment status.

Key Information: This helps you track spending against client authorizations. You can see if you're
approaching the client's authorized amount, or if you need to request additional authorization. Subtotals
show total costs against each client P/O.

When to Use This Report: When preparing to bill clients and need to show costs by their P/O. When clients
ask how much you've spent against their authorization. When you need to request a change order (showing
costs already incurred). When tracking reimbursable expenses. When verifying you haven't exceeded client
authorization limits.

Good to Know: Particularly important for cost-plus or reimbursable contracts. Clients often want to see
costs organized by their P/O numbers when you bill them.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices O/S at Month End
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows unpaid invoices that were outstanding at the end of a specific accounting period. Used
for month-end accruals and accounts payable aging analysis.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows which invoices were unpaid (outstanding) at the end of a specific accounting
period. Essential for month-end close and understanding your payables position at period end.

What You'll See: All invoices that had unpaid balances at the end of your selected G/L period, showing
vendor name, invoice details, original amounts, amount still owing at period end, aging information, and
job details.

Criteria: Select company, vendor range, and specify the G/L period (month/year). The report looks back and
shows what was outstanding at that period end.

Key Information: This is a point-in-time report - it shows your payables position at a specific date. The
aging shows how old each invoice was at that period end. Total outstanding represents your accounts
payable balance for that period.

When to Use This Report: When closing month-end and need to report accounts payable balance. When your
accountant needs to verify period-end payables. When preparing financial statements (need to show
liabilities at period end). When analyzing aging trends over time (compare month to month). When auditors
need historical payables information.

Good to Know: Even though some of these invoices may be paid now, this report shows what was owing at that
specific period end. Essential for accurate historical financial reporting.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by Invoice Number
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Lists invoices sorted by vendor invoice number. Useful for finding specific invoices quickly or
verifying invoice sequences. Use when you know the invoice number but need details.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows invoices sorted by their invoice number. Helpful when you know an invoice number
and need to quickly find it or get details.

What You'll See: Invoices listed in invoice number order showing vendor name, invoice date, description,
amounts, payment status, job information, and payment details if paid.

Criteria: Select company, invoice number range (or specific numbers), vendor range, job range, G/L period,
and date filters. Can filter by payment status.

Key Information: The invoice number sort makes it easy to scan through and locate specific invoices. If
you know the invoice number from a vendor call or a document, you can quickly find all the details in your
system.

When to Use This Report: When a vendor calls about a specific invoice number and you need to look it up.
When you have an invoice in hand and want to verify it's in the system. When checking for duplicate
invoice numbers (seeing if same number appears twice). When you need invoice details and only know the
invoice number.

Good to Know: This is a lookup tool - when you have an invoice number, this gets you to the details fast.
Much quicker than searching through vendor-based reports.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by Vendor in Job Province
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Displays invoices grouped by vendor within job within province. Shows spending by location for
provincial sales tax reporting. Use for PST/HST reporting and provincial cost analysis.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows invoices organized by province, then by job, then by vendor. Specifically designed
to help with provincial sales tax reporting and analyzing costs by location.

What You'll See: Invoices grouped first by province, then by job within that province, then by vendor
within that job. Shows invoice details, amounts including tax breakdowns, and payment status. Each level
shows subtotals.

Criteria: Select company, province, job range, vendor range, G/L period, and date filters. Can filter by
payment status.

Key Information: The provincial grouping is essential for PST/HST reporting. Different provinces have
different tax rates and rules. This report helps you see costs and taxes by location. Subtotals by
province show your total spending (and taxable amounts) in each location.

When to Use This Report: When preparing provincial sales tax returns (PST, HST, QST, etc.). When analyzing
costs by geographic location. When you need to show spending broken down by province for management
reporting. When auditors need to see provincial tax calculations. When comparing costs across different
provinces.

Good to Know: This three-level grouping (province/job/vendor) gives you the detail you need for tax
reporting while still being manageable. Essential for multi-province operations.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by Employee
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows invoices associated with specific employees. Displays vendor invoices that reference
employee numbers. Use for tracking employee-related costs and reimbursements.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows vendor invoices that are associated with specific employees. Useful for tracking
employee-related costs, reimbursements, or allocated expenses.

What You'll See: Invoices grouped by employee showing vendor name, invoice number, date, description,
amounts, and payment status. Each employee grouping shows subtotals of all invoices related to them.

Criteria: Select company, employee range, vendor range, job range, G/L period, and date filters. Can
filter by payment status (paid, unpaid, or both).

Key Information: Only shows invoices where an employee number has been entered. This might include things
like tools purchased for an employee, truck expenses assigned to a specific driver, or costs that will be
charged back to employees.

When to Use This Report: When tracking costs related to specific employees. When you need to show an
employee what expenses have been charged to them. When calculating employee tool allowances or
reimbursements. When analyzing per-employee cost patterns. When preparing to charge back costs to
employees.

Good to Know: The employee association on invoices is optional, so not all invoices will appear on this
report - only those where someone entered an employee number when processing the invoice.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by Equipment
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Displays invoices associated with specific equipment. Shows vendor costs related to each piece
of equipment. Use for tracking equipment operating costs and maintenance expenses.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows vendor invoices that are associated with specific pieces of equipment. Essential
for tracking equipment operating costs and maintenance history.

What You'll See: Invoices grouped by equipment number showing vendor name, invoice number, date,
description of work or parts, amounts, and payment status. Each equipment grouping shows total costs for
that piece of equipment.

Criteria: Select company, equipment range, vendor range, job range, G/L period, and date filters. Can
filter by payment status.

Key Information: Shows actual dollars spent on each piece of equipment including repairs, parts,
maintenance, fuel, and other operating costs. Helps you understand the true cost of owning and operating
each machine.

When to Use This Report: When analyzing equipment operating costs and deciding whether to keep or replace
a machine. When a piece of equipment breaks down and you need its maintenance history. When calculating
equipment rental rates (need to know actual costs). When budgeting equipment expenses. When preparing
equipment for sale (showing maintenance records).

Good to Know: Only shows invoices where equipment was specified. Not all costs get allocated to specific
equipment. This is particularly useful for tracking high-maintenance machines.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by Extract Date
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Lists invoices by the date they were extracted (posted) to the general ledger. Shows which
invoices were included in each G/L extract batch. Use for G/L reconciliation and audit trails.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows invoices organized by when they were extracted (posted) to the general ledger.
Essential for G/L reconciliation and understanding your month-end postings.

What You'll See: Invoices grouped by extract date showing vendor name, invoice number, invoice date,
amounts, G/L accounts, and job/cost center details. Each extract date shows totals of all invoices posted
that day.

Criteria: Select company, extract date range, vendor range, job range, and G/L period. Can filter by
payment status.

Key Information: The extract date is when the invoice hit your general ledger, which might be different
from the invoice date. Grouping by extract date shows exactly what went into your G/L on specific days.
Essential for reconciling A/P to G/L.

When to Use This Report: When closing your books and need to verify what was posted to the G/L. When your
accountant questions a G/L posting and needs to see the source invoices. When reconciling A/P subledger
to G/L control accounts. When you need to reverse a batch of extracts. When preparing for an audit and
need to show what was posted when.

Good to Know: Invoices typically get extracted in batches. This report helps you see those batches and
verify the timing of G/L postings. If an extract went into the wrong period, this helps identify which
invoices need adjustment.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by Extract Reference
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows invoices grouped by extract reference number. Displays which invoices were included in
specific G/L extract batches. Use for tracking and verifying G/L postings.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows invoices organized by their extract reference (batch number). Helps you track
exactly which invoices were posted to the G/L together in each batch.

What You'll See: Invoices grouped by extract reference number showing vendor, invoice details, amounts,
G/L accounts, job information, and posting dates. Each extract reference shows totals for that batch.

Criteria: Select company, extract reference range, vendor range, job range, and G/L period. Can filter by
payment status and extract date.

Key Information: The extract reference is like a batch number that ties together all invoices posted to
the G/L at the same time. This helps you trace G/L entries back to their source documents and verify
posting accuracy.

When to Use This Report: When your G/L shows an extract batch and you need to see what's in it. When
reconciling A/P to G/L and need to trace specific postings. When you need to reverse or adjust an extract
batch. When preparing audit documentation showing what was posted together. When investigating G/L
balance issues.

Good to Know: Each time you extract invoices to the G/L, they get a reference number. This report lets
you reconstruct exactly what was in each extract batch. Very useful when your accountant asks 'what
created this G/L entry?'

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoice to P/O Comparison
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Compares invoice amounts to purchase order amounts and highlights variances. Shows invoices that
exceed P/O amounts by specified threshold. Use for purchase order compliance monitoring.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Identifies invoices where vendors are billing different amounts than what was on your
purchase order. Helps you catch overcharges and maintain P/O control.

What You'll See: Invoice items where the billed amount differs from the P/O amount by more than your
specified variance (percentage or dollar amount). Shows P/O amount, invoice amount, variance, vendor,
descriptions, and reasons if available.

Criteria: Select company, variance threshold (percentage and/or dollar amount), vendor range, job range,
and date filters. The report shows only items exceeding your specified variance.

Key Information: This is a control report - it finds problems. Any invoice exceeding the P/O by your
variance threshold shows up here for investigation. Helps you catch unauthorized price increases, quantity
overages, or billing errors.

When to Use This Report: Regularly as part of your invoice approval process to catch overcharges. When you
want to enforce strict P/O compliance. When investigating cost overruns. When vendors seem to be billing
more than authorized. When management wants to ensure P/O controls are working.

Good to Know: Set your variance threshold appropriately - too tight and you'll get too many false
alarms, too loose and you'll miss problems. This report is a key control to prevent overpayments.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices Without Centres
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows invoices that are missing cost center (area/centre) codes. Identifies incomplete cost
coding. Use for data quality control and ensuring proper job cost allocation.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Identifies vendor invoices that don't have cost center (area/centre) information filled
in. Helps you maintain complete and accurate job cost records.

What You'll See: All invoices that are missing cost center codes, showing vendor name, invoice details,
amounts, job number (if present), and other available information. These are invoices that need to be
corrected.

Criteria: Select company, vendor range, job range, G/L period, and date filters. The report automatically
shows only invoices missing cost center codes.

Key Information: This is a cleanup/quality control report. Cost centers (areas and centres) are how you
track costs within jobs. Missing cost centers mean costs aren't properly allocated to work phases, which
can throw off your job cost reports.

When to Use This Report: Regularly as part of your data quality checks. Before running job cost reports
(to ensure all costs are properly coded). When job cost reports look wrong and you're investigating.
After training new staff on invoice entry (to check their work). When closing a job and want to ensure
complete cost allocation.

Good to Know: Run this regularly and fix the issues. Incomplete cost coding makes your job cost reports
unreliable. The sooner you catch and fix these, the better your cost tracking.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices Without Client P/O
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows invoices missing client purchase order numbers. Identifies costs that may not be
billable. Use for ensuring proper client P/O assignment and billing preparation.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Identifies vendor invoices that don't have client P/O numbers assigned. Helps you catch
costs that might not be billable or properly authorized.

What You'll See: All invoices that are missing client P/O codes, showing vendor name, invoice details,
amounts, job information, and other available data. These are invoices that may need client P/Os added.

Criteria: Select company, vendor range, job range, G/L period, and date filters. Can filter to specific
jobs or types of work. The report automatically shows only invoices missing client P/O numbers.

Key Information: This is a billing control report. If your contracts require client P/Os for billable
work, missing P/Os mean you might not be able to bill these costs. It also helps ensure all costs are
properly authorized by the client.

When to Use This Report: Before billing clients (to ensure all costs have P/Os). When preparing change
orders (identifying costs that need authorization). Regularly as a quality control check. When clients
question charges (making sure everything was authorized). When job costs seem high (checking if costs
should be billable).

Good to Know: Not all invoices need client P/Os (some might be your overhead). But for reimbursable or
cost-plus work, missing P/Os can mean you can't bill the client. Catch these early!

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by C/C
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Displays invoices paid or payable by credit card. Shows charges grouped by card number. Use for
reconciling credit card statements and tracking card spending.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows vendor invoices that were paid or will be paid by credit card. Essential for
reconciling your credit card statements and tracking card spending.

What You'll See: Invoices grouped by credit card number showing vendor name, transaction date, invoice
number, description, amounts, and payment status. Each card shows subtotals of all charges.

Criteria: Select company, credit card number range, vendor range, G/L period, and date filters. Can
filter by payment status and job.

Key Information: The report groups charges by card number, making it easy to reconcile against your card
statements. Subtotals show total spending on each card. Helps you track card usage and ensure charges are
properly authorized.

When to Use This Report: When reconciling your credit card statements. When you need to see all charges
on a specific card. When tracking employee card usage. When disputing charges with your card company.
When preparing to pay your credit card bill. When auditing credit card expenses.

Good to Know: This shows the detail behind your credit card charges. Match the totals on this report to
your card statement to make sure everything is accounted for. Any differences need investigation.

reportTrainingRecords.name: C/C Running Balance
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows credit card activity with running balance for each card. Displays charges and payments
chronologically with balance after each transaction. Use for tracking card balances and payment history.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows a running balance for each credit card - like a credit card statement showing every
charge and payment with the balance after each transaction.

What You'll See: For each card, a chronological list of all activity including charges (invoices) and
payments, with a running balance showing what you owe after each transaction. Like looking at your card
statement over time.

Criteria: Select company, credit card range, date range, and optionally vendor or job filters. The report
automatically includes both charges and payments.

Key Information: The running balance shows exactly what you owe on each card at any point in time. New
charges increase the balance, payments decrease it. Helps you understand card balances and payment timing.

When to Use This Report: When you need to know the current balance on a card. When reconciling credit
card statements and payments. When investigating when the balance on a card got too high. When planning
credit card payments. When tracking payment history on company cards.

Good to Know: This is different from the Invoices by C/C report - this one shows both sides of the
equation (charges and payments) and maintains a running balance. Very useful for understanding your card
payment status.

reportTrainingRecords.name: P/Os by Vendor
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Lists purchase orders organized by vendor. Shows P/O details, amounts, and status. Use for
tracking vendor commitments and outstanding orders.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows all your purchase orders grouped by vendor. Your main report for seeing what
you've ordered from each supplier and what's still outstanding.

What You'll See: For each vendor, all their P/Os showing P/O number, date, description, original P/O
amount, amount invoiced to date, outstanding balance, job information, and P/O status. Each vendor
grouping shows subtotals.

Criteria: Select company, vendor range, P/O number range, job range, and date filters. Can filter by P/O
status (open, closed, or all).

Key Information: Outstanding balance shows what still hasn't been invoiced yet. This represents goods or
services ordered but not yet delivered/billed. Vendor subtotals show your total commitment to each
supplier.

When to Use This Report: When a vendor asks about their P/Os. When tracking what's still on order with
each supplier. When preparing accruals (need to know what's ordered but not invoiced). When investigating
why something hasn't been delivered. When analyzing vendor relationships and order volumes.

Good to Know: Open P/Os represent commitments - money you've promised to pay when goods/services are
delivered. Track these carefully for cash flow planning.

reportTrainingRecords.name: P/Os by G/L Account
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Displays purchase orders grouped by G/L account. Shows commitments by expense category. Use for
budget tracking and analyzing spending commitments by account type.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows your purchase orders organized by G/L account (expense category). Helps you
understand commitments by type of expense.

What You'll See: P/Os grouped by G/L account showing vendor name, P/O details, dates, amounts (original,
invoiced, outstanding), job information, and status. Each G/L account shows subtotals of all P/Os charged
to that account.

Criteria: Select company, G/L account range, vendor range, job range, and date filters. Can filter by P/O
status.

Key Information: The G/L account grouping shows your commitments by expense type. For example, you can see
all your equipment rental P/Os, all your materials P/Os, etc. Subtotals show total commitments in each
expense category.

When to Use This Report: When tracking budget commitments by expense category. When management wants to
see what's been committed (not just spent) by account type. When preparing budget vs actual reports
(including commitments). When analyzing spending patterns by expense category.

Good to Know: This shows what you've committed to spend, not what you've actually spent. Add actual costs
plus outstanding P/Os to see total exposure in each account.

reportTrainingRecords.name: P/Os by Centre in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows purchase orders organized by job and cost center. Displays P/O commitments within each
work phase. Use for detailed job commitment tracking and cost center budget monitoring.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows purchase orders organized by job and then by cost center (area/centre) within each
job. Essential for tracking P/O commitments at the work phase level.

What You'll See: P/Os grouped first by job, then by cost center within that job, showing vendor name, P/O
details, amounts (original, invoiced, outstanding), and status. Each cost center shows subtotals so you
can see total commitments in each work phase.

Criteria: Select company, job range, area/centre range, vendor range, and date filters. Can filter by P/O
status.

Key Information: Cost centers break your job into phases (like 'site prep,' 'foundation,' 'framing').
This report shows P/O commitments in each phase. Outstanding amounts represent work ordered but not yet
delivered/invoiced.

When to Use This Report: When tracking job commitments by work phase. When comparing actual costs plus
commitments to cost center budgets. When identifying which phases have large outstanding P/Os. When
managing project cash flow (knowing what's coming). When preparing forecasts by cost center.

Good to Know: Add this to your actual costs to see total exposure (spent + committed) by cost center.
Essential for accurate job forecasting.

reportTrainingRecords.name: P/Os by Vendor in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Displays purchase orders grouped by vendor within each job. Shows P/O commitments per supplier
per project. Use for job-level vendor commitment tracking.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows purchase orders organized by job and then by vendor within that job. Helps you see
what you've committed to each supplier on each project.
