What You'll See: P/Os grouped first by job, then by vendor within that job, showing P/O numbers, dates,
descriptions, amounts (original, invoiced, outstanding), and status. Each vendor/job combination shows
subtotals.

Criteria: Select company, job range, vendor range, and date filters. Can filter by P/O status.

Key Information: The double grouping (job then vendor) shows both your total job commitments and which
suppliers have the largest P/Os on each project. Outstanding amounts show what's still pending delivery.

When to Use This Report: When managing job commitments and need to see vendor exposure per project. When a
vendor asks about their P/Os on a specific job. When comparing vendor commitments across projects. When
tracking which suppliers are working on which jobs. When investigating job cost overruns (seeing
commitments).

Good to Know: This helps you understand vendor relationships by project. You can see which suppliers are
your major partners on each job.

reportTrainingRecords.name: P/Os by Client P/O
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows purchase orders grouped by client P/O number. Displays your commitments against client
authorizations. Use for tracking spending against client budgets.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows your purchase orders organized by client P/O numbers. Essential for tracking
commitments against client authorizations.

What You'll See: P/Os grouped by client P/O showing vendor name, P/O details, amounts (original, invoiced,
outstanding), job information, and status. Each client P/O shows subtotals of all your P/Os tied to that
client authorization.

Criteria: Select company, client P/O range, vendor range, job range, and date filters. Can filter by P/O
status.

Key Information: This shows your commitments against client budgets. Add actual costs plus P/O commitments
to see total exposure against each client authorization. Helps prevent going over client-approved amounts.

When to Use This Report: When tracking spending against client authorizations. When you need to request
additional authorization (showing what's already committed). When clients ask what you've committed
against their P/O. When preparing change order requests. When managing cost-plus or reimbursable contracts.

Good to Know: Outstanding P/O amounts represent future costs that will be billed against the client P/O.
Track these carefully to avoid exceeding client-approved amounts.

reportTrainingRecords.name: P/Os by P/O Number
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Lists purchase orders sorted by P/O number. Useful for finding specific P/Os quickly. Use when
you know the P/O number and need details or status.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows purchase orders sorted by P/O number. Your quick lookup tool when you know a P/O
number and need details.

What You'll See: P/Os listed in P/O number order showing vendor name, dates, descriptions, amounts
(original, invoiced, outstanding), job information, and status.

Criteria: Select company, P/O number range (or specific numbers), vendor range, job range, and date
filters. Can filter by status.

Key Information: The P/O number sort makes it fast to locate specific orders. If someone references a P/O
number, you can quickly pull up all the details, see what's been invoiced, and check the status.

When to Use This Report: When a vendor or employee references a specific P/O number. When you need to look
up P/O details quickly. When checking P/O status. When verifying P/O information before calling a vendor.
When investigating why an order hasn't been delivered.

Good to Know: This is a lookup tool - when you have a P/O number, this gets you the information fast.
Much quicker than searching through vendor or job reports.

reportTrainingRecords.name: P/Os Month End O/S by Vendor in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows purchase orders that were outstanding at month end, organized by vendor within job.
Displays P/O commitments at period end. Use for month-end accruals and commitment reporting.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows which purchase orders had outstanding balances at the end of a specific accounting
period. Essential for month-end accruals and understanding your commitments at period end.

What You'll See: P/Os that were open at period end, grouped by vendor within job, showing P/O details,
original amounts, what had been invoiced by period end, and what was still outstanding at that date.

Criteria: Select company, specify the G/L period (month/year), vendor range, and job range. The report
looks back and shows P/O status at that period end.

Key Information: This is a point-in-time report showing your commitment position at a specific date. The
outstanding amounts represent goods/services ordered but not yet received or invoiced as of period end.
Essential for accrual accounting.

When to Use This Report: When closing month-end and need to report outstanding commitments. When preparing
accruals for goods ordered but not invoiced. When your accountant needs period-end commitment data. When
preparing financial statements (showing future liabilities). When analyzing commitment trends over time.

Good to Know: Even though some of these P/Os may be invoiced now, this report shows what was outstanding at
that specific period end. Critical for accurate historical financial reporting.

reportTrainingRecords.name: P/Os by Equipment
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Displays purchase orders associated with specific equipment. Shows P/Os for equipment parts,
repairs, and services. Use for equipment cost tracking and maintenance planning.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows purchase orders that are associated with specific pieces of equipment. Helps you
track equipment-related commitments and plan for maintenance costs.

What You'll See: P/Os grouped by equipment number showing vendor name, P/O details, descriptions of work or
parts, amounts (original, invoiced, outstanding), and status. Each equipment grouping shows subtotals.

Criteria: Select company, equipment range, vendor range, job range, and date filters. Can filter by P/O
status.

Key Information: Shows P/O commitments for equipment repairs, parts, maintenance, and related costs.
Outstanding amounts represent work ordered but not yet invoiced. Helps you understand future equipment
costs.

When to Use This Report: When tracking maintenance and repair commitments by machine. When planning cash
flow for equipment expenses. When a piece of equipment is in the shop and you want to know what's been
ordered. When analyzing total equipment costs (actual + committed). When preparing equipment budgets.

Good to Know: Only shows P/Os where equipment was specified. Add this to actual equipment costs to see
total equipment exposure (spent + committed).

reportTrainingRecords.name: Requisitions by Vendor
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Lists purchase requisitions organized by vendor. Shows all pending purchase requests for each
supplier. Use for reviewing and approving purchase requests before creating P/Os.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows purchase requisitions (requests to buy) grouped by vendor. Your main report for
reviewing what people are asking to purchase from each supplier.

What You'll See: For each vendor, all requisitions showing who requested it, what they want to buy,
quantities, estimated costs, approval status (pending, approved, rejected), job information, and whether
P/Os have been created yet. Each vendor grouping shows subtotals.

Criteria: Select company, vendor range, job range, and date filters. Can filter by approval status to see
only pending requests, only approved, etc.

Key Information: Requisitions are the first step in purchasing - someone identifies a need and requests
approval to buy. The vendor grouping helps you see all requests going to each supplier, which helps batch
orders and get better pricing. Approval status shows what needs your attention.

When to Use This Report: When reviewing pending purchase requests for approval. When you want to batch
multiple requests to the same vendor into one order. When tracking what's been requested from each
supplier. When following up on requisitions that haven't been converted to P/Os yet. When controlling
spending before commitments are made.

Good to Know: This is your control point - you review and approve (or reject) requisitions before they
become actual purchase orders. Once approved, requisitions typically get converted to P/Os.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Requisitions by Vendor in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Displays purchase requisitions grouped by vendor within each job. Shows what's been requested
from each supplier for each project. Use for coordinating job purchasing with vendors.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows purchase requisitions organized by job and then by vendor within that job. Helps
you see what's been requested from each supplier for each project.

What You'll See: Requisitions grouped first by job, then by vendor within that job, showing requester name,
item descriptions, quantities, estimated costs, approval status, and whether P/Os have been issued. Each
vendor/job combination shows subtotals.

Criteria: Select company, job range, vendor range, and date filters. Can filter by approval status.

Key Information: The job/vendor grouping helps you coordinate purchasing. You can see all requests for a
specific supplier on a specific job, which helps batch orders and negotiate better pricing. Subtotals show
total requested from each vendor per job.

When to Use This Report: When you want to batch multiple requests to the same vendor on the same job (to
reduce delivery charges or get quantity discounts). When coordinating with vendors about job materials. When
reviewing what's being requested from your major suppliers. When planning material deliveries to job sites.

Good to Know: This grouping helps you be strategic about purchasing - seeing all requests to one vendor lets
you combine them into larger, more economical orders.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Requisitions by Centre in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows purchase requisitions organized by job and cost center. Displays requested items for
each work phase. Use for reviewing job-related purchase requests by area.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows purchase requisitions organized by job and then by cost center (area/centre)
within each job. Helps you review what's being requested for each phase of work.

What You'll See: Requisitions grouped first by job, then by cost center within that job, showing requester,
vendor, item descriptions, quantities, estimated costs, approval status, and whether P/Os have been issued.
Each cost center shows subtotals.

Criteria: Select company, job range, area/centre range, vendor range, and date filters. Can filter by
approval status.

Key Information: Cost centers represent work phases (like 'site prep,' 'foundation,' 'framing'). This
report shows what's being requested for each phase. Helps you understand material and service needs by work
area and control job spending at the request stage.

When to Use This Report: When reviewing purchase requests for job work phases. When a project manager wants
to see what their crews are requesting. When you need to prioritize requests based on which phase of work is
active. When tracking job spending before it becomes committed. When coordinating material deliveries with
work schedules.

Good to Know: This gives project managers visibility into what their teams are requesting for each phase of
work. Helps coordinate purchasing with construction schedules.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Requisitions by GL Account
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Displays purchase requisitions grouped by G/L account. Shows requested purchases by expense
category. Use for reviewing spending requests by account type.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows purchase requisitions organized by G/L account (expense category). Helps you
review purchase requests by type of expense.

What You'll See: Requisitions grouped by G/L account showing requester name, vendor, item descriptions,
quantities, estimated costs, approval status, job information, and whether P/Os have been created. Each G/L
account shows subtotals.

Criteria: Select company, G/L account range, vendor range, and date filters. Can filter by approval status
and job.

Key Information: The G/L account grouping helps you see what's being requested in each expense category.
For example, you can review all office supply requests, all equipment rental requests, etc. Subtotals show
total requested spending in each account.

When to Use This Report: When reviewing purchase requests by expense type before approval. When you need to
see spending patterns by category. When budget constraints require prioritizing certain expense types. When
management wants to review requested spending by account. When analyzing department spending habits.

Good to Know: This helps you control spending at the request stage - before actual P/Os are issued. You can
see what people are asking to buy in each category and make decisions accordingly.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Requisitions by Equipment
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows purchase requisitions associated with specific equipment. Displays requested items for
equipment repairs and maintenance. Use for tracking equipment-related purchase requests.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows purchase requisitions (requests to buy) that are associated with specific pieces
of equipment. Helps you track what's been requested for equipment repairs and maintenance.

What You'll See: Requisitions grouped by equipment number showing requester, vendor, what was requested,
quantities, estimated costs, approval status, and whether P/Os have been issued. Each equipment grouping
shows subtotals.

Criteria: Select company, equipment range, vendor range, and date filters. Can filter by approval status
(approved, pending, rejected).

Key Information: Requisitions are requests to buy - they haven't been ordered yet (that's the P/O). This
shows what people are asking to purchase for each piece of equipment. Helps you understand equipment needs
and plan maintenance spending.

When to Use This Report: When reviewing equipment purchase requests before approving. When tracking
equipment maintenance requests. When a machine needs work and you want to see what's already been
requested. When budgeting equipment repairs. When identifying high-maintenance machines.

Good to Know: Once requisitions are approved, they typically get converted to P/Os. This report shows
requests before they become actual purchase orders.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Receiving by P/O
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Lists receiving records organized by purchase order within vendor. Shows what has been
delivered against each P/O. Use for tracking P/O fulfillment and delivery history.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows receiving records (deliveries) organized by purchase order within vendor. Your
main report for tracking what's been delivered against each P/O.

What You'll See: For each vendor, their P/Os with receiving records showing delivery dates, items received,
quantities, who received them, and any notes. Shows both what was ordered and what was actually delivered.

Criteria: Select company, vendor range, P/O number range, and date range for receiving dates. Can filter to
specific P/Os or vendors.

Key Information: This shows your receiving history by P/O. You can see when deliveries happened, what came
in, and compare received quantities to ordered quantities. Essential for verifying deliveries and resolving
discrepancies with vendors.

When to Use This Report: When verifying that P/Os have been fulfilled. When a vendor claims they delivered
something and you need to check. When comparing actual deliveries to what was ordered. When investigating
missing items. When closing out P/Os and ensuring everything was received. When resolving delivery disputes
with vendors.

Good to Know: The P/O grouping makes it easy to see the complete delivery history for each order. You can
track multiple deliveries against a single P/O and verify everything arrived.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Backorders by P/O
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows P/Os where some items have been received but not all. Displays partially filled orders.
Use for tracking incomplete deliveries and following up with vendors.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Identifies purchase orders where you've received some items but not everything yet.
Helps you track partially filled orders and follow up on outstanding items.

What You'll See: P/Os grouped by vendor showing P/O number, item descriptions, quantity ordered, quantity
received so far, quantity still outstanding, and dates. Only shows P/Os with partial deliveries (some items
received, some still pending).

Criteria: Select company, vendor range, P/O number range, and date filters. The report automatically shows
only P/Os with incomplete deliveries.

Key Information: These are P/Os in progress - delivery has started but isn't complete. The outstanding
quantities show exactly what's still coming. Important for following up with vendors about the rest of your
order.

When to Use This Report: When following up with vendors about incomplete deliveries. When you've received
part of an order and need to know what's still coming. When investigating why a P/O is taking a long time to
fill. When job sites report missing materials (checking if it's on order but not delivered yet). When you
want to close out old P/Os and need to identify ones with outstanding items.

Good to Know: Partial deliveries are common - vendors might split shipments or have items on backorder.
This report helps you stay on top of what's still coming.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Backorders by Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows P/O items that haven't been fully received, organized by job. Displays what's still on
order for each project. Use for tracking outstanding deliveries by job.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows P/O items that haven't been completely delivered yet, organized by job. Helps you
track what's still on order for each project.

What You'll See: Items grouped by job showing vendor name, P/O number, item descriptions, quantity ordered,
quantity received so far, quantity still outstanding, and dates. Each job shows subtotals of outstanding
items.

Criteria: Select company, job range, vendor range, and P/O date filters. The report automatically shows only
items where quantity received is less than quantity ordered.

Key Information: The job grouping helps project managers see what materials are still coming to their sites.
Outstanding quantities show exactly what's still on order. Essential for coordinating work schedules with
material deliveries.

When to Use This Report: When a job site is waiting for materials and you need to check status. When planning
work schedules and need to know what's coming. When project managers ask about pending deliveries. When
following up with vendors about late deliveries. When investigating job delays due to missing materials.

Good to Know: The job-based grouping makes this report perfect for project managers. They can see at a glance
what's still on order for their projects and plan accordingly.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Material Receiving Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Prints formatted receiving documents showing items received, one receipt per page. Use for
creating receiving documentation and warehouse paperwork.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Creates formal receiving documents - one page per receipt showing what was delivered.
Used for warehouse documentation and receiving records.

What You'll See: Professional formatted receiving reports, one per receipt, showing vendor name, P/O number,
delivery date, detailed list of items received with quantities, descriptions, and who received them. Suitable
for filing and documentation.

Criteria: Select company, P/O number range, vendor range, and date range for receiving dates. Usually run
for specific receipts you need to document.

Key Information: This is a formal document report - designed to be printed and filed. Each receipt gets its
own page with complete details. Serves as your official record of what was delivered, when, and who accepted
it.

When to Use This Report: When you need official documentation of what was received. When warehouse staff need
receiving paperwork to file. When vendors dispute deliveries and you need proof of receipt. When auditors
need receiving documentation. When creating permanent records for significant deliveries.

Good to Know: This is your formal receiving documentation - more polished than the other receiving reports.
One page per receipt makes it easy to file and retrieve later.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Vendor List
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Lists vendors with address and contact information sorted by vendor name. Shows basic vendor
details. Use for vendor directory and contact lookup.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows a list of your vendors with their contact information, sorted by vendor name.
Your vendor directory for looking up addresses, phone numbers, and contacts.

What You'll See: Vendor names (sorted alphabetically), vendor codes, addresses, phone numbers, fax numbers,
primary contact persons, email addresses, and any important notes. Basic directory information for each
vendor.

Criteria: Select company and vendor range. Can filter to specific vendors or run for all.

Key Information: The alphabetical sort by vendor name makes it easy to look up vendors. Shows all the
information you need to contact a vendor - addresses, phone numbers, contacts, etc. No financial information
- just directory details.

When to Use This Report: When you need to look up a vendor's contact information. When someone asks 'who do
we use for [type of supplier]?' When creating a vendor directory for staff. When you need phone numbers to
call vendors. When verifying or updating vendor information. When new staff need a vendor list.

Good to Know: This is a simple contact list - no balances or transactions. Just the basics you need to get
in touch with vendors. Think of it as your vendor phone book.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Vendor Status Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows vendor outstanding balances and year-to-date totals in vendor code order. Displays
summary of activity with each vendor. Use for reviewing vendor relationships and account status.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows a summary for each vendor including what you owe them and year-to-date activity.
Your high-level report for understanding your vendor relationships.

What You'll See: For each vendor, their current outstanding balance (what you owe), year-to-date purchases,
year-to-date payments, holdback amounts, and other accumulations. Sorted by vendor code. Shows the big
picture of each vendor relationship.

Criteria: Select company and vendor range. Usually run for all vendors to get a complete picture of your
accounts payable.

Key Information: Outstanding balance is what you currently owe each vendor. Year-to-date purchases show your
total business with them this year. The total outstanding from this report should match your accounts
payable balance in the general ledger.

When to Use This Report: When you need a high-level view of your vendor relationships. When reconciling A/P
subledger to G/L (total outstanding should match). When reviewing which vendors you owe the most to. When
analyzing your major suppliers by annual spending. When management wants to see vendor summary information.

Good to Know: This is taken from vendor records (not invoices). Compare it to the Vendor Aged Invoice Report
- both should show the same total outstanding. If they don't match, there's a reconciliation issue.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Vendor Aged Invoice Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows unpaid invoices aged by how long they've been outstanding, grouped by vendor. Displays
aging in buckets (current, 30, 60, 90+ days). Use for accounts payable aging analysis.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows unpaid vendor invoices with aging information organized by vendor. Your main
report for accounts payable aging - understanding how old your unpaid bills are.

What You'll See: For each vendor, their unpaid invoices with amounts broken into aging buckets (current,
0-30 days, 31-60 days, 61-90 days, over 90 days). Shows invoice numbers, dates, amounts, and age. Each
vendor shows subtotals by aging bucket.

Criteria: Select company, vendor range, and specify the G/L period to age from (usually the current period).
The aging is calculated backwards from this period.

Key Information: Aging shows how long invoices have been sitting unpaid. Current means due this period, 30
days means one period old, etc. The aging buckets help you identify problem areas - large amounts in the 60+
day columns mean you're getting behind with vendors.

When to Use This Report: When managing accounts payable and prioritizing who to pay. When vendors complain
about late payments. When preparing cash flow reports (showing payment obligations by age). When management
wants to review payables aging. When your accountant needs aging information for financial statements.

Good to Know: This is one of your most important A/P reports. Compare it to the Vendor Status Report - they
should show the same total outstanding. Aging helps maintain good vendor relationships by identifying old
unpaid bills.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Vendor Job Aged Invoice Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Shows aged unpaid invoices grouped by vendor within job. Displays how long invoices have been
outstanding for each vendor on each project. Use for job-level payables aging analysis.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows unpaid vendor invoices with aging information, organized by vendor within job.
Helps you see how long you've owed each supplier on each project.

What You'll See: Invoices grouped first by vendor, then by job within that vendor, with amounts broken into
aging buckets (current, 30 days, 60 days, 90+ days). Shows invoice numbers, dates, amounts, and age. Each
vendor/job combination shows subtotals by aging bucket.

Criteria: Select company, vendor range, job range, and specify the G/L period to age from (usually current
period).

Key Information: Aging shows how long invoices have been unpaid. The job grouping helps you see which
projects have old unpaid bills. Aging buckets show whether payables are current or getting old. Very
important for managing vendor relationships.

When to Use This Report: When managing accounts payable by project. When vendors complain about late
payments and you need to see the details. When a job is having payment issues and you need to identify old
outstanding invoices. When preparing to pay vendors and want to prioritize by age and job. When analyzing
which projects have payment problems.

Good to Know: The double grouping (vendor then job) gives you both perspectives - you can see all your aging
with a vendor, broken down by which jobs the old invoices are for.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Vendor by Supplier Type List
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Lists vendors organized by supplier type. Shows contact information grouped by vendor
category. Use for finding vendors by what they supply.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows vendors organized by supplier type (category). Helps you find vendors by what they
provide - like electrical, concrete, equipment rental, etc.

What You'll See: Vendors grouped by supplier type showing vendor name, contact information (address, phone,
email), primary contact person, and any notes. Each supplier type grouping shows all vendors in that
category.

Criteria: Select company, supplier type range, and vendor range. Can filter to specific types or run for all
types.

Key Information: The supplier type grouping makes it easy to find vendors by what they do. For example, if
you need an electrical supplier, you can look at all vendors classified as electrical. Very useful for
sourcing and vendor selection.

When to Use This Report: When looking for vendors who provide a specific type of product or service. When
sourcing new suppliers (seeing who's already in your system by category). When preparing bid lists by trade.
When someone asks 'who do we use for concrete suppliers?' When analyzing your vendor base by category.

Good to Know: The supplier type classification is set up in vendor maintenance. This report is only as useful
as your vendor classification - make sure vendors are properly categorized!

reportTrainingRecords.name: Vendor Mailing List
reportTrainingRecords.summary:
Creates a mailing list of vendors with addresses in vendor code order. Use for mass mailings,
creating labels, or distributing information to multiple vendors.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Creates a mailing list showing vendor names and addresses sorted by vendor code. Used for
mass mailings, creating labels, or any time you need vendor addresses.

What You'll See: A list of vendors with their mailing addresses, sorted by vendor code. Shows company name,
attention line if applicable, street address, city, province/state, postal code, and country.

Criteria: Select company and vendor range. Can filter to specific types of vendors if needed.

Key Information: The addresses are formatted for mailing purposes. The vendor code sort order makes it easy
to find specific vendors in the list. Useful for creating mailing labels or importing into other systems.

When to Use This Report: When you need to send something to multiple vendors (like tax forms, policy
updates, insurance certificates). When creating mailing labels for vendor communications. When you need a
vendor address list for distribution purposes. When exporting vendor addresses to another system.

Good to Know: This is a simple address list - no financial information. Perfect for administrative tasks
that require vendor mailing addresses.

reportTrainingRecords.name: LEMS Billings by Centre in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows LEMS (Labour Equipment Materials Services) charges grouped by cost centre within jobs. Use this to prepare billings and track costs by work area.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See all LEMS charges organized by cost centre within each job. Perfect for 
preparing invoices or analyzing costs by specific work areas on a project.

What You'll See: Jobs with their cost centres listed underneath, showing labour, equipment, material, 
and subcontract charges for each centre. Includes quantities, rates, and extended amounts. Organized by 
job then by centre.

Criteria: Select specific jobs or a range, choose a date range for charges, filter by cost centre, and 
choose billing status (billed, unbilled, or all).

Key Information: LEMS stands for Labour, Equipment, Materials, and Services (subcontracts). This report 
groups all these charge types by cost centre, making it easy to see what each work area consumed. The 
billing amounts shown include markup and are ready for invoicing.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare progress billings organized by work area
• Review charges by cost centre before invoicing
• Analyze which work areas consumed the most resources
• Track unbilled LEMS charges by centre
• Compare actual centre costs to budget
• Prepare backup detail for project invoices

Good to Know: This is one of the most detailed LEMS reports. If your project billing is organized by 
work areas (centres), this report gives you exactly what you need. Use the billing status filter to see 
only unbilled items when preparing your next invoice.

reportTrainingRecords.name: LEMS by Centre in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows cost detail for LEMS charges by centre in job. Displays internal costs rather than billing amounts - use this for cost analysis and job costing.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Analyze the actual costs (not billing amounts) of labour, equipment, materials, 
and services by cost centre within jobs. This is for internal cost tracking and analysis.

What You'll See: Jobs with cost centres listed underneath, showing LEMS charges at cost (not billing 
rates). Includes labour hours and costs, equipment usage and costs, material quantities and costs, and 
subcontract amounts. Organized by job then by centre.

Criteria: Select jobs and date ranges, filter by cost centre, choose which charge types to include 
(labour, equipment, materials, subcontracts, or all).

Key Information: This report shows costs, not billing amounts. Use this for internal management and cost 
analysis. The difference between this report and LEMS Billings by Centre is that this shows what things 
cost you, while the billing report shows what you charge the client (with markup).

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze true project costs by work area
• Compare actual costs to budget by centre
• Calculate profit margins by subtracting costs from billings
• Track resource consumption at cost for management
• Identify cost overruns by work area
• Prepare cost reports for project managers

Good to Know: Keep this report internal - it shows your actual costs without markup. Use the LEMS 
Billings report when preparing customer invoices. This report is valuable for understanding your true 
profitability by comparing costs here to billing amounts on the other report.

reportTrainingRecords.name: LEMS Progress Draw
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Calculates progress billing amounts based on percentage complete and contract values. Use this for schedule of values billing and progress draw invoices.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Prepare progress draw invoices based on percentage of work completed. Shows 
contract amounts, percent complete, earned amounts, and billing calculations.

What You'll See: Cost centres or line items with their contract amounts, current percent complete, 
amount earned to date, previous billings, and current billing amount. Includes holdback calculations if 
applicable. Typically organized by schedule of values line items.

Criteria: Select the job, choose the billing period, enter percent complete for each item (or use 
stored values), and set holdback percentages if applicable.

Key Information: Progress draws are based on percentage complete, not actual costs. You bill the client 
for the percentage of each contract line item that's been completed. The report calculates: Contract 
Amount × Percent Complete = Amount Earned, then subtracts previous billings to get the current billing 
amount. Holdback is calculated separately and held until project completion.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare monthly progress billing invoices
• Calculate earned revenue based on work completed
• Generate schedule of values billing applications
• Track cumulative billings versus contract amounts
• Calculate and track holdback retainage
• Prepare AIA-style progress billing applications

Good to Know: This is the standard report for construction progress billing. You update the percent 
complete each billing period, and the report calculates what to bill. The percent complete should 
reflect actual work completed, not costs incurred - a common mistake is mixing percentage-complete 
billing with cost-based billing.

reportTrainingRecords.name: LEMS Summary
reportTrainingRecords.summary: High-level summary of all LEMS charges by category. Perfect for a quick overview of labour, equipment, materials, and subcontract totals.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Get a quick, high-level summary of LEMS charges grouped into major categories. 
Shows totals for labour, equipment, materials, and subcontracts without overwhelming detail.

What You'll See: Summary totals for each major charge category - labour hours and amounts, equipment 
usage and amounts, material costs, and subcontract amounts. Can be organized by job, by period, or 
overall totals depending on report parameters.

Criteria: Select jobs and date ranges, choose which charge categories to include, filter by billing 
status (billed/unbilled), and choose summary level (by job, by period, or grand total).

Key Information: This is the "big picture" LEMS report - no detail, just category totals. Use this 
when you need a quick answer to "how much labour/equipment/materials have we used" without wading 
through pages of detail. The other LEMS reports give you detail by centre, date, or item.

When to Use This Report:
• Get a quick snapshot of LEMS charges on a job
• Compare labour vs. equipment vs. materials spending
• Check total unbilled LEMS without detail
• Prepare high-level cost summaries for management
• Estimate the size of your next progress billing
• Review period-over-period LEMS spending trends

Good to Know: Start with this report to get the big picture, then drill into the detailed LEMS reports 
if you need more information. This is perfect for daily or weekly check-ins on project activity - you 
can quickly see if spending is tracking as expected without sorting through pages of transactions.

reportTrainingRecords.name: LEMS Accruals by Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows unbilled LEMS work by job for month-end revenue accrual journal entries. Breaks down labour, equipment, materials, and subcontract that needs to be accrued.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Calculate unbilled LEMS revenue at month end to prepare accrual journal entries. 
Shows work performed but not yet invoiced that needs to be recognized as revenue in the current period.

What You'll See: Jobs with unbilled work broken down by category - labour, equipment, materials, and 
scaffolding. Shows dollar amounts for each category plus totals by job. Includes the date range of work 
covered and count of billing items. Report totals show the complete accrual amount needed. Organized by 
job and area.

Criteria: Select the work date range (typically the current month), choose jobs and areas to include, and 
filter to show only unbilled items. The date range should match your accounting period for proper revenue 
recognition.

Key Information: This report was specifically designed to support month-end accrual journal 
entries. At month end, you need to recognize revenue for work performed even if it hasn't been invoiced 
yet. This report shows exactly how much unbilled work exists by category (labour, equipment, materials, 
scaffolding). Use these totals to create your accrual journal entry debiting Work in Progress and 
crediting the appropriate revenue accounts.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare month-end revenue accrual journal entries
• Calculate unbilled revenue for financial statements
• Support percentage-of-completion revenue recognition
• Verify that all work performed is recognized in the correct period
• Break down unbilled amounts by revenue category for proper G/L posting
• Document work in progress amounts for financial reporting

Good to Know: Run this report at month end before closing your books. The totals by category (labour, 
equipment, materials, scaffolding) help you post to the correct G/L revenue accounts. The accrual you 
record this month will reverse next month when you actually invoice the work. This ensures revenue is 
recognized in the period the work was performed, which is required for proper revenue recognition and 
percentage-of-completion accounting. The report separates hourly amounts as its own category 
to track it separately from general labour and materials.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Client List
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows client contact information including names, addresses, phone numbers, and last update dates. Perfect for reviewing your client list or creating a contact directory.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Get a complete directory of your clients with all their contact details 
in one place.

What You'll See: Client names, client codes, phone and fax numbers, mailing addresses, and the 
date each client record was last updated. Everything is sorted by client name for easy browsing.

Criteria: Pick which clients to include - you can select specific clients, a range of client 
codes, or all active clients.

When to Use This Report:
• Create a phone list for your accounts receivable team
• Print a client directory for new staff members
• Verify client addresses before mailing statements
• Export contact info for your CRM or email system
• Double-check that client contact details are current
• Share client contact information with project managers

Good to Know: This is your go-to report for basic client info. The last update date helps you 
spot records that might need refreshing - if a client hasn't been updated in years, their info 
might be stale.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Client Status Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Displays current outstanding balances and year-to-date totals for each client. Taken directly from client master records for a snapshot of who owes you money.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Get a quick financial overview of each client showing what they owe and 
their year-to-date activity. This comes straight from the client master file.

What You'll See: For each client, you'll see their outstanding balance, year-to-date invoices, 
year-to-date payments, and year-to-date finance charges. Clients are listed in client code 
order.

Criteria: Choose which clients to include, filter by client code range, or run for all clients. 
You can also limit to clients with outstanding balances only.

Key Information: The outstanding balance shown here should match the total from the Client Aged 
Invoice Report (ARCREP c). If they don't match, there's a data integrity issue to investigate. 
The client status comes from the client master record, while the aged report comes from actual 
invoices.

When to Use This Report:
• Review client balances at month-end before running statements
• Identify which clients have outstanding balances for collections
• Compare with Client Aged Invoice Report to verify data integrity
• Get a quick snapshot of year-to-date billing and payment activity
• Review client financial status before approving new work
• Prepare summary information for management reports

Good to Know: Always reconcile this with the Client Aged Invoice Report - they should show the 
same total outstanding. This report is faster to run but the Aged Invoice Report gives you more 
detail about when invoices are due.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Client Aged Invoice Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows how old each client's unpaid invoices are with aging buckets. Built from actual invoice transactions so you can see exactly which invoices are overdue.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See the age of outstanding invoices for each client broken into aging 
periods (current, 30 days, 60 days, 90+ days). Essential for collections and understanding cash 
flow.

What You'll See: Each client with their outstanding invoices grouped into aging buckets based on 
the invoice G/L period. You'll see current amounts, 30-day-old amounts, 60-day-old amounts, 90+ 
day amounts, plus any holdback, and total outstanding. Organized by client code.

Criteria: Select a G/L period to age from (usually current period), choose which clients to 
include, and optionally filter by outstanding balance thresholds.

Key Information: Aging is calculated based on G/L periods, not invoice dates. So a September 
invoice would be 30 days old in October, 60 days old in November, etc. The total should match 
the Client Status Report - if they don't match, you have a reconciliation issue to investigate.

When to Use This Report:
• Run collections and identify which invoices need follow-up
• Prepare month-end aged accounts receivable for financial statements
• Analyze collection patterns and payment behavior by client
• Identify clients with significantly overdue balances
• Verify receivables balances with your accountant
• Monitor the health of your accounts receivable

Good to Know: This is one of the most important A/R reports. Run it monthly and keep copies for 
your records. Compare the total to the Client Status Report (ARCREP b) - they should always 
match. If a client shows 90+ days outstanding, it's time for a collections call!

reportTrainingRecords.name: Client Job Aged Invoice Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Similar to the Client Aged Invoice Report but broken down by job within each client. Perfect when you need to see aging by project.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: View aged outstanding invoices organized by job within client. Great for 
tracking which specific projects have aging receivables.

What You'll See: Clients with their jobs listed underneath, showing aging buckets for each job. 
You'll see current, 30-day, 60-day, 90+ day amounts, holdback, and totals - all broken down by 
job.

Criteria: Pick a G/L period to age from, select which clients and jobs to include, filter by job 
status, and set balance thresholds if desired.

Key Information: This gives you more detail than the standard Client Aged Invoice Report by 
showing which projects are causing the aging. If one job is significantly past due, you can focus 
your collections efforts on that specific project. Aging still works the same way - based on G/L 
periods, not invoice dates.

When to Use This Report:
• Track receivables for specific projects or contracts
• Identify which jobs have aging issues within a client
• Focus collection calls on specific project invoices
• Monitor holdback releases by job
• Review project-specific payment patterns
• Prepare job-level receivables information for project managers

Good to Know: Use this instead of the regular aged report when you're managing multiple projects 
for the same client. It helps you see if payment issues are across all jobs or isolated to one 
project - maybe a client is disputing invoices on one job but paying promptly on others.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Client Log Action Items
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists clients who have action items due including follow-up tasks, assigned staff, and priorities. Helps you track customer service tasks and collections follow-ups.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Keep track of follow-up tasks and action items related to clients. Never 
miss a callback or forget to send that document a client requested.

What You'll See: A list of clients with outstanding action items showing the follow-up date, who 
the task is assigned to, priority level, and a description of what needs to be done.

Criteria: Filter by follow-up date range (like this week or overdue), select specific clients, 
choose action type, filter by assigned person, or set priority levels.

When to Use This Report:
• Check your daily or weekly to-do list for client follow-ups
• See which action items are overdue and need immediate attention
• Review tasks assigned to specific team members
• Track collections follow-up calls that are scheduled
• Monitor customer service commitments you've made to clients
• Prepare for weekly team meetings about client activities

Good to Know: This is your client relationship management tool within the A/R system. Use it to 
log when you promise to call someone back, when documents need to be sent, or when you need to 
follow up on a payment. The priority field helps you focus on the most important items first.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Client Running Balance Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows every invoice and payment for a client in date order with a running balance. Like a bank statement but for your client's account.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See the complete transaction history for a client with a running balance 
that shows how their account balance changed over time.

What You'll See: All invoices and payments for each client listed chronologically. Each line 
shows the date, transaction description, invoice amount (if applicable), payment amount (if 
applicable), and the running balance after each transaction. Reads like a bank statement.

Criteria: Select which clients to include and choose a date range for transactions. You can also 
filter to show only transactions after a certain balance threshold.

When to Use This Report:
• Answer client questions about their account history
• Research when and how payments were applied to specific invoices
• Show a client exactly how their balance reached the current amount
• Verify that payments were applied correctly
• Investigate billing disputes by reviewing the transaction history
• Create a client account summary for your records

Good to Know: This is the report to use when a client calls with questions about their account. 
You can see exactly what happened when - every invoice you sent them and every payment they made. 
The running balance makes it easy to explain how their current balance was calculated.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Daily Force Account
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists daily charges for time and materials (T&M) work including labour, equipment, and materials. Use this to prepare force account billings.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track daily charges on time and materials contracts (also called force 
account work). Shows labour hours, equipment usage, and materials consumed each day for billing.

What You'll See: Daily detail of work performed organized by date showing labour hours by worker 
and pay type, equipment hours by unit, and materials used. Includes quantities, rates, and 
extended amounts for each item.

Criteria: Select the job, choose a date range for the daily work, filter by cost centre, client 
P/O, or specific date. Pick which charge types to include (labour, equipment, materials, or all).

Key Information: Force account and time and materials (T&M) mean the same thing - you're billing 
for actual time and materials used, not a lump sum price. This report shows the daily detail you 
need to support your billings. Rates shown are the billable rates, not your internal costs.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare daily or weekly T&M invoices for clients
• Support change order billings with daily detail
• Provide backup documentation for client-requested billing details
• Verify that all daily charges are being captured for billing
• Review T&M work before preparing an invoice
• Track daily production and costs on T&M projects

Good to Know: Many clients require detailed daily reports for T&M work - this gives you that 
detail. The report shows billable rates and amounts, so you can attach it directly to invoices as 
backup. Make sure all your timesheets, equipment tickets, and material receipts are entered before 
running this.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Labour, Equipment & Materials
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Comprehensive summary of labour, equipment, and material charges for T&M billing. Groups costs by type with quantities, rates, and totals.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Get a complete summary of all labour, equipment, and material charges for 
time and materials billing. Shows totals by cost type for invoice preparation.

What You'll See: Charges grouped into three sections - labour (by occupation and pay type), 
equipment (by unit), and materials (by item). Each section shows quantities, billing rates, and 
extended amounts. Subtotals by category and grand totals.

Criteria: Select the job and date range, filter by cost centre, client P/O, or billing status 
(billed vs. unbilled). Choose which charge types to include or run for all.

Key Information: This is like a summary version of the Daily Force Account report - instead of 
daily detail, you get totals by cost category. Perfect for creating clean, professional invoices 
without overwhelming daily detail. Rates are billing rates with markup already applied.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare T&M invoices showing summary totals by category
• Review total charges before creating an invoice
• Provide clients with a clean summary (save the daily detail for backup)
• Estimate the size of your next T&M invoice
• Compare labour vs. equipment vs. material costs on a project
• Analyze cost patterns on T&M work

Good to Know: Most clients prefer this summary format for their invoice rather than pages of daily 
detail. You can always provide the Daily Force Account report as backup if they ask. This report 
groups similar items together making it much easier to read than raw daily transactions.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Labour by Employee
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows T&M labour charges organized by employee with breakdown by area and client P/O. Includes hours, rates, and amounts for billing verification.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See labour charges broken down by individual worker for time and materials 
projects. Helps verify billing accuracy and track productivity by employee.

What You'll See: Each employee listed with their labour hours broken down by work area and client 
purchase order. Shows regular hours, overtime, double time, billing rates, and extended amounts. 
Subtotals by employee.

Criteria: Select the job and date range, choose specific employees or all, filter by work area, 
client P/O, pay type (regular/OT/DT), or billing status.

Key Information: This shows billing detail by worker - if a client questions the hours or rates for 
a specific person, this is your backup. The hours shown are billable hours (already approved 
timesheets), and rates include your markup. The breakdown by area and P/O helps track charges to 
specific parts of the work.

When to Use This Report:
• Respond to client questions about specific workers' hours or rates
• Verify labour charges before preparing an invoice
• Track individual worker productivity on T&M projects
• Provide detailed backup for labour portions of invoices
• Analyze which workers are most utilized on T&M work
• Compare actual employee hours to estimates

Good to Know: Some clients want to see exactly who worked on their project and for how long - this 
report gives them that detail. The breakdown by client P/O is important if different parts of the 
work are funded separately. Keep this as backup documentation for your invoices.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by Client
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists all invoice details organized by client. Shows invoice numbers, dates, amounts, and what's still outstanding.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Get a detailed list of invoices for specific clients showing everything 
about each invoice including what's been paid and what's still owed.

What You'll See: For each client, you'll see all their invoices with invoice numbers, dates, 
description, original amounts, amounts paid, and outstanding balances. Includes G/L period, terms, 
and due dates.

Criteria: Select specific clients or a range, choose a date range for invoices, filter by G/L 
period, show only outstanding invoices, or include all invoices (paid and unpaid).

When to Use This Report:
• Review all billing for a specific client
• Prepare documentation for a client meeting or dispute
• Verify invoice details before making collection calls
• Analyze billing patterns for a customer
• Export invoice data for a specific client
• Double-check that all work was properly invoiced

Good to Know: This is your go-to report for looking up invoice details by customer. Unlike the 
aged reports that show balances in buckets, this shows you line-by-line detail of every invoice. 
Great for answering specific questions about individual invoices.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by G/L Account
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists invoices organized by general ledger revenue account. Use this to analyze revenue by account type or to reconcile invoice detail to G/L postings.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See invoices grouped by the G/L revenue accounts they were posted to. Perfect 
for analyzing revenue by account category or reconciling invoice detail to the general ledger.

What You'll See: G/L accounts with their invoices listed underneath. Shows invoice numbers, dates, 
clients, job references, descriptions, and amounts. Subtotals by G/L account show total revenue posted 
to each account. Organized by G/L account number.

Criteria: Select which G/L accounts to include (revenue accounts typically), choose a date range or G/L 
period, filter by client or job if needed, and choose whether to include voided invoices.

Key Information: Each invoice line item is posted to a specific G/L revenue account. This report groups 
them by account so you can see what was posted where. The subtotals by account should match your G/L 
revenue postings for the period. Useful for finding posting errors or analyzing revenue mix.

When to Use This Report:
• Reconcile invoice detail to G/L revenue accounts
• Analyze revenue by account category (labour revenue, material revenue, etc.)
• Verify that invoices were posted to the correct G/L accounts
• Prepare revenue detail for financial statement analysis
• Investigate G/L account balance discrepancies
• Track revenue by business line or service type

Good to Know: At month-end, the totals on this report should tie exactly to your G/L revenue account 
postings. If they don't match, you may have invoices posted to the wrong account or G/L entries that 
didn't come from invoices. This is a key reconciliation report for your accounting close process.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by Centre in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows invoices organized by cost centre within each job. Track billing by work area and see which centres have been invoiced.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: View invoices broken down by cost centre within jobs. Great for tracking which 
work areas have been billed and analyzing revenue by cost centre.

What You'll See: Jobs with their cost centres listed underneath, showing invoices related to each 
centre. Includes invoice numbers, dates, amounts, and descriptions. Subtotals by centre show how much 
has been billed for each work area. Organized by job then by centre.

Criteria: Select specific jobs or a range, choose cost centres, filter by date range or G/L period, and 
choose whether to include voided or only outstanding invoices.

Key Information: When you invoice for work, it's typically associated with specific cost centres (work 
areas). This report shows you what's been invoiced by centre, which is useful for comparing billings to 
budgets by work area, or understanding which parts of the job have generated revenue.

When to Use This Report:
• Compare billings to budget by cost centre
• Track which work areas have been invoiced
• Analyze revenue by work area or activity type
• Verify that all completed work has been invoiced
• Review billing patterns by cost centre
• Prepare centre-level billing summaries for project managers

Good to Know: If your job costing and budgeting is organized by cost centres, this report helps you see 
the revenue side by centre. Compare this to your cost reports by centre to understand profitability at 
the work area level. Some centres might be profitable while others are losing money.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by Job in Client
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists invoices organized by job within each client. See all billing for each project and track total invoiced amounts by job.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: View invoices grouped by job within client. Perfect for tracking total billing 
by project and seeing all invoices related to specific jobs.

What You'll See: Clients with their jobs listed underneath, showing all invoices for each job. Includes 
invoice numbers, dates, descriptions, amounts, and payment status. Job subtotals show total invoiced for 
each project. Organized by client then by job.

Criteria: Select specific clients and jobs, choose date ranges or G/L periods, filter by invoice status 
(paid, outstanding, or all), and optionally include voided invoices.

Key Information: This groups invoices by project, making it easy to see total billing per job. The job 
subtotals show cumulative invoiced amounts, which you can compare to contract amounts, budgets, or costs 
to understand project performance and billing completion.

When to Use This Report:
• Review all billing for a specific project
• Track total invoiced versus contract amount by job
• Compare billing to budget on a per-project basis
• Verify that all work on a job has been invoiced
• Prepare project billing summaries for clients
• Analyze billing patterns across multiple jobs for one client

Good to Know: If you manage multiple projects for the same client, this report helps you see billing by 
project. You can quickly identify which jobs are fully invoiced, which are partially invoiced, and which 
might have unbilled work. The job subtotals are key for project financial tracking.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by Client P/O in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows invoices organized by client purchase order within jobs. Essential when clients issue multiple POs per project and require billing by PO number.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track invoicing by client purchase order number within projects. Critical when 
clients issue separate POs for different phases or portions of work and require PO-specific billing.

What You'll See: Jobs with client P/O numbers listed underneath, showing invoices related to each PO. 
Includes invoice numbers, dates, amounts, and descriptions. P/O subtotals show how much has been billed 
against each purchase order. Organized by job then by client P/O.

Criteria: Select jobs and date ranges, filter by specific client P/O numbers, choose invoice status, and 
optionally limit to invoices over certain amounts.

Key Information: Many clients issue multiple purchase orders for a single project - perhaps one PO per 
phase, change order, or funding source. This report tracks billing against each PO so you can ensure you 
don't exceed PO limits and can bill to the correct PO number. The subtotals by PO show total billed 
versus available PO amounts.

When to Use This Report:
• Track billing against multiple client POs on one project
• Ensure invoices don't exceed client PO limits
• Verify that invoices reference the correct client P/O numbers
• Compare billing to available PO balances
• Prepare PO-specific billing summaries for clients
• Identify when you're approaching PO limits and need a new PO

Good to Know: Clients often have strict controls on purchase orders and require invoices to reference 
specific PO numbers. This report helps ensure compliance with client PO requirements. If you're 
approaching a PO limit, you can see it in the subtotals and request a new PO before billing more work.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices O/S at Month End
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows which invoices were unpaid at the end of a specific G/L period. Critical for month-end close and financial reporting.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See exactly which invoices were outstanding at the end of any G/L period. 
Essential for month-end close, preparing financial statements, and historical reporting.

What You'll See: All invoices that had an outstanding balance at the end of the selected G/L 
period. Shows invoice details, original amounts, and the unpaid balance as of that period-end.

Criteria: Choose the G/L period you want to report as of (like September 2025), select which 
clients to include, and optionally filter by balance thresholds.

Key Information: This report is a point in time snapshot. Even if an invoice has been paid since 
then, if it was outstanding at the end of that period, it will appear on this report. This is 
exactly what you need for month-end closing and should match your G/L accounts receivable balance 
for that period.

When to Use This Report:
• Close your books and prepare month-end financial statements
• Reconcile accounts receivable to the general ledger for a specific period
• Prepare audit documentation showing receivables at period-end
• Answer questions about what was owed at the end of last month/quarter/year
• Compare current receivables to what was outstanding last month
• Verify historical aged receivables balances

Good to Know: Always run this as part of your month-end closing process. The total should tie to 
your accounts receivable control account in the G/L for that period. Keep copies of this report 
as part of your permanent records - you'll need them for audits and historical reference.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices GST Remittance
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Summarizes taxable sales and GST collected for tax remittance. Use this to prepare your GST/HST return and verify tax amounts.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Calculate the GST (Goods and Services Tax) you've collected on sales for 
your tax remittance reporting. Shows taxable sales and tax collected.

What You'll See: Invoices grouped by tax rate showing taxable sales amounts and the GST 
collected. Includes subtotals by tax rate (if you have different GST/HST rates) and grand totals 
for your reporting period.

Criteria: Select the date range or G/L period for your reporting period, filter by specific 
clients if needed, and choose which tax types to include (GST, HST, etc.).

Key Information: This shows the GST you collected from customers - you'll need this for the 
sales section of your GST return. Make sure the period matches your CRA reporting period 
(monthly, quarterly, or annual). The report uses invoice dates, not payment dates, since GST is 
reported on accrual basis.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare your GST/HST return for CRA (Canada Revenue Agency)
• Verify tax calculations before filing your return
• Reconcile collected GST to your G/L GST payable account
• Respond to CRA inquiries about GST collected
• Prepare documentation for your accountant at tax time
• Audit your GST calculations for accuracy

Good to Know: Run this report for each GST reporting period and keep it with your tax records. If 
you have both GST and HST transactions (different provinces), the report will break them out 
separately. Remember to also run your A/P GST reports to get the input tax credits side of the 
equation.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices PST Remittance
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Summarizes taxable sales and PST collected for provincial tax remittance. Use this for your PST return and provincial tax verification.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Calculate the PST (Provincial Sales Tax) you've collected for your 
provincial tax authority. Shows taxable sales and tax collected by province.

What You'll See: Invoices grouped by province and tax rate showing taxable sales amounts and the 
PST collected. Includes subtotals by province and tax rate, plus grand totals for your reporting 
period.

Criteria: Select the date range or G/L period for your reporting period, choose which provinces to 
include, filter by specific clients if needed, and select tax types.

Key Information: PST rates and rules vary by province - BC, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, and Quebec 
each have their own systems. This report groups sales by province so you can file separate returns 
for each. Like GST, PST reporting is typically accrual-based, using invoice dates not payment 
dates.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare PST returns for provincial tax authorities
• File separate returns for each province where you collected PST
• Verify provincial tax calculations before filing
• Reconcile collected PST to your G/L PST payable accounts
• Respond to provincial tax authority inquiries
• Prepare documentation for year-end tax filings

Good to Know: Each province has different reporting frequencies and thresholds. Make sure you know 
your filing requirements for each province where you do business. Keep these reports with your tax 
records - provincial audits can go back several years.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by Invoice Number
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists invoices in invoice number sequence. Simple, straightforward listing useful for finding specific invoices or reviewing invoice activity chronologically.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See invoices listed in invoice number order. Simple and straightforward - useful 
for locating specific invoice numbers or reviewing all invoice activity in sequence.

What You'll See: Invoices listed in invoice number sequence showing client, job, date, description, 
amounts, and payment status. Since invoice numbers are typically assigned chronologically, this gives you 
a time-ordered view of billing activity.

Criteria: Enter a range of invoice numbers (from/to), or select date ranges, G/L periods, clients, or 
jobs to limit the list. Choose whether to include voided or paid invoices.

When to Use This Report:
• Look up details for a specific invoice number
• Review all invoices in a number range
• Find missing invoice numbers in a sequence
• Verify invoice numbering is sequential
• Get a chronological view of billing activity
• Research invoices when you only have an invoice number

Good to Know: This is the simplest invoice report - just a straight list by invoice number. Use it when 
you need to find a specific invoice quickly or when other groupings (by client, job, etc.) aren't 
relevant. The sequential numbering makes it easy to spot gaps in your invoice sequence.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoices by Equipment
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows invoices containing equipment charges organized by equipment unit. Track which equipment has been billed and analyze equipment revenue.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See invoices that include equipment charges, organized by equipment unit. Perfect 
for tracking equipment billing and analyzing which equipment generates revenue.

What You'll See: Equipment units with their related invoices listed underneath. Shows invoice numbers, 
dates, clients, jobs, equipment hours or usage, billing rates, and amounts. Equipment subtotals show 
total revenue generated by each piece of equipment. Organized by equipment ID.

Criteria: Select specific equipment or a range, choose date ranges or G/L periods, filter by client or 
job, and choose whether to include only billed or all equipment charges.

Key Information: When you invoice for equipment usage, this report tracks it by equipment unit. The 
subtotals show total billing revenue generated by each piece of equipment. Useful for understanding 
equipment utilization, profitability, and billing patterns. Only shows equipment that was actually billed 
to customers (external billing).

When to Use This Report:
• Track billing revenue by equipment unit
• Analyze which equipment generates the most revenue
• Verify that all equipment usage was properly invoiced
• Review equipment billing rates and amounts
• Prepare equipment utilization reports for management
• Compare equipment billing to equipment costs

Good to Know: This only shows equipment that was billed externally to clients. For internal equipment 
usage within your own jobs, you'll need equipment timesheet or transfer reports. Use this report to see 
which equipment is most profitable and whether rental rates are appropriate.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Overdue Invoices
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists invoices that are past their due date and still have outstanding balances. Your collections priority list showing how many days each invoice is overdue.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Focus your collections efforts on invoices that are actually overdue. See 
exactly which invoices are late and by how many days.

What You'll See: Invoices with outstanding balances that are past their due date. Shows invoice 
number, client, date, due date, days overdue, and outstanding amount. Sorted by how long they've 
been overdue.

Criteria: Set how many days overdue qualifies as late (like 30 days), filter by client, choose 
minimum balance amounts to focus on larger items, or select specific date ranges.

Key Information: Days overdue is calculated from the invoice due date (invoice date + payment 
terms) to today. An invoice 60 days overdue is more urgent than one that's 10 days overdue. The 
report helps you prioritize your collection calls - start with the oldest and largest balances 
first.

When to Use This Report:
• Make your daily or weekly collection call list
• Prioritize which clients to contact about late payments
• Identify seriously delinquent accounts (90+ days)
• Monitor collection performance and payment trends
• Decide which accounts might need to go to collections
• Report on overdue receivables to management

Good to Know: This report is more action-oriented than the aged reports because it focuses on 
actual due dates, not G/L periods. An invoice could be current in the aged report but still be 
overdue if the payment terms expired. Use this for collections, use the aged reports for financial 
reporting.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Payments by Client
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows all payment receipts organized by client. See when clients paid, how much, and which invoices the payments were applied to.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track payment history by client showing when they paid you and how those 
payments were applied to their invoices.

What You'll See: For each client, all payment receipts with payment dates, amounts, reference 
numbers (like check numbers), and which invoices each payment was applied against. Organized by 
client name or code.

Criteria: Select specific clients or a range, choose a date range for payments, filter by G/L 
period, select payment method (check, wire transfer, etc.), or filter by payment amount 
thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Research when and how a client made payments
• Verify that payments were applied to the correct invoices
• Answer client questions about their payment history
• Track payment patterns and timing for specific clients
• Locate a specific payment by check number or reference
• Prepare documentation for payment disputes or research

Good to Know: This is the payment side of the story - use it with invoice reports to see the 
complete picture. If a client says they paid an invoice but you show it as outstanding, this 
report will show whether the payment exists and how it was applied. Sometimes payments get 
misapplied to the wrong invoice!

reportTrainingRecords.name: Payments by G/L Period
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows payment receipts organized by G/L accounting period. Essential for month-end reconciliation and cash receipts reporting.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See all payments you received during specific G/L periods. Critical for 
month-end close, cash receipts reconciliation, and financial reporting.

What You'll See: All payment receipts grouped by the G/L period they were posted in. Shows 
payment dates, clients, amounts, references, and which invoices were paid. Subtotals by period and 
grand totals.

Criteria: Select which G/L periods to include (like September-November 2025), filter by client, 
choose payment methods, or set minimum payment amounts.

Key Information: The G/L period shown is when the payment was posted to accounting, which might be 
different from when the check was dated or when you deposited it. This is the official period for 
financial reporting. The total should match your cash receipts in the G/L for that period.

When to Use This Report:
• Reconcile cash receipts to the general ledger each month
• Verify that all payments are properly posted to the right period
• Prepare month-end cash receipts documentation
• Track cash flow by accounting period
• Research payments posted in a specific month
• Provide payment detail for financial statement preparation

Good to Know: Always run this as part of month-end close. The total payments shown should tie 
exactly to your G/L cash receipts account for the period. If they don't match, you have a posting 
error or reconciliation issue to investigate. Keep this report with your monthly close 
documentation.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Payments by Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows payment receipts organized by project/job. Track which jobs have received payments and monitor project cash flow.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See payment receipts broken down by job/project. Great for understanding 
project cash flow and which jobs are getting paid versus which are outstanding.

What You'll See: Payments grouped by job showing payment dates, clients, amounts, references, and 
invoice applications. Job totals show how much cash each project has brought in.

Criteria: Select specific jobs or a range, choose a date range for payments, filter by G/L period, 
select clients, or filter by job status (active, completed, etc.).

When to Use This Report:
• Monitor cash flow on specific projects
• Track payment timing and patterns by job
• Provide payment information to project managers
• Compare payments received to amounts invoiced by project
• Identify jobs where payments are lagging behind billing
• Review payment history before closing out a project

Good to Know: This is especially useful for project-based businesses where you need to track cash 
by job. If a job has high billing but low payments, you might have a collections issue on that 
specific project. Compare this to invoice reports by job to see your complete project financial 
picture.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Payments by Client Invoice
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows payment receipts with full detail of which specific invoices each payment was applied to. Perfect for verifying payment applications.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See the complete detail of how payments were applied to invoices. Shows 
the connection between each payment and the specific invoices it paid.

What You'll See: Each payment with a breakdown showing exactly which invoices it was applied to 
and how much went to each invoice. Shows payment references, dates, client names, invoice numbers, 
and application amounts.

Criteria: Select clients, date ranges, G/L periods, specific invoice numbers, or payment 
references to research. Filter by minimum amounts or payment methods.
