Key Information: This shows payment application detail - when a client sends one check but pays 
multiple invoices, this report shows the split. If they send a partial payment, you can see 
exactly which invoice(s) it was applied against. Essential for researching payment application 
questions.

When to Use This Report:
• Research how a specific payment was applied to invoices
• Answer client questions about payment applications
• Verify that payments were applied correctly
• Investigate payment disputes or misapplications
• Train staff on proper payment application procedures
• Audit payment processing for accuracy

Good to Know: When investigating payment issues, this is often the most detailed report you need. 
It shows not just that a payment was received, but exactly where that money went. If a client says 
they paid invoice #12345 but you show it as outstanding, this report will show whether their 
payment was misapplied to a different invoice.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Client Statements
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Creates professional statements showing unpaid invoices for each client. Use the Email button to automatically send personalized statements with your company branding.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate and email professional statements to clients showing their 
outstanding invoices and account balance. This is your standard monthly billing statement process.

What You'll See: For each client, a formatted statement listing all open (unpaid) invoices with 
dates, invoice numbers, descriptions, and amounts due. Shows current balance and aging (30/60/90+ 
days). The statement includes your company logo and branding (or formats for letterhead if you 
prefer).

Criteria: Select which clients should receive statements, set a statement date (usually month-end), 
choose whether to include zero-balance clients, and set minimum balance thresholds if desired.

Key Information: When you click the Email button, the system automatically breaks out individual 
statements for each client, attaches them as PDFs, and sends personalized emails using the contact 
information from each client record. The email includes your company logo, a professional template, 
and customizes the greeting with the client contact's name. You can also print statements instead 
of emailing them.

When to Use This Report:
• Send monthly statements to all clients with outstanding balances
• Email statements for specific clients who request them
• Create year-end or quarter-end customer statements
• Mail printed statements as part of your collections process
• Provide account summaries when clients ask for their balance
• Send gentle payment reminders before making collection calls

Good to Know: Most companies send statements monthly - it's a gentle reminder to clients about 
outstanding invoices. The Email button does all the work - it splits the report by client, creates 
individual PDFs, and sends personalized emails with your branding. Some clients won't pay until 
they receive a statement, even if they have the invoices. Make sure your client contact email 
addresses are current!

reportTrainingRecords.name: Financial Dashboard
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Executive financial dashboard showing key financial metrics and KPIs at a glance. Visual snapshot of financial health and performance.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display executive financial dashboard with key metrics, KPIs, and visual indicators. Provides at-a-
glance financial health snapshot. Essential for executive financial monitoring and decision-making.

What You'll See: Comprehensive financial dashboard showing: (1) A/R Ageing - aging buckets and collection status, (2) A/P 
Ageing - payment obligations by age, (3) Cash Position - current cash and trends, (4) Committed Costs - P/O commitments and 
exposure, (5) Unextracted Activity - pending transactions not yet in G/L, (6) Key Ratios - current ratio, debt levels, WIP, 
(7) Trends - graphs showing financial trends over time. Visual presentation with charts, gauges, and traffic light indicators 
(green/yellow/red) for problem areas. Single-page executive view of financial status.

Criteria: Select as-of date for dashboard, choose company or consolidated view, set thresholds for traffic light indicators 
(e.g., over 90 days = red), and choose time period for trends (30/60/90 days).

Key Information: The financial dashboard is an executive tool showing financial health at a glance. Key elements:

• A/R Ageing: Shows collection status - how much is current, 30/60/90+ days old. Red flags indicate aged receivables 
requiring collection action.

• A/P Ageing: Shows payment obligations - what is due now, what is coming due. Helps cash flow planning.

• Cash Position: Current cash balance and trend. Critical for liquidity monitoring.

• Committed Costs: P/O commitments not yet invoiced - future cash obligations. Important for cash flow forecasting.

• Unextracted Activity: Transactions recorded but not yet posted to G/L - affects accuracy of financial reports.

• Financial Ratios: Current ratio (current assets / current liabilities), debt ratios, WIP levels - indicators of financial 
health.

• Trends: Graphs showing how metrics are moving - improving or deteriorating.

Traffic light indicators highlight problems: Green = healthy, Yellow = attention needed, Red = immediate action required. 
Essential for executives to monitor financial performance without reading detailed reports.

When to Use This Report:
• Daily/weekly executive financial monitoring
• Quick financial health checks
• Board presentations and executive meetings
• Identify financial issues requiring attention
• Track financial KPIs and trends
• Support data-driven financial decisions

Good to Know: Review this daily or weekly. Red indicators require immediate attention. Trends are as important as current 
numbers - is cash increasing or decreasing? Drill down into specific reports for details on problem areas. Keep unextracted 
activity low for accurate financial reporting. Essential executive tool for financial oversight and proactive management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Unextracted A/P Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows A/P invoices and labour not yet extracted to G/L. Identify pending transactions affecting financial accuracy and completeness.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display A/P invoices and payroll that have been recorded but not yet extracted (posted) to the General 
Ledger. Identify pending transactions affecting financial accuracy. Essential for G/L completeness and month-end close.

What You'll See: Unextracted A/P invoices and payroll transactions showing amounts, dates entered, days unextracted, G/L 
periods, vendors/employees, and reasons not yet extracted. Highlights old unextracted items requiring action. Shows impact on 
G/L accuracy. Organized by age or G/L period.

Criteria: Select date ranges and G/L periods, set aging thresholds (e.g., over 30 days), filter by vendors or types, and 
choose detail level.

Key Information: Extraction posts transactions from subsidiary ledgers (A/P, P/R) to the General Ledger. Unextracted 
transactions create timing differences - they exist in A/P or payroll but not yet in G/L. This causes: (1) Incomplete G/L 
balances, (2) Inaccurate financial statements, (3) Reconciliation issues, (4) Month-end close delays. Common reasons for 
delay: awaiting approval, coding errors, missing information, batch errors. This report identifies pending items so they can 
be extracted. Essential for G/L accuracy and timely financial close.

When to Use This Report: Run before month-end close, identify delayed extractions requiring action, support G/L reconciliation, 
ensure financial statement completeness, track extraction timing and delays, and prepare for period close.

Good to Know: Extract regularly (daily or weekly) to keep current. Unextracted items over 30 days indicate problems. Extract 
everything before month-end close for accurate financials. Essential for G/L accuracy and timely closes.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Unextracted Labour Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows labour/timesheets not yet extracted to G/L. Identify pending payroll transactions affecting job costs and G/L accuracy.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display labour timesheets recorded but not yet extracted (posted) to General Ledger. Identify pending 
payroll affecting job costs and G/L. Essential for complete job costing and G/L accuracy. Similar to Unextracted A/P but 
specifically for labour. Use to ensure timely labour extraction, support month-end close, maintain job cost accuracy, verify 
labour G/L completeness, and track extraction delays.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Unextracted Ageing Schedule
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows aging of unextracted A/P transactions. Track how long transactions have been pending extraction to prioritize processing.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display aging schedule of unextracted A/P showing how long transactions have been pending. Prioritize 
extraction processing based on age. Shows unextracted A/P in aging buckets (current, 30, 60, 90+ days old) to highlight 
extraction delays. Use to prioritize old unextracted items, track extraction timeliness, support month-end extraction push, 
and identify chronic extraction delays.

reportTrainingRecords.name: A/R Ageing By Company
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows A/R aging by company. Analyze receivables aging and collection status by company for multi-company management.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display A/R aging organized by company showing receivables aging across the organization. Analyze 
collection status by company. Essential for multi-company receivables management. Shows aging buckets (current, 30, 60, 90+ 
days) by company with totals and trends. Use to compare collection performance across companies, identify companies with aging 
issues, support consolidated collections management, track company-level collection KPIs, and prepare aging reports by company.

reportTrainingRecords.name: A/R Ageing By Client
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows A/R aging by client. Identify clients with aging receivables requiring collection action.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display A/R aging by client showing which clients have aged receivables. Identify collection problems 
and prioritize collection efforts. Essential for targeted collections management.

What You'll See: Clients with aging detail showing current and aged amounts (30, 60, 90+ days), total outstanding, aging 
percentages, and payment patterns. Highlights problem clients with significant aged balances. Organized by client with aging 
breakdown.

Criteria: Select as-of G/L period, choose clients, set aging buckets (30/60/90 or custom), filter by aging thresholds, and 
choose detail level.

When to Use This Report: Prioritize collection efforts by client, identify problem accounts requiring attention, support 
collection calls and follow-up, track client payment performance, prepare for credit decisions, and focus on worst aging first. 

Good to Know: Clients with over 60% in 90+ days are collection problems. Focus collection efforts on largest aged amounts for 
best impact. Use with payment performance reports. Essential for effective collections management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: A/R Ageing By Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows A/R aging by job. Analyze receivables aging by project for job-level collections management.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display A/R aging by job showing receivables aging at the project level. Track collections by job. 
Essential for project-based collections management. Shows aging by job with client detail, useful when project managers are 
responsible for collections. Use to track job-level collection performance, identify jobs with aging issues, support project 
manager collection accountability, analyze aging patterns by job type, and prepare job aging reports.

reportTrainingRecords.name: A/P Committed Cost Schedule
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows A/P committed costs (P/O commitments not yet invoiced). Track future payment obligations and cash flow exposure.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display A/P committed costs showing P/O commitments not yet invoiced. Track future payment obligations. 
Essential for cash flow forecasting and exposure management.

What You'll See: P/Os with committed amounts not yet invoiced showing vendors, jobs, P/O amounts, amounts invoiced to date, 
remaining commitments, expected invoice timing, and total exposure. Shows future cash obligations from existing commitments. 
Organized by vendor, job, or due date.

Criteria: Select as-of date, choose jobs or vendors, set minimum commitment thresholds, filter by expected timing, and choose 
detail level.

Key Information: Committed costs = P/O amounts not yet invoiced. When you issue a P/O, you commit to pay - even though no 
invoice yet. These become future cash obligations. This report shows: (1) Total committed exposure, (2) When invoices will 
come (cash flow timing), (3) Which jobs have significant commitments, (4) Vendor exposure (how much committed to each). 
Essential for cash flow forecasting and managing exposure.

When to Use This Report: Forecast future cash needs, track P/O commitment exposure, support cash flow planning, identify jobs 
with high commitments, manage vendor payment exposure, and prepare commitment reports for management.

Good to Know: Committed costs become invoices and then payments. Large commitments require cash planning. Track commitment-to-
budget ratios on jobs. Essential for proactive cash flow management and avoiding cash shortfalls.

reportTrainingRecords.name: A/P Vendor Cost Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows costs by vendor over time. Analyze spending patterns and vendor relationships for cost management.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display costs by vendor over time showing spending patterns. Analyze vendor relationships and spending. 
Essential for vendor management and cost analysis.

What You'll See: Vendors with spending detail showing amounts by period, trends, year-over-year comparisons, payment terms, 
and spending patterns. Shows which vendors receive the most spending and how spending changes over time. Organized by vendor 
with trend analysis.

Criteria: Select vendors and date ranges, choose time period grouping (monthly, quarterly), set minimum spending thresholds, 
and choose detail level.

When to Use This Report: Analyze vendor spending patterns, support vendor negotiations (volume discounts), identify cost 
reduction opportunities, track vendor relationships, prepare for vendor reviews, and compare spending across vendors.

Good to Know: High-volume vendors may qualify for better pricing. Use spending patterns in vendor negotiations. Track spending 
concentration - too much with one vendor creates risk. Essential for strategic vendor management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Invoice Turnover Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows A/R invoice turnover metrics (how quickly invoices are collected). Measure collection effectiveness and cash conversion efficiency.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display A/R invoice turnover metrics showing how quickly invoices are collected. Measure collection 
effectiveness and days sales outstanding (DSO). Essential for cash flow and collections performance analysis.

What You'll See: Turnover metrics showing: (1) Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) - average days to collect, (2) Invoice-to-Cash 
cycle time, (3) Collection efficiency, (4) Turnover ratio (sales / receivables), (5) Trends over time, (6) Comparisons by 
client, job, or company. Shows how efficiently you convert invoices to cash. Lower DSO = faster collection = better cash flow. 
Organized by period with trend analysis.

Criteria: Select date ranges, choose calculation methods, set benchmark targets (e.g., DSO < 45 days), filter by clients or 
jobs, and choose detail level.

Key Information: DSO (Days Sales Outstanding) = Average days from invoice to payment. Construction average: 60-75 days. Lower 
is better - faster collection improves cash flow. Turnover ratio = Annual revenue / Average A/R balance. Higher is better - 
means collecting faster. Track trends - improving or deteriorating? Compare to industry benchmarks. Use to measure collection 
effectiveness and set improvement goals. Essential for cash flow optimization.

When to Use This Report: Measure collection performance, track DSO and turnover trends, benchmark against industry standards, 
identify improvement opportunities, support collection process improvements, and prepare cash flow reports.

Good to Know: Reducing DSO by 10 days can significantly improve cash flow. Track monthly to catch trends early. Compare to 
competitors and industry. Essential for optimizing working capital and cash flow.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Group Counts and Hours
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows workforce counts and hours grouped by various dimensions (company, union, trade, level, province). Flexible labour analytics dashboard.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display workforce counts and hours with flexible grouping options. Analyze labour statistics by 
company, union, trade, apprentice level, or province. Essential for comprehensive labour analytics and workforce planning.

What You'll See: Workforce statistics grouped by selected dimension showing employee counts, total hours, hours by type 
(straight time, overtime, premium), average hours per employee, and trends over time. Flexible dashboard report that can 
group by: (1) Company/Book - workforce by company, (2) Union - workforce by union affiliation, (3) Trade/Craft - workforce by 
occupation, (4) Level - workforce by apprentice level, (5) Province - workforce by work location. Shows detail or summary 
based on selection. Organized by chosen grouping dimension.

Criteria: Choose grouping dimension (company, union, trade, level, province), select date ranges, filter by additional 
criteria (jobs, specific groups, etc.), set detail level (summary or detail), and choose time period grouping (daily, weekly, 
monthly).

Key Information: This is a flexible dashboard report that adapts based on your grouping selection:

• Group by Company/Book: Shows workforce statistics by company - how many employees, total hours, and trends by company. Use 
for comparing workforce size and activity across companies.

• Group by Union: Shows workforce statistics by union affiliation - workforce size, hours, and activity by union. Use for 
union workforce tracking and union relations.

• Group by Trade/Craft: Shows workforce statistics by occupation/trade - how many of each trade, total hours, and utilization 
by skill set. Use for workforce planning by trade and understanding skill mix.

• Group by Level: Shows workforce statistics by apprentice level (1st year, 2nd year, journeyman, etc.) - workforce 
composition by experience level. Use for apprenticeship program tracking and skill level analysis.

• Group by Province: Shows workforce statistics by work location/province - where employees are working geographically. Use 
for regional workforce analysis and compliance reporting (like interprovincial labour tracking).

The report provides both summary (counts and totals only) and detail (with employee lists) views. Detail views show which 
specific employees are in each group. Essential for flexible labour analytics and workforce intelligence.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze workforce statistics from multiple perspectives
• Track workforce counts and hours by various dimensions
• Support workforce planning and resource allocation
• Compare workforce metrics across groups
• Prepare labour statistics and analytics reports
• Create workforce dashboards and KPI tracking
• Support union, apprenticeship, and compliance reporting

Good to Know: This is your flexible labour analytics tool - one report that can show workforce statistics grouped many 
different ways. Change the grouping to analyze different aspects of your workforce. Use summary view for high-level metrics 
and trends. Use detail view when you need to see which specific employees are in each group. Compare time periods to track 
workforce growth or contraction. Essential dashboard tool for workforce intelligence and data-driven labour management. Run 
regularly to track workforce KPIs and trends.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Termination Counts
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows termination counts and statistics (also called ROE counts). Track workforce terminations and turnover for reporting and analysis.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display termination counts and statistics (Records of Employment - ROE data). Track workforce 
terminations, turnover rates, and termination patterns. Essential for turnover analysis and ROE compliance reporting.

What You'll See: Termination statistics showing terminated employee counts, termination dates, termination reasons (quit, 
layoff, dismissal, end of contract, etc.), hours worked before termination, ROE information, and trends over time. Can be 
grouped by company, union, trade, termination reason, or time period. Shows termination patterns and turnover rates. Organized 
by selected grouping with termination detail.

Criteria: Select date ranges for terminations, choose grouping dimension (company, union, trade, reason), filter by 
termination types or reasons, set time period groupings (weekly, monthly), and choose detail level.

Key Information: Records of Employment (ROE) must be issued when employees are terminated. This report tracks terminations for 
ROE processing and turnover analysis. Shows: (1) Who was terminated and when, (2) Why they were terminated (reason codes), 
(3) How many hours they worked (for ROE insurable hours), (4) Termination patterns and trends. Essential for:

• ROE Compliance: Tracking who needs ROEs and ensuring they are issued within required timeframes (typically 5 days)
• Turnover Analysis: Understanding termination rates, patterns, and reasons across the organization
• Workforce Planning: Identifying retention issues and high-turnover areas requiring attention
• Cost Management: High turnover creates recruiting, training, and productivity costs

Termination reasons typically include: Quit (voluntary), Layoff (lack of work), Dismissal (performance/conduct), End of 
Contract (temporary/project end), Retirement. Different reasons have different implications for unemployment insurance and 
company costs. Essential for HR compliance and workforce stability management.

When to Use This Report:
• Track terminations for ROE processing and compliance
• Analyze turnover rates and patterns
• Identify retention issues by company, union, or trade
• Review termination reasons and trends
• Support workforce planning and retention strategies
• Prepare termination and turnover reports for management
• Calculate turnover costs and impact

Good to Know: High turnover rates (over 30-40% annually in construction) indicate retention problems and cost money in 
recruiting and training. Track termination reasons - high voluntary quits may indicate compensation or work environment 
issues, while high layoffs indicate work volume problems. Seasonal terminations (end of construction season) are normal. Use 
this regularly to monitor workforce stability and ensure timely ROE processing. ROEs must be issued within 5 calendar days of 
termination or last pay period - late ROEs result in penalties. Essential for HR compliance and workforce management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Residence Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows employees by residence location (city, province). Track where employees live for local hire requirements and travel planning.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display employees organized by residence location showing where employees live. Track employee home 
locations for local hire requirements, travel planning, and regional workforce analysis. Essential for local hire compliance 
and workforce demographics.

What You'll See: Employees grouped by residence location (city, province, postal code) showing employee counts, names, trades, 
companies, current job assignments, and distance from work sites. Shows where employees live geographically. Can be grouped by 
province, city, or proximity to specific locations. Organized by geographic location with employee detail.

Criteria: Choose grouping (province, city, postal code), select job sites for distance calculations, filter by companies or 
trades, set distance thresholds (e.g., local = within 50 km), and choose detail level.

Key Information: Employee residence information is important for several reasons:

• Local Hire Requirements: Many projects (especially government or community benefit agreements) require hiring local 
residents. This report shows which employees qualify as local (typically within 50-75 km of project). Essential for proving 
local hire compliance.

• Travel and Per Diem: Employees living far from work sites may be entitled to travel allowances, per diems, or camp 
accommodations. Distance from home determines travel costs and entitlements.

• Workforce Demographics: Understanding where employees live helps with recruitment, retention (long commutes cause turnover), 
and workforce planning (can we staff remote projects?).

• Regional Workforce Analysis: Shows labor pool by region. Helps identify where to recruit and where workforce is concentrated.

• Emergency Contact: In emergencies, knowing employee locations helps with communication and family notifications.

The report can calculate distances from job sites to show which employees are "local"  versus "out of town." Essential for 
local hire compliance, travel cost management, and workforce demographics.

When to Use This Report:
• Verify local hire requirements and compliance
• Calculate travel allowances and per diems based on distance
• Analyze workforce by residence location
• Support recruitment in specific geographic areas
• Plan accommodations for out-of-town workers
• Prepare local hire reports for clients or government
• Review commute distances and retention risks

Good to Know: Local hire requirements vary by project - typically 50-75 km radius qualifies as "local". Some agreements 
require specific percentages of local hires (e.g., 30% of workforce must be local residents). Update employee addresses 
regularly to keep this accurate. Long commutes (over 1 hour each way) increase turnover - consider this in retention planning. 
Remote projects may require camps or travel rotations for out-of-town workers. Essential for local hire compliance and 
workforce planning.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Rental Agreements by Job in Client
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows rental agreements for equipment organized by job within client. Track rental commitments and agreements by project and client.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display equipment rental agreements organized by client and job. Track rental commitments, 
agreement terms, rates, and rental periods for equipment. Essential for managing rental agreements by project and 
client.

What You'll See: Clients with their jobs listed underneath, showing equipment rental agreements for each job. Displays 
equipment details, rental vendors, agreement start and end dates, rental rates, terms, and total rental commitments. 
Shows active and upcoming rental agreements. Organized by client, then job, then equipment.

Criteria: Select clients and jobs, choose date ranges for agreement periods, filter by rental vendors or equipment 
types, and set agreement status (active, upcoming, all).

When to Use This Report:
• Track rental commitments by client and job
• Review rental agreements for specific projects
• Plan equipment rental costs by job
• Support client billing for rental equipment
• Manage rental vendor relationships by project
• Prepare rental documentation for clients

Good to Know: Rental agreements commit you to rental costs for specific periods. Organizing by client and job helps 
track which rentals are for which projects. Use this to plan rental costs, bill clients for rental equipment, and 
ensure rental periods align with job schedules. Essential for managing external equipment rentals by project.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Rental Agreements Coming Due
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows rental agreements expiring soon or coming due for renewal. Proactively manage agreement renewals, extensions, or returns.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display equipment rental agreements expiring soon or coming due for renewal. Identify rental 
agreements requiring action (renewal, extension, or return) before expiry. Essential for proactive rental agreement 
management.

What You'll See: Rental agreements with approaching end dates showing equipment, rental vendors, current agreement 
terms, expiry dates, days until expiry, and rental rates. Highlights agreements expiring soon or already expired. Can 
show agreements in expiry order. Organized by expiry date with agreement detail.

Criteria: Set expiry window (e.g., expiring in next 60 days), filter by jobs or equipment types, choose warning 
thresholds (e.g., warn at 45 days, urgent at 15 days), and optionally include already expired agreements.

When to Use This Report:
• Identify rental agreements expiring soon
• Plan renewals, extensions, or equipment returns
• Avoid unexpected rental agreement lapses
• Contact rental vendors about upcoming expirations
• Coordinate equipment needs with rental periods
• Prevent automatic renewals if equipment no longer needed

Good to Know: Run this monthly to catch expiring rental agreements early. Gives time to decide whether to renew, 
extend, or return equipment. Some agreements auto-renew unless you give notice (often 30-60 days). If equipment is no 
longer needed, coordinate return to avoid unnecessary rental costs. Proactive management prevents unwanted renewals 
and ensures equipment availability when needed.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Equipment List
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists all equipment with descriptions and basic information. Simple equipment directory for reference and documentation.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate a simple list of all equipment with descriptions and basic details. Essential 
reference document for equipment codes and organization.

What You'll See: All equipment listed with equipment codes, descriptions, equipment types, makes, models, status 
(active, inactive, etc.), current locations (job or yard), and basic details. Simple directory without detailed 
financial or usage information. Organized by equipment code, type, or location.

Criteria: Filter by equipment status (active, inactive, all), choose equipment types or categories, select current 
locations, and pick sort order (by code, description, type, or location).

When to Use This Report:
• Create equipment code reference documentation
• Train staff on equipment organization and codes
• Verify equipment setup and descriptions
• Quick equipment code lookup for timesheets
• Export equipment directory for other uses
• Review active and inactive equipment

Good to Know: This is the simplest equipment report - just a directory with basic information. Use for training and 
reference. For detailed financial or usage information, use specialized equipment reports. Keep this handy for 
equipment code reference and quick lookups.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Equipment Activity
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists equipment transfers and timesheets in chronological and logical order. Shows incoming, job/yard/exchange, timesheets, then outgoing in sequence.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display complete equipment activity showing transfers and timesheets in chronological and 
logical order. Tracks equipment movement and usage with proper sequencing. Essential for understanding equipment flow 
and activity.

What You'll See: Equipment with chronological activity showing transfers and timesheets in logical sequence. On each 
day, displays: (1) incoming transfers first, (2) job/yard/exchange movements, (3) usage timesheets, (4) outgoing 
transfers last. Shows complete audit trail of where equipment went and what it did. Organized by equipment in date 
order with logical sequencing.

Criteria: Select equipment and date ranges, choose activity types to include (transfers, timesheets, all), filter by 
locations (jobs, yards), and set detail level.

Key Information: The logical sequencing is critical - on the same day, incoming transfers happen before usage, and 
usage happens before outgoing transfers. This creates an accurate timeline of equipment activity. Shows: transfer-in 
from yard to job, work on job (timesheets), transfer-out from job back to yard. Essential for tracking equipment 
utilization and movement.

When to Use This Report:
• Track complete equipment activity and movement
• Audit equipment transfers and usage
• Verify equipment location history
• Investigate equipment utilization patterns
• Support equipment billing and cost tracking
• Create equipment activity documentation

Good to Know: The logical daily sequence (incoming, then job activity, then timesheets, then outgoing) ensures the 
activity timeline makes sense. Equipment cannot be used before it arrives or after it leaves. This report creates an 
accurate audit trail showing exactly where equipment went and what work it did. Essential for equipment management 
and utilization tracking.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Equipment by Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows equipment currently assigned to or working on each job. Track equipment allocation and deployment by project.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display equipment organized by job showing which equipment is assigned to or working on each 
project. Track equipment allocation and deployment. Essential for job equipment management.

What You'll See: Jobs with equipment currently on each job showing equipment descriptions, types, makes, models, 
ownership (owned, rented, client-supplied), arrival dates, and usage status. Shows which equipment is deployed where. 
Organized by job with equipment detail.

Criteria: Select jobs, choose as-of date (current or historical), filter by equipment types or ownership, and set 
detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Review equipment currently on each job
• Track equipment allocation by project
• Verify equipment deployment matches needs
• Support job mobilization and demobilization
• Create job equipment inventories
• Plan equipment movement between jobs

Good to Know: Shows current equipment deployment by job. Use this to understand which equipment is where and whether 
jobs have the equipment they need. Helps identify over-equipped or under-equipped jobs. Essential for equipment fleet 
management and ensuring efficient equipment utilization across projects.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Equipment by Yard
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows equipment currently at each yard or storage location. Track yard inventory and equipment availability.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display equipment organized by yard showing which equipment is at each yard or storage 
location. Track yard inventory and equipment availability. Essential for yard equipment management.

What You'll See: Yards with equipment currently at each location showing equipment descriptions, types, makes, models, 
ownership, arrival dates, and availability status. Shows which equipment is available versus committed. Organized by 
yard with equipment detail.

Criteria: Select yards, choose as-of date, filter by equipment types or availability status, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Review equipment inventory by yard
• Identify available equipment for mobilization
• Track yard equipment capacity and storage
• Support equipment allocation decisions
• Create yard inventory documentation
• Verify equipment returns to yards

Good to Know: Shows which equipment is sitting in yards and available for deployment. Use this to find available 
equipment when jobs need it. Helps prevent unnecessary rentals when owned equipment is available in a yard. Essential 
for yard management and maximizing equipment utilization.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Equipment by Owner & Operator
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows equipment organized by owning company and operating company. Track equipment ownership and cross-company usage.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display equipment organized by owning company and operating company. Track equipment ownership 
and cross-company usage. Essential for multi-company equipment fleet management.

What You'll See: Owning companies with equipment they own, showing which companies are currently operating that 
equipment. Displays equipment details, ownership, current operator, locations, and usage. Shows equipment owned by one 
company but used by another. Organized by owning company then operating company.

Criteria: Select owning companies, filter by operating companies, choose equipment types, and set as-of date.

When to Use This Report:
• Track equipment ownership by company
• Identify cross-company equipment usage
• Support intercompany equipment billing
• Manage shared equipment across companies
• Review equipment utilization by owner and operator
• Calculate equipment ownership costs by company

Good to Know: In multi-company organizations, equipment owned by one company may be used by another. This report tracks 
ownership versus operation, essential for intercompany equipment charges and shared fleet management. Use for equipment 
sharing across divisions or companies.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Equipment by Rate Group
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows equipment organized by rate group. Track billing rates and organize equipment by rate categories.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display equipment organized by rate group. Track billing rates and organize equipment by rate 
categories. Essential for rate management and billing organization.

What You'll See: Rate groups with equipment in each group showing equipment details, billing rates (hourly, daily, 
weekly, monthly), rate effective dates, and current assignments. Groups equipment by similar rates for billing and 
cost purposes. Organized by rate group with equipment detail.

Criteria: Select rate groups, choose as-of date for rates, filter by equipment types, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Review equipment organized by billing rates
• Verify rate group assignments
• Support rate updates and management
• Create rate schedules for clients
• Organize equipment by billing categories
• Analyze equipment rates and pricing

Good to Know: Rate groups organize equipment with similar rates for easier billing and rate management. Instead of 
setting individual rates for every piece of equipment, you assign equipment to rate groups. Use this to verify rate 
group assignments and create rate schedules.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Equipment Renewals
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows renewal dates for equipment inspections, insurances, and licenses. Track upcoming renewals to maintain compliance.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display equipment with upcoming renewal dates for inspections, insurance policies, licenses, 
and permits. Track renewals to maintain compliance and avoid lapses. Essential for equipment compliance management.

What You'll See: Equipment with renewal items showing renewal types (annual inspection, insurance, license plate, 
permits, etc.), current expiry dates, renewal due dates, and days until renewal. Highlights items expiring soon or 
already expired. Organized by equipment with renewal detail or by renewal date.

Criteria: Set renewal date window (e.g., due in next 90 days), filter by renewal types, choose equipment or locations, 
set warning thresholds, and optionally include expired items.

Key Information: Equipment requires periodic renewals for compliance and safety. Annual inspections verify equipment is 
safe. Insurance must stay current. Licenses and permits must be renewed. Expired renewals can ground equipment or 
create legal liability. This report provides early warning to schedule renewals before expiry. Essential for compliance 
and keeping equipment legally operational.

When to Use This Report:
• Identify equipment renewals coming due
• Schedule inspections before expiry dates
• Renew insurance policies and licenses on time
• Maintain equipment compliance and legality
• Prevent equipment downtime from expired renewals
• Plan renewal costs and budgets

Good to Know: Run this monthly to catch upcoming renewals. Give yourself 60-90 days for inspections (they book up). 
Expired inspections ground equipment - it cannot legally work. Expired insurance creates massive liability exposure. 
Expired licenses result in fines. Proactive renewal management prevents these problems and keeps equipment working 
legally and safely.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Equipment Inventory
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows equipment inventory with SKU, make, model, serial numbers, and license plates. Complete equipment identification and tracking information.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display complete equipment inventory with identification details including SKU, make, model, 
serial numbers, and license plates. Essential for equipment tracking and identification.

What You'll See: Equipment with complete identification details showing SKU codes, manufacturers, models, serial 
numbers, VIN numbers, license plate numbers, year of manufacture, and other identifying information. Complete equipment 
inventory with all tracking details. Organized by equipment type or SKU.

Criteria: Select equipment types, filter by makes or models, choose current locations, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Create complete equipment inventory documentation
• Track equipment by serial numbers and VINs
• Support equipment insurance and registration
• Verify equipment identification details
• Prepare equipment lists for audits
• Export inventory for asset management

Good to Know: This is your complete equipment identification inventory. SKUs, serial numbers, and VINs uniquely 
identify equipment. License plates track registered vehicles. Use this for insurance documentation, registration, 
theft reporting, and asset management. Essential reference document for equipment fleet.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Equipment First 6 Months
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows fiscal year opening balance and first 6 months of rental costs by equipment. Track equipment costs for first half of fiscal year.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display equipment rental costs for the first six months of the fiscal year. Shows opening 
balances and monthly or accumulated rental costs. Essential for equipment cost tracking and reconciliation.

What You'll See: Equipment with fiscal year opening balances, then rental costs by month for the first six months 
(months 1-6 of fiscal year). Shows either current month costs or accumulated to-date costs. Equipment subtotals show 
total costs through month 6. Organized by equipment with monthly detail.

Criteria: Select equipment and fiscal year, choose reporting mode (current month or accumulated to-date), filter by 
equipment types, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Track equipment rental costs for first half of year
• Reconcile equipment costs to G/L for months 1-6
• Review monthly equipment cost trends
• Support month-end close for equipment
• Analyze equipment cost patterns by period
• Prepare first-half equipment cost documentation

Good to Know: Similar to job first 6 months report but for equipment. The fiscal year is split into two 6-month 
reports for manageability. Use with Last 6 Months report for complete fiscal year. Essential for equipment cost 
tracking and G/L reconciliation.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Equipment Last 6 Months
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows opening balance at end of first six months and last 6 months of rental costs by equipment. Track equipment costs for second half of fiscal year.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display equipment rental costs for the last six months of the fiscal year. Shows opening 
balance at month 7 and monthly or accumulated rental costs. Essential for equipment cost tracking and reconciliation.

What You'll See: Equipment with opening balance at end of month 6 (from first 6 months), then rental costs by month 
for the last six months (months 7-12 of fiscal year). Shows either current month costs or accumulated to-date costs. 
Equipment subtotals show total costs through year-end. Organized by equipment with monthly detail.

Criteria: Select equipment and fiscal year, choose reporting mode (current month or accumulated to-date), filter by 
equipment types, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Track equipment rental costs for second half of year
• Reconcile equipment costs to G/L for months 7-12
• Review monthly equipment cost trends
• Support year-end close for equipment
• Analyze equipment cost patterns by period
• Prepare second-half equipment cost documentation

Good to Know: Covers months 7-12 of fiscal year. Opening balance is from First 6 Months report. Use both reports for 
complete fiscal year equipment costs. Essential for equipment cost tracking and G/L reconciliation.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Equipment Costs and Revenue
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows A/P costs, A/R revenues, and journal entries for equipment over a G/L period range. Analyze equipment profitability and cost recovery.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display equipment costs and revenues over a G/L period range. Shows A/P costs (rental expenses, 
repairs, fuel), A/R revenues (billings to jobs), and journal entries. Analyze equipment profitability and cost 
recovery. Essential for equipment financial analysis.

What You'll See: Equipment with costs and revenues showing A/P costs (rentals, maintenance, fuel, repairs), A/R 
revenues (billings to jobs for equipment usage), journal entries, and calculated net profit or loss (revenue minus 
cost). Shows whether equipment is profitable or losing money. Organized by equipment with financial detail.

Criteria: Select equipment and G/L period range, filter by equipment types or jobs, choose detail level (summary or 
transaction detail), and set minimum thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze equipment profitability over time
• Verify equipment revenues cover costs
• Identify equipment losing money
• Support equipment ownership decisions
• Calculate equipment ROI and cost recovery
• Review equipment financial performance

Good to Know: Equipment should generate more revenue (billings to jobs) than costs (rentals, maintenance, fuel). This 
report shows the financial reality. Owned equipment with high maintenance costs may not be profitable. Rented equipment 
must generate enough billable hours to cover rental costs. Essential for equipment ownership and rental decisions.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheets by Equipment
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows equipment timesheets organized by equipment. Track usage hours, costs, and billing by individual piece of equipment.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display equipment timesheets organized by equipment showing usage hours, costs, and billings. 
Track how each piece of equipment is being used. Essential for equipment utilization and cost tracking.

What You'll See: Equipment with timesheet detail showing dates, jobs, centres, operators, hours worked, equipment 
costs, and billing amounts. Equipment subtotals show total hours and costs per piece. Shows how much each piece of 
equipment worked and where. Organized by equipment with timesheet detail.

Criteria: Select equipment and date ranges, filter by jobs or centres, choose detail level, and set minimum hour 
thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Track equipment usage hours by piece
• Analyze equipment utilization and productivity
• Verify equipment timesheets and billing
• Calculate equipment cost recovery
• Support equipment maintenance scheduling
• Review equipment deployment effectiveness

Good to Know: Shows where each piece of equipment worked and how many hours. Use to calculate equipment utilization 
(worked hours versus available hours). Low utilization means equipment is sitting idle. High utilization means 
equipment is productive. Essential for equipment fleet management and utilization analysis.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheets by Centre in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows equipment timesheets organized by centre within job. Track equipment usage by work element for cost allocation.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display equipment timesheets organized by centre within job. Track equipment usage by work 
element for accurate cost allocation. Essential for job cost equipment tracking.

What You'll See: Jobs with centres listed underneath, showing equipment timesheets for each centre. Displays equipment 
used, hours worked, costs, and billing amounts by centre. Centre subtotals show total equipment costs per work element. 
Organized by job and centre with equipment detail.

Criteria: Select jobs and centres, choose date ranges, filter by equipment types, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Track equipment costs by work element
• Allocate equipment usage to centres
• Compare equipment costs to budgets by centre
• Support job cost equipment analysis
• Verify equipment is charged to correct centres
• Review centre equipment consumption

Good to Know: Equipment usage gets charged to centres for job costing. This shows which centres consumed which 
equipment. Use to track equipment costs by work element and verify costs are allocated correctly. Essential for 
accurate job cost equipment tracking.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheets by Equipment in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows equipment timesheets organized by equipment within job. Track which equipment worked on each job and total usage.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display equipment timesheets organized by equipment within job. Track which equipment worked on 
each job and total usage. Essential for job equipment cost tracking.

What You'll See: Jobs with equipment listed underneath, showing timesheets for each piece of equipment on that job. 
Displays dates, hours, costs, and billing amounts by equipment. Equipment subtotals show total usage per piece on each 
job. Organized by job and equipment with timesheet detail.

Criteria: Select jobs, choose date ranges, filter by equipment or equipment types, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Track equipment usage by job
• Review which equipment worked on each project
• Calculate job equipment costs by piece
• Support job equipment cost analysis
• Verify job equipment charges
• Compare equipment deployment to job needs

Good to Know: Shows which equipment worked on each job and how much. Use to understand job equipment consumption and 
costs. Helps identify over-equipped or under-equipped jobs. Essential for job equipment management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheets by Client P/O
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows equipment timesheets organized by client P/O. Track equipment usage by client authorization for billing and cost tracking.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display equipment timesheets organized by client P/O. Track equipment usage by client 
authorization for billing and cost tracking. Essential for P/O-based equipment billing.

What You'll See: Client P/Os with equipment timesheets showing equipment used, hours worked, costs, and billing amounts 
by P/O. P/O subtotals show total equipment charges per authorization. Shows equipment consumption against client P/Os. 
Organized by client P/O with equipment detail.

Criteria: Select client P/Os and jobs, choose date ranges, filter by equipment types, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Track equipment usage by client P/O
• Prepare P/O-based equipment billing
• Monitor equipment charges against P/O limits
• Show clients equipment detail by their P/O
• Support P/O equipment cost management
• Verify P/O equipment allocations

Good to Know: When work is organized by client P/Os, this shows equipment consumption by authorization. Use to track 
equipment charges against P/O budgets and prepare P/O-based billing. Essential for cost-plus and T&M work with 
equipment charges.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Equipment Time Entry Sheets
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Prints blank equipment timesheet forms for field data collection. Field crews record equipment usage hours on these forms.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate blank equipment timesheet forms for field data collection. Provides pre-printed forms 
that field crews fill out to record equipment usage hours. Essential for field equipment time tracking.

What You'll See: Blank equipment timesheet forms showing equipment lists, date fields, hour fields, and job/centre 
coding fields. Forms can be pre-populated with expected equipment on each job. Field crews write in hours worked and 
other details. Organized by job or date for field collection.

Criteria: Select jobs and date ranges, choose which equipment to include on forms, set form layout (daily, weekly), 
and choose pre-population options.

When to Use This Report:
• Create timesheet forms for field crews
• Provide standardized forms for equipment time recording
• Support field equipment tracking processes
• Enable consistent equipment time data collection
• Facilitate weekly or daily equipment time entry
• Give field crews pre-printed timesheet forms

Good to Know: This is a physical form (paper or tablet) for field collection. Field crews record equipment usage hours, 
then someone enters the data into the system. Pre-printed forms with expected equipment make data collection easier and 
more consistent. Essential for reliable field equipment time tracking.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Equipment without Timesheets
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows equipment on jobs that have no timesheets for the period. Identify missing equipment time entries and unbilled usage.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display equipment on jobs that have no timesheets for the selected period. Identify missing 
equipment time entries and potentially unbilled equipment usage. Essential for timesheet compliance and billing 
completeness.

What You'll See: Equipment that is assigned to jobs but has no timesheets for the selected period. Shows equipment 
details, current job assignments, and timesheet gaps. Highlights potential missing time entries or equipment sitting 
idle. Organized by job or equipment.

Criteria: Select date ranges, choose jobs, filter by equipment types, and set minimum gap thresholds (e.g., no 
timesheet for 7+ days).

Key Information: Equipment on a job should have timesheets showing usage. Missing timesheets mean: (1) data entry is 
incomplete (forgot to enter time), (2) equipment is idle (sitting unused), or (3) equipment has been removed but 
transfer not recorded. This report identifies these situations. Missing timesheets can result in unbilled equipment 
usage (lost revenue) or inaccurate job costs.

When to Use This Report:
• Identify missing equipment timesheets
• Ensure complete equipment time entry
• Find unbilled equipment usage
• Identify idle equipment on jobs
• Support timesheet compliance and completeness
• Verify equipment transfers and assignments

Good to Know: Run this weekly to catch missing timesheets. Equipment on jobs should be working and have timesheets. 
Missing timesheets mean lost billing or incomplete data. If equipment is truly idle, consider moving it to another job. 
Essential for billing completeness and equipment utilization.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Equipment External Billings Preview
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows preview of equipment billings to external clients for selected job and date. Calculate billable equipment charges before invoicing.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display preview of equipment billings to external clients for a specific job and date ceiling. 
Calculate billable equipment charges before creating invoices. Essential for equipment billing verification.

What You'll See: Equipment with billable usage showing equipment details, hours or units worked, billing rates, and 
calculated billing amounts for external client invoicing. Preview what will be billed before actually creating invoices. 
Organized by equipment with billing detail.

Criteria: Select job and date ceiling (bill up to this date), choose billing rates or rate schedules, filter by 
equipment or clients, and set minimum billing thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Preview equipment billings before invoicing
• Verify equipment billing amounts and rates
• Calculate total equipment charges for period
• Support external client equipment billing
• Review billable equipment usage before invoicing
• Prepare equipment billing documentation

Good to Know: External billings are to clients (versus internal billings between jobs or companies). This preview shows 
what equipment charges will be invoiced to clients. Review this before creating actual invoices to verify amounts and 
catch errors. Essential for accurate client equipment billing.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Weekly Timesheet Audit
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows weekly timesheet information and reports suspicious or missing data. Identify equipment timesheet errors, gaps, and anomalies.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Audit equipment timesheets for a week identifying suspicious patterns, missing data, and 
potential errors. Report anomalies for investigation and correction. Essential for equipment timesheet quality control.

What You'll See: Weekly equipment timesheet data with flagged anomalies including: equipment with excessive hours 
(more than possible in a day/week), missing timesheets for assigned equipment, duplicate entries, unusual patterns, and 
data quality issues. Highlights suspicious or questionable timesheet data for review. Organized by issue type or 
equipment.

Criteria: Select week or date range, choose jobs, set audit thresholds (e.g., flag if more than 24 hours in a day), 
and filter by issue types.

Key Information: Audit flags potential timesheet errors: excessive hours (equipment cannot work 30 hours in a day), 
missing data (equipment on job but no timesheet), inconsistencies (transferred out but still has timesheets), and 
unusual patterns. These issues indicate data entry errors, fraud, or process problems. Essential for timesheet data 
quality and billing accuracy.

When to Use This Report:
• Audit weekly equipment timesheets for errors
• Identify suspicious or impossible timesheet data
• Find missing equipment time entries
• Support timesheet quality control processes
• Investigate timesheet anomalies before billing
• Ensure timesheet data accuracy and completeness

Good to Know: Run this weekly before processing payroll or billing. Catches obvious errors like 30-hour days or missing 
timesheets. Fixing errors before billing prevents invoice corrections and client disputes. Some anomalies indicate 
fraud or intentional misreporting. Essential for timesheet data integrity and billing accuracy.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Transfers by Transfer No
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows equipment transfers organized by transfer number. Track individual transfer transactions in sequential order.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display equipment transfers organized by transfer number. Track individual transfer transactions 
in sequential order. Essential for transfer documentation and audit trail.

What You'll See: Transfers in transfer number order showing equipment moved, transfer dates, from locations (job or 
yard), to locations, transfer reasons, who authorized the transfer, and confirmation status (received or pending). 
Complete transfer transaction detail in sequential order. Organized by transfer number.

Criteria: Select transfer number ranges, choose date ranges, filter by transfer types or statuses, and set detail 
level.

When to Use This Report:
• Review transfer transactions in sequential order
• Verify specific transfer details by transfer number
• Create transfer documentation and audit trail
• Support transfer investigations and research
• Track transfer volume and activity
• Prepare transfer reports by period

Good to Know: Transfer numbers create sequential transaction records for equipment movements. Use this to review transfer 
history in order or look up specific transfer details. Essential for transfer audit trail and documentation.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Transfers by Equipment
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows transfers organized by equipment. Track movement history for each piece of equipment showing where it went and when.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display transfers organized by equipment showing complete movement history for each piece. Track 
where equipment went and when. Essential for equipment location history and utilization tracking.

What You'll See: Equipment with transfer history showing dates, from locations, to locations, transfer numbers, reasons, 
and confirmation status. Complete movement history for each piece showing everywhere it has been. Organized by equipment 
in chronological transfer order.

Criteria: Select equipment and date ranges, filter by locations or transfer types, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Review complete movement history by equipment
• Track where equipment has been deployed
• Analyze equipment utilization patterns
• Verify equipment location history
• Support equipment tracking and accountability
• Create equipment movement documentation

Good to Know: Shows everywhere a piece of equipment has been. Use to track equipment deployment history, understand 
utilization patterns (how often it moves between jobs), and verify current location. Essential for equipment fleet 
management and location tracking.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Transfers by Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows transfers organized by job. Track equipment movements to and from each job showing mobilization and demobilization.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display transfers organized by job showing equipment movements to and from each job. Track 
mobilization and demobilization activity. Essential for job equipment movement tracking.

What You'll See: Jobs with transfer activity showing equipment transferred in, transferred out, dates, from/to locations, 
transfer numbers, and confirmation status. Shows mobilization (transfers in) and demobilization (transfers out) for each 
job. Organized by job with transfer detail.

Criteria: Select jobs and date ranges, filter by transfer direction (in, out, all), choose equipment types, and set 
detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Track equipment mobilization to jobs
• Review equipment demobilization from jobs
• Analyze job equipment movement patterns
• Support job mobilization planning
• Verify equipment transfers to/from jobs
• Create job equipment movement documentation

Good to Know: Shows equipment flowing to and from jobs. Use to track job mobilization (equipment arriving) and 
demobilization (equipment leaving). Helps coordinate equipment needs with job schedules. Essential for job equipment 
management and mobilization planning.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Transfers by Yard
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows transfers organized by yard. Track equipment movements to and from each yard showing arrivals and departures.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display transfers organized by yard showing equipment movements to and from each yard. Track 
arrivals and departures from yard locations. Essential for yard equipment movement tracking.

What You'll See: Yards with transfer activity showing equipment transferred in, transferred out, dates, from/to locations, 
transfer numbers, and confirmation status. Shows arrivals (transfers in) and departures (transfers out) for each yard. 
Organized by yard with transfer detail.

Criteria: Select yards and date ranges, filter by transfer direction (in, out, all), choose equipment types, and set 
detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Track equipment arrivals at yards
• Review equipment departures from yards
• Analyze yard equipment flow patterns
• Support yard capacity and logistics planning
• Verify equipment returns to yards
• Create yard movement documentation

Good to Know: Shows equipment flowing to and from yards. Use to track yard activity (equipment coming and going) and 
manage yard inventory levels. Helps coordinate equipment storage and deployment. Essential for yard equipment management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job Equipment Inventory
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows current equipment inventory on each job based on transfers. Calculate current job equipment holdings from transfer activity.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display current equipment inventory on each job calculated from transfer activity. Shows which 
equipment is currently assigned to each job based on transfers in and out. Essential for job equipment inventory 
management.

What You'll See: Jobs with current equipment inventory showing equipment currently on each job, arrival dates, days on 
job, and equipment details. Calculated from transfers - equipment transferred in and not yet transferred out is on the 
job. Current inventory snapshot based on transfer history. Organized by job with equipment detail.

Criteria: Select jobs and as-of date (current or historical), filter by equipment types or ownership, and set detail 
level.

Key Information: Job equipment inventory is calculated from transfers. Equipment transferred to a job and not yet 
transferred out is currently on that job. This provides current equipment holdings by job. Different from Equipment by 
Job report which may use different logic - this one is strictly transfer-based. Essential for job equipment inventory 
tracking based on documented transfers.

When to Use This Report:
• Review current equipment inventory by job
• Calculate job equipment holdings from transfers
• Verify equipment location based on transfer records
• Support job equipment management
• Create job equipment inventory snapshots
• Reconcile equipment locations to transfers

Good to Know: This inventory is transfer-based - shows equipment that has been formally transferred to jobs and not yet 
transferred out. If transfers are not recorded promptly, inventory may be inaccurate. Use this to verify transfer records 
match physical equipment locations. Essential for transfer-based equipment tracking.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Yard Equipment Inventory
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows current equipment inventory at each yard based on transfers. Calculate current yard equipment holdings from transfer activity.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display current equipment inventory at each yard calculated from transfer activity. Shows which 
equipment is currently at each yard based on transfers in and out. Essential for yard equipment inventory management.

What You'll See: Yards with current equipment inventory showing equipment currently at each yard, arrival dates, days at 
yard, and equipment details. Calculated from transfers - equipment transferred in and not yet transferred out is at the 
yard. Current inventory snapshot based on transfer history. Organized by yard with equipment detail.

Criteria: Select yards and as-of date (current or historical), filter by equipment types or ownership, and set detail 
level.

Key Information: Yard equipment inventory is calculated from transfers. Equipment transferred to a yard and not yet 
transferred out is currently at that yard. This provides current equipment holdings by yard. Different from Equipment by 
Yard report which may use different logic - this one is strictly transfer-based. Essential for yard equipment inventory 
tracking based on documented transfers.

When to Use This Report:
• Review current equipment inventory by yard
• Calculate yard equipment holdings from transfers
• Verify equipment location based on transfer records
• Support yard equipment management and capacity planning
• Create yard equipment inventory snapshots
• Reconcile equipment locations to transfers

Good to Know: This inventory is transfer-based - shows equipment that has been formally transferred to yards and not yet 
transferred out. If transfers are not recorded promptly, inventory may be inaccurate. Use this to verify transfer records 
match physical equipment at yards. Essential for transfer-based yard inventory tracking.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Equipment Internal Billings Preview
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows internal billing preview for equipment between jobs or companies to a specified date ceiling. Calculate intercompany equipment charges before billing.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display preview of internal equipment billings between jobs or companies for a specific job to a 
date ceiling. Calculate intercompany or inter-job equipment charges before creating internal billings. Essential for 
internal equipment billing verification.

What You'll See: Equipment with internal billable usage showing equipment details, hours or days, internal billing rates, 
and calculated internal billing amounts. Preview what will be billed internally before creating actual internal invoices. 
Shows equipment charges between jobs or between companies in the organization. Organized by equipment with billing detail.

Criteria: Select job and date ceiling (bill up to this date), choose internal billing rates or rate schedules, filter by 
equipment or owning/using companies, and set minimum billing thresholds.

Key Information: Internal billings are between jobs or between companies within the organization (versus external billings 
to clients). When equipment owned by one company is used by another company, or when equipment on one job is used by 
another job, internal billing allocates costs. This preview shows calculated charges before creating internal invoices. 
Essential for intercompany equipment cost allocation.

When to Use This Report:
• Preview internal equipment billings before invoicing
• Verify intercompany equipment billing amounts and rates
• Calculate internal equipment charges for period
• Support intercompany equipment cost allocation
• Review internal billable equipment usage
• Prepare internal billing documentation

Good to Know: Internal billings allocate equipment costs within the organization - between divisions, companies, or jobs. 
Different from external billings which are to clients. Review this preview before creating internal invoices to verify 
amounts. Essential for intercompany equipment cost allocation and shared equipment management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Unconfirmed Transfers
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows list of unconfirmed transfers with blank received field. Identify transfers that have not been confirmed as received at destination.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display transfers that have not been confirmed as received (blank received field). Identify 
transfers pending confirmation at destination. Essential for transfer completion and equipment location accuracy.

What You'll See: Transfers with blank received field showing equipment transferred, transfer dates, from locations, to 
locations, transfer numbers, and days pending confirmation. Highlights transfers that were sent but not confirmed as 
received at destination. Organized by transfer date or equipment.

Criteria: Select date ranges, filter by jobs, yards, or equipment, set minimum pending days (e.g., unconfirmed for 7+ 
days), and choose detail level.

Key Information: Equipment transfers have two steps: (1) transfer out from origin (sent), (2) transfer in at destination 
(received). Unconfirmed transfers have been sent but not confirmed as received. This creates uncertainty about equipment 
location. Equipment may be: in transit, lost, received but not confirmed, or transferred incorrectly. Unconfirmed 
transfers must be investigated and resolved. Essential for equipment location accuracy and accountability.

When to Use This Report:
• Identify transfers pending confirmation
• Follow up on unconfirmed equipment receipts
• Investigate potentially lost or misdirected equipment
• Ensure transfer completion and documentation
• Support equipment location accuracy
• Maintain transfer accountability and control

Good to Know: Run this regularly (weekly) to catch unconfirmed transfers. Transfers unconfirmed for more than a few days 
indicate problems - equipment may be lost or transfers not properly documented. Follow up immediately to locate equipment 
and confirm receipt. Essential for equipment accountability and preventing lost equipment. Require receiving confirmation 
within 24-48 hours of transfer.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Account List
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists all general ledger accounts with descriptions and types. Your master chart of accounts directory for reference.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate a complete list of all G/L accounts in your chart of accounts. Essential 
reference document for account numbers, descriptions, and account types.

What You'll See: All G/L accounts listed with account numbers, full descriptions, account types (asset, 
liability, equity, revenue, expense), and account status (active/inactive). Can show balances if desired. 
Organized by account number or by account type.

Criteria: Select specific accounts or ranges, filter by account type (assets, liabilities, revenue, expenses), 
choose active only or include inactive, and optionally include current balances.

When to Use This Report:
• Create a chart of accounts reference document
• Verify account numbers and descriptions
• Train new accounting staff on the account structure
• Audit chart of accounts setup and organization
• Export account list for other systems or reports
• Review account types and classifications

Good to Know: This is your chart of accounts reference. Keep an updated copy for training and reference. When 
adding new accounts, review this to maintain consistent numbering and naming conventions. Inactive accounts 
still appear in history but can't be used for new transactions.

reportTrainingRecords.name: First 6 Months Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows account balances for fiscal year opening and the first 6 months. Essential for mid-year financial reporting and G/L reconciliation.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display account balances for the fiscal year opening and first 6 months (months 1-6). 
Critical for mid-year close and reconciling the G/L to subsidiary ledgers.

What You'll See: Accounts with opening balance (start of fiscal year), then monthly activity and balances for 
months 1 through 6. Shows debits, credits, and ending balance for each month. Ending balance at month 6 becomes 
the opening balance for the Last 6 Months report. Organized by account number.

Criteria: Select accounts or ranges, filter by account type, choose whether to suppress zero-balance accounts, 
and set detail level (summary or full monthly detail).

Key Information: This breaks the fiscal year in half for reporting. The first 6 months report covers months 1-6 
with opening balance from year start. The ending balance at month 6 ties to the opening balance on the Last 6 
Months report. Together they give you the complete fiscal year. Essential for mid-year close and G/L 
reconciliation.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare mid-year financial close and reporting
• Reconcile G/L to subsidiary ledgers for first 6 months
• Review first-half-year account activity and balances
• Support mid-year audits with monthly detail
• Analyze account trends through first 6 months
• Verify opening balances for second half of year

Good to Know: Always run both First 6 Months and Last 6 Months together - the month 6 ending balance on this 
report must equal the opening balance on the Last 6 Months report. If they don't tie, you have a data integrity 
issue. Useful for monthly G/L close reconciliation.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Last 6 Months Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows account balances for last 6 months with opening balance from end of month 6. Completes the fiscal year when combined with First 6 Months report.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display account balances for the second half of the fiscal year (months 7-12). Opening 
balance is the ending balance from month 6. Essential for year-end close and full-year reconciliation.

What You'll See: Accounts with opening balance (end of month 6), then monthly activity and balances for months 
7 through 12. Shows debits, credits, and ending balance for each month. Final month 12 balance is your fiscal 
year-end balance. Organized by account number.

Criteria: Select accounts or ranges, filter by account type, choose whether to suppress zero-balance accounts, 
and set detail level (summary or full monthly detail).

Key Information: This completes the fiscal year. Opening balance should match the ending balance from month 6 on 
the First 6 Months report. The ending balance at month 12 is your fiscal year-end balance. Together with First 
6 Months, these reports give you complete fiscal year activity. Critical for year-end close and G/L to 
subsidiary ledger reconciliation.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare year-end financial close and reporting
• Reconcile G/L to subsidiary ledgers for last 6 months
• Review second-half-year account activity and balances
• Support year-end audits with monthly detail
• Verify year-end closing balances
• Analyze account trends through last 6 months

Good to Know: Always verify the opening balance ties to month 6 ending on First 6 Months report. Run both reports 
at year-end for complete year documentation. The month 12 ending balance becomes next year's opening balance. 
Essential for monthly and annual G/L reconciliation processes.
