reportTrainingRecords.name: Account Activity Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows detailed transactions for accounts in a period with opening and closing balances. Your primary account detail and reconciliation report.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display all transaction detail for selected accounts in a specific period. Shows opening 
balance, every transaction, and closing balance. Essential for account analysis and reconciliation.

What You'll See: Accounts with opening balance, followed by all transactions (date, description, reference, 
debits, credits, running balance), and closing balance. Each transaction shows where it came from (payroll, A/P, 
A/R, J/E, etc.). Full drill-down detail for complete transaction traceability. Organized by account number.

Criteria: Select accounts and date ranges or G/L periods, filter by transaction source (A/P, A/R, payroll, J/E), 
choose transaction types, and set minimum transaction amounts.

Key Information: This is your primary account detail report. Every line shows a transaction with full context - 
where it came from, what it was for, and how it affected the account balance. The running balance helps you see 
account movement over time. Opening plus activity equals closing - if it doesn't, you have a problem.

When to Use This Report:
• Research account activity and specific transactions
• Reconcile account balances to supporting detail
• Investigate account variances or unexpected balances
• Trace transactions back to source documents
• Support month-end close with account detail
• Prepare account reconciliations for audits

Good to Know: This is your go-to report for researching account activity. When someone asks 
"whats in this account?" or "where did this balance come from?" , this report answers those questions. 
The transaction source tells you which module to look in for supporting detail.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Activity Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows detailed transactions by employee for accounts in a period. Track employee-specific expenses and activity with opening and closing balances.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display transaction detail organized by employee within accounts. Essential for tracking 
employee-specific expenses, advances, and activity.

What You'll See: Accounts with employees listed underneath, showing all transactions for each employee. Includes 
opening balance, transaction detail (dates, descriptions, amounts), and closing balance by employee. Shows which 
employees generated activity in each account. Organized by account then by employee.

Criteria: Select accounts and date ranges, choose specific employees or all, filter by transaction types, and set 
minimum transaction or balance thresholds.

Key Information: Some accounts track employee-specific activity - advances, expenses, loans, etc. This report 
breaks account activity down by employee so you can see each person's transactions and balance. Useful for 
employee advance tracking, expense analysis, and employee-specific account reconciliation.

When to Use This Report:
• Track employee advances and repayments
• Analyze employee-specific expense accounts
• Review employee activity in specific G/L accounts
• Reconcile employee-related balances
• Research transactions by specific employees
• Support employee expense reporting and analysis

Good to Know: Not all accounts have employee detail - this is most useful for accounts that track employee-
specific balances. Common examples: employee advances, employee loans, employee expense accounts, or employee-
specific benefits. The employee breakdown helps you see who's driving the account balance.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Account Budget Variances Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Compares actual G/L account costs to budget. Shows budget, actual, variance amounts and percentages for performance analysis.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Compare actual G/L account activity to budget. Shows where you're over or under budget 
with variance amounts and percentages. Essential for budget monitoring and financial control.

What You'll See: Accounts with budget amounts, actual amounts, variance (actual minus budget), and variance 
percentage. Can show monthly, year-to-date, or both. Variances highlighted to show over-budget (unfavorable) and 
under-budget (favorable) accounts. Organized by account number or by variance amount.

Criteria: Select accounts or ranges, choose reporting period (monthly, YTD, or both), filter by account type, 
set variance thresholds to highlight significant differences, and choose variance sort order.

Key Information: Budget variance is calculated as Actual minus Budget. Positive variance on expense accounts means 
over budget (unfavorable). Negative variance means under budget (favorable). For revenue accounts it's reversed - 
positive variance is good (over revenue target). The variance percentage shows the magnitude of the difference 
relative to budget.

When to Use This Report:
• Monthly budget reviews and variance analysis
• Identify accounts significantly over or under budget
• Monitor financial performance against plan
• Prepare management reports on budget compliance
• Support corrective action decisions when over budget
• Track year-to-date budget performance

Good to Know: Run this monthly to stay on top of budget performance. Large variances require investigation - 
either the budget was wrong or spending is off track. Some variance is normal, but consistent over-budget 
performance on key accounts needs attention. Use variance % to identify the most significant issues.

reportTrainingRecords.name: J/Es by Entry Number
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists journal entries in entry number sequence. Quick way to find specific entries or verify sequential numbering of journal entries.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See journal entries listed in entry number order. Locate specific entries, verify 
sequential numbering, and track journal entry usage.

What You'll See: Journal entries in entry number sequence showing entry dates, G/L periods, descriptions, 
account detail (debits and credits), and entry totals. Each entry shows all accounts affected with amounts. 
Sequential numbering makes it easy to spot missing or voided entries. Organized by entry number.

Criteria: Enter entry number ranges (from/to), filter by date ranges or G/L periods, choose entry status 
(posted, unposted, voided), and select specific entry types if applicable.

When to Use This Report:
• Look up details for specific entry numbers
• Verify sequential journal entry numbering
• Find missing entry numbers in sequence
• Research entries when you only have an entry number
• Audit journal entry completeness and sequence
• Prepare journal entry registers for documentation

Good to Know: This is the simplest J/E report - just a straight list by entry number. Use it when other groupings 
(by period, account, job) aren't relevant. Sequential numbering helps identify gaps that might indicate missing 
or deleted entries. Each entry must balance - debits equal credits.

reportTrainingRecords.name: J/Es by G/L Period
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows journal entries grouped by G/L period. Essential for month-end review and G/L period reconciliation of manual entries.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See journal entries organized by the G/L period they were posted in. Critical for 
month-end close, reviewing period activity, and G/L reconciliation.

What You'll See: Journal entries grouped by G/L period, showing entry numbers, dates, descriptions, account 
detail (debits and credits), and totals. Period subtotals show total debits and credits posted each period. 
Each entry must balance. Organized by G/L period then by entry number.

Criteria: Select which G/L periods to include, filter by entry date ranges, choose entry status (posted, 
unposted, voided), and select specific entry types or sources.

Key Information: The G/L period shown is when the entry was posted to accounting. Journal entries are manual 
adjustments to the G/L - corrections, accruals, reclassifications, etc. This report shows all manual activity 
by period. Essential for understanding what manual adjustments were made and verifying month-end entries.

When to Use This Report:
• Review all journal entries posted in a specific period
• Verify month-end adjusting entries are complete
• Prepare month-end journal entry documentation
• Audit manual G/L adjustments by period
• Research what entries were made during month-end close
• Support financial statement preparation with entry detail

Good to Know: Run this at month-end to review all manual entries before finalizing. Keep copies with month-end 
documentation. Journal entries are where you make accruals, corrections, and adjustments - this shows what was 
adjusted. Auditors will want to see this for manual entries.

reportTrainingRecords.name: J/Es by G/L Account
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows journal entries organized by G/L account. See all manual entries that affected specific accounts for analysis and research.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See journal entries grouped by the accounts they affected. Track manual adjustments to 
specific accounts and research account activity from journal entries.

What You'll See: Accounts with their journal entry activity listed underneath. Shows entry numbers, dates, 
descriptions, and amounts (debits or credits) for each entry affecting that account. Account subtotals show 
total journal entry activity by account. Organized by account number.

Criteria: Select accounts or ranges, choose date ranges or G/L periods, filter by entry types or sources, and 
set minimum transaction amounts.

When to Use This Report:
• Research journal entry activity in specific accounts
• See what manual adjustments were made to an account
• Track recurring journal entries by account
• Analyze patterns of manual adjustments
• Verify account adjustments during month-end close
• Support account reconciliation with entry detail

Good to Know: This shows only journal entry activity - transactions from other modules (A/P, A/R, payroll) won't 
appear here. Useful when you know manual adjustments were made to an account and want to see them all. Common 
uses: reviewing accrual entries, depreciation entries, or reclassification entries by account.

reportTrainingRecords.name: J/Es by Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows journal entries organized by job. Track manual G/L adjustments to specific jobs for job costing and project accounting.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See journal entries grouped by the jobs they affected. Track manual adjustments to job 
costs and revenues through journal entries.

What You'll See: Jobs with their journal entry activity listed underneath. Shows entry numbers, dates, 
descriptions, accounts affected, and amounts for each entry impacting that job. Job subtotals show total journal 
entry activity by job. Organized by job number.

Criteria: Select jobs or ranges, choose date ranges or G/L periods, filter by accounts or entry types, and set 
minimum transaction amounts.

Key Information: Many journal entries affect jobs - accruing WIP, adjusting costs, reclassifying expenses, 
recording retainage, etc. This report shows all manual G/L adjustments to each job. Important for understanding 
what manual adjustments were made to job costs or revenues beyond normal transactions.

When to Use This Report:
• Research manual adjustments to specific jobs
• Track WIP accruals and adjustments by job
• Verify month-end job costing entries
• Review job cost corrections or reclassifications
• Support job cost audits with manual entry detail
• Analyze patterns of job adjustments

Good to Know: Common job-related journal entries include: WIP accruals, revenue recognition adjustments, cost 
reclassifications between jobs, retainage adjustments, and job close-out entries. This report shows those 
manual adjustments organized by job for easy review.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job Revenue Analysis
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Analyzes revenue versus costs using centre revenue mappings. Verify that revenue centres have appropriate margins over their mapped cost centres.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Analyze the relationship between cost centres and their mapped revenue centres. Verify that 
revenue amounts appropriately exceed cost amounts based on target margins. Essential for margin verification and 
revenue/cost alignment on jobs.

What You'll See: Cost centres with their mapped revenue centres showing costs posted to cost centres, revenue posted 
to corresponding revenue centres, calculated margins (revenue minus cost), and margin percentages. Shows whether 
revenue centres have appropriate markup over their related cost centres. Includes both regular transactions and 
intercompany transactions (between companies in your system). Can include detail by transaction source (A/P invoices, 
labour, A/R invoices, journal entries). Organized by job and centre with margin calculations.

Criteria: Select jobs and date ranges, filter by cost centres or revenue centres, set target margin thresholds to 
highlight variances, choose detail level (summary or transaction detail), and optionally show only centres with 
margin issues.

Key Information: Cost centres can be mapped to revenue centres on the centre entry screen (mappings section). This 
links cost-side work (labour, materials, subcontracts) to revenue-side billing. The report compares costs in cost 
centres to revenue in their mapped revenue centres. If targeting 10% margin, revenue should be 10% more than costs. 
Margin percentage = (Revenue minus Cost) divided by Cost. Handles both regular transactions and intercompany 
transactions (where one company bills another company in your system). Intercompany transactions require proper 
revenue code mappings to match costs on one side with revenue on the other. Essential for verifying billing covers 
costs plus target margin.

When to Use This Report:
• Verify revenue centres have appropriate margins over cost centres
• Ensure billing amounts cover costs plus target markup
• Identify revenue/cost mismatches or margin shortfalls
• Support margin management and pricing verification
• Analyze revenue versus cost relationships by job
• Validate that cost-to-revenue mappings are working correctly

Good to Know: The revenue mapping system connects cost work to revenue billing at the centre level. You set up the 
mappings once in centre entry (bottom of screen), then this report verifies the relationship. If revenue centre has 
$110K and its mapped cost centre has $100K, that is 10% margin - exactly what you want. If revenue is only $105K, 
margin is only 5% - you are under-billing. For intercompany work (one company billing another company in your 
system), vendors and clients must have intercompany G/L accounts set up, and the report validates that revenue codes 
are properly mapped to match costs with revenue across companies. Essential for ensuring billing captures costs plus 
profit on both regular and intercompany work.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Balance Sheet
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Produces the balance sheet showing assets, liabilities, and equity. Your primary financial position statement at a point in time.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate the balance sheet - the financial statement showing what you own (assets), what 
you owe (liabilities), and net worth (equity) at a specific date. Fundamental financial statement.

What You'll See: Assets section (current assets, fixed assets, other assets), Liabilities section (current 
liabilities, long-term liabilities), and Equity section (capital, retained earnings, current year profit). Total 
assets must equal total liabilities plus equity. Balances shown as of the selected date. Formatted as traditional 
financial statement.

Criteria: Select the as-of date (typically period end), choose level of detail (summary or account detail), 
optionally include prior period for comparison, and choose whether to suppress zero-balance accounts.

Key Information: The balance sheet is a snapshot at a point in time showing financial position. Assets = 
Liabilities + Equity always - if not, your books don't balance. Current year profit/loss from the income 
statement flows into equity. Required for month-end close, year-end reporting, banking, bonding, and financial 
analysis.

When to Use This Report:
• Month-end and year-end financial closing and reporting
• Provide financial statements to banks, sureties, and stakeholders
• Analyze financial position and net worth
• Support loan applications and bonding requirements
• Calculate financial ratios (current ratio, debt-to-equity, etc.)
• Prepare management financial reports

Good to Know: Run this at every month-end and keep copies for your permanent records. Banks and sureties require 
it regularly. The balance sheet must balance - if assets don't equal liabilities plus equity, something is wrong 
in your G/L. Retained earnings should tie to prior year plus current year net income.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Balance Sheet - 12 Month Rolling
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows balance sheet for the last 12 months in columnar format. Track financial position trends month by month over the past year.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display balance sheet positions for the trailing 12 months. See how your financial 
position has changed over the past year month by month. Excellent for trend analysis.

What You'll See: Balance sheet accounts in rows with columns for each of the last 12 months showing ending 
balances. Assets, liabilities, and equity sections with subtotals and total balance. Shows trends in working 
capital, debt levels, and equity over time. Formatted in spreadsheet-style with month columns.

Criteria: Select the ending month (report shows prior 12 months from that date), choose level of detail, and 
optionally suppress zero-balance accounts.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze balance sheet trends over the past year
• Track working capital changes month by month
• Monitor debt levels and equity growth over time
• Identify seasonal patterns in financial position
• Prepare trend analysis for management or stakeholders
• Compare month-end positions across multiple periods

Good to Know: The 12-month rolling view helps you see patterns and trends that single-month balance sheets miss. 
Watch for consistent trends (growing debt, declining cash, increasing receivables) that might indicate issues or 
opportunities. Seasonal businesses benefit from seeing the full annual cycle.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Income Statement (EBITDA)
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Produces the income statement showing revenue, expenses, and profit/loss. Shows EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, Amortization).
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate the income statement (profit and loss) showing revenue, expenses, and net 
income. Includes EBITDA calculation. Essential financial performance statement.

What You'll See: Revenue section (sales, other revenue), Cost of Sales, Gross Profit, Operating Expenses 
(broken down by category), EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization), then 
Interest, Depreciation, and Taxes, resulting in Net Income. Shows both current period and year-to-date. 
Formatted as traditional financial statement.

Criteria: Select the reporting period, choose level of detail (summary or account detail), optionally include 
prior period comparison, and choose whether to show budget comparison.

Key Information: EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization) is a key profitability 
measure that shows operational performance before financing and accounting decisions. Many lenders and investors 
focus on EBITDA. Net income flows to retained earnings on the balance sheet. Required for month-end close, 
financial reporting, and performance analysis.

When to Use This Report:
• Month-end and year-end financial closing and reporting
• Analyze profitability and operational performance
• Provide financial statements to banks, sureties, and stakeholders
• Calculate EBITDA for lending covenants or valuations
• Review revenue and expense trends
• Support management decision-making with profit data

Good to Know: Run this monthly and keep copies for permanent records. EBITDA is often required for loan covenants 
and bonding. The net income from this statement flows to equity on the balance sheet. Review gross profit margin 
and EBITDA percentage as key performance indicators.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Income Statement - Current vs Previous Year
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Compares current year income statement to previous year same period. Shows year-over-year changes in revenue, expenses, and profitability.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Compare current period income statement to the same period last year. Shows year-over-
year growth or decline in revenue, expenses, and profit. Essential for performance trending.

What You'll See: Income statement with three columns - current year, prior year (same period), and variance 
(change from prior year). Shows revenue, expenses, and profit with year-over-year comparison and variance 
percentage. Highlights significant increases or decreases. Formatted as comparative financial statement.

Criteria: Select the current period to report (automatically pulls prior year comparison), choose level of detail, 
set variance thresholds to highlight significant changes, and choose whether to show percentages.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze year-over-year performance trends
• Identify revenue growth or decline by category
• Track expense changes year over year
• Prepare management reports on annual performance
• Support strategic planning with historical comparison
• Communicate performance to stakeholders

Good to Know: Year-over-year comparison is essential for understanding whether you're improving or declining. 
Growth in revenue is good, but watch the expense growth rate - if expenses grow faster than revenue, profit 
margins shrink. Large variances need investigation to understand causes.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Income Statement - 12 Month Rolling
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows income statement for the last 12 months in columnar format. Track revenue, expenses, and profit trends month by month over the past year.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display income statement performance for the trailing 12 months. See revenue, expense, 
and profit trends month by month over the past year. Excellent for trend analysis.

What You'll See: Income statement accounts in rows with columns for each of the last 12 months. Shows revenue, 
cost of sales, gross profit, expenses, and net income for each month. Includes totals and year-to-date 
accumulation. Formatted in spreadsheet-style with month columns showing trends.

Criteria: Select the ending month (report shows prior 12 months from that date), choose level of detail, and 
optionally suppress zero-activity accounts.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze profitability trends over the past year
• Track revenue patterns and seasonality month by month
• Monitor expense trends and identify anomalies
• Identify seasonal patterns in business performance
• Prepare trend analysis for management
• Compare monthly profit margins over time

Good to Know: The 12-month rolling view reveals trends and patterns. Watch for consistent revenue trends (growing 
or declining), seasonal patterns, and expense trends. Spot unusual months that might indicate data issues or 
exceptional events. Calculate average monthly revenue and profit to understand typical performance.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Statement of Earnings
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Produces the statement of earnings showing revenue and expenses. Alternative profit and loss format focusing on operational earnings.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate the statement of earnings - a financial statement showing revenue and expenses 
resulting in net earnings. Alternative format to the EBITDA income statement.

What You'll See: Revenue section (all revenue categories and sources), Expense section (organized by expense 
type - operating expenses, administrative, etc.), resulting in Net Earnings. Shows both current period and year-
to-date. Different format from EBITDA statement - focuses on operational earnings. Formatted as traditional 
financial statement.

Criteria: Select the reporting period, choose level of detail (summary or account detail), optionally include 
prior period comparison, and choose whether to show budget comparison.

Key Information: This is an alternative profit and loss format. Where the EBITDA statement separates interest, 
taxes, depreciation, and amortization, this statement integrates them into the expense categories. The net 
earnings result should match net income on the EBITDA statement - it's the same number, different presentation. 
Use whichever format stakeholders prefer.

When to Use This Report:
• Month-end and year-end financial reporting (alternative format)
• Provide financial statements when EBITDA format not preferred
• Analyze revenue and expense performance
• Support stakeholders who prefer traditional earnings format
• Compare current and prior period operational performance
• Prepare earnings-focused financial analysis

Good to Know: Both EBITDA income statement and statement of earnings show profitability - just different formats. 
EBITDA focuses on operational performance before financing and depreciation; earnings format integrates all 
expenses. Use whichever your stakeholders prefer or understand better.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cash Flow
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Produces the cash flow statement showing operating, financing, and investing activities. Shows how cash changed during the period.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate the cash flow statement showing sources and uses of cash. Breaks cash flow into 
operating activities, financing activities, and investing activities. Essential for understanding cash generation.

What You'll See: Operating Activities (net income adjusted for non-cash items and working capital changes), 
Investing Activities (purchases/sales of fixed assets, investments), Financing Activities (loans, equity, 
distributions), resulting in net increase/decrease in cash. Reconciles to cash balance change. Formatted as 
traditional cash flow statement.

Criteria: Select the reporting period, choose level of detail, and optionally include prior period for comparison.

Key Information: The cash flow statement explains how your cash balance changed - did you generate cash from 
operations or use it? Operating cash flow should be positive - that means the business generates cash. Investing 
activities usually use cash (buying equipment). Financing activities show borrowing/repayment. Required for 
financial reporting and stakeholder communication.

When to Use This Report:
• Month-end and year-end financial reporting
• Analyze cash generation from operations
• Provide financial statements to banks and stakeholders
• Understand sources and uses of cash
• Support cash management and forecasting
• Evaluate business cash-generating ability

Good to Know: You can be profitable but cash-poor if profit is tied up in receivables or inventory. Operating 
cash flow is often more important than net income for survival. Positive operating cash flow means the business 
generates cash; negative means it consumes cash.

reportTrainingRecords.name: General & Admin Expenses by Region
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows G&A expenses broken down by region. Track administrative overhead costs by geographic area for multi-location operations.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Analyze general and administrative expenses by region or operating location. Track 
overhead costs across geographic areas for multi-location businesses.

What You'll See: Regions with their G&A expense accounts and amounts listed underneath. Shows administrative 
salaries, office expenses, rent, utilities, insurance, and other overhead by location. Region subtotals show 
total G&A costs by area. Can include budget comparison. Organized by region.

Criteria: Select regions and reporting periods, choose which G&A expense categories to include, optionally show 
budget comparison, and set minimum expense thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze G&A costs by operating location
• Compare administrative overhead across regions
• Track regional office expenses and efficiency
• Monitor regional G&A budget compliance
• Support regional profitability analysis
• Identify opportunities for G&A cost reduction by location

Good to Know: For multi-region operations, understanding G&A costs by location is essential. Some regions may 
have higher overhead due to size, market conditions, or efficiency. Use this to benchmark regions against each 
other and identify best practices or problem areas.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cash Flow Projection
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Projects the cash flow statement using actuals for closed periods and budget amounts for future periods. For parent company and lender reporting.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate a forward-looking cash flow statement combining actual results for closed periods 
with budgeted amounts for future periods. Provides a projected view of cash generation and usage over the coming 
months. Essential for parent company reporting, lender compliance, and near-term cash planning.

What You'll See: The same three-section cash flow format - Operating Activities (actual net income and working 
capital changes blending into budgeted projections), Investing Activities (actual and projected capital 
expenditures), Financing Activities (actual and projected loan and equity movements) - resulting in a projected 
net increase/decrease in cash and ending cash balance. The header identifies which periods are actual and which 
are projected.

Criteria: Select the fiscal year, the last period with actual data (the as-of period), and the number of months 
to project forward (typically 1-3). The report automatically uses GL actuals for closed periods and budget 
amounts for future periods.

Key Information: The projection uses whatever budget amounts have been entered in the GL for future periods. If 
budget amounts are missing for an account, that account will contribute zero to the projected periods - review 
budget entry completeness before distributing this report. The opening cash balance always comes from the actual 
fiscal year opening, so the projected ending cash is grounded in real numbers.

When to Use This Report:
• Monthly reporting package to parent company or head office
• Quarterly lender and bonding company submissions
• Internal cash planning and liquidity review
• Anticipate cash shortfalls before they occur
• Support draw scheduling and subcontractor payment planning

Good to Know: The projection is only as good as the budget data behind it. If actuals are consistently running 
above or below budget, the projected periods will reflect that gap. For a quick reasonableness check, compare 
the projected net income line against recent actual months - a large swing is usually a sign that income 
statement budgets need updating. This report does not replace a weekly cash flow built from AR aging and AP due 
dates; it is a strategic monthly view suited for formal reporting.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Account Transactions
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows all transactions for selected accounts with complete detail. Comprehensive account activity from all sources (A/P, A/R, payroll, J/Es).
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display complete transaction detail for accounts from all sources. Shows every 
transaction that affected selected accounts - comprehensive account activity report.

What You'll See: Accounts with all transactions listed chronologically - from A/P, A/R, payroll, job costing, 
journal entries, and other sources. Shows dates, descriptions, references, sources, debits, credits, and running 
balances. Complete drill-down detail for transaction traceability. Organized by account with opening and closing 
balances.

Criteria: Select accounts and date ranges, filter by transaction source (A/P, A/R, payroll, J/E, etc.), choose 
transaction types, set minimum amounts, and optionally filter by jobs or other dimensions.

Key Information: This is the most comprehensive account detail report - shows every transaction from every source. 
Unlike Account Activity (GLAREP d) which may summarize, this shows complete transaction-level detail. Essential 
for detailed account analysis and reconciliation. The transaction source tells you which module it came from.

When to Use This Report:
• Detailed account research and analysis
• Complete account reconciliation with transaction detail
• Trace every transaction affecting an account
• Support detailed audits with complete transaction history
• Investigate account discrepancies at transaction level
• Prepare detailed account documentation

Good to Know: This is your most detailed account report - complete transaction history from all sources. Use when 
you need to see every single transaction. For high-level review, use Account Activity. For transaction-level 
detail, use this. The running balance helps verify account integrity.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job G/L Activity by Source
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows G/L activity for jobs organized by transaction source. Track job costs and revenues by source module (A/P, A/R, payroll, J/E).
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display job G/L activity broken down by source - shows which modules generated costs and 
revenues for each job. Essential for understanding job cost composition.

What You'll See: Jobs with their G/L activity organized by source module (A/P costs, A/R revenue, payroll costs, 
equipment costs, journal entries, etc.). Shows amounts by source type for each job. Job subtotals show total 
activity from each source. Organized by job then by source.

Criteria: Select jobs or ranges, choose date ranges or G/L periods, filter by specific sources, select accounts 
or account types, and set minimum transaction amounts.

Key Information: Job costs come from multiple sources - A/P (vendor invoices), payroll (labour), equipment 
(internal rentals), and journal entries (adjustments). Revenue comes from A/R (billings). This report breaks 
down each job's activity by source, helping you understand cost and revenue composition. Essential for job cost 
analysis and verification.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze job cost composition by source
• Verify job costs from each module
• Reconcile job costs to source systems (A/P, payroll, etc.)
• Understand what drives job costs and revenues
• Support job cost audits with source detail
• Track job activity by transaction source

Good to Know: This report helps you understand job cost makeup. If a job is over budget, this shows which sources 
(A/P, payroll, equipment) are driving the overrun. The source breakdown helps identify where to look for detail - 
high A/P costs mean vendor invoices, high payroll means labour, etc.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job Cumulative G/L Activity
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows cumulative job G/L activity from inception to date. Track total job costs and revenues accumulated over the life of the job.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display job-to-date cumulative G/L activity. Shows total costs and revenues accumulated 
from job start through the selected date. Essential for job-to-date financial reporting.

What You'll See: Jobs with their cumulative G/L activity from inception to the reporting date. Shows opening 
balances (if job started in prior year), current period activity, and cumulative to-date totals. Displays costs 
by category (labour, materials, equipment, subcontracts) and revenues. Job totals show complete financial 
position to date. Organized by job.

Criteria: Select jobs and as-of dates, choose level of detail (summary or account detail), filter by G/L account 
types, and optionally include budget comparison.

Key Information: This shows life-to-date job financial activity - everything from start to the reporting date. 
Different from Job Activity by Source which shows a specific period. This is cumulative - all costs and revenues 
since the job began. Essential for understanding total job financial position and comparing to contract amounts 
or budgets.

When to Use This Report:
• Track job-to-date total costs and revenues
• Compare cumulative costs to budgets or contracts
• Prepare job financial position reports
• Support job profitability analysis with cumulative data
• Verify job-to-date G/L balances
• Calculate work-in-progress and over/under billings

Good to Know: For long-running jobs, this shows the complete financial picture from start to current. The to-date 
totals include everything - prior years plus current year. Compare cumulative costs to contract value to see 
remaining available budget. Essential for percentage-of-completion accounting.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job Revenue Activity by Client Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows job revenue organized by client. Track billing activity and revenue by customer for revenue analysis and client reporting.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display job revenue activity grouped by client. Analyze billing and revenue patterns by 
customer. Essential for client revenue analysis and relationship management.

What You'll See: Clients with their jobs and revenue activity listed underneath. Shows billings, revenue 
recognition, receivables, and payments by job within client. Client subtotals show total revenue activity by 
customer. Includes current period and year-to-date. Organized by client then by job.

Criteria: Select clients and jobs, choose date ranges or G/L periods, filter by revenue accounts or types, and 
set minimum revenue thresholds.

Key Information: This organizes revenue by client relationship rather than just by job. Useful for understanding 
which clients generate the most revenue, tracking client billing patterns, and analyzing client profitability. 
Some clients may have multiple jobs - this consolidates their total activity. Essential for customer relationship 
and revenue management.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze revenue by client or customer
• Track billing activity for key clients
• Identify top revenue-generating clients
• Prepare client-specific revenue reports
• Support client relationship management with revenue data
• Calculate client concentration and diversification

Good to Know: Understanding revenue by client helps manage customer relationships and risk. Client concentration 
(too much revenue from one client) creates risk. This report helps identify your most valuable clients and track 
their revenue contribution. Use for account management and strategic planning.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Gross Profit Margin by Region
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows revenue, cost of sales, and gross profit margin by region. Analyze profitability across geographic areas for multi-location operations.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Analyze gross profit performance by region or operating location. Track revenue, cost of 
sales, and gross margin across geographic areas.

What You'll See: Regions with their revenue, cost of sales, gross profit (revenue minus cost), and gross profit 
margin percentage. Shows which regions are most profitable. Region subtotals and percentages allow comparison. 
Can show trends over time. Organized by region.

Criteria: Select regions and reporting periods, choose whether to show current period, YTD, or trends, optionally 
include prior year comparison, and set minimum revenue thresholds.

Key Information: Gross profit margin = (Revenue - Cost of Sales) / Revenue. Shows profitability before G&A 
expenses. Different regions may have different margins due to market conditions, competition, project mix, or 
operational efficiency. Essential metric for understanding regional performance and profitability.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze profitability by geographic region
• Compare gross profit margins across locations
• Identify high-performing and underperforming regions
• Track regional margin trends over time
• Support strategic decisions about regional operations
• Benchmark regional performance

Good to Know: Gross margin is a key profitability indicator. Regions with consistently low margins need attention - 
either improve efficiency, raise prices, or reconsider operations there. High-margin regions may offer best 
practices to apply elsewhere. Target margins vary by industry but consistency matters.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Person Diary
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows diary entries and notes for selected people. Track conversations, incidents, performance issues, and important events by individual.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display diary entries and notes recorded for people. Track conversations, incidents, 
performance issues, disciplinary actions, and important events by individual. Essential for HR documentation and 
employee record keeping.

What You'll See: People with their diary entries showing dates, entry types (conversation, incident, performance, 
etc.), descriptions, notes, and who made the entry. Chronological record of interactions and events for each person. 
Can include confidential entries visible only to authorized users. Organized by person with entries in date order.

Criteria: Select people or employees, choose date ranges, filter by entry type (all entries, incidents only, 
performance only, etc.), and set visibility level (include or exclude confidential entries).

Key Information: The person diary provides chronological documentation for HR purposes. Entry types typically include 
conversations, incidents, performance issues, disciplinary actions, safety matters, and general notes. Each entry 
records who made it and when. Confidential entries may be restricted to HR or management. Essential for documenting 
employee interactions, progressive discipline, performance management, and maintaining personnel records.

When to Use This Report:
• Review employee history and documentation
• Support performance reviews with documented incidents
• Track progressive discipline and corrective actions
• Document conversations and important events
• Prepare for terminations with complete record
• Support HR investigations and reviews

Good to Know: Good documentation protects the company. The person diary creates a chronological record of interactions, 
incidents, and performance issues. Date and document conversations, warnings, and incidents when they happen. This 
documentation becomes essential for performance management, progressive discipline, and defending employment decisions. 
Always maintain confidentiality and follow company HR policies when using this report.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Trade Tickets by Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows employees with trade tickets (certifications, licenses, qualifications) organized by job. Verify required certifications are on site.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display employees with their trade tickets and certifications organized by job. Verify that 
workers on each job have required licenses, certifications, and qualifications. Essential for compliance and safety 
management.

What You'll See: Jobs with employees listed underneath, showing each employee's trade tickets, certifications, 
licenses, and qualifications. Includes ticket types (journeyman, apprentice level, safety tickets, equipment licenses, 
etc.), issue dates, and expiry dates. Shows which certifications are current and which are expiring soon. Organized 
by job with employee detail.

Criteria: Select jobs, choose which ticket types to include (journeyman, apprentice, safety, equipment, all), filter 
by expiry status (current, expiring soon, expired, all), and set date thresholds for expiry warnings.

Key Information: Trade tickets include journeyman and apprentice certifications, safety tickets (confined space, fall 
protection, WHMIS, first aid, etc.), equipment licenses (crane, forklift, etc.), and professional certifications. Many 
jobs require specific certifications for workers on site. This report verifies compliance by showing which 
certifications each employee has. Expiry tracking ensures certifications stay current. Essential for safety compliance 
and meeting job requirements.

When to Use This Report:
• Verify employees on job have required certifications
• Support safety compliance and job requirements
• Identify missing certifications before mobilization
• Track certification coverage by job
• Prepare certification documentation for clients
• Support union and apprenticeship ratio compliance

Good to Know: Many jobs require specific certifications - journeymen for supervision, safety tickets for hazardous 
work, equipment licenses for operation. Use this before mobilizing to ensure workers have needed tickets. Clients may 
require proof of certifications. Some jurisdictions mandate journeyman-to-apprentice ratios. This report helps verify 
compliance and prevent issues from uncertified workers on site.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Trade Tickets by Expiry Date
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows trade tickets organized by expiry date. Identify certifications expiring soon so employees can renew before expiry.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display trade tickets and certifications organized by expiry date. Identify certifications 
expiring soon so employees can renew them before they lapse. Essential for maintaining certification compliance and 
avoiding expired tickets.

What You'll See: Trade tickets organized by expiry date showing employees, ticket types, issue dates, expiry dates, 
and days until expiry. Highlights tickets expiring soon or already expired. Can show tickets in expiry order or grouped 
by ticket type. Organized by expiry date with employee and certification detail.

Criteria: Select date range for expiry window (e.g., expiring in next 90 days), filter by ticket types, choose 
employees or all staff, set expiry thresholds (e.g., warn at 60 days, urgent at 30 days), and optionally include 
already expired tickets.

Key Information: Trade tickets and certifications have expiry dates and must be renewed periodically. First aid expires 
every 3 years, WHMIS every 3 years, fall protection every 3 years, some safety tickets annually, equipment licenses 
vary. Expired certifications mean employees cannot legally perform that work. This report provides early warning so 
employees can schedule renewal training before expiry. Essential for maintaining workforce certification compliance.

When to Use This Report:
• Identify certifications expiring soon
• Schedule renewal training before tickets expire
• Proactively manage certification compliance
• Notify employees of upcoming expiry dates
• Prevent expired certifications from affecting work
• Plan training budgets and schedules

Good to Know: Run this monthly to catch expiring certifications early. Give employees 60-90 days notice so they can 
schedule renewal training. Some courses book up months in advance. Expired tickets mean workers cannot perform that 
work legally - they must be pulled from those tasks until renewed. Proactive management prevents compliance issues and 
work interruptions from unexpected expiries.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Temporary Foreign Worker List
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists temporary foreign workers with work permit and visa information. Track permits, expiry dates, and compliance for foreign worker programs.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display temporary foreign workers with their work permit and visa details. Track work permits, 
visa status, expiry dates, and compliance requirements for temporary foreign worker programs. Essential for immigration 
compliance and foreign worker management.

What You'll See: Foreign workers with their work permit information including permit types, permit numbers, issue 
dates, expiry dates, visa status, employer restrictions, and program details (LMIA, TFWP, etc.). Shows permit status 
(current, expiring soon, expired) and any restrictions or conditions. Organized by worker with permit detail.

Criteria: Select workers or show all foreign workers, filter by permit type or program, set expiry date thresholds, 
choose permit status (current, expiring, all), and optionally include historical permit information.

Key Information: Canada's Temporary Foreign Worker Program (TFWP) allows employers to hire foreign nationals when 
qualified Canadians are not available. Requires Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) and proper work permits. Work 
permits have expiry dates and may have employer or location restrictions. Employers must comply with program 
requirements including wages, working conditions, and reporting. This report tracks permit status and ensures 
compliance with immigration regulations.

When to Use This Report:
• Track foreign worker permits and visa status
• Identify permits expiring soon for renewal
• Ensure immigration compliance for foreign workers
• Support TFWP program audits and reporting
• Verify work authorization before employment
• Maintain foreign worker documentation

Good to Know: Employing foreign workers without valid permits is illegal and carries serious penalties. Work permits 
must be renewed before expiry - start renewal process 4-6 months early. Some permits have employer or location 
restrictions - verify workers can legally work for you at their job site. Government conducts TFWP compliance 
inspections - maintain accurate records. Essential for legal foreign worker employment.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Area & Centre List
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists areas with their cost centres showing budget, commitment, and cost summaries. Quick reference for area and centre organization with financial totals.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate a directory of areas and their associated cost centres with financial summary 
information. Essential reference for understanding project organization and centre structure.

What You'll See: Areas listed with their cost centres underneath, showing descriptions, budget amounts, 
commitments (outstanding P/Os), actual costs to date, and forecast amounts. Area subtotals show rolled-up 
financial data. Organized by area then by cost centre within area.

Criteria: Select jobs and areas, choose which centres to include (active, all, specific types), optionally 
include financial summaries, and filter by minimum budget or cost amounts.

Key Information: Areas are major work packages or phases (Site Work, Concrete, Framing, etc.). Centres are 
detailed cost codes within areas (Excavation, Footings, Walls, etc.). This report shows the hierarchy and 
provides quick financial summaries. Use as a reference to understand project cost structure and organization.

When to Use This Report:
• Create reference documentation for project cost structure
• Train project staff on area and centre organization
• Quick lookup of centre descriptions and codes
• Review area organization and financial summaries
• Verify cost centre setup and hierarchy
• Provide cost code reference for field crews

Good to Know: This is your cost structure reference. Areas group related work together; centres provide detailed 
tracking within areas. Good projects have clear, logical area/centre structures that match how work is actually 
performed and managed. Keep this handy for cost code reference.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Area Consolidated Cost Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows complete cost picture by area: budgets, commitments, costs, and adaptive forecasts. Your primary area-level cost control report with all key metrics.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display comprehensive cost information by area including budgets, commitments (outstanding 
P/Os), actual costs, and adaptive forecasts. The definitive area-level cost control report showing complete 
financial picture by area, owner P/O, job, and centre.

What You'll See: Areas with detailed cost breakdown - original budget, current budget (after transfers), 
commitments (open P/Os), actual costs to date, forecast at completion (from adaptive forecasting), variance to 
budget, and cost to complete. Broken down by labour hours, labour costs, material, equipment, subcontracts, and 
other. Shows complete cost picture by area. Organized by area, owner P/O, job, then centre.

Criteria: Select jobs and areas, choose reporting basis (budget, actual, forecast), filter by owner P/Os or 
centres, set variance thresholds, and choose detail level (summary or full detail).

Key Information: This is your primary area cost control report. Shows everything needed to manage costs at the 
area level. Commitments are outstanding P/Os that will become costs. Forecast uses adaptive forecasting - early 
in the project it's budget-weighted; later it's actual-weighted based on progress. Variance = Forecast minus 
Budget. Cost to complete = Forecast minus Actual. Essential for project cost control.

When to Use This Report:
• Primary area-level cost control and monitoring
• Monthly project cost reviews and forecasting
• Identify areas over or under budget
• Track commitments and pending costs by area
• Prepare management cost reports by work area
• Support project forecasting and earned value analysis

Good to Know: This is likely your most-used cost report at the area level. Combines budget, actual, commitments, 
and adaptive forecast into one comprehensive view. The forecast adapts based on actual performance - if you're 
trending over/under budget, the forecast reflects that. Essential for proactive cost management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Area Budget Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows current or original budget amounts by area. Compare original budgets to current budgets after budget transfers and changes.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display budget information by area showing original budgets and current budgets (after 
transfers). Track how budgets have changed during the project.

What You'll See: Areas with budget amounts broken down by cost type (labour hours, labour cost, materials, 
equipment, subcontracts, other). Shows both original budget (initial plan) and current budget (after transfers 
and adjustments). Area subtotals show total budgets by work area. Organized by area.

Criteria: Select jobs and areas, choose whether to show original budget, current budget, or both, filter by 
specific cost types, and set minimum budget thresholds.

Key Information: Original budget is the initial plan at project start. Current budget reflects transfers between 
areas or centres during the project. Budget transfers reallocate funding without changing total project budget - 
moving money from one area to another as work scope changes. This shows how area budgets have evolved.

When to Use This Report:
• Review area budget allocations and changes
• Compare original budget to current budget by area
• Track budget transfers and reallocations
• Verify area budget setup and amounts
• Prepare budget documentation by work area
• Support budget change analysis and audit

Good to Know: Budget transfers are common as projects progress and scope clarifies. An area might get more budget 
from another area if work increases. The difference between original and current budget shows how funding has 
been reallocated. Use with Budget Transfer reports for complete budget change history.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Area Cost Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows actual or forecast costs by area. Track area cost consumption and adaptive forecasts at completion without budget comparison detail.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display actual costs or forecasted costs by area. Simpler than the Consolidated report - 
focuses on costs only without budget and commitment detail.

What You'll See: Areas with cost amounts broken down by type (labour hours, labour cost, materials, equipment, 
subcontracts, other). Can show actual costs to date or forecast costs at completion (from adaptive forecasting). 
Area subtotals show total costs by work area. Organized by area.

Criteria: Select jobs and areas, choose whether to show actual costs, forecast costs, or both, filter by cost 
types, and set minimum cost thresholds.

Key Information: Actual costs are what has been spent to date. Forecast costs are adaptive predictions at 
completion based on current performance and progress. Early in projects, forecast is budget-weighted. Later, 
forecast is actual-weighted. This report is simpler than Area Consolidated - just costs without all the budget 
and commitment detail. Use when you only need cost information.

When to Use This Report:
• Review area cost consumption without budget detail
• Track actual costs by work area
• See forecast costs at completion by area
• Simpler cost view without budget comparison
• Quick cost check by area
• Export cost data for external analysis

Good to Know: Use Area Consolidated when you need the full picture (budget, commitments, costs, forecast). Use 
this Area Cost report when you only care about the cost numbers themselves. The forecast shown uses the same 
adaptive algorithm as the Consolidated report.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Area List
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists all areas with descriptions and basic information. Simple directory of work areas for reference and documentation.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate a simple list of all areas with descriptions. Basic reference document for area 
codes and organization.

What You'll See: All areas listed with area codes, full descriptions, jobs they belong to, and basic status 
information. Simple directory without financial detail. Organized by area code or by job.

Criteria: Select jobs, filter by area status (active, closed, all), choose sort order (by area code or 
description), and optionally include area notes or details.

When to Use This Report:
• Create area code reference documentation
• Train staff on area organization
• Verify area setup and descriptions
• Quick area code lookup
• Export area directory for other uses
• Review project area structure

Good to Know: This is the simplest area report - just a directory. Use Area & Centre List for more detail 
including centres. Use Area Budget or Area Consolidated for financial information. This is just for reference and 
documentation of the area structure.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Area P/O Tracking
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Compares A/R invoices posted to areas versus P/O amounts allocated to those areas. Track billing against client P/O authorizations by work area.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track client purchase order allocations by area and compare to amounts billed. Ensure you 
don't exceed client P/O authorization on any area. Essential for cost-plus or T&M work with P/O limits.

What You'll See: Areas with their client P/O allocations and A/R invoice amounts posted. Shows P/O amount 
authorized for each area, invoiced to date, remaining available amount, and percentage consumed. Area subtotals 
show total P/O tracking. Alerts when approaching or exceeding P/O limits. Organized by area then by client P/O.

Criteria: Select jobs and areas, filter by client P/O numbers, choose threshold for warnings (90% consumed, etc.), 
and optionally show only areas approaching limits.

Key Information: Clients often issue P/Os with not-to-exceed amounts by area or phase. You allocate portions of 
client P/Os to areas. As you bill (create A/R invoices), amounts are consumed against those allocations. This 
report shows how much P/O authorization you've used by area and how much remains. Critical for avoiding billing 
over authorization limits.

When to Use This Report:
• Monitor client P/O consumption by area
• Identify areas approaching P/O limits
• Prevent billing over client P/O authorization
• Track available P/O balance by work area
• Request P/O increases before running out
• Support billing and P/O management

Good to Know: On cost-plus or T&M work, client P/Os typically have not-to-exceed amounts. You allocate those 
amounts to areas or phases. This tracks consumption so you know when to request additional P/O authorization. 
Running this regularly prevents the embarrassment of billing over authorization.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Budget Transfers by Transfer No
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists budget transfers in transfer number sequence. Track budget reallocations between centres and areas with complete detail.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See budget transfer transactions in transfer number order. Track how budgets have been 
reallocated between centres and areas during the project.

What You'll See: Budget transfers in sequential number order showing dates, descriptions, source centres (budget 
transferred from), destination centres (budget transferred to), amounts by cost type (labour, material, equipment, 
etc.), and reasons. Each transfer shows both sides - amounts leaving source and amounts arriving at destination. 
Organized by transfer number.

Criteria: Enter transfer number ranges, filter by date ranges, choose jobs or centres involved, and select 
specific transfer types if applicable.

Key Information: Budget transfers move budget between centres without changing total job budget. Common reasons: 
scope changes, work resequencing, correcting initial budget allocation errors, or responding to field conditions. 
Transfers must balance - amount leaving source equals amount entering destination. Creates audit trail of budget 
changes.

When to Use This Report:
• Review budget transfer history in sequence
• Look up specific transfer transaction details
• Audit budget reallocation activity
• Verify budget transfer processing
• Document budget change reasons and approvals
• Prepare budget change register

Good to Know: Budget transfers are normal project management - you reallocate budget as understanding of work 
improves. The sequential list helps track all transfers chronologically. Look for transfer descriptions to 
understand why budgets changed. Frequent transfers might indicate budget issues.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Budget Transfers by Centre
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows budget transfers organized by cost centre. See all budget changes affecting specific centres for detailed centre-level analysis.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display budget transfers grouped by the centres they affected. Track how each centre's 
budget has changed through transfers.

What You'll See: Cost centres with all budget transfers affecting them - both amounts transferred in (increases) 
and amounts transferred out (decreases). Shows dates, transfer numbers, descriptions, amounts by cost type, and 
net change to centre budget. Centre subtotals show total budget change from transfers. Organized by centre.

Criteria: Select jobs and centres, choose date ranges, filter by specific transfer types, and set minimum transfer 
amounts.

When to Use This Report:
• Research why a centre's budget changed
• See all transfers affecting specific centres
• Compare original budget to current budget by centre
• Calculate net budget change per centre from transfers
• Support centre-level budget variance analysis
• Audit budget changes at the centre level

Good to Know: When a centre's current budget differs from original budget, this shows why. Some centres gain 
budget (transfers in exceed transfers out), others lose budget (transfers out exceed transfers in). The net change 
explains the difference between original and current budgets. Essential for understanding budget evolution.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Centre List
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists all cost centres with descriptions and basic information. Simple directory of centres for reference and documentation.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate a simple list of all cost centres with descriptions and basic details. Essential 
reference document for centre codes and organization.

What You'll See: All cost centres listed with centre codes, full descriptions, areas they belong to, jobs, cost 
types (labour, material, equipment, subcontract, other), and status. Simple directory without financial detail. 
Organized by centre code, area, or job.

Criteria: Select jobs and areas, filter by centre status (active, closed, all), choose cost types, and select 
sort order (by centre code, description, or area).

When to Use This Report:
• Create centre code reference documentation
• Train staff on centre organization and cost structure
• Verify centre setup and descriptions
• Quick centre code lookup for timesheet or cost coding
• Export centre directory for other systems
• Review project cost centre structure

Good to Know: This is the simplest centre report - just a directory with descriptions. Use for training field 
staff on cost codes or as a reference document. For financial details, use Centre Budget, Cost, or Consolidated 
Cost reports. Keep this handy for cost code reference.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Unit Quantity Entry Sheet
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Data collection form for quantity entry showing centres, units, budgets, and to-date quantities with space to write current completed quantities.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate a data collection form for field crews to record completed quantities. Shows 
centres with quantity tracking, units of measure, budget quantities, to-date quantities, with blank space to write 
in current period completed quantities.

What You'll See: Cost centres with quantity tracking showing descriptions, cost types, units of measure, budget 
quantities, and to-date quantities completed. In detail mode, includes blank rows or space for field crews to 
write in quantities completed during current period. Organized by centre.

Criteria: Select jobs and centres with quantity tracking, choose which cost types to include, optionally include 
space for period-by-period entry, and select detail level.

Key Information: This is a physical form (paper or tablet) for field collection. Field crews use it to record 
quantities completed (cubic yards placed, square feet installed, linear feet completed, etc.). The form shows what 
was budgeted and what's been done to date so crews know where they stand. Data collected gets entered into J/C 
Quantities Entry.

When to Use This Report:
• Create quantity collection forms for field crews
• Provide supervisors with forms to track quantities
• Support weekly or monthly quantity tracking
• Enable consistent quantity data collection
• Give field crews context (budget and to-date)
• Facilitate earned value and progress tracking

Good to Know: Quantity tracking is powerful for earned value and productivity analysis, but only if you collect 
the data. This form makes collection easier and more consistent. Field crews record quantities, someone enters 
them into the system, then you can run productivity and forecasting reports. Good quantity data drives good 
project management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Profit Analysis Summary
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Analyzes project profitability with budget, actual, forecast, and gross profit. Comprehensive profit summary with earned value metrics and margin analysis.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Analyze project profitability comprehensively. Shows budget, actual costs, adaptive 
forecast, revenues, and calculated gross profit with earned value metrics. The primary profitability analysis 
report.

What You'll See: Projects with complete profit picture - budgeted costs, actual costs to date, commitments, 
adaptive forecast at completion, revenues (billed and unbilled), gross profit (revenue minus forecast cost), gross 
profit percentage, earned value metrics, and cost/schedule performance indices. Shows both dollars and percentages. 
Can drill down to areas or centres. Organized by job with financial summaries.

Criteria: Select jobs, choose reporting basis (budget, forecast, actual), filter by areas or centres, include 
earned value metrics, and set detail level (summary or detailed breakdown).

Key Information: This is your primary profitability report. Gross profit = Revenue minus Forecast Cost. The 
forecast uses adaptive forecasting (budget-weighted early, actual-weighted later). Earned value metrics show: Cost 
Performance Index (CPI = earned/actual), Schedule Performance Index (SPI = earned/planned), and forecasted final 
margins. Essential for executive reporting and project financial management.

When to Use This Report:
• Executive project profitability reviews
• Monthly financial performance reporting
• Forecast gross profit at completion
• Calculate earned value and performance indices
• Support strategic project decisions
• Prepare management and stakeholder profit reports

Good to Know: This is likely your most important project financial report. Shows whether you'll make or lose money 
at completion. The adaptive forecast gives realistic profit projections based on actual performance. CPI < 1.0 = 
over budget. SPI < 1.0 = behind schedule. Essential for proactive project management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Centre Consolidated Cost Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows complete cost picture by centre: budgets, commitments, costs, and adaptive forecasts. Your primary centre-level cost control report with all key metrics.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display comprehensive cost information by centre including budgets, commitments (outstanding 
P/Os), actual costs, and adaptive forecasts. The definitive centre-level cost control report showing complete 
financial picture.

What You'll See: Cost centres with detailed breakdown - original budget, current budget (after transfers), 
commitments (open P/Os), actual costs to date, forecast at completion (from adaptive forecasting), variance to 
budget, and cost to complete. Broken down by labour hours, labour costs, material, equipment, subcontracts, and 
other. For labour centres, includes quantities and productivity metrics. Organized by cost centre.

Criteria: Select jobs and centres, choose reporting basis (budget, actual, forecast), filter by areas or cost 
types, set variance thresholds, and choose detail level (summary or full detail).

Key Information: This is your primary centre-level cost control report - most detailed view of costs. Commitments 
show outstanding P/Os that will become costs. Forecast uses adaptive forecasting that weighs budget early in work 
and actual performance later. Variance = Forecast minus Budget. Cost to complete = Forecast minus Actual. Shows 
everything needed to manage costs at the work element level.

When to Use This Report:
• Primary detailed cost control and monitoring by work element
• Monthly detailed cost reviews and forecasting
• Identify specific centres over or under budget
• Track commitments and pending costs by centre
• Prepare detailed management cost reports
• Support detailed project forecasting and earned value

Good to Know: This is your most detailed cost control report. More granular than Area Consolidated. Use when you 
need centre-by-centre detail to understand cost performance. The adaptive forecast gives you realistic at-
completion projections based on actual trends. Essential for proactive cost management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Centre Budget Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows original and current budget amounts by cost centre. Compare initial budgets to current budgets after transfers and changes.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display budget information by cost centre showing original budgets and current budgets 
(after transfers). Track how centre budgets have changed.

What You'll See: Cost centres with budget amounts broken down by cost type (labour hours, labour cost, materials, 
equipment, subcontracts, other). Shows both original budget (initial plan) and current budget (after transfers). 
Centre subtotals show budget by work element. Can show quantities for labour centres. Organized by cost centre.

Criteria: Select jobs and centres, choose whether to show original budget, current budget, or both, filter by cost 
types, optionally include quantities, and set minimum budget thresholds.

Key Information: Original budget is the initial plan. Current budget reflects budget transfers during the project. 
The difference shows budget reallocations. For labour centres, can show budgeted quantities (hours, units) along 
with dollar amounts. This is your detailed centre-level budget reference.

When to Use This Report:
• Review centre budget allocations and amounts
• Compare original to current budget by centre
• Verify centre budget setup and distribution
• Track budget changes from transfers
• Prepare detailed budget documentation
• Support budget analysis at work element level

Good to Know: This is your detailed budget reference at the centre (work element) level. More detailed than Area 
Budget. Use to understand budget distribution across all work elements. The difference between original and current 
shows how budgets have been reallocated during the project.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Centre Cost Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows actual or forecast costs by centre. Track centre cost consumption and adaptive forecasts without budget comparison detail.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display actual costs or forecasted costs by centre. Simpler than Consolidated report - 
focuses on costs only without budget and commitment detail.

What You'll See: Cost centres with cost amounts broken down by type (labour hours, labour cost, materials, 
equipment, subcontracts, other). Can show actual costs to date or forecast costs at completion (from adaptive 
forecasting). For labour centres, includes hour and quantity detail. Centre subtotals by area or job. Organized by 
centre.

Criteria: Select jobs and centres, choose whether to show actual costs, forecast costs, or both, filter by cost 
types or areas, and set minimum cost thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Review centre cost consumption without budget detail
• Track actual costs by work element
• See forecast costs at completion by centre
• Simpler cost view for reporting
• Export cost data for external analysis
• Quick cost check without budget comparison

Good to Know: Use Centre Consolidated when you need the full picture (budget, commitments, costs, forecast, 
variance). Use this Centre Cost report when you only need the cost numbers themselves. The forecast uses the same 
adaptive algorithm. Simpler report for when budget comparison isn't needed.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Centre Commitment Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows commitments (open P/Os) by centre. Track outstanding purchase orders that will become costs. Essential for cash flow and cost forecasting.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display commitments by centre - outstanding purchase orders that represent future costs. 
Critical for understanding pending costs and cash flow requirements.

What You'll See: Cost centres with their commitment amounts broken down by cost type. Shows open P/O amounts that 
haven't been invoiced yet. Can include P/O detail (vendor, P/O number, amounts). Centre subtotals show total 
commitments by work element. Organized by centre.

Criteria: Select jobs and centres, filter by vendors or P/O types, choose whether to show summary or P/O detail, 
and set minimum commitment thresholds.

Key Information: Commitments are open P/Os - money you're obligated to pay but haven't been invoiced for yet. 
They represent future costs. Actual costs + Commitments = total exposure. Essential for cash flow forecasting and 
understanding total cost position. When vendors invoice, commitments convert to actual costs.

When to Use This Report:
• Track outstanding P/Os and future costs by centre
• Forecast cash flow requirements from open P/Os
• Calculate total exposure (actual + committed) by centre
• Review what costs are pending by work element
• Support commitment control and P/O management
• Identify centres with large pending costs

Good to Know: Commitments bridge the gap between budgets and actual costs. You've placed P/Os but haven't been 
invoiced yet. Tracking commitments prevents surprises - you know money is coming. Total exposure = Actual + 
Committed. If that exceeds budget, you have a problem even if actual costs look fine.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Budget to Actual Comparison
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Compares centre budgets to actual costs with variance. Simple side-by-side comparison without commitments or forecast detail.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Compare centre budgets to actual costs showing variance. Simplified comparison report 
focusing on budget versus actual performance.

What You'll See: Cost centres with budget amounts, actual costs, and variance (actual minus budget) by cost type. 
Shows over/under budget status clearly. Can show variance amounts and percentages. Centre subtotals show budget 
versus actual summary. Organized by centre.

Criteria: Select jobs and centres, choose reporting period or date ranges, set variance thresholds to highlight 
significant differences, and filter by areas or cost types.

Key Information: This is a straightforward budget versus actual comparison. Positive variance on costs = over 
budget (unfavorable). Negative variance = under budget (favorable). Simpler than Consolidated Cost which includes 
commitments and forecasts. Use when you just want to see how actual costs compare to budget without additional 
complexity.

When to Use This Report:
• Simple budget performance monitoring by centre
• Identify centres over or under budget
• Calculate variance amounts and percentages
• Prepare straightforward budget versus actual reports
• Quick budget compliance check
• Support variance analysis without forecast complexity
