Good to Know: This is the simplest budget comparison - just budget, actual, and variance. Use when you don't need 
commitments or forecasts. Good for straightforward budget monitoring. For complete cost picture including 
commitments and adaptive forecasts, use Centre Consolidated Cost.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Centre Variance Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows variance between forecast and budget by centre. Identify centres projecting over or under budget with adaptive forecast variance analysis.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Analyze centre variances between adaptive forecast and budget. Identify centres projecting 
over or under budget at completion based on current performance and adaptive forecasting.

What You'll See: Cost centres with budget amounts, adaptive forecast at completion, and variance (forecast minus 
budget). Shows variance amounts and percentages by cost type. Highlights centres projecting overruns or underruns. 
Can include actual costs and commitments for context. Organized by centre, often sorted by variance magnitude.

Criteria: Select jobs and centres, set variance thresholds to highlight significant differences, filter by areas or 
cost types, choose whether to show only overruns or all variances, and set minimum budget amounts.

Key Information: Variance = Forecast minus Budget. Positive variance = projected overrun (unfavorable). Negative 
variance = projected underrun (favorable). The forecast uses adaptive forecasting based on actual performance - 
more reliable than simple budget tracking. This identifies problem centres before work is complete, giving time to 
respond.

When to Use This Report:
• Identify centres projecting over or under budget
• Focus management attention on problem areas
• Calculate projected overrun or underrun by centre
• Support variance analysis and investigation
• Prepare management exception reports
• Trigger corrective action on overrunning centres

Good to Know: This is your exception report - focuses attention on centres with significant variances. The adaptive 
forecast makes this more accurate than comparing budget to actual alone. Large variances need investigation and 
action. Run monthly to catch problems early while there's still time to respond.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Centre Variance by Client P/O
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows centre variance organized by client purchase order. Track budget variance by client P/O for cost tracking and change order management.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Analyze centre variances organized by client P/O. Track budget performance by client 
authorization and identify where P/O-specific work is over or under budget.

What You'll See: Client P/Os with their centres listed underneath, showing budget, forecast, and variance for 
each centre within that P/O. P/O subtotals show total variance by purchase order. Highlights P/Os with significant 
variances. Organized by client P/O then by centre.

Criteria: Select jobs and client P/Os, set variance thresholds, filter by centres or areas, choose whether to show 
only overruns, and set minimum budget amounts.

Key Information: When work is organized by client P/Os, this shows variance by authorization. Essential for 
identifying when P/O-specific work is consuming more budget than planned. Helps determine when change orders or 
additional P/Os are needed. The P/O organization helps communicate budget issues to clients in their terms.

When to Use This Report:
• Track budget variance by client P/O
• Identify P/Os with budget overruns
• Support change order requests with variance detail
• Communicate budget issues to clients by their P/O
• Manage cost-plus or T&M work by authorization
• Determine when additional P/O funding needed

Good to Know: Organizing variance by client P/O helps client communication. You can show the client which of 
their P/Os are tracking over or under budget (e.g., P/O #123 is $50K over budget). This facilitates change order 
discussions and helps request additional funding in client terms they understand.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Centre Client P/O Cross Reference
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows which client P/Os are allocated to which centres. Map the relationship between centres and client authorizations for billing and tracking.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display the cross-reference between cost centres and client P/Os. Shows which centres are 
charged to which client authorizations. Essential for understanding P/O allocation and billing structure.

What You'll See: Cost centres with their associated client P/Os, showing P/O numbers, descriptions, allocated 
amounts, and usage status. Can show from either perspective - centres with their P/Os, or P/Os with their centres. 
Organized by centre and P/O or vice versa.

Criteria: Select jobs, choose whether to organize by centre or by P/O, filter specific centres or P/Os, and 
optionally include allocation amounts and usage.

Key Information: This shows the mapping between your internal cost structure (centres) and client authorizations 
(P/Os). One centre might bill to multiple P/Os. One P/O might cover multiple centres. This cross-reference helps 
you understand the relationships, verify billing setup, and track P/O consumption by work element.

When to Use This Report:
• Understand centre to client P/O relationships
• Verify billing setup and P/O allocations
• Create reference documentation for billing
• Train staff on P/O and centre relationships
• Support billing and invoicing processes
• Review P/O allocation structure

Good to Know: The cross-reference can be complex - one centre billing to multiple P/Os (shared work) or one P/O 
covering multiple centres (broad authorization). This report maps those relationships for reference and billing 
support. Keep this handy for billing questions.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Productivity Factor by Discipline
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows productivity factors by trade/discipline where budgets and quantities are entered. Identify which trades are gaining or losing productivity versus plan.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Analyze labour productivity by trade or discipline (occupation). Shows where productivity 
gains or losses have been made compared to budget for centres with quantity tracking.

What You'll See: Trades/disciplines with productivity metrics - budgeted hours per unit, actual hours per unit 
(from to-date performance), productivity factor (actual vs budget ratio), and productivity gain/loss percentage. 
Shows which trades are performing better or worse than planned. Trade subtotals summarize by discipline. Organized 
by trade/discipline.

Criteria: Select jobs and labour centres with quantities, choose trades/disciplines, filter by productivity variance 
thresholds, and set minimum quantity or hour thresholds.

Key Information: Productivity factor = Actual hours per unit / Budget hours per unit. Factor < 1.0 = productivity 
gain (taking fewer hours than budgeted). Factor > 1.0 = productivity loss (taking more hours). Organized by trade 
shows which disciplines are performing well or poorly. Essential for crew management and improving estimates.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze productivity by trade or discipline
• Identify high-performing and underperforming trades
• Calculate actual production rates by discipline
• Support crew management and training decisions
• Improve future estimating with productivity feedback
• Recognize productive crews or address problem trades

Good to Know: Trade-level productivity analysis helps you understand which crews or disciplines need support. If 
carpenters are at 0.85 productivity factor (15% better than budget) but concrete at 1.20 (20% worse), you know 
where to focus attention. Use for crew management and estimate feedback.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Unit Quantity Overrun Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows centres where quantity to date exceeds forecast quantity. Identify work elements consuming more units than planned - early warning of overruns.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Identify centres where actual quantities consumed exceed forecast quantities. Early warning 
system for quantity overruns before they become cost problems.

What You'll See: Labour centres with quantities tracked (cubic yards, square feet, linear feet, etc.) showing 
forecast quantity, quantity to date, overrun amount (actual minus forecast), and overrun percentage. Only shows 
centres where actual exceeds forecast. Sorted by overrun severity. Organized by centre or overrun amount.

Criteria: Select jobs and centres with quantity tracking, set overrun thresholds (percentage or amount), filter by 
areas, and choose minimum quantity levels.

Key Information: For centres tracking quantities, this catches overruns early. If forecast was 100 cubic yards but 
you've already poured 110, that's a 10% quantity overrun. Quantity overruns often lead to cost overruns. This 
report alerts you before quantities become costs - giving time to investigate and respond. Essential for proactive 
project control.

When to Use This Report:
• Early warning system for quantity overruns
• Identify centres consuming more units than planned
• Catch quantity issues before they become cost issues
• Investigate why actual quantities exceed forecasts
• Support change order or budget revision decisions
• Monitor quantity-based work performance

Good to Know: This is an early warning system - quantity overruns happen before cost overruns. If you're placing 
more concrete than planned, costs will follow. Catching quantity overruns early gives you time to investigate (is 
it scope change? measurement error? waste?) and respond before the cost impact hits.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Centre Productivity Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Compares budgeted labour productivity to forecast productivity for labour centres. Analyze where labour is more or less productive than planned.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Analyze labour productivity by comparing budget to forecast amounts on centres where 
budgets and quantities are tracked. Identify productivity gains or losses.

What You'll See: Labour centres with budget quantities, forecast quantities, budget hours, forecast hours, budget 
labour cost, forecast labour cost, and calculated productivity rates (hours per unit). Shows variance between 
budgeted and forecast productivity. Identifies centres where productivity is better or worse than planned. 
Organized by cost centre.

Criteria: Select jobs and labour centres, choose date ranges, filter by production rate variances, and set minimum 
quantity or hour thresholds.

Key Information: For labour centres with quantities (concrete yards, square feet, linear feet, etc.), this 
calculates productivity as hours per unit. Compares budgeted productivity to forecast productivity based on actual 
performance. Positive variance = less productive than planned. Negative variance = more productive than planned. 
Essential for understanding labour efficiency and crew performance.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze labour productivity by work element
• Identify where crews are more/less productive than planned
• Calculate actual production rates (hours per unit)
• Support labour planning with actual productivity data
• Improve future estimating with productivity feedback
• Recognize high-performing crews or identify training needs

Good to Know: Productivity analysis is powerful for construction management. If budgeted 2 hours per cubic yard but 
actually achieving 1.5 hours per yard, that's 25% productivity gain. If achieving 2.5 hours per yard, that's 25% 
productivity loss. Use this to manage crews and improve estimates.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Centre Snapshot History
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows historical snapshots by centre over time. Track how actual costs, progress, and forecasts have evolved throughout the project.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display centre snapshots captured at various dates showing how costs, progress, and 
adaptive forecasts have evolved. Track the trajectory of work over time.

What You'll See: Cost centres with snapshots listed chronologically showing snapshot dates, actual costs at each 
snapshot, quantities complete (if tracked), progress percentages, and forecast at completion from each snapshot. 
Shows how forecasts have changed as work progressed and actuals accumulated. Organized by centre then by snapshot 
date.

Criteria: Select jobs and centres, choose date ranges for snapshots, filter by snapshot types or sources, and set 
minimum cost or progress thresholds.

Key Information: Snapshots are point-in-time captures taken regularly (monthly, at draws, etc.). Each snapshot 
records actual costs, progress, and adaptive forecast at that moment. Comparing snapshots over time shows: (1) how 
work progressed, (2) how forecasts changed as actuals accumulated, (3) where trends improved or deteriorated. 
Essential for earned value analysis and performance trending.

When to Use This Report:
• Track cost and forecast evolution over time
• Analyze how forecasts have changed as work progressed
• Perform earned value trending analysis
• Identify when forecasts started deteriorating
• Support project reviews with historical data
• Document progress and forecast changes for stakeholders

Good to Know: Snapshot history is powerful for understanding project trajectory. If forecasts steadily worsen over 
time, that indicates ongoing issues. If forecasts stabilize or improve, that shows problem resolution. Early 
snapshots are budget-heavy; later snapshots are actual-heavy as the adaptive algorithm adjusts.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Centre Cost to Complete
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows remaining costs to complete work on centres. Cost to complete = Budget minus Actual, with latest snapshot/draw data. Essential for forecasting and cash flow.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Calculate and display cost to complete (remaining costs) by centre. Shows budget less 
actual costs with latest snapshot/draw information. Critical for forecasting remaining spending and cash flow.

What You'll See: Cost centres with budget amounts, actual costs to date, and calculated cost to complete (budget 
minus actual). Includes latest snapshot data showing progress. Broken down by cost type (labour, material, 
equipment, subcontracts, other). Centre subtotals show remaining costs by work element. Organized by centre.

Criteria: Select jobs and centres, choose as-of date, filter by cost types, optionally include latest snapshot 
detail, and set minimum remaining cost thresholds.

Key Information: Cost to complete = Budget minus Actual = money still to be spent. If budget is $100K and actual 
is $60K, cost to complete is $40K. This tells you how much more you need to spend to finish the work. Incorporates 
latest snapshot/draw data for progress-adjusted calculations. Essential for cash flow forecasting and remaining 
funding requirements.

When to Use This Report:
• Forecast remaining costs to complete project
• Calculate cash flow requirements by centre
• Track remaining spending by work element
• Support project funding and financing decisions
• Prepare cost-to-complete reports for stakeholders
• Identify centres near completion (low cost to complete)

Good to Know: Cost to complete helps answer "how much more do we need to spend?" Critical for cash flow management 
and funding. If actual exceeds budget, cost to complete is negative (overrun). Sum of cost to complete across all 
centres tells you total remaining project spending. Use with snapshot data for progress-weighted estimates.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Centre Costs and Revenue Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows A/P costs, labour costs, and A/R revenues by centre for a G/L period range. Reconcile job costing to G/L with detailed source breakdown.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display costs and revenues by centre for a specific G/L period range. Shows A/P costs 
(vendor invoices), labour costs (payroll), and A/R revenues (billings). Essential for reconciling job costing to 
the general ledger.

What You'll See: Cost centres with costs broken down by source - A/P invoices (vendors), labour timesheets 
(payroll), and A/R invoices (billings to client). Shows amounts by G/L period for the selected range. Centre 
subtotals show total costs and revenues by work element. Can show detail transactions or just summaries. Organized 
by centre then by source.

Criteria: Select G/L period range (from/to), choose jobs and centres, filter by transaction sources (A/P, labour, 
A/R), set detail level, and choose minimum transaction amounts.

Key Information: This shows centre activity for specific G/L periods from the sources that create costs and 
revenues. A/P invoices create costs, labour timesheets create costs, A/R invoices create revenues. The period-
specific view helps reconcile job costing to G/L and understand what activity occurred in specific periods. 
Essential for month-end close and G/L reconciliation.

When to Use This Report:
• Reconcile job costing to G/L by centre for specific periods
• Review period-specific cost and revenue activity
• Support month-end close with source detail
• Analyze costs and revenues by transaction source
• Prepare period-based cost and revenue reports
• Verify job cost posting to G/L

Good to Know: The period-specific view is essential for G/L reconciliation. Shows what costs and revenues were 
posted to job costing in specific G/L periods. The totals should tie to G/L job cost accounts. Use at month-end to 
ensure job costing and G/L are in sync.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job List
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists all jobs with basic information and status. Simple directory of projects for reference and documentation.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate a simple list of all jobs with descriptions and basic details. Essential reference 
document for job codes and organization.

What You'll See: All jobs listed with job codes, full descriptions, clients, job types, status (active, closed, 
etc.), project managers, and basic financial totals. Simple directory without detailed financial information. 
Organized by job code, client, or status.

Criteria: Filter by job status (active, closed, all), choose clients, select job types, and pick sort order (by job 
code, description, client, or project manager).

When to Use This Report:
• Create job code reference documentation
• Train staff on job organization and codes
• Verify job setup and descriptions
• Quick job code lookup for timesheets or cost coding
• Export job directory for other uses
• Review active and closed jobs

Good to Know: This is the simplest job report - just a directory with basic information. Use for training and 
reference. For detailed financial information, use Job Status, Job Cash Position, or other financial job reports. 
Keep this handy for job code reference.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job Status Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows contract, budget, forecast, commitments, to-date costs, and to-date billings by job. Primary job-level financial status report.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display comprehensive job financial status. Shows contract amounts, budgets, forecasts, 
commitments, actual costs to date, and billings to date. The primary job-level financial summary report.

What You'll See: Jobs with complete financial picture - contract amount, original budget, current budget (after 
transfers), adaptive forecast at completion, commitments (open P/Os), actual costs to date, billings to date, and 
calculated metrics (gross profit, percent complete, etc.). Shows financial health and status of each job. Organized 
by job with summary totals.

Criteria: Select jobs and clients, choose as-of date, set detail level (summary or breakdown by area/centre), and 
optionally filter by job status or type.

Key Information: This is your primary job financial summary - shows everything executives need to understand job 
status. Contract = what client will pay. Budget = original plan. Forecast = adaptive prediction at completion. 
Commitments = outstanding P/Os. Actual = costs to date. Billings = invoiced to date. Essential for executive job 
reviews and status reporting.

When to Use This Report:
• Executive job financial reviews and status updates
• Monthly or quarterly job performance reporting
• Quick overview of all job financial positions
• Identify jobs with issues (over budget, under-billed, etc.)
• Support strategic project portfolio management
• Prepare management job status reports

Good to Know: This is likely your most-used executive job report. Gives complete financial picture at a glance. Run 
regularly to monitor job health. Red flags: forecast exceeds contract (will lose money), costs exceed billings (cash 
flow problem), or commitments plus costs exceed budget (overrun coming).

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job Cash Position Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows to-date costs, A/P net and holdback, total paid out, to-date billings, A/R net and holdback, total paid in, and net cash balance by job.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display job cash position - money in versus money out. Shows costs, payments to vendors, 
billings, payments from clients, and net cash balance. Essential for job cash flow management.

What You'll See: Jobs with cash position detail - to-date costs, A/P amounts net and holdback, total paid to 
vendors, to-date billings, A/R amounts net and holdback, total received from clients, and net cash balance (money in 
minus money out). Shows whether jobs are cash positive or negative. Organized by job with financial summaries.

Criteria: Select jobs and clients, choose as-of date, optionally include holdback detail, and set minimum cash 
balance thresholds.

Key Information: Cash position = Total received from client minus Total paid to vendors and employees. Positive = 
client has paid you more than you've paid out (good cash flow). Negative = you've paid out more than client has 
paid you (cash drain). Holdback is money retained from billings or payments. Essential for understanding job cash 
flow and funding needs.

When to Use This Report:
• Monitor job cash flow and cash position
• Identify jobs draining cash versus generating cash
• Support job financing and funding decisions
• Track holdback amounts on jobs
• Calculate working capital tied up in jobs
• Prepare cash flow reports for management

Good to Know: Profitable jobs can still drain cash if billing lags costs. A job can be making money but negative cash 
position means you're funding it. Track this to avoid cash flow problems. Large negative positions indicate you need 
to bill more or collect faster. Essential for construction cash management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job Over/Under Billings Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows to-date costs, forecast and contract amounts, pro-rated billings, to-date billings, and over/under billing amounts. Essential for WIP adjustments.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Calculate over/under billings (work in progress adjustments) for jobs. Compares actual 
billings to what should have been billed based on costs and percentage complete. Essential for financial statement 
WIP calculations and revenue recognition.

What You'll See: Jobs with to-date costs, forecast costs, contract amounts, calculated pro-rated billings (based on 
percent complete), actual to-date billings, and over/under billing amounts. Over-billed jobs have billed more than 
earned. Under-billed jobs have earned more than billed. Organized by job with WIP calculations.

Criteria: Select jobs and as-of date, choose calculation method (cost-to-cost or units complete), and set minimum 
WIP thresholds.

Key Information: Pro-rated billing = Contract amount times percent complete. Percent complete = Actual costs divided 
by forecast costs. Over-billed (liability) = billed more than earned - you owe work. Under-billed (asset) = earned 
more than billed - client owes you. This determines work-in-progress adjustments for financial statements. Essential 
for percentage-of-completion accounting.

When to Use This Report:
• Calculate WIP adjustments for month-end or year-end close
• Support percentage-of-completion revenue recognition
• Identify over-billed jobs (liabilities) and under-billed jobs (assets)
• Prepare financial statement WIP schedules
• Support accounting for long-term contracts
• Determine earned revenue versus billed revenue

Good to Know: Critical for financial reporting under percentage-of-completion accounting. Over-billed creates 
deferred revenue (liability) - you've been paid for work not done. Under-billed creates unbilled receivable (asset) 
- you've done work not yet billed. Run at period-end for WIP adjustments. Auditors will want this.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job First 6 Months Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows year opening balances and first 6 months of fiscal year cost and revenue amounts by job. Essential for reconciling job ledger to G/L.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display job costs and revenues for the first six months of the fiscal year. Shows opening 
balances and activity for months 1-6. Essential for reconciling job ledger to G/L and month-end closures.

What You'll See: Jobs with fiscal year opening balances, then costs and revenues by month for the first six months 
(months 1-6 of fiscal year). Shows cumulative totals through month 6. Organized by job with monthly detail and 
period totals.

Criteria: Select jobs and fiscal year, choose level of detail (summary or breakdown by cost type), and optionally 
include prior year comparison.

Key Information: The fiscal year is split into two 6-month reports for manageability. This covers months 1-6. Job 
totals should reconcile to corresponding G/L accounts. Opening balances come from prior year-end. Monthly activity 
shows costs and revenues posted each month. Use with Last 6 Months report for complete fiscal year. Essential for 
job ledger to G/L reconciliation.

When to Use This Report:
• Reconcile job ledger to G/L for first half of fiscal year
• Support month-end close for months 1-6
• Review job activity by month for first half year
• Verify opening balances and monthly activity
• Prepare job ledger documentation for first 6 months
• Support financial audits with job detail

Good to Know: Run at each month-end during first half of fiscal year to ensure job ledger reconciles to G/L. The 
totals by job should match G/L job cost accounts. Keep these reports as month-end documentation. Use with Last 6 
Months report to cover complete fiscal year.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job Last 6 Months Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows opening balance at end of month 6 and last 6 months of fiscal year activity by job. Essential for reconciling job ledger to G/L.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display job costs and revenues for the last six months of the fiscal year. Shows opening 
balance at month 7 (from month 6 close) and activity for months 7-12. Essential for reconciling job ledger to G/L 
and month-end closures.

What You'll See: Jobs with opening balance at end of month 6 (accumulated through first half), then costs and 
revenues by month for the last six months (months 7-12 of fiscal year). Shows cumulative totals through year-end. 
Organized by job with monthly detail and period totals.

Criteria: Select jobs and fiscal year, choose level of detail (summary or breakdown by cost type), and optionally 
include prior year comparison.

Key Information: This covers months 7-12 of fiscal year. Opening balance is cumulative through month 6 (from First 6 
Months report). Job totals should reconcile to corresponding G/L accounts. Monthly activity shows costs and revenues 
posted each month in second half. Use with First 6 Months report for complete fiscal year. Essential for job ledger 
to G/L reconciliation.

When to Use This Report:
• Reconcile job ledger to G/L for second half of fiscal year
• Support month-end close for months 7-12
• Review job activity by month for second half year
• Verify mid-year balances and monthly activity
• Prepare job ledger documentation for last 6 months
• Support year-end close and financial audits

Good to Know: Run at each month-end during second half of fiscal year to ensure job ledger reconciles to G/L. The 
totals by job should match G/L job cost accounts. Keep these reports as month-end documentation. Opening balance 
should match ending balance from First 6 Months report.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job Profit Accrual Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Uses expected revenue, costs and profit, G/L revenue and costs, with derived profit accrual and work in progress amounts by job.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Calculate profit accrual and work-in-progress for jobs. Compares expected financial position 
(based on percentage complete) to actual G/L amounts. Determines accruals needed for accurate financial reporting.

What You'll See: Jobs with expected revenue (based on percent complete), expected costs, expected profit, actual 
G/L revenue, actual G/L costs, actual G/L net profit, calculated profit accrual needed, and WIP adjustment amounts. 
Shows what needs to be accrued to match economic reality. Organized by job with accrual calculations.

Criteria: Select jobs and as-of date, choose calculation method (percentage-of-completion or completed contract), and 
set minimum accrual thresholds.

Key Information: Expected revenue = Contract times percent complete. Expected profit = Expected revenue minus 
expected costs. Profit accrual = Expected profit minus Actual G/L profit. WIP = Expected revenue minus Actual G/L 
revenue. These accruals adjust G/L to match economic reality under percentage-of-completion accounting. Essential for 
accurate financial statements on long-term contracts.

When to Use This Report:
• Calculate profit accruals for month-end or year-end close
• Determine WIP adjustments for financial statements
• Support percentage-of-completion accounting
• Prepare accrual journal entries for jobs
• Reconcile economic performance to G/L reporting
• Support financial statement preparation for contractors

Good to Know: Critical for contractors using percentage-of-completion accounting. G/L only knows actual transactions 
(invoices, costs). This calculates what profit you've actually earned based on work completed, then determines 
accruals needed to adjust G/L to economic reality. Run at period-end for financial statement accuracy.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job Recent Activity Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows most recent date of activity by job for job costing, labour, A/R invoices, A/R payments, A/P P/Os, and A/P invoices. Identify active versus stale jobs.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display most recent activity dates for each job across all systems. Shows when each job last 
had activity in job costing, labour, billing, payments, P/Os, and invoices. Essential for identifying active versus 
dormant jobs.

What You'll See: Jobs with most recent activity dates shown by category - last job cost transaction, last labour 
timesheet, last A/R invoice (billing), last A/R payment received, last A/P P/O, and last A/P invoice. Shows which 
jobs are currently active and which have been idle. Can highlight jobs with no recent activity. Organized by job 
with activity dates.

Criteria: Select jobs, set activity date thresholds (e.g., no activity in 90 days), choose which activity types to 
include, and optionally show only stale jobs.

Key Information: Jobs with no recent activity may be: (1) complete but not closed, (2) suspended, (3) forgotten and 
needing attention, or (4) improperly coded. This report helps identify jobs that need cleanup or closure. Recent 
activity in some areas but not others can indicate issues (e.g., costs but no billing = unbilled work).

When to Use This Report:
• Identify jobs ready for closure (no recent activity)
• Find dormant or suspended jobs
• Support job cleanup and housekeeping
• Identify jobs with unbilled work (costs but no A/R)
• Review job activity patterns
• Prepare job status for management review

Good to Know: Helps keep job list clean and current. Jobs with no activity in 90+ days probably need attention - 
either close them or investigate why they're idle. Jobs with costs but no recent billing may have unbilled work. 
Jobs with billing but no costs may be incorrectly coded. Great housekeeping tool.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Centre to Source Comparison
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Compares centre revenue amounts to source system (A/R) revenue amounts. Reconcile job cost revenue to billing records and identify discrepancies.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Compare revenue amounts in job costing centres to revenue in the A/R system. Reconcile to 
ensure job revenue matches billing records. Identify and investigate discrepancies.

What You'll See: Cost centres with two revenue amounts - centre revenue (from job costing) and source revenue 
(from A/R invoices), with variance between them. Shows which centres have discrepancies between job cost revenue 
and actual billings. Highlights variances for investigation. Organized by centre.

Criteria: Select jobs and centres, choose reporting periods, set variance thresholds to highlight significant 
differences, and filter by minimum revenue amounts.

Key Information: Revenue should match between job costing centres and A/R billing. If they don't match, either: 
(1) invoices weren't coded to the right centres, (2) revenue recognition differs from billing, or (3) there's a 
data error. This report identifies discrepancies so you can investigate and correct. Essential for job revenue 
integrity and financial accuracy.

When to Use This Report:
• Reconcile job cost revenue to A/R billing system
• Identify centres with revenue discrepancies
• Investigate variance between job revenue and billings
• Support financial close with revenue reconciliation
• Audit job cost revenue integrity
• Ensure billing is coded to correct centres

Good to Know: Revenue discrepancies indicate problems - invoices coded wrong, revenue recognition issues, or errors. 
Run this regularly to catch and fix discrepancies early. Clean revenue data is essential for accurate job 
profitability analysis and financial reporting.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job Cost Transaction Comparison
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Compares centre cost and revenue to detailed transactions. Verify job cost summaries match transaction detail for data integrity.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Compare centre cost and revenue summary amounts to detailed transaction totals. Verify job 
costing data integrity by confirming summaries match transaction detail.

What You'll See: Cost centres with two sets of amounts - centre summary amounts (from centre records) and 
transaction totals (from detailed transaction records), with variance between them. Shows where summary and detail 
don't match. Highlights discrepancies for investigation. Organized by centre.

Criteria: Select jobs and centres, choose reporting periods, set variance thresholds, and filter by cost or revenue 
types.

Key Information: Centre records store summary amounts (total costs, total revenues). Transactions store detail 
(individual invoices, timesheets, etc.). Summary should equal sum of detail. If they don't match, there's a data 
integrity issue - transactions not properly rolled up, missing transactions, or corrupted data. This report 
identifies problems so you can investigate and fix.

When to Use This Report:
• Verify job costing data integrity
• Confirm centre summaries match transaction detail
• Identify data integrity issues in job costing
• Support financial audits with reconciliation
• Investigate suspected data problems
• Ensure job cost accuracy and reliability

Good to Know: This is a data integrity check. Discrepancies indicate system issues that need immediate attention. 
Run periodically to ensure job costing data is reliable. If you find discrepancies, investigate and resolve before 
making business decisions based on the data.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job Costs and Revenue Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows A/P costs, labour costs, and A/R revenues by job for a G/L period range. Reconcile job costing to G/L at the project level.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display costs and revenues by job for specific G/L periods. Shows A/P costs (vendor 
invoices), labour costs (payroll), and A/R revenues (billings). Essential for job-level G/L reconciliation.

What You'll See: Jobs with costs broken down by source - A/P invoices (vendors), labour timesheets (payroll), and 
A/R invoices (billings to client). Shows amounts by G/L period for the selected range. Job subtotals show total 
costs and revenues by project. Can drill down to centre or transaction detail. Organized by job then by source.

Criteria: Select G/L period range (from/to), choose jobs, filter by transaction sources (A/P, labour, A/R), set 
detail level, and choose minimum transaction amounts.

Key Information: This shows job activity for specific G/L periods from all cost and revenue sources. The period-
specific view helps reconcile job costing to G/L and understand what activity occurred in specific periods at the 
project level. The totals by source (A/P, labour, A/R) should tie to corresponding G/L accounts. Essential for 
month-end close and G/L reconciliation.

When to Use This Report:
• Reconcile job costing to G/L at project level for specific periods
• Review period-specific cost and revenue activity by job
• Support month-end close with job-level source detail
• Analyze which jobs had activity in specific periods
• Prepare job-based cost and revenue reports by period
• Verify job cost posting to G/L by project

Good to Know: Same as Centre Costs and Revenue but at job level instead of centre level. Use for job-level G/L 
reconciliation and understanding project-level activity by period. The totals should tie to G/L job cost accounts. 
Run at month-end to ensure job costing and G/L match.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Labour By Multiplier Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows labour costs organized by billing multiplier for cost-plus work. Calculate markup on labour costs for cost-plus billing and invoice preparation.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display labour costs grouped by billing multiplier. Calculate marked-up labour amounts for 
cost-plus billing. Essential for cost-plus invoicing and markup verification.

What You'll See: Labour costs grouped by multiplier (e.g., 1.15x, 1.20x, 1.25x) showing base labour cost and 
calculated billing amount (cost times multiplier). Shows which labour is marked up at which rates. Can include 
detail by employee, trade, or centre. Multiplier subtotals show total markup by rate. Organized by multiplier then 
by detail.

Criteria: Select jobs and periods, choose which multipliers to include, filter by employees or trades, set detail 
level, and choose minimum cost thresholds.

Key Information: On cost-plus work, labour is billed at cost times a multiplier (e.g., 1.15 = cost + 15%). 
Different labour may have different multipliers (trade labour 1.15x, supervision 1.10x, etc.). This report groups 
labour by multiplier and calculates billing amounts. Essential for preparing cost-plus labour invoices and 
verifying markup calculations.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare cost-plus labour invoices with markup
• Calculate billing amounts for cost-plus labour
• Verify labour markup calculations by multiplier
• Show clients labour costs and markup detail
• Analyze labour markup and margins by rate
• Support cost-plus billing processes

Good to Know: Cost-plus contracts specify labour multipliers (often different rates for different labour types). 
This report organizes labour by those multipliers and calculates billing amounts. The markup (multiplier minus 1.0) 
covers overhead and profit. Essential for cost-plus billing accuracy.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Client P/O Labour Dispersion
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows how labour hours are distributed across client P/Os. Track labour consumption by client authorization for billing and P/O management.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display labour costs allocated to client P/Os after dispersion rules and labour corrections are applied. 
Track corrected labour costs by client authorization for accurate P/O management and billing.

What You'll See: Client P/Os with labour costs allocated to them (after dispersion and corrections), broken down by 
employee, trade, or date. Shows regular hours, overtime hours, and costs by P/O. P/O subtotals show total corrected 
labour allocation per authorization. Can compare to P/O limits. Organized by client P/O with labour detail 
underneath.

Criteria: Select jobs and client P/Os, choose date ranges, filter by employees or trades, set detail level 
(summary or full detail), and optionally include P/O limits for comparison.

Key Information: This reports from the labour_dispersion table which includes both automatic cost allocation 
(dispersion rules) and any manual labour corrections. If supervisors posted timesheets to wrong centres, corrections 
move costs to the right centres without touching payroll. Shows accurate labour costs by P/O for project management, 
even if original timesheets had errors. Essential for P/O-based cost tracking and billing.

When to Use This Report:
• Track corrected labour costs by client P/O
• Monitor labour allocation against P/O authorization limits
• Prepare P/O-based labour billing with corrected costs
• Show clients accurate labour costs by their P/O
• Review labour cost allocation across P/Os after corrections
• Support P/O management and billing with accurate data

Good to Know: Reports from labour_dispersion table, not raw timesheets. This means costs reflect both automatic 
dispersion (premiums, travel, meals to separate centres) and manual labour corrections (fixing posting errors). If 
timesheets were posted to wrong centres, corrections move costs without touching payroll. This gives project 
managers accurate costs for P/O tracking even when original posting had errors.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Centre Labour Dispersion
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows how labour hours are distributed across cost centres. Analyze labour consumption by work element for cost control and productivity.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display labour costs allocated to cost centres after dispersion rules and labour corrections are applied. 
Track corrected labour costs by work element for accurate cost control and analysis.

What You'll See: Cost centres with labour costs allocated to them (after dispersion and corrections), broken down 
by employee, trade, or date. Shows regular hours, overtime hours, and costs by centre. Centre subtotals show total 
corrected labour by work element. Can compare to budgets. Organized by centre with labour detail underneath.

Criteria: Select jobs and centres, choose date ranges, filter by employees or trades, set detail level, and 
optionally include budget comparison.

Key Information: Reports from labour_dispersion table which includes automatic cost allocation (dispersion rules 
that split premiums, travel, meals, etc. to separate centres) and manual labour corrections (fixing posting errors). 
Shows accurate labour costs by centre for project management even if original timesheets had errors. Essential for 
centre-level cost control with corrected data.

When to Use This Report:
• Track corrected labour costs by cost centre
• Analyze accurate labour allocation across work elements
• Compare corrected actual labour to budget by centre
• Identify centres with accurate cost allocation after corrections
• Support centre-level cost control with corrected data
• Review labour cost allocation across project

Good to Know: Shows how labour costs are allocated across centres after both automatic dispersion (premiums, travel, 
meals split to separate centres per dispersion rules) and manual corrections (fixing posting errors). If supervisors 
posted timesheets to wrong centres, corrections move costs to the right centres without touching payroll. Essential 
for accurate centre-level cost control.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Labour Dispersion
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows how individual employees distribute their labour across centres, jobs, or P/Os. Track employee time allocation and utilization.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display how each employee's labour costs are allocated across centres, jobs, or P/Os after dispersion and 
corrections. Track corrected employee cost allocation by individual.

What You'll See: Employees with their labour costs allocated across centres, jobs, or P/Os (after dispersion and 
corrections). Shows regular hours, overtime hours, and costs by allocation. Employee subtotals show total costs and 
where each person's labour costs were allocated. Organized by employee with allocation detail.

Criteria: Select employees and jobs, choose date ranges, filter by centres or P/Os, and set detail level.

Key Information: Reports from labour_dispersion table showing where each employee's costs ended up after automatic 
dispersion rules and any manual corrections. Different from raw timesheets - shows corrected cost allocation for 
accurate project management even if original posting had errors.

When to Use This Report:
• Track individual employee cost allocation after corrections
• Review where employee labour costs were allocated
• Verify corrected employee cost distribution
• Analyze employee cost patterns by individual
• Support employee cost management with accurate data
• Understand individual employee cost allocation

Good to Know: Shows where each employee's costs ended up in job costing after automatic dispersion (premiums, 
travel, meals to separate centres) and manual corrections. Gives accurate view of employee cost allocation even 
when timesheets were originally posted incorrectly. Essential for accurate employee cost tracking by individual.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Occupation Labour Dispersion
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows how labour hours are distributed by trade or occupation. Analyze labour consumption by skill type across centres or jobs.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display how labour costs are allocated by trade or occupation across centres or jobs. Track corrected cost 
allocation by skill type after dispersion and corrections.

What You'll See: Trades/occupations with labour costs allocated across centres or jobs (after dispersion and 
corrections). Shows regular hours, overtime hours, and costs by allocation. Trade subtotals show total costs and 
allocation by skill type. Can compare to budgeted trade mix. Organized by occupation with allocation detail.

Criteria: Select trades/occupations and jobs, choose date ranges, filter by centres or areas, set detail level, 
and optionally include budget comparison.

Key Information: Reports from labour_dispersion table showing how trade/occupation costs are allocated across 
centres after automatic dispersion and manual corrections. Shows accurate cost allocation by skill type for project 
management even if original timesheets had posting errors.

When to Use This Report:
• Track corrected labour costs by trade or skill type
• Analyze how trade costs are allocated across work
• Compare actual trade cost allocation to planned mix
• Verify accurate trade cost allocation after corrections
• Support trade-based cost management
• Understand trade cost allocation patterns

Good to Know: Shows where each trade's costs are allocated after dispersion rules and corrections. Gives accurate 
view of which centres or jobs consumed carpenter costs versus electrician costs versus laborer costs, even if 
original timesheets were posted incorrectly. Essential for accurate trade-based cost management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job Daily Labour at T&M Rates
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows daily labour hours at time and materials billing rates by job. Calculate daily billable amounts for T&M invoicing with day-by-day detail.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display daily labour hours at T&M billing rates organized by job and date. Calculate daily 
billable amounts for time and materials invoicing with complete day-by-day detail.

What You'll See: Jobs with dates showing labour hours at T&M billing rates. Displays employees, trades, regular 
hours, overtime hours, billing rates, and calculated billing amounts by day. Daily subtotals show total billable 
amounts each day. Job totals show complete T&M labour billing. Organized by job then by date.

Criteria: Select jobs and date ranges, filter by T&M rate schedules, choose detail level (summary or full employee 
detail), and set minimum billing thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare daily T&M labour invoices
• Calculate billable amounts with day-by-day detail
• Show clients daily labour activity at billing rates
• Track daily billable labour amounts for cash flow
• Support daily T&M billing and reporting
• Verify T&M rate applications by day

Good to Know: Daily detail is often required for T&M work - clients want to see exactly who worked each day and at 
what rates. This provides that day-by-day detail with calculated billing amounts. The billing rates (not costs) are 
what gets invoiced. Essential for detailed T&M billing support.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Centre Labour at T&M Rates
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows labour hours at time and materials billing rates by centre. Calculate billable labour amounts for T&M invoicing organized by work element.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display labour hours at T&M billing rates organized by centre. Calculate billable amounts 
for time and materials invoicing by work element.

What You'll See: Cost centres with labour hours shown at T&M billing rates. Displays regular hours, overtime 
hours, billing rates for each hour type, and calculated billing amounts. Shows what to bill the client (at marked-
up rates) versus cost. Centre subtotals show total billable amounts by work element. Organized by centre.

Criteria: Select jobs and centres, choose date ranges, filter by T&M rate schedules or billing status (billed/
unbilled), and set minimum billing amount thresholds.

Key Information: T&M work bills labour at customer rates (usually pay rate plus markup) rather than cost. This 
shows hours at those billing rates organized by centre. Essential for preparing T&M invoices showing billable 
amounts by work element. The difference between billing amounts and costs is gross margin on labour.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare time and materials labour invoices by centre
• Calculate billable labour amounts by work element
• Show clients labour detail by centre at billing rates
• Track billable hours and amounts by work element
• Verify T&M billing calculations by centre
• Calculate gross margin on T&M labour by centre

Good to Know: Same concept as other T&M labour reports but organized by centre instead of by employee or job. 
Useful when billing T&M by work area or when clients want labour detail by centre. Shows billing amounts, not 
costs. The centre organization helps clients understand where labour was consumed.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Client P/O Labour at T&M Rates
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows labour hours at T&M billing rates by client P/O. Calculate billable labour amounts for T&M invoicing organized by client authorization.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display labour hours at T&M billing rates organized by client P/O. Calculate billable 
amounts for time and materials invoicing by client authorization.

What You'll See: Client P/Os with labour hours shown at T&M billing rates. Displays regular hours, overtime hours, 
billing rates, and calculated billing amounts by P/O. P/O subtotals show total billable amounts per authorization. 
Can include detail by employee or trade. Organized by client P/O.

Criteria: Select client P/Os and jobs, choose date ranges, filter by T&M rate schedules or billing status, set 
detail level, and choose minimum billing thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare T&M labour invoices by client P/O
• Calculate billable labour amounts by authorization
• Show clients labour detail by their P/O at billing rates
• Track billable hours against P/O limits
• Verify T&M billing by client authorization
• Calculate available P/O balance after labour

Good to Know: Organizing T&M labour by client P/O helps with authorization management. You can track how much 
billable labour has been charged to each P/O (e.g., P/O #123 has $45K in billable labour) and compare to the P/O 
limit. Essential for T&M work with multiple P/Os where you need to track consumption by authorization.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Client P/O Unions at T&M Rates
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows labour hours at T&M billing rates by client P/O and union/trade. Calculate billable amounts with trade breakdown by authorization.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display labour hours at T&M billing rates organized by client P/O and union/trade. 
Calculate billable amounts with trade detail by client authorization.

What You'll See: Client P/Os with unions/trades listed underneath, showing labour hours at T&M billing rates by 
trade. Displays regular hours, overtime hours, billing rates, and calculated billing amounts. Trade subtotals by 
P/O show billable amounts by skill type per authorization. Organized by P/O then by union/trade.

Criteria: Select client P/Os and unions/trades, choose date ranges, filter by T&M rate schedules, set detail level, 
and choose minimum billing thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare T&M labour invoices with trade breakdown by P/O
• Calculate billable amounts by trade and authorization
• Show clients trade detail for their P/Os at billing rates
• Track trade mix consumption against P/O authorizations
• Verify trade-based T&M billing by P/O
• Support detailed T&M invoicing with trade breakout

Good to Know: Combines T&M billing with trade detail organized by client P/O. Useful when clients want to see both 
what was billed to their P/O AND what trades were used. Shows billable amounts (not costs) by trade and P/O. More 
detailed than Client P/O Labour at T&M Rates.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Labour at T&M Rates
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows labour hours at T&M billing rates by individual employee. Calculate billable amounts for T&M invoicing with employee detail.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display labour hours at T&M billing rates organized by individual employee. Calculate 
billable amounts with employee-level detail for time and materials invoicing.

What You'll See: Employees with their labour hours shown at T&M billing rates. Displays regular hours, overtime 
hours, billing rates for each employee, and calculated billing amounts. Employee subtotals show total billable 
amounts by individual. Can include dates and centres worked. Organized by employee.

Criteria: Select employees and jobs, choose date ranges, filter by T&M rate schedules or billing status, set 
detail level, and choose minimum billing thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare T&M labour invoices with employee detail
• Calculate billable amounts by individual employee
• Show clients who worked and at what billing rates
• Track billable hours by employee for T&M work
• Verify employee T&M billing rate applications
• Calculate gross margin on T&M labour by employee

Good to Know: Employee-level detail for T&M billing. Some clients want to see exactly who worked and at what 
billing rates. This provides that individual detail with calculated billing amounts. The employee billing rates 
(not pay rates) are what gets invoiced. Essential for detailed T&M billing transparency.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Work Order List
reportTrainingRecords.summary: List of Work Orders

reportTrainingRecords.name: Work Order Due Dates
reportTrainingRecords.summary: W/Os and Permits Due

reportTrainingRecords.name: Transaction Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows detailed job cost transactions across all sources. Complete transaction-level detail for research, audit, and analysis.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display detailed job cost transaction records showing every transaction that affected job 
costs. Provides complete transaction-level detail from all sources for research, audit, and detailed analysis.

What You'll See: Individual job cost transactions showing dates, reference numbers, sources (A/P invoice, labour 
timesheet, journal entry, etc.), descriptions, jobs, centres, accounts, quantities, and amounts. Complete drill-down 
detail to transaction level. Can show all transaction types or filter to specific sources. Organized by date, job, 
centre, or transaction type.

Criteria: Select date ranges, filter by jobs, centres, or areas, choose transaction sources (A/P, labour, A/R, J/E), 
set amount thresholds, and select level of detail.

Key Information: This is your most detailed job cost report - every single transaction. Shows exactly what costs hit 
which centres from which sources. The transaction source tells you where it came from (A/P invoice #, labour batch #, 
journal entry #, etc.). Essential for detailed research, answering questions, and audit support. Can generate large 
amounts of data - filter appropriately.

When to Use This Report:
• Research specific transactions or costs
• Detailed audit of job cost activity
• Investigate cost discrepancies or questions
• Trace transactions from source to job cost
• Support detailed analysis and data export
• Prepare detailed documentation for audits

Good to Know: This is your detail research tool. When summary reports show something unusual and you need to dig into 
the details, use this. Shows complete transaction audit trail. Can be large - filter by date, job, or centre to keep 
it manageable. Essential for answering detailed questions about job costs.

reportTrainingRecords.name: SKU List
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows inventory discrepancies where purchase quantities don't match sales. Displays current stock levels, cost analysis, and pricing history. Use for physical inventory reconciliation or identifying slow-moving items.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Helps you find SKUs where the quantities purchased don't match what was sold or
transferred out. This is your go-to report for physical inventory counts and spotting inventory
problems.

What You'll See: Current stock on hand (calculated as purchases minus sales), total costs of what
you've purchased, total revenue from sales, the dates and prices of your last purchase and last
sale, SKU type, unit of measure, list price, and whether the item is still active.

Criteria: Select your company and a range of SKU numbers. The report automatically shows only items
where purchases and sales don't match - in other words, items that are currently in your inventory
or where there might be counting errors.

Key Information: The 'Current Count' column shows how many units you should have on hand. This is
simply what you've purchased minus what you've sold. The 'Last Purchase Price' shows what you
most recently paid for the item. The 'Last Sale Price' shows what you most recently charged.

When to Use This Report: When you're doing a physical inventory count and need to know what should
be on your shelves. When you notice discrepancies and want to investigate missing or extra
inventory. When you want to identify items that aren't moving (you bought them but haven't sold
them). When you need to compare what you're paying versus what you're charging. When preparing for
an audit or cycle count.

Good to Know: This report only shows items where there's a difference between purchases and sales -
it won't show items where everything purchased has been sold. If you don't see an item, it means
all purchases have been accounted for in sales.

reportTrainingRecords.name: SKU Transaction History
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Detailed transaction history for a single SKU showing all receipts and transfers with running balance. Includes FIFO cost tracking and inventory valuation. Use to trace SKU movements and verify stock levels.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows you the complete history of a single item - every time it came in and every time
it went out. This is like a bank statement for your inventory, showing exactly where each item came
from and where it went.

What You'll See: Every transaction for the item including the date, whether it came in or went out,
the transfer number, where it came from or where it went to, how many units, the price per unit, the
total cost, and a running balance showing how many you had after each transaction. Special detail
lines show exactly which purchase batches were used when items went out (FIFO tracking).

Criteria: Select your company, the specific SKU you want to trace, optionally a region, and a date
range. You can look at all history or just specific time periods.

Key Information: At the bottom you'll see a summary showing total units received, total units
consumed, current units on hand, and the current dollar value of what's in stock. The 'FIFO Draw
Detail' lines (in italics) explain which specific purchases were used up when items were
transferred out - this helps track costs accurately.

When to Use This Report: When you need to trace where specific inventory came from or went to. When
investigating why your inventory count doesn't match what you expected. When you need to verify
charges on an invoice against actual transfers. When preparing for an audit and need to show the
complete trail of an item. When analyzing how fast certain materials are being used. When you want
to understand the cost of inventory on hand.

Good to Know: FIFO means 'First In, First Out' - the system assumes the oldest inventory gets used
first. The colored boxes at the top give you a quick visual summary of your inventory activity. Each
transaction is numbered so you can reference the original transfer document if needed.

reportTrainingRecords.name: SKU by Region
reportTrainingRecords.summary: SKU by region

reportTrainingRecords.name: SKU Stock Counts
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Comprehensive inventory movement report showing all transfers in and out by SKU, type, and region. Displays source/destination details, quantities, rates, and extended amounts. Use for detailed inventory analysis and physical count preparation.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Shows all inventory movements organized by region, item type, and individual items. This
is your comprehensive inventory activity report - perfect for preparing physical counts and seeing
what's moving in each location.

What You'll See: Every inventory transfer including the date, transfer number, item number and
description, item type, region, where it came from or went to (with full details like vendor names
for purchases, job numbers for transfers to jobs, etc.), quantity, price, total amount, and who
counted it. The report groups everything by region first, then by item type, then by individual
item.

Criteria: Select your company, a range of SKU numbers, date range, and optionally a specific region
or transfer type. You can run this for all regions or focus on one location.

Key Information: The report shows subtotals at each level - by region, by item type within each
region, and by individual item. At the very bottom you'll see grand totals. For purchases, it shows
the vendor name and invoice number. For returns from jobs, it shows the job number and area. The
average price per item is calculated automatically.

When to Use This Report: When preparing for a physical inventory count and you need to print what
should be in each region. When you want to see all activity for specific types of items. When
reconciling inventory between the warehouse and job sites. When reviewing purchase activity and
making sure prices look correct. When you need to see who is responsible for inventory in each
region (shows supervisors and directors). When investigating problems in a specific location or with
specific item types.

Good to Know: The source and destination descriptions are very detailed - for example, instead of
just seeing 'RT' you'll see 'Returned from Job 12345/Area A' or 'Purchased from ABC Supply on
invoice 98765'. This makes it much easier to understand what actually happened. The report also
tracks who physically counted the inventory and when, which is helpful for accountability.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Document List
reportTrainingRecords.summary: List of P/M Documents

reportTrainingRecords.name: Document Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Document Information including job, area, center, initiator, and response

reportTrainingRecords.name: Punch List
reportTrainingRecords.summary: List of P/M Punch Lists

reportTrainingRecords.name: Punch Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Punch List Information

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cheques by Employee
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists all payroll cheques organized by employee. Shows earnings, deductions, and net pay for each cheque. Perfect for reviewing an employee's complete pay history.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See all payroll cheques for specific employees showing complete earnings and 
deduction detail. Review pay history, verify payroll calculations, or research payroll questions.

What You'll See: Employees with their cheques listed underneath. Each cheque shows gross earnings (regular, 
overtime, double time), all deductions (CPP, EI, taxes, union dues, etc.), and net pay. Includes hours 
worked, vacation/statutory accruals, and benefits. Organized by employee number or name.

Criteria: Select specific employees or a range, choose pay date ranges or G/L periods, filter by union or 
job, and choose whether to include voided cheques.

When to Use This Report:
• Review an employee's complete pay history
• Verify payroll calculations for specific employees
• Research employee questions about their paycheques
• Prepare year-end pay summaries for employees
• Audit payroll accuracy for selected employees
• Track earnings and deductions over time

Good to Know: This is your go-to report for employee payroll history. When an employee has a question about 
their pay, this shows you exactly what they were paid and how it was calculated. The detail includes 
everything from their cheque stub - all earnings, all deductions, and the net amount.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cheques by G/L Period
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows all payroll cheques grouped by accounting period. Essential for month-end payroll reconciliation and G/L verification.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See all payroll cheques posted in specific G/L periods. Critical for month-end 
close, payroll expense reconciliation, and G/L account verification.

What You'll See: Cheques grouped by the G/L period they were posted in, showing employee names, cheque 
numbers, dates, gross earnings, total deductions, and net pay. Period subtotals show total payroll for each 
accounting period. Organized by G/L period then by employee.

Criteria: Select which G/L periods to include, filter by employee range, union, or job, and choose whether 
to include voided cheques.

Key Information: The G/L period shown is when the cheque was posted to accounting, which may differ from the 
cheque date or pay period ending date. The total gross earnings should match your payroll expense in the G/L 
for that period. This is your primary reconciliation report for payroll.

When to Use This Report:
• Reconcile payroll to the general ledger each month
• Verify that all cheques are posted to the correct period
• Prepare month-end payroll expense documentation
• Calculate total payroll costs by accounting period
• Support financial statement preparation
• Audit payroll posting accuracy

Good to Know: Always run this as part of month-end close. The total should tie exactly to your G/L payroll 
expense accounts for the period. If they don't match, you have a posting error or reconciliation issue to 
investigate. Keep this report with your monthly close documentation.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cheques by Union
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists payroll cheques organized by union or trade. Track union payroll, verify union dues deductions, and prepare union remittance reports.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See payroll cheques grouped by union or trade classification. Perfect for tracking 
union payroll costs and preparing union remittance documentation.

What You'll See: Unions with their members' cheques listed underneath. Shows employee names, cheque dates, 
gross earnings, union dues deducted, and net pay. Union subtotals show total payroll and total dues by 
union. Organized by union code then by employee.

Criteria: Select specific unions or all unions, choose date ranges or G/L periods, filter by job, and set 
minimum pay thresholds if desired.

When to Use This Report:
• Calculate total payroll by union for cost analysis
• Verify union dues deductions before remittance
• Prepare documentation for union remittance payments
• Track labour costs by trade or union
• Support union reporting requirements
• Analyze payroll distribution across unions

Good to Know: Use this before preparing union remittance payments to verify the amounts being remitted. The 
union dues subtotals should match your liability accounts. Most unions require detailed reporting of hours 
worked and dues collected - this provides that detail.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cheque Record
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Prints the actual payroll cheque format with stub detail. Use this to reprint lost cheques or create manual cheques.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Print actual paycheques in the standard cheque format including all stub detail. 
Reprint lost or damaged cheques or create manual adjustment cheques.

What You'll See: A formatted cheque with the employee's name, net amount, cheque number, and date in the 
cheque portion. The stub shows all earnings, deductions, and year-to-date totals in the standard payroll 
stub format. Matches what employees receive on payday.

Criteria: Select specific cheque numbers to print, choose employees, or select by date range. Can print 
individual cheques or batches.

Key Information: This prints on cheque stock (blank cheque forms). Make sure you have the correct cheque 
stock loaded before printing. The format matches your standard paycheque layout with earnings detail on the 
left stub and deductions detail on the right stub.

When to Use This Report:
• Reprint lost or damaged employee paycheques
• Print manual adjustment cheques
• Replace voided cheques that need to be reissued
• Print cheques for employees who were missed in the regular payroll run
• Create paper backup copies of EFT payments if required

Good to Know: Make sure you're printing on the correct cheque stock - test with a blank sheet first. When 
reprinting lost cheques, make sure the original was voided in the system. For manual cheques, verify the 
cheque number sequence doesn't conflict with regular payroll.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cheques by Form Number
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists cheques in cheque number sequence. Quick way to find specific cheque numbers or verify sequential numbering.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See cheques listed in cheque number order. Useful for locating specific cheques, 
verifying cheque number sequences, and tracking cheque usage.

What You'll See: Cheques listed in cheque number sequence showing employee names, dates, gross pay, 
deductions, and net pay. Sequential numbering makes it easy to spot missing or voided cheques in the 
sequence. Organized by cheque number.

Criteria: Enter a cheque number range (from/to), or filter by date range, employee, or G/L period. Choose 
whether to include voided cheques.

When to Use This Report:
• Look up details for a specific cheque number
• Verify sequential cheque numbering
• Find missing cheque numbers in a sequence
• Track cheque stock usage
• Research cheques when you only have a cheque number
• Reconcile cheque register to bank statements

Good to Know: This is the simplest cheque report - just a straight list by cheque number. Use it when other 
groupings (by employee, period, etc.) aren't relevant. The sequential numbering helps you spot gaps that 
might indicate missing or stolen cheque stock.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Reprint Cheque Attachments
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Reprints the detailed cheque stub/advice slip without the actual cheque. Provide employees with earnings detail when they need a replacement stub.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Print just the cheque stub detail (earnings and deductions) without printing an 
actual cheque. Give employees replacement stubs when they've lost the original.

What You'll See: The detailed cheque stub format showing all earnings (regular, overtime, travel, etc.), all 
deductions (taxes, CPP, EI, union dues, etc.), and year-to-date totals. This is what appears on the employee 
cheque stub, but printed separately without the cheque portion.

Criteria: Select specific employees and date ranges, choose individual cheques, or select by G/L period. Can 
print for one employee or multiple employees at once.

When to Use This Report:
• Provide replacement pay stubs to employees who lost theirs
• Give employees detailed earnings breakdown without reprinting cheques
• Create documentation for employee files or HR records
• Provide pay detail for loan applications or other employee needs
• Print historical pay stubs from past periods

Good to Know: This is safer than reprinting actual cheques when employees just need the detail. It provides 
all the same information as the original cheque stub but doesn't create a negotiable cheque. Useful for 
employees who use direct deposit but still need pay detail documentation.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cheque Incentive Accruals
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows incentive pay accruals by employee and cheque. Track safety bonuses, production incentives, and other accrued incentive payments.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track incentive pay accruals including safety bonuses, production incentives, and 
other performance-based compensation that accrues over time.

What You'll See: Employees with their incentive accruals shown by type - personal safety, group safety, 
production bonuses, etc. Shows amounts accrued, amounts paid, and balances owing. Typically organized by 
employee or by incentive type.

Criteria: Select employees and date ranges, choose specific incentive types, filter by union or job, and set 
minimum accrual thresholds.

Key Information: Incentive pay often accrues throughout the year and pays out quarterly or annually. This 
report tracks what each employee has earned but not yet been paid. Common incentives include safety bonuses 
(individual and crew), production bonuses, and performance rewards. The balances shown are liabilities until 
paid.

When to Use This Report:
• Calculate total incentive liabilities for financial reporting
• Prepare quarterly or annual incentive payouts
• Verify incentive calculations before payment
• Track safety bonus accruals by employee
• Answer employee questions about accrued incentives
• Support year-end accrual journal entries

Good to Know: Run this before incentive payout periods to verify amounts. The accruals shown here should 
match your incentive liability accounts in the G/L. Many companies pay safety bonuses quarterly - this helps 
you calculate who's eligible and how much they've earned.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cheque WCB Assessments
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows WCB (Workers Compensation Board) assessments by cheque. Calculate employer WCB costs for remittance to provincial WCB offices.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Calculate WCB (Workers Compensation) assessments based on payroll. Shows assessable 
earnings and WCB costs by employee and rate class for remittance to WCB.

What You'll See: Employees grouped by WCB rate class showing their assessable earnings and calculated WCB 
assessment amounts. Each rate class has a different WCB rate (e.g., office workers at 0.5%, carpenters at 
3.5%). Shows totals by rate class and grand totals. Organized by WCB classification.

Criteria: Select date ranges or G/L periods, choose specific WCB rate classes, filter by job or province, 
and set minimum earning thresholds.

Key Information: WCB rates vary by occupation and province. Higher-risk jobs (construction, heavy equipment) 
have higher rates than office work. Not all earnings are assessable - some components like certain 
allowances may be excluded. The total assessments shown are what you owe the provincial WCB office.

When to Use This Report:
• Calculate monthly or annual WCB assessments for remittance
• Verify WCB calculations before payment
• Analyze WCB costs by rate classification
• Support WCB audits and reporting requirements
• Calculate true labour burden costs including WCB
• Reconcile WCB liability accounts to G/L

Good to Know: WCB is an employer cost (not deducted from employee pay) that can be significant - often 2-5% 
of payroll depending on industry. Run this monthly to track WCB liability. The assessments by rate class 
help you understand which occupations drive your WCB costs.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cheque Timesheet Fringe
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows fringe benefit costs associated with timesheets. Track vacation, statutory holiday, and other fringe costs accrued on timesheet hours.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track fringe benefit costs that accrue based on timesheet hours. Shows vacation pay, 
statutory holiday pay, and other fringes accrued on worked hours.

What You'll See: Timesheets with their associated fringe costs - vacation accruals, statutory holiday
