accruals, safety pay, and other benefits that accrue based on hours worked. Shows the base hours, the fringe 
rate, and the fringe cost. Organized by employee or by job.

Criteria: Select employees and date ranges, choose which fringe types to include (vacation, statutory, 
safety, etc.), filter by job or cost centre, and set minimum threshold amounts.

Key Information: Fringe costs accrue as employees work but aren't paid until later. For example, vacation 
pay accrues at 4% or 6% on each hour worked, but pays out when the employee takes vacation. This report 
shows those accruing costs so you can properly track the true cost of labour on jobs. Essential for accurate 
job costing.

When to Use This Report:
• Calculate true labour costs on jobs including fringes
• Track vacation and statutory holiday accruals by job
• Verify fringe cost calculations in job costing
• Support job cost reporting with full labour burden
• Analyze fringe costs as percentage of base labour
• Prepare accrual entries for fringe liabilities

Good to Know: Fringe costs typically add 10-20% to base labour costs (vacation 4-6%, statutory holidays 4%, 
safety bonuses varies). These costs must be included in job costing for accurate profitability. The accruals 
shown here should match your fringe liability accounts in the G/L.

reportTrainingRecords.name: RRSP & Pension by Employee
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows RRSP and pension contributions by employee. Track retirement plan contributions for both employee and employer portions.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track RRSP and pension plan contributions showing both employee deductions and 
employer matching contributions. Essential for pension plan administration and remittance.

What You'll See: Employees with their retirement plan contributions detailed by cheque. Shows employee RRSP 
deductions, employer RRSP contributions, employee pension deductions, employer pension contributions, and 
totals. Organized by employee with period and year-to-date totals.

Criteria: Select employees and date ranges, choose specific plan types (RRSP, pension, or both), filter by 
union or job, and set minimum contribution thresholds.

Key Information: This tracks both employee contributions (deducted from pay) and employer contributions 
(matched or additional). The totals shown here should match your pension liability accounts and the amounts 
you remit to the pension plan administrator. Different unions may have different pension plans.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare monthly pension plan remittances
• Verify RRSP contribution amounts before remitting to plan administrator
• Track year-to-date contributions for individual employees
• Calculate total employer pension costs
• Support employee RRSP contribution receipts
• Reconcile pension liability accounts

Good to Know: Most pension plans require monthly remittances of both employee and employer contributions. Use 
this report to calculate the total remittance amount. The year-to-date totals are important for individual 
employee RRSP receipts at year-end.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cheques by EFT Batch
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists electronic funds transfer (direct deposit) payments by batch. Verify EFT amounts before transmitting to the bank.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See all direct deposit payments grouped by EFT batch. Verify amounts and employee 
details before transmitting the EFT file to your bank.

What You'll See: EFT batches with their payment details - employee names, bank account information (masked), 
net pay amounts, and batch totals. Shows everything that will be in the electronic payment file sent to the 
bank. Organized by EFT batch number.

Criteria: Select specific EFT batch numbers, choose date ranges, or filter by employee. Can show approved 
batches only or include pending batches.

Key Information: EFT batches must be approved before the electronic file is sent to the bank. This report 
shows exactly what will be transmitted - verify all amounts and account numbers are correct. The batch total 
is the total amount that will be debited from your payroll bank account.

When to Use This Report:
• Verify EFT payment details before transmission to bank
• Review batch totals against available bank balance
• Document EFT payments for payroll records
• Verify employee bank account information is correct
• Research direct deposit issues or questions
• Support bank reconciliation of EFT transactions

Good to Know: Always review this report before transmitting EFT files to the bank. Once transmitted, 
corrections are difficult. Make sure your bank account can cover the batch total. Keep copies of this report 
as documentation of what was transmitted to the bank.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cheque Summary by Employee
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Aggregates cheque data in a summary format similar to employee master records. Shows totals rather than individual cheque detail.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See summarized payroll data for employees in a format similar to their master record. 
Shows totals and year-to-date amounts without individual cheque detail.

What You'll See: Employee summary records showing total hours, total earnings, total deductions, and 
year-to-date accumulations. Format mirrors the employee master record but shows actual paid amounts rather 
than setup information. No individual cheque detail - just aggregated totals.

Criteria: Select employees and date ranges to summarize, choose which accumulations to include (YTD, period, 
etc.), and filter by union or job.

When to Use This Report:
• Review employee year-to-date totals without cheque-by-cheque detail
• Compare actual paid amounts to employee master records
• Prepare high-level employee earnings summaries
• Verify YTD accumulations for multiple employees
• Support year-end reporting and T4 preparation
• Analyze payroll trends without excessive detail

Good to Know: This is a condensed view - great when you need summary totals but individual cheque detail 
would be too much. The format matches employee records making it familiar to payroll staff. Use the detailed 
Cheques by Employee report when you need to see individual paycheques.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Cheques by Cheque Amount
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists cheques sorted by net pay amount. Useful for bank reconciliation and identifying unusually large or small payments.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See cheques sorted by net pay amount from largest to smallest (or vice versa). 
Helpful for bank reconciliation and spotting unusual payment amounts.

What You'll See: Cheques listed by net pay amount showing employee names, cheque numbers, dates, gross 
earnings, deductions, and net pay. Sorted by amount making it easy to find specific dollar values or spot 
outliers. Can sort largest to smallest or smallest to largest.

Criteria: Choose date ranges or G/L periods, set minimum and maximum amount thresholds, select employees, and 
choose sort order (ascending or descending by amount).

When to Use This Report:
• Find cheques matching specific dollar amounts for bank reconciliation
• Identify unusually large or small paycheques for review
• Locate outstanding cheques by amount when reconciling
• Verify cheque amounts against bank statements
• Spot potential payroll errors by finding outlier amounts
• Research specific payment amounts quickly

Good to Know: When your bank statement shows a specific amount cleared but you're not sure which cheque it 
is, this report helps you find it quickly. Also useful for identifying data entry errors - a $10,000 cheque 
that should have been $1,000 will stand out at the top of the list.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Pay Periods by Employee
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows pay period summaries by employee. Review earnings and deductions summarized by pay period rather than by individual cheque.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See employee earnings summarized by pay period. Shows total earnings, deductions, and 
net pay for each pay period without individual cheque detail.

What You'll See: Employees with their pay periods listed, showing period ending dates, total hours, gross 
earnings, total deductions, and net pay for each period. Provides a period-by-period view of employee pay 
without the detail of individual cheques. Organized by employee then by pay period.

Criteria: Select employees and date ranges, choose specific pay periods, filter by union or job, and set 
minimum earnings thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Review employee pay period by period
• Track pay trends over multiple periods
• Verify period totals without cheque-level detail
• Analyze employee earnings patterns by pay period
• Prepare period-based earnings summaries
• Support payroll variance analysis by period

Good to Know: This is useful when you want to see pay by period rather than by individual cheque. If 
employees receive multiple cheques in a period (regular plus bonus, for example), this combines them into 
period totals for a cleaner view.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Union Remittance Spreadsheet
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Creates an Excel spreadsheet for union remittances formatted according to union requirements. Export remittance data in the format required by each union.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate union remittance spreadsheets in the specific format required by each union. 
Export dues, pension, and benefit remittance data formatted for union submission.

What You'll See: An Excel spreadsheet formatted according to the selected union's requirements. Typically 
includes employee details (name, SIN, classification), hours worked, earnings, union dues, pension 
contributions, health and welfare contributions, and other union-specific items. Format varies by union.

Criteria: Select the remittance type (which union), choose the remittance period (usually monthly), and 
select which employees or jobs to include.

Key Information: Each union has specific reporting requirements and formats for monthly remittances. This 
report is configured to match those requirements. The spreadsheet can typically be uploaded directly to the 
union's reporting portal or emailed with the remittance payment. Includes both employee deductions and 
employer contributions.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare monthly union remittance reports
• Submit required data to union offices
• Create union remittance payment backup documentation
• Verify dues and benefit amounts before remitting
• Support union audits with detailed remittance records
• Upload data to union reporting portals

Good to Know: Different unions have different formats - make sure you select the correct remittance type. The 
spreadsheet is typically due monthly along with the remittance payment. Unions use this data to credit 
member accounts for pension and benefits.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Uncashed Cheques
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists payroll cheques that have been issued but not yet cashed. Track outstanding cheques for bank reconciliation and follow-up.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Identify payroll cheques that have been issued but haven't cleared the bank yet. 
Essential for bank reconciliation and tracking down old uncashed cheques.

What You'll See: Cheques that have been issued but not marked as cashed/cleared, showing employee names, 
cheque numbers, dates, amounts, and how many days the cheque has been outstanding. Sorted by age (oldest 
first) or by employee. Shows total dollar value of uncashed cheques.

Criteria: Set a cutoff date (show cheques issued before this date), choose employees, set minimum age 
threshold (like 30 days), and filter by minimum cheque amount.

Key Information: Cheques become stale-dated (too old to cash) after 6 months in most jurisdictions. This 
report helps identify cheques that need follow-up before they become stale. Old uncashed cheques may indicate 
lost cheques, incorrect addresses, or terminated employees who need to be contacted.

When to Use This Report:
• Perform monthly bank reconciliation
• Identify old cheques that need employee follow-up
• Find stale-dated cheques before they expire
• Track outstanding payroll cheques for cash management
• Verify that terminated employees cashed their final cheques
• Support year-end bank reconciliation

Good to Know: Run this monthly as part of bank reconciliation. Follow up on cheques older than 60-90 days - 
contact the employee to reissue if lost. Very old uncashed cheques may need to be voided and the funds 
escheated to the province as unclaimed property.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Reprint Employee Cheque Advice
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Reprints employee cheque advice/stubs without the actual cheque. Provide employees with replacement pay documentation.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Reprint the employee pay advice (cheque stub detail) without creating an actual 
cheque. Provide replacement pay documentation when employees need it.

What You'll See: The employee pay advice format showing earnings breakdown, all deductions, net pay, and 
year-to-date totals. This is the same information that appears on the employee cheque stub, printed 
separately for employee records.

Criteria: Select specific employees, choose cheques by date range or cheque number, and optionally filter by 
G/L period or union.

When to Use This Report:
• Provide replacement pay stubs to employees who lost theirs
• Give employees pay detail for loans, mortgages, or other applications
• Create pay documentation for employee personnel files
• Provide historical pay information for tax or legal purposes
• Give employees year-end pay summaries
• Support direct deposit employees who need paper documentation

Good to Know: This is the same as Reprint Cheque Attachments (report f) - both provide employee pay detail 
without creating negotiable cheques. Safer than reprinting actual cheques when employees just need the 
earnings detail. Particularly useful for direct deposit employees who don't receive paper cheques.

reportTrainingRecords.name: P/R Costs by Union
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows total payroll costs broken down by union. Includes wages plus employer burden costs like CPP, EI, WCB, and benefits.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Calculate total true payroll costs by union including not just wages but also 
employer burden costs (CPP, EI, WCB, benefits, etc.). See the complete cost picture.

What You'll See: Unions with their total costs broken down - gross wages paid, employer CPP, employer EI, 
WCB assessments, vacation costs, statutory holiday costs, benefits, and total burden. Shows both the direct 
wage cost and the employer overhead costs. Organized by union.

Criteria: Select unions and date ranges, choose which cost components to include, filter by job, and set 
minimum threshold amounts.

Key Information: This shows true fully-loaded labour costs. An employee making $50,000 actually costs you 
more when you add CPP, EI, WCB, vacation, statutory holidays, benefits, and other burden costs. This report 
shows that complete picture by union. Essential for accurate job costing and bidding.

When to Use This Report:
• Calculate true fully-loaded labour costs by union
• Determine labour burden rates for job costing
• Analyze total payroll costs including overhead
• Compare cost structures across different unions
• Support labour cost budgeting and bidding
• Calculate average burden percentage by union

Good to Know: Many companies only look at gross wages when analyzing labour costs, but the true cost is wages 
plus burden. Depending on the union and benefits package, burden can add 20-40% to the base wage. Use these 
complete costs for accurate job costing and estimating.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Province Payroll Tax
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Calculates provincial payroll taxes (like Ontario EHT, Quebec QHT). Shows employer payroll tax liability by province.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Calculate provincial payroll taxes such as Ontario Employer Health Tax (EHT) or 
Quebec Health Services Fund. Shows employer tax liability based on total payroll by province.

What You'll See: Payroll totals by province with calculated provincial payroll tax. Shows total assessable 
payroll (some provinces have exemption thresholds), applicable tax rate, and tax owing. Organized by 
province. Includes both remittance amounts and year-to-date totals.

Criteria: Select the reporting period (monthly, quarterly, annual depending on province), choose which 
provinces to include, and filter by date range or G/L period.

Key Information: Provincial payroll taxes vary by province. Ontario has EHT (varying rates based on payroll 
level with exemptions for small payrolls). Quebec has Health Services Fund. Manitoba, Newfoundland have 
their own versions. The province is determined by where the work was performed, not employee residence. This 
is an employer cost, not a deduction from employee pay.

When to Use This Report:
• Calculate monthly or annual provincial payroll tax remittances
• Verify provincial tax calculations before payment
• Track payroll tax costs by province
• Support multi-province payroll tax reporting
• Reconcile provincial tax liabilities to G/L
• Respond to provincial tax authority inquiries

Good to Know: Each province has different rates, exemptions, and filing frequencies. Ontario EHT, for example, 
has exemptions up to $1M of payroll. Make sure you understand your obligations in each province where you 
have employees. These are additional employer costs on top of CPP, EI, and WCB.

reportTrainingRecords.name: PD7A - Current Source Deductions
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Prepares the PD7A form showing current payroll source deductions (CPP, EI, income tax) for Canada Revenue Agency remittance.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate the PD7A statement of account for current source deductions. Shows CPP, EI, 
and income tax deducted and owing to Canada Revenue Agency (CRA).

What You'll See: The PD7A format showing employee CPP contributions, employer CPP contributions, employee EI 
premiums, employer EI premiums, federal income tax deducted, provincial income tax deducted, and the total 
amount due. Format matches the official CRA PD7A form.

Criteria: Select the remittance period (monthly, semi-monthly, quarterly, or annual depending on your 
remitter type), choose the specific period to report, and select book or company.

Key Information: The PD7A reports source deductions that must be remitted to CRA. Most companies remit 
monthly (by the 15th of the following month). The total shown is what you owe CRA for that period. The 
report breaks down employee contributions, employer contributions, and tax deductions separately as required 
by CRA.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare monthly source deduction remittances to CRA
• Complete the PD7A form for CRA reporting
• Verify source deduction calculations before remitting
• Reconcile payroll tax liabilities to G/L accounts
• Document CRA remittances for your records
• Respond to CRA inquiries about source deductions

Good to Know: Run this for each remittance period and keep it with your CRA payment records. The remittance 
is due by the 15th of the month following the pay period. Late payments incur penalties and interest. Make 
sure the amounts match your liability accounts in the G/L.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Union Dues by Province
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows union dues deducted grouped by province. Essential for provincial union remittances when unions are organized by province.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track union dues deductions broken down by province. Required when union structures 
are provincial and remittances must be made to each provincial union office separately.

What You'll See: Provinces with their union dues totals - shows employees working in each province, dues 
deducted, and totals by province and union. Organized by province then by union within province.

Criteria: Select date ranges or G/L periods, choose specific provinces, filter by union, and set minimum 
threshold amounts for reporting.

Key Information: Some unions are organized provincially, requiring separate remittances to each provincial 
office. Employees are assigned to provinces based on where they work, not where they live. This report 
calculates the remittance amount for each provincial union office.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare provincial union dues remittances
• Calculate amounts owing to each provincial union office
• Track labour costs and dues by province
• Verify provincial dues deductions before remitting
• Support multi-province union reporting requirements
• Reconcile provincial union dues liability accounts

Good to Know: Not all unions require provincial breakdown, but construction unions often do. The province is 
determined by the job location, not employee residence. If you have jobs in multiple provinces, you'll need 
this report to properly remit to each provincial union office.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee List
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists all employees with basic information including names, employee numbers, status, and contact details. Your master employee directory.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Get a complete list of all employees with their basic information. Your master 
employee directory for reference, verification, and reporting.

What You'll See: Employees listed with names, employee numbers, SIN (masked or full depending on security), 
addresses, phone numbers, hire dates, termination dates (if applicable), union/trade, and employment status 
(active, terminated, on leave). Organized by employee number or name.

Criteria: Select specific employees or ranges, filter by employment status (active only, terminated, all), 
choose unions or trades, filter by hire date ranges, and select which information fields to display.

When to Use This Report:
• Create employee contact lists or directories
• Verify employee information for HR purposes
• Export employee data for other systems
• Review employment status across the workforce
• Prepare employee lists for safety meetings or communications
• Audit employee master file data

Good to Know: This is the simplest employee report - basic directory information without payroll or financial 
detail. Great for creating phone lists, verifying addresses, or getting a headcount. Filter to active only 
for your current workforce, or include terminated to see historical employees.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Comprehensive employee report showing detailed information about employee records. More detailed than the Employee List - includes rates, accumulations, and employment details.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate detailed employee reports with comprehensive information beyond basic 
directory data. Includes employment details, pay rates, year-to-date accumulations, and more.

What You'll See: Employee records with extensive detail - personal information, employment dates and status, 
union and occupation information, all pay rate components, year-to-date earnings and deductions, accrued 
liabilities (vacation, statutory, incentives), and current balances. Much more comprehensive than the basic 
Employee List. Organized by employee.

Criteria: Select employees or ranges, filter by employment status, union, or occupation, choose which 
sections to include (personal, rates, accumulations, etc.).

When to Use This Report:
• Comprehensive employee information reviews
• Audit employee records for accuracy and completeness
• Prepare detailed employee documentation for HR purposes
• Review employee pay structures and accumulations
• Support employee termination processing with complete data
• Provide detailed employee information for audits

Good to Know: This is the full employee report - everything about each employee in one place. Use the simpler 
Employee List when you just need contact information. This report is useful when you need the complete picture 
including rates, YTD totals, and liabilities.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee WCB Remittance
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows employee taxable and assessable earnings for WCB remittance. Calculate total earnings, WCB assessable amounts, and remittance by employee.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate WCB (Workers Compensation Board) remittance information by employee. Shows 
taxable earnings, assessable earnings, and WCB remittance amounts.

What You'll See: Employees with their earnings broken down - total taxable earnings, WCB assessable earnings 
(some earnings may not be assessable), applicable WCB rate based on classification, and calculated WCB 
remittance amount. Shows both employee detail and totals. Organized by employee or by WCB class.

Criteria: Select employees and date ranges, filter by WCB classification or province, choose whether to show 
only assessable earnings or all earnings, and set minimum earning thresholds.

Key Information: Not all earnings are WCB assessable - some allowances or benefits may be excluded. This shows 
both total earnings and the portion that's assessable for WCB. The WCB rate depends on the employee's 
classification (office, construction, high-risk, etc.). The calculated remittance is what you owe WCB for each 
employee.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare WCB remittance calculations by employee
• Verify WCB assessable earnings are calculated correctly
• Support WCB audits with employee-level detail
• Track WCB costs at the employee level
• Calculate total WCB remittance amounts
• Analyze WCB cost drivers by employee classification

Good to Know: WCB audits often request this level of detail. The difference between taxable and assessable 
earnings shows non-assessable components. Make sure employees are in the correct WCB class - incorrect 
classification leads to incorrect assessments and potential penalties.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Occupation List
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists employees grouped by occupation/trade. See your workforce organized by job classification with rates and union information.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See employees organized by occupation or trade classification. Perfect for analyzing 
workforce composition, managing union requirements, and tracking skilled trades.

What You'll See: Occupations/trades with their employees listed underneath. Shows employee names, pay rates, 
union affiliation, certification levels (journeyman, apprentice, etc.), hire dates, and employment status. 
Organized by occupation then by employee. Includes headcounts by occupation.

Criteria: Select specific occupations or all, filter by union, choose employment status (active, terminated, 
all), and set certification level filters (journeyman, apprentice, etc.).

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze workforce composition by trade or occupation
• Track skilled trades headcount and certification levels
• Verify journeyman to apprentice ratios for union compliance
• Plan labour requirements by occupation
• Review pay rates within each occupation
• Identify skills gaps or training needs by trade

Good to Know: Essential for construction and trades-based businesses. Many unions have requirements for 
journeyman to apprentice ratios - this report helps you track those. Also useful for planning job staffing 
when you know what trades you need.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Owed Amounts
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows amounts owed to employees including accrued vacation, statutory pay, incentives, and advances. Track all employee liabilities.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track all amounts owed to employees - accrued vacation, statutory holiday pay, 
incentive bonuses, and outstanding advances. Your complete employee liability report.

What You'll See: Employees with their owed amounts broken down - vacation pay accrued, statutory holiday pay 
accrued, safety incentives earned but not paid, last incentive payment date, outstanding advances to be 
repaid, and totals. Shows both amounts owed TO employees and amounts owed BY employees. Organized by employee.

Criteria: Select employees and filter by minimum owed amounts, choose which liability types to include 
(vacation, statutory, incentives, advances), and filter by union or employment status.

Key Information: This tracks accrued liabilities - money employees have earned but not yet been paid. Vacation 
and statutory pay accrue over time and pay out when taken or at termination. Safety incentives accrue and pay 
quarterly or annually. Advances are the opposite - amounts paid to employees that need to be repaid through 
payroll deductions.

When to Use This Report:
• Calculate total vacation and statutory pay liabilities for financial reporting
• Prepare quarterly or annual incentive payout calculations
• Answer employee questions about accrued vacation or incentive balances
• Verify liabilities match G/L vacation and incentive accounts
• Calculate final pay amounts for terminating employees
• Track outstanding employee advances and repayments

Good to Know: Run this at month-end to verify your accrued vacation and incentive liabilities. The totals 
should match your G/L liability accounts. When employees terminate, these balances must be paid out on their 
final cheque - this report shows exactly what's owed.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Rates Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows all hourly pay rates and components for each employee. Displays base rates, premium rates, and special pay components.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See all pay rate components for employees - base hourly rates, overtime rates, travel 
rates, and premium rates. Your complete employee rate card.

What You'll See: Employees with their complete pay structure - regular hourly rate, overtime rate (typically 
1.5x), double time rate (2x), travel rate, shift premiums, lead hand premiums, foreman rates, and any other 
special pay components. Shows effective dates for rate changes. Organized by employee.

Criteria: Select employees or ranges, filter by union or occupation, choose which pay components to display, 
and filter by employment status.

When to Use This Report:
• Verify employee pay rates for payroll processing
• Review rate structures across the workforce
• Audit pay rates for union contract compliance
• Prepare documentation for rate changes or union negotiations
• Calculate labour costs for job estimating
• Answer employee questions about their pay rates

Good to Know: This shows the complete pay structure, not just base rates. Important for understanding total 
labour costs - overtime at 1.5x and double time at 2x add up quickly. Use this to verify that rates match 
union agreements or employment contracts.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Missed Safety Pay
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Identifies employees who missed safety bonus payments they should have received. Track safety pay that needs to be corrected or paid.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Find employees who were eligible for safety bonuses but didn't receive them. Identify 
missing safety pay that needs to be corrected and paid.

What You'll See: Employees who worked during safety bonus periods but didn't receive their safety pay. Shows 
the period worked, hours that should have earned safety pay, expected safety amount, and why it was missed 
(if determinable). Organized by employee and period.

Criteria: Select the safety pay period to review, choose employees or groups, filter by job, and set minimum 
hour thresholds for eligibility.

Key Information: Safety bonuses often have eligibility requirements (minimum hours, no incidents, etc.). This 
report identifies employees who met the criteria but didn't get paid - usually due to payroll processing 
errors, missed periods, or data entry issues. These need to be corrected with adjustment cheques.

When to Use This Report:
• Audit safety bonus payment accuracy after each safety pay period
• Identify employees owed safety pay adjustments
• Verify safety pay calculations were processed correctly
• Prepare adjustment cheques for missed safety payments
• Respond to employee inquiries about missing safety pay
• Quality control safety bonus processing

Good to Know: Run this after each safety bonus payout to catch errors early. Safety pay is important to 
employees and missing payments damage morale. Fix any missed payments quickly with adjustment cheques. Common 
reasons for missed safety pay include new hires not yet in the system or employees who changed jobs mid-period.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Anomaly Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Identifies questionable or inconsistent employee record data. Find data quality issues that need attention or correction.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Identify potential data quality issues and inconsistencies in employee records. Find 
problems that could cause payroll errors or reporting issues.

What You'll See: Employees with questionable data conditions such as: missing addresses, invalid SINs, 
conflicting dates (termination before hire), active employees with no recent pay, missing union information, 
invalid pay rates, incomplete tax forms, or other data integrity issues. Shows the anomaly type and affected 
fields. Organized by anomaly type or employee.

Criteria: Choose which anomaly types to check (all or specific types), select employees or ranges, filter by 
employment status, and set severity levels (critical, warning, informational).

Key Information: Data quality issues can cause payroll errors, missed deductions, tax problems, or reporting 
failures. This report finds problems proactively so you can fix them before they cause issues. Common anomalies 
include incomplete addresses (can't mail T4s), invalid SINs (CRA reporting fails), missing rates (won't 
calculate pay correctly).

When to Use This Report:
• Audit employee data quality before important processes (year-end, payroll, etc.)
• Find and fix employee record problems proactively
• Verify data integrity after employee setup or changes
• Prepare for CRA reporting by finding SIN or address issues
• Clean up employee master file data
• Identify employees needing updated information

Good to Know: Run this monthly to catch problems early. Very important to run before year-end to ensure T4s 
can be printed and mailed. Many anomalies are simple fixes (add an address, update a rate) but will cause 
major problems if not corrected.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Earnings & Costs Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows employee earnings plus employer costs like CPP, EI, and WCB. See the complete cost of employing each person including burden.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Calculate the true fully-loaded cost of each employee including base earnings plus all 
employer burden costs (CPP, EI, WCB, benefits, etc.). Understand total labour costs.

What You'll See: Employees with their gross earnings broken down by type (regular, overtime, etc.) plus all 
employer costs - employer CPP contributions, employer EI premiums, WCB assessments, vacation accruals, 
statutory pay accruals, benefit costs, and total burden. Shows both the amount paid to the employee and the 
additional employer costs. Organized by employee.

Criteria: Select employees and date ranges, choose which cost components to include, filter by job or union, 
and set minimum earnings thresholds.

Key Information: This shows the complete picture - an employee making $50,000 might cost you $65,000 when you 
include all employer costs. Burden typically runs 20-40% depending on benefits and WCB rates. Essential for 
accurate job costing, budgeting, and understanding true labour costs.

When to Use This Report:
• Calculate true fully-loaded labour costs by employee
• Determine average burden percentages for job costing
• Analyze total cost of employment including all burden
• Support labour cost budgeting with complete cost data
• Compare employee costs including all employer contributions
• Prepare comprehensive labour cost reports for management

Good to Know: Many people only think about gross wages, but burden adds significantly to labour costs. Use 
these complete costs for job estimating and budgeting. The burden percentage varies by employee - higher 
earners hit CPP and EI maximums reducing burden %, while some occupations have higher WCB rates.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Tax & No Tax Earnings Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows earnings broken down by taxable and non-taxable components. Essential for tax reporting and understanding employee taxation.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Analyze employee earnings separated into taxable and non-taxable components. Critical 
for tax reporting, T4 preparation, and understanding how earnings are taxed.

What You'll See: Employees with earnings broken down into taxable components (regular pay, overtime, bonuses, 
etc.) and non-taxable components (non-taxable allowances, tax-exempt benefits, etc.). Shows CPP pensionable 
earnings, EI insurable earnings, and income tax taxable earnings separately as they may differ. Organized by 
employee with year-to-date totals.

Criteria: Select employees and date ranges, choose which tax categories to display, filter by union or job, 
and set minimum earning thresholds.

Key Information: Not all earnings are taxed the same way. Some components are taxable for income tax but not 
CPP. Some are taxable for CPP but not EI. Understanding these differences is critical for accurate tax 
reporting. This report shows which earnings fall into which categories. Essential for T4 preparation and tax 
compliance.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare year-end T4 tax forms
• Verify taxable versus non-taxable earnings calculations
• Audit tax withholding accuracy
• Understand CPP, EI, and income tax bases for employees
• Support tax reporting and compliance
• Research employee tax questions or CRA inquiries

Good to Know: The three key taxable earning bases are: CPP pensionable (used to calculate CPP), EI insurable 
(used to calculate EI), and income tax taxable (used to calculate income tax). These amounts can differ. For 
example, some allowances are taxable for income tax but not CPP or EI.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Month End Owing Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows liabilities owed to employees at the end of a G/L period. Essential for month-end accrual entries and financial reporting.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Calculate employee liabilities at month-end for financial reporting. Shows accrued 
vacation, statutory pay, incentives, and other amounts owed at period-end.

What You'll See: Employees with their liability balances as of the selected month-end - vacation pay accrued, 
statutory holiday pay accrued, safety and other incentives earned but unpaid, and any other employee 
liabilities. Shows opening balances, accruals during the period, amounts paid, and ending balances. Organized 
by employee with period totals.

Criteria: Select the G/L period end date, choose which liability types to include, filter by employee or 
union, and set minimum balance thresholds.

Key Information: This is your month-end accrual report for employee liabilities. The totals should match your 
G/L liability accounts for vacation, statutory pay, and incentives. Use these amounts for month-end accrual 
journal entries. Shows balances as of a specific point in time, unlike the general Employee Owed Amounts 
report which shows current balances.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare month-end accrual journal entries for employee liabilities
• Verify liability balances match G/L accounts at period-end
• Support financial statement preparation with liability detail
• Calculate total employee liabilities for balance sheet reporting
• Track liability movement period over period
• Provide auditors with employee liability documentation

Good to Know: Run this at month-end and keep copies for your permanent records. The ending balances become 
next month's opening balances. These liabilities must be on your balance sheet - vacation and statutory pay 
liabilities can be significant, especially with a large workforce.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Rates by Job Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows employee pay rates organized by job. See which employees worked on which jobs and at what rates.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See employee pay rates organized by job or project. Track which employees work on 
which jobs and their applicable rates for those jobs.

What You'll See: Jobs with their employees and pay rates. Shows employee names, their base rates, overtime 
rates, and any job-specific rate adjustments or premiums. Some employees may have different rates on different 
jobs (certified rates, prevailing wage rates, etc.). Organized by job then by employee.

Criteria: Select specific jobs or ranges, choose employees, filter by union or occupation, and set date ranges 
for when employees worked on jobs.

Key Information: Some jobs require specific pay rates - prevailing wage projects, certified rate jobs, or 
union agreements tied to specific job types. This report shows the actual rates used on each job, which may 
differ from the employee's base rate. Essential for job costing accuracy and compliance with prevailing wage 
requirements.

When to Use This Report:
• Verify correct rates were used on specific jobs
• Audit prevailing wage or certified rate compliance
• Calculate accurate labour costs by job
• Review which employees worked on which projects
• Prepare job-specific payroll reports for clients
• Support prevailing wage audits with rate documentation

Good to Know: Particularly important for government or prevailing wage jobs where rates are mandated. The rates 
shown here should match job requirements. If an employee's base rate is lower than the job's prevailing wage, 
they should be paid the higher prevailing wage rate on that job.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Local Hire & Indigenous Status Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Tracks local hire and Indigenous employee status. Support community benefit requirements and Indigenous employment reporting.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track employees by local hire status and Indigenous identity. Support community benefit 
agreements, Indigenous employment commitments, and related reporting requirements.

What You'll See: Employees with their local hire status (local to the project area or imported), Indigenous 
status, residence location, and hours/earnings on jobs. Shows counts and percentages of local hire and 
Indigenous employees. Organized by project or overall workforce. Can show by job to track project-specific 
commitments.

Criteria: Select jobs or projects, choose employees, filter by local hire status (local, non-local, all), 
filter by Indigenous status, and set date ranges for employment periods.

Key Information: Many projects, especially government or resource sector jobs, have community benefit 
requirements for local hire and Indigenous employment. This report tracks compliance with those commitments. 
Local hire typically means employees from the region where the project is located. Indigenous status is self-
identified and confidential.

When to Use This Report:
• Track compliance with local hire and Indigenous employment commitments
• Prepare community benefit agreement reports
• Calculate local hire percentages by project
• Support Indigenous procurement and employment reporting
• Document employment diversity for clients or government
• Monitor progress toward employment equity goals

Good to Know: Indigenous status and related data is confidential and self-identified. Use this data only for 
legitimate reporting purposes and protect employee privacy. Some projects require specific percentages (e.g., 
40% local hire) - this report helps track compliance.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Purchase & Repayment Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Tracks employee purchases (tools, equipment, uniforms) and repayment schedules through payroll deductions.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track items purchased for employees (tools, equipment, uniforms, etc.) and their 
repayment through payroll deductions. Manage employee purchase programs.

What You'll See: Employees with their purchases listed - item descriptions, purchase amounts, repayment 
schedules, amounts deducted to date, and balances owing. Shows whether repayment is on track, completed, or 
behind schedule. Organized by employee or by vendor.

Criteria: Select employees, filter by purchase type or vendor, choose repayment status (active, completed, 
delinquent), and set date ranges for purchases.

Key Information: Companies often provide tools, boots, or equipment to employees with repayment through payroll 
deductions. This tracks those advances and ensures repayment is happening. If an employee terminates, any 
remaining balance must be recovered from final pay or written off. The outstanding balances are assets (money 
owed to you by employees).

When to Use This Report:
• Track employee purchase repayment status
• Verify payroll deductions are recovering purchase costs
• Identify employees behind on repayments
• Calculate balances to recover from terminating employees
• Reconcile employee advance balances to G/L accounts
• Manage employee tool and equipment programs

Good to Know: Make sure repayment agreements are documented and signed by employees. When employees terminate, 
you can recover the balance from final pay, but there are limits on how much you can deduct without consent. 
The outstanding balances should reconcile to your employee advance asset account.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Job Information Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows current job assignments and work location information for employees. See who is working where.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See current job assignments and work locations for employees. Track where your 
workforce is deployed and who is working on which projects.

What You'll See: Employees with their current job assignments showing job codes, job names, work locations, 
supervisors, assignment start dates, and employment status on each job. Can show historical assignments or 
just current placements. Organized by job, employee, or location.

Criteria: Select jobs or employees, filter by work location or region, choose assignment dates, and filter by 
employment status (active only or all).

When to Use This Report:
• See current workforce deployment by job or location
• Track employee assignments and transfers between jobs
• Plan workforce allocation and staffing
• Identify available employees not currently assigned
• Prepare job-specific employee rosters
• Support job site safety and attendance tracking

Good to Know: Essential for multi-job operations where employees move between projects. Helps you know where 
everyone is at any given time. Current job assignments determine which job's rates and rules apply to each 
employee. Use this for crew planning and deployment decisions.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Within WCB Class
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Lists employees grouped by WCB classification code. Track workforce by WCB rate class for workers compensation reporting.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See employees organized by their WCB (Workers Compensation Board) classification. 
Essential for WCB reporting, rate verification, and understanding WCB cost drivers.

What You'll See: WCB classification codes with their employees listed underneath. Shows employee names, 
occupations, earnings, WCB rates for that class, and calculated WCB assessments. Includes employee counts by 
WCB class. Organized by WCB classification then by employee.

Criteria: Select specific WCB classes or all, filter by province (WCB is provincial), choose employees, and 
set date ranges for earnings.

Key Information: WCB rates vary dramatically by classification - office workers might be 0.5% while high-risk 
trades like iron workers could be 8%. Employees must be in the correct WCB class for accurate assessment and 
compliance. The classification determines the WCB rate applied to their earnings. Incorrect classification can 
lead to under or overpayment of WCB.

When to Use This Report:
• Verify employees are in correct WCB classifications
• Analyze WCB costs by classification
• Prepare WCB reporting and remittances
• Support WCB audits with classification documentation
• Track workforce composition by risk category
• Identify employees needing WCB classification updates

Good to Know: WCB audits often focus on classification - they want to ensure employees are in the right class 
for their actual work. Office workers doing occasional field work should be in a blended class or split. This 
report helps you prove employees are correctly classified.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee T4 Information
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows employee T4 tax information for the year. Displays employment income, CPP, EI, income tax, and all boxes required for T4 forms.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate T4 tax information for employees. Shows all amounts required to complete T4 
tax forms including employment income, deductions, and other reportable amounts.

What You'll See: Employees with their T4 information - Box 14 (employment income), Box 16 (employee CPP), Box 
18 (employee EI), Box 22 (income tax deducted), Box 24 (EI insurable earnings), Box 26 (CPP pensionable 
earnings), and other T4 boxes as applicable (PPIP, pension adjustments, union dues, charitable donations, 
etc.). Organized by employee.

Criteria: Select the tax year, choose employees or ranges, and filter by specific T4 box values if needed.

Key Information: This report shows exactly what will appear on employee T4 forms. Run this before printing T4s 
to verify amounts are correct. The totals by box type should match your CRA remittances for the year. Any 
errors found here must be corrected before issuing T4s to employees or filing with CRA.

When to Use This Report:
• Verify T4 information before year-end T4 printing
• Review employee T4 amounts for accuracy
• Reconcile T4 totals to CRA remittances for the year
• Answer employee questions about their T4 amounts
• Prepare for CRA T4 filing and submission
• Identify T4 discrepancies before distribution to employees

Good to Know: T4s must be issued to employees by end of February and filed with CRA by end of February. Run 
this report in January to verify everything before the deadline. Box 14 (employment income) should match the 
sum of all income tax taxable earnings for the year.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Consecutive Days Worked Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Tracks consecutive days worked by employees. Monitor for fatigue issues, union rules, and health and safety concerns.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track how many consecutive days employees have worked without a day off. Monitor for 
fatigue issues, compliance with union rules, and health and safety concerns.

What You'll See: Employees with their consecutive days worked streaks showing start date of the streak, number 
of consecutive days, total hours worked in the streak, and current status (still ongoing or ended). Flags 
employees exceeding thresholds (e.g., 7 days, 14 days, 20+ days). Organized by consecutive days (longest 
streaks first) or by employee.

Criteria: Set the minimum consecutive days threshold to report (e.g., show only 7+ days), choose date ranges, 
select employees or jobs, and filter by union or status.

Key Information: Working too many consecutive days causes fatigue, increases accident risk, and may violate 
union agreements or safety regulations. Many unions require days off after certain periods (e.g., 1 day off 
per 7 days worked). This report identifies employees who need scheduled time off for health and safety or 
compliance reasons.

When to Use This Report:
• Monitor employee fatigue and health concerns
• Ensure compliance with union rest day requirements
• Identify employees who need scheduled days off
• Support workplace health and safety programs
• Prevent accidents caused by worker fatigue
• Plan crew rotations and time-off schedules

Good to Know: Run this weekly during busy periods. Long consecutive work streaks (20+ days) significantly 
increase accident risk and violate most union agreements. Schedule mandatory days off for anyone working 
excessive consecutive days. This is a health and safety issue, not just a compliance matter.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Premiums Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows premium pay received by employees such as shift differentials, lead hand premiums, and other special pay. Track premium pay by employee.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track premium pay components by employee including shift differentials, lead hand pay, 
foreman premiums, and other special pay. Analyze premium pay costs and patterns.

What You'll See: Employees with their premium pay broken down by type - shift differential (evening, night, 
weekend), lead hand premium, foreman premium, certification premium, travel premium, and other special pay 
components. Shows hours, rates, and amounts for each premium type. Organized by employee or premium type.

Criteria: Select employees and date ranges, choose which premium types to include, filter by job or union, and 
set minimum amount thresholds.

Key Information: Premiums are additional pay above base rates for special circumstances (night shift, lead 
hand duties, etc.). Common premiums: shift differential ($2-3/hour for night shift), lead hand ($2-4/hour for 
crew leadership), foreman ($5-8/hour for supervision). These add significantly to labour costs and should be 
tracked for job costing.

When to Use This Report:
• Track total premium pay costs by employee
• Analyze shift differential and premium patterns
• Calculate premium pay as percentage of base pay
• Verify premium pay calculations and rates
• Include premium costs in job costing and budgeting
• Support labour cost analysis and reporting

Good to Know: Premium pay can add 10-20% to base labour costs on jobs with lots of night shifts or lead hand 
assignments. These costs must be included in job budgets and estimates. Track who's receiving lead hand or 
foreman premiums to ensure they're warranted and properly authorized.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Days Since Employee Hired
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows total days worked for each employee since their hire date. Track employee tenure and total days of service.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Calculate total days worked by employees since hire. Track employee tenure, service 
length, and total working days for seniority or benefits purposes.

What You'll See: Employees with their hire dates, total calendar days since hire, total days actually worked, 
and the difference (days not worked due to layoffs, leaves, etc.). Shows employment tenure both as calendar 
time and actual working days. Organized by employee or by seniority.

Criteria: Select employees, set hire date ranges, filter by employment status (active, terminated, all), and 
choose minimum service thresholds.

Key Information: This tracks actual working days, not just calendar days since hire. Important for construction 
where employees may have seasonal layoffs. Some benefits or seniority systems are based on days worked rather 
than calendar tenure. Shows both total days since hire and actual days with timesheets.

When to Use This Report:
• Track employee seniority based on days worked
• Calculate benefits eligibility tied to service length
• Prepare seniority lists for union purposes
• Analyze employee retention and tenure
• Support pension or benefit calculations based on service
• Identify long-service employees for recognition

Good to Know: The difference between calendar days since hire and actual days worked shows periods of layoff, 
leave, or unemployment. In seasonal industries this difference can be significant. Some union seniority systems 
use actual days worked rather than hire date for ranking.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheet Hourly Earnings by Employee
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows hourly earnings from timesheets by employee. Track regular, overtime, and other hourly earnings for each employee.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track hourly earnings by employee showing all hour types and their associated earnings. 
See complete hourly compensation breakdown by individual.

What You'll See: Employees with their timesheet hours broken down by type - regular hours and earnings, 
overtime hours and earnings, double time, travel time, and any other hourly pay components. Shows rates and 
extended amounts. Employee subtotals show total hours and earnings by type. Organized by employee.

Criteria: Select employees and date ranges, filter by jobs or unions, choose which hour types to include, and 
set minimum hour or earning thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Track employee hourly earnings by pay type
• Analyze overtime versus regular time by employee
• Verify timesheet earnings calculations
• Review employee total hours and earnings for a period
• Calculate average earnings by employee and hour type
• Support payroll reconciliation by employee

Good to Know: This focuses on hourly pay components only. Other earnings like bonuses or allowances are in the 
Timesheet Other Earnings report. The breakdown by hour type helps you understand how much of each employee's 
pay is regular versus premium (overtime, double time, etc.).

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheet Other Earnings by Employee
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows non-hourly earnings from timesheets by employee. Track bonuses, allowances, and other special pay not based on hours.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track non-hourly earnings by employee - bonuses, allowances, lump sum payments, and 
other special pay that isn't tied to hours worked.

What You'll See: Employees with their non-hourly earnings listed - safety bonuses, tool allowances, mileage, 
living out allowances, per diems, production bonuses, and other special pay. Shows amounts and descriptions. 
Employee subtotals show total other earnings by type. Organized by employee.

Criteria: Select employees and date ranges, filter by jobs or earning types, choose which non-hourly components 
to include, and set minimum amount thresholds.

Key Information: Not all pay is hourly. Employees may receive bonuses (safety, production), allowances (tools, 
uniforms), reimbursements (mileage, living out), or other special pay. This report tracks those non-hourly 
components. Combined with hourly earnings, this gives you complete timesheet-based compensation.

When to Use This Report:
• Track non-hourly pay components by employee
• Verify bonuses and allowances were paid correctly
• Analyze special pay costs separate from hourly wages
• Review employee allowances and reimbursements
• Calculate total other earnings by type and employee
• Support payroll reconciliation for non-hourly pay

Good to Know: Use this with the Hourly Earnings report to get complete timesheet compensation. Some components 
like safety bonuses can be significant. This helps you track those separately from hourly wages.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheets by G/L Account
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheets organized by G/L account. Essential for reconciling labour costs to the general ledger and verifying posting accuracy.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See timesheets grouped by the G/L expense accounts they were posted to. Critical for 
month-end reconciliation and verifying labour costs match the general ledger.

What You'll See: G/L accounts with their timesheet entries listed underneath. Shows employee names, dates, 
hours, and costs (including fringe for transacted timesheets). The cost column has GST recovery amounts 
removed. Account subtotals show total labour costs posted to each G/L account. Organized by G/L account.

Criteria: Select which G/L accounts to include, choose date ranges or G/L periods, filter by employee or job, 
and choose whether to include only transacted timesheets or all.

Key Information: Timesheets post to G/L expense accounts when transacted. This report shows that detail so you 
can reconcile to the G/L. The totals by account should match your G/L labour expense for the period. Essential 
for month-end close and verifying payroll costs are in the right accounts.

When to Use This Report:
• Reconcile timesheet costs to G/L labour expense accounts
• Verify timesheets posted to correct G/L accounts
• Prepare month-end labour cost reconciliation
• Support financial statement preparation with labour detail
• Audit G/L posting accuracy for payroll
• Investigate G/L account variances or discrepancies

Good to Know: Run this at month-end and reconcile the totals to your G/L. If they don't match, you have a 
posting error or unreconciled difference. The costs include fringe for transacted timesheets, giving you true 
fully-loaded labour costs by account.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheets by Centre in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows labour timesheets organized by cost centre within jobs. Track labour hours and costs by work area for job costing.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See labour timesheets grouped by cost centre within jobs. Essential for job costing, 
tracking labour by work area, and analyzing productivity by centre.

What You'll See: Jobs with their cost centres listed underneath, showing all timesheet entries for each centre. 
Displays employee names, dates, regular hours, overtime hours, other hour types, and costs (including fringe 
when transacted). Centre subtotals show total hours and costs by work area. Organized by job then by cost 
centre.

Criteria: Select jobs and cost centres, choose date ranges or G/L periods, filter by employee or occupation, 
and choose whether to include costed/transacted timesheets only or all.

Key Information: The cost column includes fringe benefits for transacted timesheets and has GST recovery removed. 
This gives you true job costing amounts by centre. Use this to compare actual labour costs to budget by work 
area, track which centres are consuming the most labour, and analyze productivity by centre.

When to Use This Report:
• Track labour hours and costs by cost centre
• Compare actual labour to budget by work area
• Analyze which centres are using the most labour
• Prepare detailed job cost reports by work area
• Review timesheet detail for specific cost centres
• Support job cost variance analysis by centre

Good to Know: This is one of your primary labour job costing reports. The costs shown here should feed into 
your job cost system. If you organize work by centres (excavation, concrete, framing, etc.), this shows labour 
consumption by each work area.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheets by Date in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheets organized by date within jobs. Track daily labour activity and costs on specific projects day by day.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See timesheet detail by date within jobs. Track daily labour deployment, hours, and 
costs on projects for daily job management and analysis.

What You'll See: Jobs with dates listed underneath, showing all timesheet entries for each day. Displays 
employee names, hours, work descriptions, and costs. The cost column includes fringe for transacted timesheets 
with GST recovery removed. Daily subtotals show total hours and costs each day. Organized by job then by date.

Criteria: Select jobs and date ranges, filter by employees or cost centres, choose whether to include only 
transacted timesheets, and set minimum hour thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Track daily labour activity on jobs
• Review daily crew sizes and hours worked
• Analyze labour costs by day for specific projects
• Compare daily production to labour input
• Monitor daily labour deployment and patterns
• Support daily job cost reporting

Good to Know: Useful for project managers tracking daily activity. Shows exactly who worked each day and what 
it cost. The daily subtotals help identify unusually high or low labour days that might need investigation or 
indicate productivity issues.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheets by Occupation in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheets organized by occupation or trade within jobs. Track labour hours and costs by trade classification.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See timesheets grouped by occupation or trade within jobs. Track labour by skill type 
and analyze workforce composition and costs by trade.

What You'll See: Jobs with occupations/trades listed underneath, showing all timesheet entries for each trade. 
Displays employee names, dates, hours, and costs. Occupation subtotals show total hours and costs by trade. 
Organized by job then by occupation.

Criteria: Select jobs and occupations, choose date ranges, filter by unions or certification levels, and set 
minimum hour thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Track labour hours and costs by trade on jobs
• Analyze workforce composition by occupation
• Compare planned versus actual trade mix on projects
• Verify union trade ratios and requirements
• Prepare trade-specific labour reports for clients
• Support labour planning by trade requirements

Good to Know: Essential for trades-based construction work. Shows which trades consumed the most hours on each 
job. Helps ensure you have the right trade mix and can identify when you're heavy or light in certain trades 
compared to plan.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheets by Client P/O in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheets organized by client purchase order within jobs. Track billable hours by client P/O for time and materials billing.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track labour hours by client purchase order number within jobs. Essential for time and 
materials (T&M) billing and managing multiple client P/Os per project.

What You'll See: Client P/O numbers with their timesheet entries listed underneath. Shows employee names, 
dates, hours (regular, overtime, etc.), labour costs, and billing amounts if applicable. P/O subtotals show 
total hours and costs charged to each client purchase order. Organized by client P/O.

Criteria: Select jobs and client P/O numbers, choose date ranges, filter by employees or occupations, and set 
whether to include billed or unbilled hours.

Key Information: Many clients issue multiple P/Os for a single job - perhaps one per phase or funding source. 
Timesheets can be coded to specific client P/Os. This report shows labour consumption by P/O, helping ensure 
you don't exceed P/O limits and properly bill to the right P/O number. The P/O subtotals show total labour 
charged against each purchase order.

When to Use This Report:
• Track labour hours charged to each client P/O
• Prepare time and materials billing by purchase order
• Ensure labour charges don't exceed client P/O limits
• Verify timesheets are coded to correct client P/Os
• Prepare detailed billing backup by purchase order
• Track available balance on each client P/O

Good to Know: Critical for T&M work with multiple client P/Os. Each P/O typically has a not-to-exceed amount - 
this report helps you track consumption against those limits. When approaching a P/O limit, you need to 
request a new P/O before continuing work.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheets by Employee in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheets organized by employee within jobs. Track individual employee hours and productivity on specific projects.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See timesheet detail by employee within jobs. Track individual employee hours, 
productivity, and costs on specific projects.

What You'll See: Jobs with their employees listed underneath, showing all timesheet entries for each employee. 
Displays dates, hours by type (regular, overtime, etc.), work descriptions, cost centres worked, and costs. 
Employee subtotals show total hours and costs by individual. Organized by job then by employee.

Criteria: Select jobs and employees, choose date ranges or G/L periods, filter by occupation or union, and set 
minimum hour thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Track individual employee hours on specific jobs
• Review employee time allocation across jobs
• Analyze employee productivity by job
• Verify timesheet accuracy for individual employees
• Prepare employee-specific time reports for clients
• Calculate total hours worked by each person on a project

Good to Know: Useful for understanding who worked on a job and how much time they spent. The employee subtotals 
show total contribution by individual. Good for analyzing whether certain employees are more productive or 
identifying training needs.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheets by Cheque
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheets grouped by payroll cheque. See which timesheets contributed to each paycheque for reconciliation and verification.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Link timesheets to the paycheques they were paid on. See exactly which timesheet hours 
contributed to each employee paycheque.

What You'll See: Paycheques with their timesheet entries listed underneath. Shows employee names, cheque 
numbers, pay dates, and all timesheets paid on that cheque including dates worked, hours, rates, and earnings. 
Cheque subtotals show total hours and earnings from timesheets. Organized by cheque.

Criteria: Select cheque number ranges, choose employees, filter by pay dates or G/L periods, and select whether 
to include voided cheques.

When to Use This Report:
• Reconcile timesheet hours to paycheque earnings
• Verify which timesheets were paid on specific cheques
• Research payroll discrepancies or employee questions
• Show employees exactly which hours were on each paycheque
• Audit payroll processing accuracy
• Link timesheet detail to payroll records

Good to Know: This is the bridge between time entry and payroll. When employees question their pay, this shows 
exactly which hours were included. The timesheet totals should match the gross earnings on the cheque (or close 
after accounting for other earnings like bonuses).

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheet WCB Earnings by Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows WCB assessable earnings from timesheets by job. Calculate WCB assessments by project for workers compensation reporting.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track WCB (Workers Compensation Board) assessable earnings by job. Calculate WCB 
assessment costs at the project level.

What You'll See: Jobs with their WCB assessable earnings by classification. Shows hours, assessable amounts, 
WCB rates for each class, and calculated WCB assessments. Job subtotals show total WCB costs by project. 
Organized by job then by WCB classification.

Criteria: Select jobs and date ranges, filter by WCB classifications, choose provinces (WCB is provincial), and 
set minimum earning thresholds.

Key Information: WCB assessments are an employer cost that varies by job based on the trades used. Higher-risk 
trades have higher WCB rates. This report shows WCB costs by job so you can include them in job costing. 
Essential for accurate fully-loaded labour costs on projects.

When to Use This Report:
• Calculate WCB assessment costs by job for job costing
• Track WCB assessable earnings at the project level
• Include WCB costs in fully-loaded labour rates by job
• Analyze WCB cost impact across different projects
• Support job cost reporting with WCB burden detail
• Prepare WCB cost documentation by project

Good to Know: WCB costs vary significantly by project depending on the trade mix. A job with lots of high-risk 
trades (ironworkers, heavy equipment operators) will have much higher WCB costs than office or lower-risk 
work. Include these costs in job budgets and estimates.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheet Earnings by WCB Class
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheet earnings organized by WCB classification. Calculate WCB assessments by rate class for workers compensation remittance.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track earnings by WCB classification for WCB assessment calculations and remittance. 
Show assessable earnings grouped by WCB rate class.

What You'll See: WCB classification codes with their earnings listed underneath. Shows assessable amounts, WCB 
rates, and calculated assessments. Classification subtotals show total assessable earnings and WCB costs by 
rate class. Organized by WCB classification.

Criteria: Select WCB classifications and date ranges, filter by province, choose jobs, and set minimum earning 
thresholds.

Key Information: This is your WCB remittance report. Shows assessable earnings by WCB class with the applicable 
rates and calculated assessments. The totals should match your WCB remittance to the provincial WCB office. 
Different classes have vastly different rates - office might be 0.5% while high-risk construction could be 8%.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare WCB remittance calculations and payments
• Calculate WCB assessments by classification
• Verify WCB rate applications are correct
• Track assessable earnings by WCB class for reporting
• Support WCB audits with classification detail
• Analyze WCB cost drivers by rate class

Good to Know: Run this monthly for WCB remittance preparation. The calculated assessments are what you owe the 
WCB office for the period. Make sure employees are in the correct WCB class - misclassification can result in 
penalties during WCB audits.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheets at T&M Rates by Employee
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheets at time and materials billing rates by employee. Calculate billable amounts for T&M invoicing by employee.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Calculate billable labour amounts for time and materials (T&M) projects. Shows hours at 
billing rates rather than cost rates, organized by employee.

What You'll See: Employees with their hours shown at T&M billing rates. Displays regular hours, overtime hours, 
billing rates for each hour type, and calculated billing amounts. Shows what to bill the client (at marked-up 
rates) versus cost. Employee subtotals show total billable amounts by individual. Organized by employee.

Criteria: Select employees and jobs, choose date ranges, filter by T&M rate schedules or billing status 
(billed/unbilled), and set minimum billing amount thresholds.

Key Information: T&M work bills at customer rates (usually pay rate plus markup) rather than cost. This shows 
hours at those billing rates. For example, an employee paid $30/hr might bill at $55/hr on a T&M job. This 
report calculates the $55/hr amounts for billing, not the $30/hr cost. Essential for T&M invoicing.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare time and materials billing invoices
• Calculate billable labour amounts by employee
• Track billable hours and amounts for T&M jobs
• Show clients labour detail at billing rates
• Verify T&M billing calculations before invoicing
• Calculate gross margin on T&M labour (billing rates vs. costs)

Good to Know: Don't confuse this with cost reports - these are billing amounts at marked-up rates. Use this 
for client invoicing on T&M work. The difference between amounts here and actual costs is your gross margin on 
labour.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheets at T&M Rates by Centre
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheets at time and materials billing rates by cost centre. Calculate billable amounts for T&M invoicing by work area.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Calculate billable labour amounts for time and materials (T&M) projects. Shows hours at 
billing rates rather than cost rates, organized by cost centre.

What You'll See: Cost centres with their hours shown at T&M billing rates. Displays labour hours by centre, 
billing rates, and calculated billing amounts. Shows what to bill the client for each work area. Centre 
subtotals show total billable amounts by work area. Organized by cost centre.

Criteria: Select jobs and cost centres, choose date ranges, filter by T&M rate schedules or billing status, 
and set minimum billing thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare T&M billing by work area or cost centre
• Calculate billable labour amounts by cost centre
• Show clients labour detail by work area at billing rates
• Track which cost centres generate the most T&M billing
• Verify T&M billing calculations by work area
• Analyze gross margin by cost centre (billing vs. cost)

Good to Know: Same as T&M by Employee but organized by cost centre instead. Useful when you bill T&M by work 
area rather than by individual. Shows billing amounts, not costs. The centre subtotals are what you bill the 
client for each work area.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheet Hours by Week
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheet hours summarized by week. Track weekly labour hours and identify overtime patterns and trends.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track labour hours summarized by week. Analyze weekly labour patterns, overtime trends, 
and workforce utilization week by week.

What You'll See: Weeks with total hours broken down - regular hours, overtime hours, other hour types, and 
total hours. Can show by employee, by job, or overall. Weekly totals help identify patterns and trends. 
Organized by week.

Criteria: Select date ranges by week, filter by employees or jobs, choose whether to show detail or summary 
only, and set minimum hour thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Track weekly labour hours and overtime patterns
• Monitor workforce utilization week by week
• Identify weeks with excessive overtime
• Analyze labour trends over multiple weeks
• Plan workforce needs based on historical weekly hours
• Compare week-to-week labour consumption

Good to Know: Weekly summaries smooth out daily variations and show broader patterns. Useful for identifying
