sustained high overtime periods or weeks with unusually low hours. The weekly view is good for workforce 
planning and trend analysis.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheets by Equipment
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheets for labour working with specific equipment. Track labour associated with equipment operation or work areas.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track labour hours associated with specific equipment or equipment-based work areas. 
See which employees worked with which equipment.

What You'll See: Equipment units with their associated labour timesheets. Shows employee names, dates, hours, 
and costs for labour working with each piece of equipment. Equipment subtotals show total labour associated 
with each unit. Organized by equipment.

Criteria: Select equipment units, choose date ranges, filter by employees or operators, and set minimum hour 
thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Track operator labour associated with equipment
• Calculate total labour costs for equipment operation
• Analyze equipment-based work area labour consumption
• Verify equipment operator timesheets
• Support equipment utilization and cost analysis
• Track which employees operate which equipment

Good to Know: Useful when timesheets are coded to equipment - common for operators, equipment-specific crews, 
or work organized around equipment. Shows both equipment usage and associated labour costs together.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheets by Trade in Day
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows daily timesheet summary by trade or occupation. Track daily workforce composition and hours by trade classification.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See daily labour deployment by trade or occupation. Track workforce composition and 
hours by skill type on a day-by-day basis.

What You'll See: Dates with trades/occupations listed underneath, showing employee counts, total hours, and 
labour costs for each trade that day. Daily totals show overall workforce composition. Organized by date then 
by trade.

Criteria: Select date ranges and trades, filter by jobs, set minimum headcount or hour thresholds, and choose 
whether to include indirect labour.

When to Use This Report:
• Track daily workforce composition by trade
• Monitor daily trade mix and crew sizes
• Verify union trade ratio requirements daily
• Analyze trade deployment patterns over time
• Support daily crew planning and staffing
• Track which trades worked each day

Good to Know: Useful for construction projects tracking trade composition daily. Shows how your workforce mix 
changes day to day as different trades are needed. Helps ensure proper trade mix for work being performed.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheets by Centre in Day
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows daily timesheet summary by cost centre. Track daily labour deployment and hours by work area.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: See daily labour deployment by cost centre. Track how labour is distributed across work 
areas each day for daily job management.

What You'll See: Dates with cost centres listed underneath, showing employee counts, total hours, and labour 
distribution for each centre that day. Shows which work areas had labour and how many people/hours. Daily 
totals show overall labour deployment. Organized by date then by cost centre.

Criteria: Select jobs and date ranges, choose specific cost centres, filter by minimum headcount or hours, and 
select whether to include indirect labour.

When to Use This Report:
• Track daily labour deployment by work area
• Monitor workforce allocation across cost centres daily
• Review daily production crew sizes by work area
• Analyze labour distribution patterns over time
• Support daily job management and crew planning
• Track which centres had activity each day

Good to Know: Useful for supervisors and project managers tracking daily crew deployment. Shows where your 
labour force was working each day. Helps identify days with unusual crew sizes or allocation patterns that 
might indicate problems or opportunities.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employees without Timesheets
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Identifies active employees with no timesheets for a period. Find missing timesheets and verify time entry completion.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Find active employees who should have timesheets but don't for the selected period. 
Identify missing timesheets before payroll processing.

What You'll See: Active employees with no timesheet entries for the selected period. Shows employee names, 
last timesheet date, current job assignments, and employment status. Helps identify who's missing time entry. 
Organized by employee.

Criteria: Select the date range to check, filter by employment status (active only typically), choose jobs or 
unions, and exclude known inactive periods if desired.

Key Information: Active employees should have timesheets for every pay period. Missing timesheets mean either: 
(1) time wasn't entered yet, (2) employee didn't work that period, or (3) employment status is wrong. This 
report helps identify missing time entry before payroll runs. Finding these early prevents payroll errors or 
missed paycheques.

When to Use This Report:
• Verify timesheet completion before running payroll
• Identify employees missing time entry for the period
• Follow up on incomplete timesheet submissions
• Verify employment status (active employees should have timesheets)
• Quality control time entry processes
• Prevent payroll issues from missing timesheets

Good to Know: Run this before every payroll to catch missing timesheets. Better to find missing time entry now 
than after payroll when employees didn't get paid. Sometimes reveals employees marked active who should be 
terminated or on leave.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheet Costs by Employee
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows total timesheet costs by employee including wages and burden. Track fully-loaded labour costs by individual.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Track total timesheet-based labour costs by employee including wages, fringe, and 
burden. See fully-loaded employee costs from timesheets.

What You'll See: Employees with their total timesheet costs showing base wages, fringe benefits (vacation, 
statutory, etc.), employer burden (CPP, EI, WCB), and total fully-loaded costs. Employee totals show complete 
cost of employment from timesheets. Organized by employee.

Criteria: Select employees and date ranges, filter by jobs, choose which cost components to include (wages, 
fringe, burden), and set minimum cost thresholds.

Key Information: This shows true fully-loaded labour costs from timesheets - not just wages but all associated 
costs. An employee paid $50,000 in wages might cost $65,000 total when you include fringe and burden. Essential 
for accurate job costing and understanding true employee costs.

When to Use This Report:
• Calculate fully-loaded labour costs by employee
• Analyze total cost of employment including all burden
• Track timesheet-based costs by individual
• Compare employee total costs across workforce
• Support labour cost budgeting with complete costs
• Verify job costing includes all labour burden

Good to Know: The difference between wages and total costs is the burden - typically 20-40% depending on 
benefits and WCB rates. Use these fully-loaded costs for accurate job costing and pricing. Looking only at 
wages understates true labour costs.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Aged Invoice Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows aged balances by client in client code order across all companies. Aging based on invoice G/L periods working backwards from specified period.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display aged receivable balances by client across all companies in the shared environment. Shows 
consolidated aging across the organization. Essential for enterprise-wide receivables management.

What You'll See: Clients with aged balances across all companies showing aging buckets (current, 30 days, 60 days, 90+ 
days), total outstanding, and company detail. Aging calculated from invoice G/L periods working backwards from specified 
period. Consolidated view of client receivables across the enterprise. Organized by client in client code order.

Criteria: Select as-of G/L period for aging calculation, choose clients, filter by companies, set aging buckets (30/60/90 
or custom), and set minimum balance thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Review consolidated client aging across all companies
• Manage enterprise-wide receivables and collections
• Identify clients with aging issues across the organization
• Support corporate collections management
• Analyze total client exposure across companies
• Prepare consolidated aging reports for executives

Good to Know: This is the enterprise-level view of client aging. Same client may owe money to multiple companies - this 
consolidates it all. Use to manage total client risk and collections across the organization. Essential for multi-company 
receivables management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Intercompany Activity
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows intercompany transactions between companies in the shared environment. Track internal billing and transactions across companies.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display intercompany transactions showing billing and activity between companies in the shared 
environment. Track internal transactions across the organization. Essential for intercompany reconciliation and audit.

What You'll See: Intercompany transactions showing company pairs (billing company and billed company), transaction types 
(invoices, payments, transfers), amounts, dates, and balances. Shows internal billing activity between companies. 
Organized by company pair with transaction detail.

Criteria: Select date ranges and G/L periods, choose company pairs, filter by transaction types, and set minimum amount 
thresholds.

Key Information: Intercompany transactions occur when one company bills or transfers to another company within the 
organization. Examples: Company A bills Company B for shared services, equipment rental between companies, labor sharing, 
cost allocations. These create receivables on one side and payables on the other. This report tracks and reconciles 
internal activity. Essential for intercompany balance verification.

When to Use This Report:
• Track intercompany billing and transactions
• Reconcile intercompany balances between companies
• Audit internal billing across the organization
• Support consolidated financial statements
• Verify intercompany transactions for elimination entries
• Analyze internal cost allocations and transfers

Good to Know: Intercompany balances must reconcile - Company A's receivable from Company B should equal Company B's 
payable to Company A. Use this to verify balances match and identify reconciliation issues. Critical for consolidated 
financial reporting where intercompany transactions are eliminated.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job Unextracted Activity
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows job activity that has not been extracted to shared reporting. Identify transactions not yet included in shared cost pools.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display job activity that has not been extracted to shared reporting or cost pools. Identify 
transactions not yet included in shared allocations. Essential for shared cost completeness and timing.

What You'll See: Jobs with unextracted activity showing transactions (labor, A/P, A/R, etc.) that have not been extracted 
to shared reporting, dates, amounts, and days unextracted. Highlights activity waiting for extraction to shared cost 
pools or allocation. Organized by job with unextracted transaction detail.

Criteria: Select jobs and companies, choose date ranges, filter by activity types, set minimum aging thresholds (e.g., 
unextracted for 30+ days), and choose detail level.

Key Information: In shared environments, job activity may be extracted to shared cost pools for allocation across 
companies. Unextracted activity has occurred but has not yet been included in shared allocations. This creates timing 
differences and incomplete shared reporting. This report identifies activity waiting for extraction. Essential for shared 
cost completeness and accurate allocation.

When to Use This Report:
• Identify job activity not yet extracted to shared pools
• Ensure timely extraction of shared costs
• Support month-end shared allocation processes
• Verify shared cost pool completeness
• Track extraction timing and delays
• Prepare for shared cost allocations

Good to Know: Unextracted activity creates incomplete shared allocations. Run this before month-end to ensure all activity 
is extracted and allocated properly. Delays in extraction mean delayed or inaccurate cost allocations. Essential for 
timely and complete shared cost management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Control Accounts
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows G/L control account balances across companies and compares to subsidiary ledgers. Verify control account reconciliation.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display G/L control account balances across companies and compare to subsidiary ledger totals. 
Verify control accounts reconcile to detail. Essential for financial accuracy and internal controls.

What You'll See: Control accounts (A/R control, A/P control, job cost control, etc.) with G/L balances, subsidiary ledger 
totals, and calculated variances. Shows whether control accounts match detail ledgers. Highlights reconciliation issues. 
Organized by company and account with comparison detail.

Criteria: Select companies and as-of date, choose control accounts to verify, set variance thresholds for reporting, and 
filter by account types.

Key Information: Control accounts in G/L should equal the sum of subsidiary ledger detail. A/R control = sum of customer 
balances. A/P control = sum of vendor balances. Job cost control = sum of job costs. Variances indicate errors, timing 
differences, or missing transactions. This report verifies reconciliation across the organization. Essential for financial 
accuracy and month-end close.

When to Use This Report:
• Verify control account reconciliation at month-end
• Identify control account variances requiring investigation
• Support financial close and audit processes
• Ensure G/L balances match subsidiary ledgers
• Maintain financial data integrity across companies
• Track reconciliation issues and trends

Good to Know: Run this at month-end before closing books. Control accounts must reconcile to subsidiary ledgers - variances 
indicate errors that must be corrected. Common issues: unposted transactions, incorrect account coding, timing differences. 
Auditors require control account reconciliation. Essential for financial accuracy.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Shared Account Activity
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows activity in shared G/L accounts across companies. Track shared costs and allocations for enterprise-wide expenses.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display activity in shared G/L accounts showing costs incurred and allocations made across 
companies. Track shared costs and enterprise-wide expenses. Essential for shared cost management and allocation.

What You'll See: Shared G/L accounts with transaction activity showing costs incurred, companies charged, allocation 
percentages or methods, and distributed amounts. Shows how shared costs are pooled and allocated across the organization. 
Organized by shared account with allocation detail.

Criteria: Select shared accounts and date ranges, choose allocation periods, filter by companies, and set detail level.

Key Information: Shared accounts pool costs that benefit multiple companies (head office rent, IT systems, executive 
salaries, shared services). Costs are allocated to benefiting companies using allocation methods (headcount, revenue, 
square footage, etc.). This report shows activity in shared pools and how costs are distributed. Essential for 
enterprise-wide cost management.

When to Use This Report:
• Track shared cost pool activity
• Review cost allocations across companies
• Verify allocation methods and percentages
• Support shared service cost management
• Analyze enterprise-wide expense trends
• Prepare shared cost documentation and support

Good to Know: Shared costs require clear allocation methods and documentation. Use this to verify allocations are 
reasonable and properly distributed. Companies receiving allocations should understand what they are paying for. Essential 
for transparent and fair shared cost management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Payment Performance
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows client payment performance metrics across companies. Analyze payment timing and collection effectiveness enterprise-wide.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display client payment performance metrics across companies showing payment timing, days to pay, 
and collection effectiveness. Analyze payment patterns enterprise-wide. Essential for collections management and credit 
decisions.

What You'll See: Clients with payment performance metrics including average days to pay, payment timing consistency, 
percentage paid on time, percentage paid late, and payment trends. Shows how quickly clients pay across all companies. 
Organized by client with performance detail.

Criteria: Select clients and date ranges, filter by companies, set performance thresholds (e.g., on-time = within 30 
days), and choose calculation methods.

Key Information: Payment performance tracks how clients actually pay versus payment terms. Good payers pay on time 
consistently. Slow payers take 60-90+ days. This affects cash flow and credit risk. Analyzing across all companies 
provides complete picture of client payment behavior. Use to identify problem clients, set credit limits, and focus 
collection efforts. Essential for enterprise-wide credit management.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze client payment patterns across companies
• Support credit limit and term decisions
• Identify slow-paying clients requiring attention
• Measure collection effectiveness
• Track payment performance trends over time
• Prepare client payment reports for management

Good to Know: Payment history predicts future behavior. Clients who consistently pay slowly across multiple companies are 
high risk. Use this to set appropriate credit terms and limits. Proactive credit management prevents bad debts. Essential 
for enterprise-wide risk management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Shared Revenue Analysis
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows revenue from shared jobs allocated across companies. Analyze shared revenue distribution and allocation methods.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display revenue from shared jobs showing how revenue is allocated across companies. Analyze shared 
revenue distribution and allocation methods. Essential for shared job revenue management.

What You'll See: Shared jobs with revenue showing total billed, company allocations, allocation percentages or methods, 
and distributed amounts. Shows how shared job revenue is split across companies. Organized by shared job with allocation 
detail.

Criteria: Select shared jobs and date ranges, choose allocation periods, filter by companies, and set detail level.

Key Information: Shared jobs are worked by multiple companies with revenue allocated based on contribution (labor hours, 
costs incurred, agreed splits, etc.). This report shows how revenue is distributed and which companies benefit. Essential 
for joint venture management, shared project accounting, and fair revenue allocation across the organization.

When to Use This Report:
• Track shared job revenue allocations
• Review revenue distribution across companies
• Verify allocation methods and fairness
• Support shared project accounting
• Analyze joint venture revenue splits
• Prepare shared revenue documentation

Good to Know: Shared revenue allocation should match effort and contribution. Use this to verify allocations are fair and 
properly documented. Important for internal equity and joint venture partner relationships. Essential for shared job 
revenue management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job Outstanding Profit
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows outstanding profit (unbilled revenue) on jobs across companies. Calculate earned but not yet billed profit enterprise-wide.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display outstanding profit (earned but not yet billed) on jobs across companies. Calculate unbilled 
revenue and profit enterprise-wide. Essential for financial reporting and revenue recognition.

What You'll See: Jobs with outstanding profit showing costs to date, percent complete, earned revenue (based on percent 
complete), actual billings to date, and unbilled revenue (earned minus billed). Shows how much profit has been earned but 
not yet invoiced across all companies. Organized by company and job with calculation detail.

Criteria: Select companies and jobs, choose as-of date, set percent complete calculation method, and set minimum unbilled 
thresholds.

Key Information: Outstanding profit = Earned revenue minus Billed revenue. Earned revenue = Contract amount times Percent 
complete. This represents work completed but not yet invoiced. For financial reporting, this becomes unbilled receivable 
(asset). Consolidated across companies provides enterprise-wide unbilled revenue. Essential for percentage-of-completion 
accounting and WIP reporting.

When to Use This Report:
• Calculate unbilled revenue across the enterprise
• Support percentage-of-completion revenue recognition
• Prepare consolidated WIP schedules
• Identify under-billing situations requiring invoices
• Support consolidated financial reporting
• Track earned revenue awaiting billing

Good to Know: Large outstanding profit means you have done work not yet billed - get invoices out. For financial statements, 
outstanding profit becomes unbilled receivable. Critical for accurate financial reporting under percentage-of-completion 
accounting. Essential for enterprise-wide revenue recognition.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job Cost Balance Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows job cost balances across companies and verifies they balance to G/L. Reconcile job ledger to general ledger enterprise-wide.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display job cost balances across companies and verify they reconcile to G/L control accounts. 
Ensure job ledger balances to general ledger enterprise-wide. Essential for job cost accuracy and financial close.

What You'll See: Companies with job cost totals, G/L job cost control account balances, and calculated variances. Shows 
whether job ledger totals match G/L across all companies. Highlights reconciliation issues requiring investigation. 
Organized by company with comparison detail.

Criteria: Select companies and as-of date, choose cost types to reconcile (labor, material, equipment, all), set variance 
thresholds, and filter by magnitude.

Key Information: Job cost ledger should equal G/L job cost control accounts. Sum of job costs = G/L control account balance. 
Variances indicate errors or unposted transactions. This report verifies balance across the entire enterprise. Essential 
for job cost integrity and month-end close. Auditors require this reconciliation.

When to Use This Report:
• Reconcile job ledger to G/L at month-end across companies
• Verify job cost accuracy enterprise-wide
• Identify reconciliation issues requiring correction
• Support consolidated financial close
• Maintain job cost data integrity
• Prepare for financial audits

Good to Know: Run this at month-end before closing books. Job ledger must balance to G/L - variances indicate errors. 
Common issues: unposted batches, incorrect cost types, timing differences. Essential for financial accuracy across the 
enterprise.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Payments By Client
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows client payments across all companies. Track consolidated payment activity and cash receipts enterprise-wide.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display client payments across all companies showing consolidated payment activity. Track cash 
receipts and payment patterns enterprise-wide. Essential for consolidated collections management.

What You'll See: Clients with payment detail across all companies showing payment dates, amounts, companies receiving 
payment, invoices paid, and payment methods. Consolidated view of client payment activity. Organized by client with 
payment detail.

Criteria: Select clients and date ranges, filter by companies receiving payments, choose payment types or methods, and set 
detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Track client payments across all companies
• Review consolidated payment activity
• Analyze client payment patterns enterprise-wide
• Support consolidated cash management
• Verify payment allocation across companies
• Prepare consolidated payment reports

Good to Know: Shows total client payment activity across the organization. Use to understand client payment behavior and 
cash flow patterns. Essential for enterprise-wide collections management and cash forecasting.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Job Aged Invoice Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows aged invoices by client within job across companies. Analyze job-level aging for project collections management.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display aged invoices by client within job across companies. Analyze aging at the job level for 
project-focused collections. Essential for job-based receivables management.

What You'll See: Jobs with client invoices showing aging buckets (current, 30, 60, 90+ days), total outstanding, and 
company detail. Shows aging organized by job rather than just by client. Useful for tracking collections by project. 
Organized by job and client with aging detail.

Criteria: Select jobs and clients, choose as-of G/L period for aging, filter by companies, set aging buckets, and set 
minimum balance thresholds.

When to Use This Report:
• Review aging by job and project
• Support job-focused collections efforts
• Track project-level receivables across companies
• Identify job-specific collection issues
• Analyze aging patterns by project type
• Prepare job aging reports for project managers

Good to Know: Different from standard client aging which groups all clients together. This organizes by job so you can see 
which projects have collection issues. Useful when project managers are responsible for collections. Essential for 
job-based receivables management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Labour Hours And Cost Summary
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows labor hours and costs summarized across companies. Analyze consolidated workforce utilization and labor costs.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display labor hours and costs summarized across companies showing consolidated workforce activity. 
Analyze enterprise-wide labor utilization and costs. Essential for workforce management and cost analysis.

What You'll See: Labor summary across companies showing total hours, labor costs, labor types (straight time, overtime, 
premium), trades or occupations, and cost per hour metrics. Consolidated view of workforce activity. Can show trends over 
time. Organized by company, trade, or period.

Criteria: Select companies and date ranges, filter by trades or occupations, choose summary levels (company, trade, job), 
and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze consolidated labor hours and costs
• Track workforce utilization enterprise-wide
• Review labor cost trends across companies
• Support workforce planning and budgeting
• Compare labor costs across companies or trades
• Prepare consolidated labor reports for executives

Good to Know: Provides enterprise-wide view of labor activity. Use to understand total workforce deployment and costs 
across the organization. Helps identify labor cost trends and utilization patterns. Essential for consolidated workforce 
management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Failed Emails
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows emails that failed to send across companies. Identify and retry failed email communications.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display emails that failed to send across companies showing failed communication attempts. Identify 
and retry failed emails. Essential for ensuring important communications reach recipients.

What You'll See: Failed emails across companies showing email types (invoices, statements, reports, notifications), 
intended recipients, failure dates, failure reasons (invalid address, server error, etc.), and retry status. Shows which 
communications did not reach intended recipients. Organized by company and failure type.

Criteria: Select companies and date ranges, filter by email types or recipients, choose failure reasons, and set retry 
status.

Key Information: Failed emails mean important communications did not reach recipients - invoices not received, statements 
not sent, reports not delivered. Common causes: invalid email addresses, server errors, recipient blocks. These must be 
investigated and resolved. Failed invoices delay payment. Failed notifications cause missed information. Essential for 
communication reliability.

When to Use This Report:
• Identify failed email communications
• Investigate and correct email delivery issues
• Retry failed important emails (invoices, statements)
• Update invalid email addresses
• Ensure critical communications reach recipients
• Monitor email system reliability

Good to Know: Check this regularly (weekly). Failed invoice emails delay payment - resend immediately. Invalid email 
addresses need correction in master files. Some failures indicate email server issues requiring IT attention. Essential 
for reliable business communications.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Labour Cost Summary by Centre
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows labour costs summarized by centre across companies in shared environment. Analyze workforce costs by work element enterprise-wide.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display labour costs summarized by centre across companies in the shared environment. Analyze 
workforce costs by work element enterprise-wide. Essential for shared labour cost analysis.

What You'll See: Centres with labour cost totals across companies showing hours, labour costs, labour types (straight time, 
overtime, premium), cost per hour, and company detail. Consolidated view of labour costs by centre. Shows which work 
elements consume the most labour. Organized by centre with company breakdown.

Criteria: Select centres, jobs, and date ranges, filter by companies, choose cost types (actual, burden, all), and set 
detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze labour costs by work element across companies
• Compare centre labour consumption enterprise-wide
• Support shared job cost analysis
• Track labour allocation across companies
• Review workforce deployment by centre
• Prepare consolidated labour cost reports

Good to Know: Shows labour costs by centre across all companies working on shared jobs. Use to understand which work 
elements are most labour-intensive across the organization. Essential for shared job labour cost management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Shared Client P/O Labour Dispersion
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows labour hours and costs by client P/O across companies. Track shared workforce activity by client authorization.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display labour hours and costs organized by client P/O across companies in shared environment. 
Track shared workforce activity by client authorization. Essential for P/O-based labour billing across companies.

What You'll See: Client P/Os with labour detail across companies showing employees, hours worked, labour costs, companies 
providing labour, and cost breakdown. Shows which companies contributed labour to each client P/O. Organized by client P/O 
with company and employee detail.

Criteria: Select client P/Os and date ranges, filter by companies or employees, choose cost types, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Track labour by client P/O across companies
• Prepare P/O-based labour billing for shared work
• Analyze labour contribution by company
• Support T&M billing on shared jobs
• Verify P/O labour allocations
• Show clients labour detail by authorization

Good to Know: When multiple companies work on the same client P/O, this shows each company's labour contribution. Use for 
P/O-based billing on shared work. Essential for multi-company P/O management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Shared Centre Labour Dispersion
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows labour hours and costs dispersed across centres and companies. Analyze how workforce is allocated to work elements enterprise-wide.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display labour hours and costs showing how workforce is dispersed across centres and companies. 
Analyze workforce allocation to work elements enterprise-wide. Essential for shared labour dispersion analysis.

What You'll See: Centres with labour dispersion across companies showing hours, costs, employees, companies providing labour, 
and allocation detail. Shows which companies worked on which centres and how much. Organized by centre with company and 
employee breakdown.

Criteria: Select centres and jobs, choose date ranges, filter by companies or employees, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze labour allocation across centres and companies
• Track workforce dispersion by work element
• Review multi-company labour contributions
• Support shared job labour analysis
• Compare company labour deployment
• Prepare labour dispersion reports

Good to Know: Dispersion shows how labour is spread across centres and companies. Use to understand workforce allocation 
patterns on shared jobs. Essential for multi-company labour management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Shared Employee Labour Dispersion
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows labour hours and costs by individual employee across jobs and companies. Track where each employee works in shared environment.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display labour hours and costs by individual employee across jobs and companies. Track where each 
employee works in the shared environment. Essential for employee utilization and cost tracking.

What You'll See: Employees with labour dispersion showing jobs, centres, hours, costs, and companies. Shows where each 
employee worked and how their time was distributed. Organized by employee with job and centre detail.

Criteria: Select employees and date ranges, filter by jobs, companies, or centres, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Track where employees worked across jobs and companies
• Analyze employee utilization and deployment
• Review individual labour allocation patterns
• Support employee cost tracking in shared environment
• Verify timesheet accuracy and completeness
• Prepare employee labour reports

Good to Know: Shows how each employee's time was distributed across work. Use to track employee utilization and verify they 
worked where expected. Essential for employee management in shared environment.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Shared Occupation Labour Dispersion
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows labour hours and costs by occupation/trade across jobs and companies. Analyze workforce deployment by skill set enterprise-wide.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display labour hours and costs by occupation/trade across jobs and companies. Analyze workforce 
deployment by skill set enterprise-wide. Essential for trade-based labour analysis.

What You'll See: Occupations/trades with labour dispersion showing jobs, hours, costs, employees, and companies. Shows where 
each trade worked and which companies provided those tradespeople. Organized by occupation with job and company detail.

Criteria: Select occupations/trades and date ranges, filter by jobs or companies, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze labour deployment by trade across companies
• Track workforce utilization by skill set
• Review trade allocation across jobs
• Support workforce planning by occupation
• Compare trade usage across companies
• Prepare trade-based labour reports

Good to Know: Shows how trades are deployed across the organization. Use to understand workforce composition and trade 
utilization patterns. Essential for trade-based workforce management in shared environment.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Shared Job Labour by Employee in Company
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows job labour organized by employee within company across shared jobs. Track which company employees worked on which shared jobs.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display job labour organized by employee within company across shared jobs. Track which company 
employees worked on which shared jobs. Essential for company labour contribution analysis.

What You'll See: Companies with employees and their job labour showing jobs worked, hours, costs, and labour detail. Shows 
which employees from each company worked on shared jobs. Organized by company and employee with job detail.

Criteria: Select companies and date ranges, filter by jobs or employees, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Track company labour contributions to shared jobs
• Review which employees worked on shared work
• Analyze company labour deployment patterns
• Support intercompany labour billing
• Verify employee job assignments across companies
• Prepare company labour contribution reports

Good to Know: Shows which company employees worked on which shared jobs. Use to track company labour contributions and 
support intercompany labour allocations. Essential for multi-company job labour tracking.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Shared Centre Hours Only Labour Dispersion
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows labour hours (without costs) dispersed across centres and companies. Analyze workforce hours allocation without cost detail.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display labour hours (without costs) showing how workforce hours are dispersed across centres and 
companies. Analyze hours allocation without cost detail. Essential for hours-only labour analysis.

What You'll See: Centres with labour hours dispersion across companies showing hours, employees, companies providing labour, 
but no cost information. Hours-only view of labour allocation. Organized by centre with company and employee breakdown.

Criteria: Select centres and jobs, choose date ranges, filter by companies or employees, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze labour hours allocation without cost sensitivity
• Track workforce hours by centre and company
• Review labour deployment patterns (hours only)
• Share labour allocation data without cost disclosure
• Support hours-based workforce analysis
• Prepare hours-only labour reports

Good to Know: Same as Shared Centre Labour Dispersion but shows only hours, not costs. Use when cost information is sensitive 
or not needed. Useful for sharing labour allocation data with project managers or clients without disclosing costs. 
Essential for cost-neutral labour reporting.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Roll Call
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows employee roll call by job across companies. Create attendance lists for field supervisors to track who is on site.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate employee roll call lists by job across companies. Create attendance lists for field 
supervisors to track who is on site. Essential for daily workforce accountability in shared environment.

What You'll See: Jobs with expected employee lists across companies showing employee names, trades, companies employing them, 
and space to mark attendance. Provides supervisor check-list for daily roll call. Can be organized by trade, company, or 
alphabetically. Used for tracking who shows up each day.

Criteria: Select jobs and date, filter by companies or trades, choose sort order, and set format.

When to Use This Report:
• Create daily attendance lists for supervisors
• Track workforce accountability on site
• Support daily roll call and attendance
• Verify expected workforce shows up
• Identify absent employees
• Prepare field attendance documentation

Good to Know: Roll call is daily attendance tracking. Supervisors use this list to check who shows up. Missing employees need 
follow-up. Use to maintain workforce accountability across companies working on shared jobs. Essential for daily site 
management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Time Entry Sheet
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Prints blank time entry forms used by supervisors to record hours across companies. Field data collection forms for shared workforce.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate blank time entry forms used by supervisors to record hours across companies. Field data 
collection forms for shared workforce. Essential for field time collection in multi-company environment.

What You'll See: Blank time entry forms showing employee lists by job, date fields, hour fields for different pay types 
(straight time, overtime, premium), centre/cost code fields, and company fields. Forms can be pre-populated with expected 
employees. Supervisors write in hours worked. Organized by job for field collection.

Criteria: Select jobs and date ranges, choose which employees to include on forms, set form layout (daily, weekly), pre-
populate options, and include companies.

When to Use This Report:
• Create time entry forms for field supervisors
• Provide standardized forms for time recording
• Support field time collection processes
• Enable consistent time data collection across companies
• Facilitate weekly or daily time entry
• Give supervisors pre-printed timesheet forms

Good to Know: This is a physical form (paper or tablet) for field collection. Supervisors record hours, then someone enters 
the data. Pre-printed forms with expected employees make data collection easier. Essential for reliable field time tracking 
in shared environment.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Reporting Relationships
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows organizational reporting relationships (who reports to whom) across companies. Display supervisory structure and org chart.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display organizational reporting relationships showing who reports to whom across companies. Visualize 
supervisory structure and org chart. Essential for understanding organizational hierarchy in shared environment.

What You'll See: Organizational chart or hierarchy showing supervisors, employees reporting to them, supervisory levels, 
companies, and reporting chains. Can be shown as org chart (graphical) or list (hierarchical indentation). Shows complete 
reporting structure across companies. Organized by supervisory level or reporting chain.

Criteria: Select companies and organizational units, choose display format (chart or list), filter by supervisory levels, and 
set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Display organizational reporting structure
• Show who reports to whom across companies
• Create organizational charts for documentation
• Review supervisory relationships and spans of control
• Support organizational planning and restructuring
• Prepare org charts for presentations

Good to Know: Shows formal reporting relationships - who each employee reports to. Use to understand organizational structure 
and supervisory chains. Essential for organizational clarity in multi-company environment.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Sign-on Sheet
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Prints sign-on sheets for employees to sign when arriving at site. Track daily attendance and site access across companies.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Generate sign-on sheets for employees to sign when arriving at site. Track daily attendance and site 
access across companies. Essential for attendance accountability and safety compliance.

What You'll See: Sign-on sheets with employee lists by job showing names, companies, trades, and signature lines. Employees 
sign when they arrive on site. Provides attendance record and confirms who is on site. Can include time-in fields. Organized 
by job and company for site entry.

Criteria: Select jobs and date, filter by companies, choose format (list or table), and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Create daily sign-on sheets for site entry
• Track employee attendance and site access
• Support safety accountability requirements
• Document who is on site each day
• Enable emergency accountability
• Prepare attendance records for compliance

Good to Know: Sign-on sheets create attendance records and confirm who is on site. Important for safety (in emergencies, need 
to know who is present). Some clients require sign-on sheets. Use for daily attendance tracking across companies. Essential 
for safety and accountability.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheets by Supervisor
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheets organized by supervisor across companies. Cross-check that hours on time entry sheet match system entries.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display timesheets organized by supervisor across companies. Cross-check that hours on time entry 
sheet match system entries. Essential for timesheet verification and supervisor accountability.

What You'll See: Supervisors with their timesheet detail across companies showing employees they supervise, hours entered, 
dates, jobs, and totals. Shows what each supervisor submitted. Can be compared to original time entry sheets for verification. 
Organized by supervisor with timesheet detail.

Criteria: Select supervisors and date ranges, filter by jobs or companies, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Review timesheets by supervisor
• Cross-check system entries against time entry sheets
• Verify supervisor time submissions
• Support timesheet quality control
• Track supervisor accountability for time entry
• Identify discrepancies between sheets and system

Good to Know: Supervisors collect field time and enter it. This shows what they entered. Compare to original time entry sheets 
to verify accuracy. Use for timesheet quality control and supervisor accountability. Essential for timesheet verification in 
shared environment.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheet to Budget Hours
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows actual timesheet hours compared to budget hours by centre across companies. Analyze labour productivity and budget variance.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display actual timesheet hours compared to budget hours by centre across companies. Analyze labour 
productivity and budget variance. Essential for labour cost control in shared environment.

What You'll See: Centres with budget hours, actual timesheet hours, variance (over/under budget), percentage consumed, and 
company detail. Shows whether centres are on budget for labour. Highlights over-budget situations. Organized by job and centre 
with budget comparison.

Criteria: Select jobs and centres, choose date ranges, filter by companies, set variance thresholds for reporting, and choose 
detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Compare actual hours to budget hours
• Analyze labour productivity by centre
• Identify over-budget labour situations
• Track budget consumption across companies
• Support labour cost control
• Prepare budget variance reports

Good to Know: Shows whether labour is on budget across companies. Over budget means consuming more hours than planned (lower 
productivity). Use to identify problem areas and take corrective action. Essential for labour cost control on shared jobs.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Turnaround Amounts
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows turnaround amounts for time and materials billing across companies. Calculate T&M labour charges before invoicing.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display turnaround amounts (markup on costs) for time and materials billing across companies. Calculate 
T&M labour charges before invoicing. Essential for T&M billing preparation in shared environment.

What You'll See: Labour with cost amounts, turnaround/markup percentages or multipliers, calculated billing amounts, and 
company detail. Shows how cost converts to billing for T&M work. Organized by job with labour cost and billing detail.

Criteria: Select jobs and date ranges, choose turnaround rates or multipliers, filter by companies or centres, and set detail 
level.

When to Use This Report:
• Calculate T&M labour billing amounts
• Preview turnaround on labour costs before invoicing
• Verify markup calculations across companies
• Support T&M billing preparation
• Review billing rates and multipliers
• Prepare T&M invoice documentation

Good to Know: Turnaround = markup on costs for billing. On T&M work, cost × multiplier = billing amount. Use to preview T&M 
labour charges before invoicing. Essential for T&M billing preparation across companies.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheet Occupations in Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheet hours by occupation/trade within job across companies. Analyze labour deployment by skill set on jobs.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display timesheet hours by occupation/trade within job across companies. Analyze labour deployment by 
skill set on jobs. Essential for understanding workforce composition on shared jobs.

What You'll See: Jobs with occupations/trades showing hours worked, employee counts, companies providing labour, and trade 
detail. Shows which trades worked on each job and how much. Organized by job and occupation with company detail.

Criteria: Select jobs and date ranges, filter by occupations or companies, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze labour by trade on jobs
• Track workforce composition by skill set
• Review trade deployment across companies
• Support job labour analysis by occupation
• Compare trade usage across jobs
• Prepare occupation-based labour reports

Good to Know: Shows which trades worked on jobs across all companies. Use to understand workforce composition and trade 
requirements. Essential for labour analysis by skill set in shared environment.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheet Headcounts by Union
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows employee headcounts by union/trade across companies. Track workforce size by union affiliation.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display employee headcounts by union/trade across companies. Track workforce size by union affiliation. 
Essential for union workforce tracking in shared environment.

What You'll See: Unions with employee headcounts across companies showing number of employees by union, trades, companies, and 
trends over time. Shows workforce size by union affiliation. Can show daily, weekly, or period averages. Organized by union 
with company breakdown.

Criteria: Select unions and date ranges, filter by companies or jobs, choose headcount calculation method (daily average, 
period average), and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Track workforce size by union across companies
• Analyze union workforce trends
• Support union reporting and relations
• Compare workforce size across companies
• Review workforce composition by union
• Prepare union headcount reports

Good to Know: Headcount = number of employees working. Shows workforce size by union across companies. Use to track union 
workforce trends and support union relations. Essential for unionized workforce management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheet Hours By Employee
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheet hours by individual employee across jobs and companies. Track employee utilization and work patterns.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display timesheet hours by individual employee across jobs and companies. Track employee utilization 
and work patterns. Essential for employee productivity tracking in shared environment.

What You'll See: Employees with their timesheet hours showing jobs worked, dates, hours by type (straight time, overtime), 
totals, and companies. Shows where each employee worked and how many hours. Organized by employee with job detail.

Criteria: Select employees and date ranges, filter by jobs or companies, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Track employee hours and utilization
• Review where employees worked across jobs
• Analyze employee work patterns
• Support employee productivity analysis
• Verify employee timesheet accuracy
• Prepare employee hour reports

Good to Know: Shows individual employee hours across all jobs. Use to track employee utilization and work patterns. Essential 
for employee management in shared environment.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheet Hours By Company
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheet hours by company across jobs and periods. Analyze company workforce activity and contributions.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display timesheet hours by company across jobs and periods. Analyze company workforce activity and 
contributions. Essential for company labour tracking in shared environment.

What You'll See: Companies with timesheet hours showing jobs, periods, total hours, employee counts, and trends. Shows how 
much each company worked. Organized by company with job and period detail.

Criteria: Select companies and date ranges, filter by jobs, choose time groupings (daily, weekly, monthly), and set detail 
level.

When to Use This Report:
• Track workforce hours by company
• Analyze company labour contributions to shared work
• Review company workforce activity trends
• Support intercompany labour tracking
• Compare workforce deployment across companies
• Prepare company labour reports

Good to Know: Shows total hours by company across shared work. Use to track company workforce contributions and compare 
activity. Essential for multi-company labour tracking.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheet Hours By Occupation
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheet hours by occupation/trade across jobs and companies. Analyze labour utilization by skill set enterprise-wide.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display timesheet hours by occupation/trade across jobs and companies. Analyze labour utilization by 
skill set enterprise-wide. Essential for trade-based labour analysis in shared environment.

What You'll See: Occupations/trades with timesheet hours across jobs and companies showing total hours, employee counts, 
companies providing labour, and trends. Shows how each trade is being utilized. Organized by occupation with job and company 
detail.

Criteria: Select occupations and date ranges, filter by jobs or companies, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze labour hours by trade across companies
• Track trade utilization enterprise-wide
• Review workforce deployment by skill set
• Support workforce planning by occupation
• Compare trade usage across companies
• Prepare occupation-based labour reports

Good to Know: Shows total hours by trade across all companies. Use to understand trade utilization and demand. Essential for 
workforce planning by skill set in shared environment.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheet Hours By Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheet hours by job across companies. Track total labour hours and workforce deployment by project.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display timesheet hours by job across companies. Track total labour hours and workforce deployment by 
project. Essential for job labour tracking in shared environment.

What You'll See: Jobs with total timesheet hours across companies showing hours, employee counts, companies contributing 
labour, trades, and trends. Shows total labour effort on each job. Organized by job with company detail.

Criteria: Select jobs and date ranges, filter by companies, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report: Track total labour hours by job, analyze job workforce effort, review company labour contributions, 
support job labour cost analysis, compare labour deployment across jobs, and prepare job labour reports.

Good to Know: Shows total labour effort on jobs across all companies. Essential for job labour tracking in multi-company 
environment.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheet Hours By Centre
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheet hours by centre across companies. Track labour hours by work element for job cost analysis.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display timesheet hours by centre across companies. Track labour hours by work element for job cost 
analysis. Essential for centre-based labour tracking in shared environment.

Criteria: Select centres and date ranges, filter by companies, and set detail level. Use to track labour by work element, 
analyze centre labour consumption, review company contributions by centre, support job cost labour analysis, and prepare 
centre labour reports across companies.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheet Hours By SIN
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheet hours by SIN across companies. Track labour using social insurance numbers for reporting and compliance.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display timesheet hours by SIN (Social Insurance Number) for regulatory reporting and payroll 
compliance tracking across companies. Use for T4 preparation, ROE reporting, government labor statistics, and multi-employer 
scenarios where same person works for multiple companies.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheet Employee Hours Only
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows employee hours only (without costs) by employee across companies. Hours-only view for cost-neutral labour reporting.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display employee timesheet hours without cost information. Same as Timesheet Hours By Employee but 
excludes costs. Use when sharing labour data with project managers or clients without disclosing cost information.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Timesheets by G/L Account
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows timesheets by G/L account across companies. Track labour charged to G/L accounts for financial analysis and verification.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display timesheets organized by G/L account across companies. Track which G/L accounts received 
labour charges for financial analysis. Use to verify labour G/L posting, support financial statement preparation, reconcile 
labour to G/L, and analyze labour by account type across companies.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Trade Ticket Levels by Job
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows trade ticket levels (journeyman, apprentice) by job across companies. Verify certification levels and ratio compliance on shared jobs.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display trade ticket levels (journeyman, apprentice, etc.) by job across companies in shared 
environment. Verify certification levels and ratio compliance on shared jobs. Essential for multi-company trade compliance.

What You'll See: Jobs with trade ticket detail across companies showing journeymen, apprentice levels (1st year, 2nd year, 
etc.), employee counts, companies providing tradespeople, and calculated ratios. Shows certification mix on each job. 
Organized by job with trade and company detail.

Criteria: Select jobs and date ranges, filter by trades or companies, choose ticket types to include, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Verify trade ticket levels on jobs across companies
• Check journeyman/apprentice ratio compliance
• Track certification mix on shared jobs
• Support union and apprenticeship compliance
• Review workforce qualification levels
• Prepare trade certification reports by job

Good to Know: Shows trade certification levels across all companies on shared jobs. Use to verify apprenticeship ratios are 
maintained across the workforce. Essential for union compliance and apprenticeship program management on shared work.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Journeyman/Apprentice Ratios
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows journeyman to apprentice ratios across jobs and companies. Verify apprenticeship ratio compliance enterprise-wide.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display journeyman to apprentice ratios across jobs and companies. Verify apprenticeship ratio 
compliance enterprise-wide. Essential for union and apprenticeship program compliance.

What You'll See: Jobs and companies with journeyman counts, apprentice counts, calculated ratios, and compliance status. 
Shows whether ratios meet requirements (typically 1 journeyman per 1-3 apprentices). Highlights ratio violations requiring 
correction. Organized by job or company with ratio detail.

Criteria: Select jobs and companies, choose date ranges, set ratio requirements by trade, and filter by compliance status.

Key Information: Unions and apprenticeship boards require minimum journeyman to apprentice ratios. Common requirement: 1 
journeyman for every 2-3 apprentices. Too many apprentices without supervision violates rules and creates safety risks. This 
report verifies compliance across all companies on shared work. Essential for avoiding violations and ensuring proper 
apprentice supervision.

When to Use This Report:
• Verify journeyman/apprentice ratio compliance
• Identify ratio violations requiring correction
• Support union and apprenticeship compliance
• Ensure proper apprentice supervision
• Track ratio compliance across companies
• Prepare ratio reports for unions and boards

Good to Know: Run this regularly to catch ratio violations early. Violations result in fines, work stoppages, and union 
grievances. Adjust workforce deployment to maintain compliant ratios. Essential for union compliance and apprentice program 
management across multiple companies.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Hire/Term Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows employee hires and terminations across companies over time. Analyze workforce turnover and hiring trends enterprise-wide.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display employee hires and terminations across companies showing workforce changes over time. Analyze 
turnover and hiring trends enterprise-wide. Essential for workforce planning and turnover analysis.

What You'll See: Companies with hire and termination activity showing employees hired, employees terminated, hire dates, 
termination dates, termination reasons, net workforce change, and trends. Shows workforce growth or contraction. Can show 
trends by month or quarter. Organized by company with hire/term detail.

Criteria: Select companies and date ranges, filter by hire/termination reasons, choose trades or occupations, and set detail 
level.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze workforce hiring and termination trends
• Calculate turnover rates across companies
• Track workforce growth or contraction
• Review termination reasons and patterns
• Support workforce planning and budgeting
• Prepare HR reports for management

Good to Know: High termination rates indicate turnover problems. More terminations than hires means shrinking workforce. Use 
to track workforce trends and identify retention issues. Essential for enterprise-wide HR management and workforce planning.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Trades by Company Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows trades/occupations by company with employee counts. Analyze workforce composition by skill set across companies.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display trades/occupations by company with employee counts showing workforce composition. Analyze 
workforce by skill set across companies. Essential for workforce composition analysis.

What You'll See: Companies with trade breakdown showing occupations, employee counts by trade, journeyman and apprentice 
counts, certification levels, and workforce composition percentages. Shows which trades each company employs. Organized by 
company with trade detail.

Criteria: Select companies and as-of date, filter by trades or certification levels, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze workforce composition by company
• Compare trade mix across companies
• Track skill set availability by company
• Support workforce planning by trade
• Review certification levels across companies
• Prepare workforce composition reports

Good to Know: Shows which trades each company has available. Use to understand workforce composition and skill availability 
across the organization. Helps with workforce planning and trade resource allocation. Essential for multi-company workforce 
management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Trades by Employee in Company Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows individual employees with their trades/occupations within company. List workforce by skill set with employee detail.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display individual employees with their trades/occupations within company. List workforce by skill 
set with employee detail. Essential for detailed workforce composition analysis.

What You'll See: Companies with employees listed by trade showing names, occupations, certification levels (journeyman, 
apprentice level), trade tickets, and employment status. Detailed employee roster organized by trade. Organized by company 
and trade with employee detail.

Criteria: Select companies and trades, filter by certification levels or employment status, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• List employees by trade within companies
• Create detailed workforce rosters by skill set
• Review employee certifications by trade
• Support workforce deployment planning
• Verify employee trade classifications
• Prepare detailed trade reports with names

Good to Know: Provides employee-level detail by trade. Use to identify which specific employees have which skills. More 
detailed than Trades by Company. Essential for detailed workforce planning and skill inventory.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Apprenticeship Board Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows apprentice information for apprenticeship board reporting across companies. Prepare regulatory reports for apprenticeship authorities.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display apprentice information formatted for apprenticeship board reporting across companies. Prepare 
regulatory reports for apprenticeship authorities. Essential for apprenticeship compliance and reporting.

What You'll See: Apprentices across companies with board-required information including names, apprentice IDs, trades, 
apprenticeship levels, registration dates, supervising journeymen, hours accumulated, employers (companies), and completion 
status. Formatted for submission to apprenticeship boards. Organized by company and trade.

Criteria: Select companies and date ranges, filter by trades or apprentice levels, choose report period for boards, and set 
detail level.

Key Information: Apprenticeship boards require periodic reports showing apprentice progress, hours worked, and program status. 
Employers must report apprentice hours to verify training progress. This report provides board-required information in proper 
format across all companies. Essential for apprenticeship program compliance and avoiding registration issues.

When to Use This Report:
• Prepare apprenticeship board reports
• Submit required apprentice progress information
• Track apprentice hours for board requirements
• Support apprenticeship program compliance
• Verify apprentice registration status
• Prepare regulatory documentation

Good to Know: Apprenticeship boards require regular reporting (typically quarterly or annually). Missing reports can result 
in apprentice registration suspension. Use this to prepare required submissions across all companies. Essential for 
maintaining apprenticeship program compliance.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Terminations by Company & Union
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows terminations organized by company and union across shared environment. Analyze turnover patterns by union and employer.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display terminations organized by company and union showing turnover patterns. Analyze workforce 
turnover by union and employer. Essential for turnover analysis in unionized multi-company environment.

What You'll See: Companies with termination detail by union showing terminated employees, termination dates, termination 
reasons, unions, and counts. Shows turnover patterns by company and union affiliation. Organized by company and union with 
termination detail.

Criteria: Select companies and date ranges, filter by unions or termination reasons, choose trades, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze terminations by company and union
• Track turnover patterns across unions
• Review termination reasons by union
• Support union relations and workforce analysis
• Compare turnover rates across companies and unions
• Prepare union termination reports

Good to Know: Shows termination patterns by union affiliation across companies. Use to identify whether turnover is company-
specific or union-specific. High union-wide turnover may indicate union issues. High company-specific turnover suggests 
management problems. Essential for workforce analysis in unionized environment.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Rates Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows employee pay rates across companies in shared environment. Review wage rates and pay structures enterprise-wide.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display employee pay rates across companies in shared environment showing wage information. Review 
pay rates and structures enterprise-wide. Essential for compensation analysis and pay equity.

What You'll See: Employees across companies with pay rate information showing base rates, overtime rates, premium rates, 
trades, companies employing them, and rate effective dates. Shows compensation across the organization. Organized by company 
and employee with rate detail.

Criteria: Select companies and employees, choose as-of date for rates, filter by trades or rate ranges, and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Review employee pay rates across companies
• Analyze compensation by trade and company
• Support pay equity analysis
• Compare rates across companies
• Verify rate compliance with union agreements
• Prepare compensation reports

Good to Know: Pay rate information is typically confidential - use appropriately. Shows compensation across companies for 
analysis. Essential for ensuring pay equity and union rate compliance in shared environment.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Staff Retention Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows staff retention metrics across companies. Analyze tenure, turnover rates, and retention effectiveness enterprise-wide.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display staff retention metrics across companies showing tenure, turnover rates, and retention 
effectiveness. Analyze workforce stability enterprise-wide. Essential for retention management.

What You'll See: Companies with retention metrics including average employee tenure, turnover rates (annual, quarterly), 
retention rates, new hire retention (90-day, 1-year), and trends over time. Shows workforce stability or turnover problems. 
Organized by company with metric detail.

Criteria: Select companies and time periods, choose retention metrics to calculate, filter by trades or employee groups, and 
set detail level.

Key Information: Staff retention measures workforce stability. Good retention = long average tenure, low turnover rates. Poor 
retention = high turnover, employees leaving quickly. Industry average turnover: 20-30% annually in construction. Higher 
indicates retention problems. This report tracks retention across companies and identifies trends. Essential for workforce 
stability management.

When to Use This Report:
• Analyze staff retention across companies
• Calculate turnover rates and trends
• Compare retention effectiveness across companies
• Identify retention problems requiring attention
• Track new hire retention success
• Prepare workforce stability reports for management

Good to Know: High turnover costs money - recruiting, training, lost productivity. Use this to identify retention issues and 
track improvement. Companies with low retention need management attention. Essential for workforce stability and cost 
control.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Most Recent Assignment
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows most recent job assignment for each employee across companies. Track current workforce deployment and availability.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display most recent job assignment for each employee across companies. Track current workforce 
deployment and availability. Essential for workforce deployment tracking.

What You'll See: Employees across companies with their most recent assignments showing current job, last worked date, 
assignment status (active, idle, terminated), days since last work, employing company, and trade. Shows where employees are 
currently working. Organized by company with employee detail.

Criteria: Select companies and as-of date, filter by trades or assignment status, set idle thresholds (e.g., no work for 30+ 
days), and choose detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Track current employee assignments across companies
• Identify available workforce for deployment
• Find idle employees without recent work
• Support workforce deployment planning
• Review workforce utilization by company
• Verify employee job assignments

Good to Know: Shows where employees are currently working or if they are idle. Use to identify available workers for new jobs 
and find idle employees. Long idle periods may indicate layoff candidates or need for reassignment. Essential for workforce 
deployment across companies.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Rate Change Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows employee pay rate changes across companies over time. Track wage increases and compensation adjustments enterprise-wide.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display employee pay rate changes across companies over time. Track wage increases and compensation 
adjustments enterprise-wide. Essential for compensation change tracking and analysis.

What You'll See: Employees with rate change history across companies showing previous rates, new rates, change amounts, 
change percentages, effective dates, change reasons, and companies. Tracks pay adjustments over time. Organized by company 
and employee with change detail.

Criteria: Select companies and date ranges, filter by employees or trades, choose change types (increases, decreases, all), 
and set detail level.

When to Use This Report:
• Track employee rate changes across companies
• Analyze wage increase patterns and timing
• Review compensation adjustments enterprise-wide
• Verify rate changes were applied correctly
• Support compensation analysis and planning
• Prepare rate change documentation

Good to Know: Shows history of rate changes across companies. Use to track wage increases, verify adjustments were applied, 
and analyze compensation trends. Essential for compensation management and audit across the organization.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Employee Anomaly Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows questionable employee record conditions across companies. Identify data quality issues and unusual situations requiring review.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display questionable employee record conditions across companies identifying data quality issues. Find 
anomalies and unusual situations requiring review. Essential for employee data quality control.

What You'll See: Employees with flagged anomalies including: missing information (SIN, address, etc.), unusual conditions 
(active but no recent work, negative vacation balances, expired certifications, etc.), data inconsistencies (hire date after 
termination, apprentice level mismatch, etc.), and compliance issues. Highlights records requiring investigation. Organized 
by company and anomaly type.

Criteria: Select companies and anomaly types to check, set thresholds for flagging (e.g., no work for 90+ days), choose 
severity levels, and filter by employees.

Key Information: Employee record anomalies indicate data quality problems or unusual situations. Common issues: active 
employees with no recent work (terminate?), missing required information (SIN, address), expired certifications, negative 
balances, data inconsistencies. These must be investigated and corrected. Essential for employee data quality and compliance.

When to Use This Report:
• Identify employee data quality issues
• Find unusual conditions requiring investigation
• Support data cleanup and correction
• Maintain employee data integrity across companies
• Verify compliance requirements are met
• Prepare for audits and system reviews

Good to Know: Run this regularly (monthly) to catch data quality issues. Some anomalies indicate process problems (why so 
many active employees with no recent work?). Clean data prevents payroll errors and compliance issues. Essential for data 
quality across the organization.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Event Log Report
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Shows system event log entries for security auditing. Track user actions, data changes, and system access for compliance and security.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Display system event log showing user actions and system events. Support security auditing, compliance, 
and activity tracking. Essential for security monitoring and audit trails.

What You'll See: Event log entries showing: (1) Event date/time and types (login, data change, delete, etc.), (2) Users 
performing actions, (3) Actions performed (created, updated, deleted), (4) Records/data affected, (5) Before/after values for 
changes, (6) IP addresses and machines, (7) Event context and details. Complete audit trail of system activity. Can filter by 
user, action type, date range, or data affected. Organized chronologically or by user.

Criteria: Select date ranges, filter by event types (login, data changes, deletions, etc.), choose specific users or records,
