show only critical events, and set detail level.

Key Information: The event log provides audit trails for: (1) Security - who logged in, when, from where, (2) Accountability - 
who changed what data, (3) Compliance - regulatory audit trails (SOX, GDPR, etc.), (4) Troubleshooting - what changed before 
problem occurred?, (5) Investigation - track suspicious or unauthorized activity. Common uses: Investigate "who changed this 
record?", Track user activity patterns, Support compliance audits, Monitor security (unauthorized access attempts), Recovery 
information (what was value before change?). Essential for security, compliance, and accountability.

When to Use This Report:
• Investigate who made specific data changes
• Support compliance and regulatory audits
• Monitor user activity and security
• Track unauthorized or suspicious actions
• Troubleshoot data issues (what changed?)
• Recover information about previous values
• Prepare audit trails for external auditors

Good to Know: Event logs can grow large - archive or purge old events regularly using Event Log Clean Up. Retention typically 
1-7 years depending on compliance requirements. Not all actions are logged - focus on security-sensitive and financial data. 
Review regularly for security monitoring. Essential for compliance (SOX, PIPEDA, GDPR) and security management.

reportTrainingRecords.name: A/P - Cheques
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Prints A/P cheques on pre-printed cheque stock. Print vendor payment cheques created through A/P Cheques processing.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Print Accounts Payable cheques on pre-printed cheque stock. Output vendor payment cheques after A/P 
Cheques processing. Essential for physical cheque production and vendor payments.

What You'll See: Physical cheques printed on cheque stock showing: (1) Cheque form numbers, (2) Vendor names and addresses, 
(3) Payment amounts (numeric and words), (4) Cheque dates, (5) Bank account information, (6) Invoice details being paid 
(invoice numbers, amounts), (7) Remittance advice (what invoices paid). Formatted for standard business cheque stock. Print 
quality suitable for bank processing.

Criteria: Select cheque batch to print, choose bank account (if multiple), set starting cheque form number, preview before 
printing, and select printer with cheque stock loaded.

Key Information: This prints actual payment cheques AFTER you process cheques in A/P Cheques. Workflow: (1) Process cheques in 
A/P Cheques (select invoices to pay), (2) Print cheques using this utility, (3) Verify print quality and form numbers, (4) 
Sign and mail cheques. Important: Use correct cheque stock (usually 3-part: cheque, remittance stub, copy). Verify alignment 
before loading full batch. Track form numbers carefully (audit trail). Spoiled cheques can be voided and reprinted. Essential 
for completing vendor payment process.

When to Use: Print vendor payment cheques, produce physical cheques for signing, complete A/P payment processing, reprint 
spoiled or damaged cheques, and prepare cheques for mailing to vendors.

Good to Know: Print test cheque first to verify alignment. Load correct cheque stock. Start with correct form number. Secure 
cheque stock (blank cheques are like cash). Dual signatures often required. Moving to EFT? This becomes less used.

reportTrainingRecords.name: P/R - Cheques
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Prints P/R cheques on pre-printed cheque stock. Print employee payroll cheques created through P/R Cheques processing.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Print Payroll cheques on pre-printed cheque stock. Output employee payment cheques after P/R Cheques 
processing. Essential for physical payroll cheque production.

What You'll See: Physical payroll cheques printed on cheque stock showing: (1) Cheque form numbers, (2) Employee names and 
addresses, (3) Net pay amounts (numeric and words), (4) Cheque dates, (5) Pay period dates, (6) Bank account information, (7) 
Earnings detail (hours, rates, amounts), (8) Deduction detail (taxes, benefits, etc.), (9) Year-to-date totals. Formatted for 
standard payroll cheque stock. Print quality suitable for bank processing.

Key Information: This prints actual payroll cheques AFTER processing payroll in P/R Cheques. Workflow: (1) Process payroll in 
P/R Cheques, (2) Print cheques using this utility, (3) Verify print quality, (4) Distribute to employees. Cheque stock usually 
includes pay stub with earnings/deductions detail. Track form numbers carefully. Employees moving to direct deposit = fewer 
physical cheques needed. Essential for completing payroll process.

When to Use: Print employee payroll cheques, produce physical paycheques for distribution, complete payroll processing, reprint 
spoiled cheques, and prepare paycheques for employee pickup/mailing. Test print first, use correct stock, secure blank cheques.

reportTrainingRecords.name: P/R - Employer/Employee T4's
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Prints T4 tax forms for employees. Print annual T4 slips after payroll year-end processing for CRA compliance.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Print T4 tax forms (Statement of Remuneration Paid) for employees. Output annual T4 slips after P/R 
Year End processing. Essential for year-end tax compliance and CRA reporting.

What You'll See: T4 tax forms printed on CRA-approved forms showing: (1) Employee information (name, address, SIN), (2) 
Employer information (name, address, payroll account), (3) Annual earnings (employment income), (4) Income tax deducted, (5) 
CPP/QPP contributions, (6) EI premiums, (7) Other benefits and deductions (RPP, union dues, etc.), (8) Province of employment. 
Formatted for CRA T4 forms - must use approved form stock or print on plain paper with proper layout.

Criteria: Select tax year, choose employees to print (all, specific, corrections), use CRA-approved forms or plain paper (with 
layout), preview before printing, and verify alignment.

Key Information: T4s must be provided to employees by last day of February following tax year. Workflow: (1) Complete P/R Year 
End processing, (2) Print T4 forms using this utility, (3) Verify accuracy, (4) Distribute to employees, (5) File T4 Summary 
with CRA. Important: Use CRA-approved T4 forms OR print on plain paper if using CRA's approved layout. Employees need T4s to 
file income tax returns. Keep copies for 6 years (CRA requirement). Electronic filing to CRA separate (T4 Summary). Essential 
for year-end tax compliance.

When to Use: Print T4s after year-end processing (by end of February), reprint lost or damaged T4s, print amended T4s for 
corrections, and prepare T4s for employee distribution. Must do this annually - CRA compliance requirement.

reportTrainingRecords.name: P/R - Electronic Funds Transfer
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Creates P/R EFT file for bank to process direct deposits. Generate electronic payment file from approved payroll EFT batches.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Create Payroll EFT (Electronic Funds Transfer) file for bank processing. Generate electronic payment 
file from approved P/R EFT batches for direct deposit. Essential for electronic payroll payments.

What You'll See: EFT file creation (not printed output) generating bank-format file containing: (1) Employee bank account 
information, (2) Net pay amounts, (3) Payment dates, (4) Transaction codes, (5) Bank routing information. File formatted to 
CPA 005 or other bank-specific standards. File uploaded to bank for processing.

Criteria: Select approved EFT batch, choose bank account (if multiple), set payment date, select file format (CPA 005, etc.), 
and specify output location for EFT file.

Key Information: EFT = direct deposit - money transferred electronically to employee bank accounts. Workflow: (1) Process 
payroll, create EFT batch, (2) Approve batch for payment, (3) Create EFT file using this utility, (4) Upload file to bank 
(online banking), (5) Bank processes deposits on payment date. Important: Approve batch BEFORE creating file. File must be 
uploaded in time (usually 1-2 days before pay date). Secure EFT files (contain sensitive banking info). Most employees prefer 
direct deposit over cheques. Essential for modern electronic payroll.

When to Use: Create EFT file for direct deposit payroll, process electronic employee payments, upload payment file to bank, and 
complete approved EFT batches. Creates file, not print. Upload file to bank online banking system.

reportTrainingRecords.name: A/P - Electronic Funds Transfer
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Creates A/P EFT file for bank to process electronic vendor payments. Generate electronic payment file from approved A/P EFT batches.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Create A/P EFT (Electronic Funds Transfer) file for bank processing. Generate electronic payment file 
from approved A/P EFT batches for vendor payments. Essential for electronic vendor payments.

Key Information: Similar to P/R EFT but for vendor payments. Many vendors now require/prefer EFT over cheques. Workflow: (1) 
Process A/P payments, create EFT batch, (2) Approve batch, (3) Create EFT file using this utility, (4) Upload to bank, (5) 
Bank processes payments. Advantages: Faster payment, lower cost (no cheque stock), better tracking, vendor preference. Secure 
EFT files. Vendors need to provide banking information. Essential for modern electronic A/P.

When to Use: Create EFT file for electronic vendor payments, process A/P payments electronically, upload payment file to bank, 
and complete approved A/P EFT batches. Creates file for bank upload, not printed output.

reportTrainingRecords.name: Approve EFT Batch
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Approves EFT payment batches before file creation. Confirm and authorize P/R or A/P EFT batches for processing and payment.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Approve EFT payment batches (P/R or A/P) before creating payment files. Confirm and authorize 
electronic payments. Essential for EFT payment authorization and control.

What You'll See: EFT batches awaiting approval showing: (1) Batch identifiers and descriptions, (2) Payment types (payroll, 
A/P), (3) Number of payments in batch, (4) Total payment amounts, (5) Payment dates, (6) Who created batch, (7) Approval 
status. Review and approve batches for payment. Organized by batch date or type.

Criteria: Select EFT batches to review (P/R, A/P, or both), show only pending approvals, filter by date or amount, review 
payment detail, and approve or reject batches.

Key Information: EFT batches must be approved before creating payment files - provides control over electronic payments. 
Workflow: (1) Payroll/A/P creates EFT batch, (2) Authorized person reviews and approves using this utility, (3) Create EFT 
file (previous utilities), (4) Upload to bank. Approval reviews: Payment amounts correct? Right payment date? Correct 
recipients? Sufficient funds? Reject suspicious or incorrect batches. Separation of duties - creator should not approve own 
batches. Essential internal control for electronic payments.

When to Use: Review and approve EFT payment batches, authorize electronic payments before processing, verify payment accuracy 
and amounts, enforce payment approval controls, and reject incorrect or suspicious batches. Required before creating EFT files. 
Good internal control - separation of duties between batch creation and approval.

reportTrainingRecords.name: P/R - Subcontractor T5018's
reportTrainingRecords.summary: Prints T5018 forms for subcontractors. Report construction subcontractor earnings for CRA compliance and year-end tax reporting.
reportTrainingRecords.trainingText:
Purpose: Print T5018 forms (Statement of Contract Payments) for subcontractors. Report construction 
subcontractor earnings for CRA compliance. Essential for construction industry year-end tax reporting.

What You'll See: T5018 tax forms printed showing: (1) Subcontractor information (name, address, business number), (2) 
Contractor information (your company), (3) Annual contract payments made, (4) Type of services, (5) Contract numbers. Formatted 
for CRA T5018 forms or plain paper with proper layout.

Key Information: T5018 required for construction companies reporting payments to subcontractors. CRA uses to track construction 
industry income. Must file if: (1) Your principal business is construction, (2) You paid subcontractors for construction 
services. Deadline: Last day of February following tax year. Report all subcontractor payments (individuals, partnerships, 
corporations). Different from employee T4s - these are for subcontractors/vendors. File T5018 Summary with CRA along with 
individual slips. Essential for construction industry tax compliance.

When to Use: Print T5018s after year-end (by end of February), report subcontractor payments to CRA, comply with construction 
industry reporting requirements, reprint forms for corrections, and prepare annual subcontractor reporting. Required annually 
for construction companies - CRA compliance.
